title: OAT Elections
body:
The election phase for the Oversight and Transparency Committee (OAT) will begin today, Thursday 9th of July, and will conclude a week later on Thursday, 16th of July. For the vote, a shutterized, weighted voting system will be utilized.

All candidates that applied have passed the preliminary eligibility check and will therefore participate in the elections. In the event that an elected candidate fails to pass the full compliance process after their election, the seat will be offered to the next eligible candidate by votes received.

The applicants are (in order of their application):

- [Manoj Kumar Desai](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/oversight-and-transparency-committee-oat-june-2026-elections-application-thread/30873/2)
- [Max Lomu](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/oversight-and-transparency-committee-oat-june-2026-elections-application-thread/30873/3)
- [Federico Holzwarth](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/oversight-and-transparency-committee-oat-june-2026-elections-application-thread/30873/4)
- [Pedro Breuer](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/oversight-and-transparency-committee-oat-june-2026-elections-application-thread/30873/5)
- [Patrick McCorry](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/oversight-and-transparency-committee-oat-june-2026-elections-application-thread/30873/7)
- [Varit Ruangsiri](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/oversight-and-transparency-committee-oat-june-2026-elections-application-thread/30873/9)
- [Alex Netto](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/oversight-and-transparency-committee-oat-june-2026-elections-application-thread/30873/10)
- [Zeptimus](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/oversight-and-transparency-committee-oat-june-2026-elections-application-thread/30873/11)
- [João Kury](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/oversight-and-transparency-committee-oat-june-2026-elections-application-thread/30873/12)
- [Rika Goldberg](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/oversight-and-transparency-committee-oat-june-2026-elections-application-thread/30873/13)
- [Tom Berry](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/oversight-and-transparency-committee-oat-june-2026-elections-application-thread/30873/14)
- [Jojo](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/oversight-and-transparency-committee-oat-june-2026-elections-application-thread/30873/15)
- [A.J. Warner](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/oversight-and-transparency-committee-oat-june-2026-elections-application-thread/30873/16)

We also held two DAO calls in which the applicants presented their case on why they'd be a good fit for the OAT. You can find the recordings [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/18msbFiLzuySjXLqPG2gYU3sS15FT5jvl/view) (Pedro Breuer, Max Lomu, Zeptimus, A.J. Warner, Jojo, Rika Goldberg) and [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1d_QEpj8c93HkqTOyUv-zzb_2D26KpJk-/view) (Patrick McCorry, Federico Holzwarth, Varit Ruangsiri, Tom Berry, João Kury).

### Application of Code of Conduct in the OAT Election

Any delegate not participating in the OAT election is free to vote however they wish. A delegate that is also participating in the election should disclose any conflict of interest when voting, but they are not expected to alter their voting in any way.

The 'Responsible Voting Policy' that was present in the first OAT election is no longer part of the [Code of Conduct](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/the-arbitrumdao-code-of-conduct/30792), or the [DAO's procedures](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/the-arbitrumdaos-procedures/30793), so delegates can spread their voting power however they wish. Delegates and participating candidates who seek to abstain from the vote can do so by voting in a neutral manner, e.g., by splitting the voting power equally across all candidates to effectively abstain.

title: PDP-26: [Public Benefit Funding] The Bridge Career Fellowship
body:
### Requested Funding: £27,000 (~$36,000)
**Project Owner:** Aleksandra Wingert (MSc), PhD Candidate, Imperial College London (@olawin.)

## Summary:
Six months of bridging support for a post-PhD researcher to complete and submit several microdosing papers that would otherwise go unpublished, giving the public a clearer and more honest account of what microdosing does, and to lay the groundwork for a new study on endometriosis and apply for the funding to run it.

The Self-Blinding Citizen Science Microdosing Study 2.0 enrolled 42 people with symptoms of anxiety and depression who either took a microdose or a placebo for four weeks. Several important analyses sit outside the PhD thesis and will not be finished in time for it: the task-based and resting-state EEG brain recordings, a paper on sleep changes and HRV, a prospective paper on microdosing, and a female-specific hormonal patterns analysis. Without dedicated time, these are unlikely to be completed for years, if ever. Finishing them would move the public picture of microdosing from scattered and uncertain to genuinely conclusive: a realistic, harm-reduction-focused account that answers the hype with evidence.

The proposal also seeds something new. The early groundwork for an independent endometriosis study — a focused literature review, scoping, and survey design — is the kind of work that centralised institutions are not likely to pay for, because they fund finished study designs, not the preparation that makes a study fundable. That is the gap public benefit funding exists to fill. Endometriosis and women's health are one of the most neglected areas of medical research, and no scoping study exists in relation to psychedelics.

This is a one-time grant with no recurring ask. The six months produce a fellowship application and a scoped, de-risked study, so PsyDAO seeds a project that then attracts independent support. PsyDAO's role is to catalyse, not to keep funding. Open-access papers and all scoping and survey materials will be shared openly, with PsyDAO named as funder.

title: PDP-27: [For Profit Funding] OPSY: Open Psychedelic Science Ecosystem
body:
### Requested Funding: €30,000 convertible loan
**Project Owner:** Steven Fülle, Founder/CEO and lead developer ( @dandycandy77 )

## Summary
A tool stack for the study of consciousness that enables people to become researchers of their own experience. Operated by OPSY B.V., Maastricht. OPSY enables people to become researchers of their own experience. Individuals investigate and analyze their own altered-states experiences in their own words, for free, and stay in control of their data, with an advanced-analysis tier for those who want to go deeper. The communities that host these experiences (retreats, facilitators and community researchers across Europe, Latin America and other legal or traditional settings) pay to run their own rigorous studies. And institutions pay to study the consented data through a participant-approved, participant-compensated marketplace. This round funds the product and proves that organizers will pay for those studies.

A working prototype is live. This round funds building the product and validating willingness-to-pay at a funded milestone over roughly 6 to 9 months.

The engine (the shared asset) is an adaptive, multimodal AI interviewer that captures experience in people's own words (text, voice, images of art, journal extracts), grounded in a structured experience-data ontology (a substance and contemplative-practice taxonomy and validated research scales) with consent and GDPR rails. A planner decides the next question; an extractor turns answers into research-grade data. Three layers operate on one engine: individuals get a free standardized program plus a paid advanced-analysis tier; organizers (retreats, facilitators, community researchers) become first paying customers via a collection agent and shareable link to run their own branded outcome studies; institutions (academic, and later pharma and public-health) pay to study the consented cohort, or run fully-private self-hosted studies, analyzed in place.

A self-liquidating convertible loan: by default PsyDAO is repaid from organizer revenue up to 1.5× the principal (€45,000); or, if OPSY raises a priced round first, the loan converts into equity at a €100,000 valuation cap (about 30% of the company) or a 20% discount to that round, whichever favors PsyDAO. The note carries 6% annual interest over a 24-month term, plus priority access for PsyDAO.

title: PDP-28: [For Profit Funding] The Doors of Perception — a contemporary dance and light performance
body:
### Requested Funding: $30,000
**Project Owner:** Dmitry Repin, Producer and Founder of Improbable Arts, LLC ( @dop2026live)

## Summary
The first ever dance-stage adaptation of Aldous Huxley's The Doors of Perception: a full-evening contemporary choreography for twelve dancers, large-scale video mapping, volumetric light, and movement-driven generative visuals, built to tour major theatres worldwide.

Huxley's 1954 book shaped seventy years of conversation about consciousness and has never been adapted for the dance stage. There is no landmark stage work for the current psychedelic renaissance, and demand is rising for non-verbal, physically intense live experience. As AI-generated media floods every screen, live movement in a shared physical space becomes structurally scarcer and more valuable. The wordless format also opens markets closed to more explicit productions.

A 70-minute touring production across 16 choreographic scenes with no spoken text: an original score, a full lighting and projection design, and a virtual production pipeline (Unreal Engine and TouchDesigner) that pre-builds each venue in software. The work premieres in Fall 2026 and becomes a touring asset generating presenter fees and guarantees over its lifetime.

Performance rights secured from the Aldous Huxley estate for worldwide touring. Full creative team attached. Barcelona creation residency completed (February 2026) and Orsolina28 (Italy) residency completed (April 2026), with the full technical system rehearsed on complete scenes. The visual pipeline is built and tested in software. The lead producer (Improbable Arts) has committed roughly 50% of the budget. Next milestones: Berlin production integration (August 2026) and a private viewing (August 27–29, 2026), then the Fall 2026 premiere.

Revenue share through a standard theatrical waterfall. PsyDAO's contribution enters the investor pool under the Production Investment Agreement. Investors recoup 100% of their capital from net receipts before any profit is distributed; thereafter net profit is split 50% to the investor pool (pro rata) and 50% to the producer and creative pool.

title: PDP-29: [For Profit Funding] Lucy's Magazine — Network and Advertisement Partnership
body:
### Requested Funding: CHF 1,600 ($1978)
**Project Owner:** Tom Saborowski from Nachtschatten Verlag (publisher of Lucy's Magazine) ( @thepsychedelichistorian)

## Summary
PsyDAO secures a recurring print/digital media presence (ads, PR, agenda listings, banner, interview, TV feature, social posts) in Lucy's Magazine and it's website in exchange for a quarterly fee paid from the PsyDAO treasury — turning treasury spend into ongoing brand reach, lead flow, and credibility within the psychedelics community that Lucy's Magazine already serves.

Lucy's Magazine is a long-running, print-and-digital psychedelic publication (events calendar, PR, interviews, soon TV segment) launching an English-language edition soon, extending its reach beyond the German-speaking market into the broader international psychedelics community — precisely the audience PsyDAO needs for visibility, partnerships, and PSY token awareness.

Concrete deliverables — the "Standard-Plus" tier:
- 1/3 page ad in Lucy's Magazine, each issue
- Agenda/events listing, at least 8x per year
- Standard banner on the Lucy's Magazine website
- One PR article per year
- Mid-size organization listing on the website (up to 2,000 characters, 2–3 photos, with backlink)
- Mutual backlink with the possibility of a subscriber affiliate commission for PsyDAO; small banner exchange (website/newsletter) negotiable as partial in-kind off

This is a cost-for-reach arrangement. PsyDAO pays Nachtschatten Verlag a quarterly fee for guaranteed placement; in return, PsyDAO receives durable, repeated brand exposure to a relevant audience, which is expected to translate into community growth, partnership leads, and PSY awareness rather than direct treasury revenue. On top of this, an affiliate-style revenue stream is available: for new magazine subscribers who sign up through a unique tracking link shared by PsyDAO, PsyDAO can earn a commission (e.g., 20%) of that subscriber's monthly subscription fee for as long as the subscription is active — giving the treasury a small but genuine recurring revenue line alongside the reach benefit.

title: [SIP-56] Symbiosis: Enabling Access to Robinhood Chain’s Tokenized Finance Ecosystem
body:
# Context
Robinhood Chain is a permissionless, Ethereum-compatible Layer 2 built on Arbitrum technology. The network uses ETH as its native gas token and uses Ethereum blobs for data availability.

Robinhood Chain is developed and backed by Robinhood as part of its broader onchain financial infrastructure strategy.

The network is optimized for tokenized real-world assets, including equities, ETFs, private assets, and other financial instruments. It supports Stock Tokens issued as standard ERC-20 tokens and is designed for assets that can be traded, self-custodied, and used across onchain financial applications.

Robinhood launched the public mainnet of Robinhood Chain on July 1, 2026, following its earlier rollout of tokenized U.S. stocks and ETFs on Arbitrum One.

 # Proposal
Enable support for Robinhood Chain in the Symbiosis protocol.

The proposal includes the following steps:
* Deploying and configuring Symbiosis contracts on Robinhood Chain to support cross-chain and on-chain operations.
* Adding a Robinhood Chain-based token to the Symbiosis AMM DEX on the host chain to enable cross-chain routing: WETH.
* Leveraging DEXs on Robinhood Chain to enable on-chain routing.
* Activating the Symbiosis Relayers Network to handle cross-chain messaging and verification for Robinhood Chain.

 # Key Points
* Supporting this network would help Symbiosis stay connected to emerging RWA-focused ecosystems. 
* Support for Robinhood Chain would enable cross-chain flow of supported assets into and out of Robinhood Chain’s tokenized finance ecosystem.

title: BOT-13: Strategic Allocation in Gecko Robotics
body:
## TLDR

A proposal to allocate 400,000 USDC from the DAO treasury to acquire common equity exposure to Gecko Robotics at an implied valuation of approximately $1.2 billion, representing a modest discount to the company’s June 2025 Series D financing at $1.25 billion.

Gecko Robotics develops autonomous inspection systems and the Cantilever platform, which transforms industrial infrastructure into high-fidelity digital twins. Rather than building humanoids directly, Gecko is creating proprietary physical-world data and AI infrastructure that support autonomous systems operating in complex industrial environments. As industrial humanoids move toward commercial deployment, accurately digitized environments are likely to become an increasingly important component of real-world training, validation, and operation.

This allocation complements the DAO’s existing investments in companies such as Figure AI, Agility Robotics, 1X, Apptronik, and Genki Robotics by adding exposure to an enabling layer of the Physical AI stack. The transaction is structured as a direct share transfer with no participation fees or carried interest, providing efficient exposure at a valuation below the company’s most recent institutional financing.

![DAO Portal Highlights (1280 x 499 px).png](ipfs://bafkreifjejehvyctgygswcjfczysqpscxajkqrac2bvf4gjcg5w2sntd2q)

## Executive Summary

The next phase of Physical AI will not be defined solely by advances in robot hardware or AI models. Autonomous systems also require accurate digital representations of the environments in which they are expected to operate. Factories, power plants, refineries, shipyards, and other industrial facilities remain largely undigitized, creating an important bottleneck as robotics moves toward large-scale commercial deployment.

Gecko Robotics addresses this challenge through an integrated platform of autonomous inspection robots and AI software that transforms industrial infrastructure into high-fidelity digital twins. Every deployment expands a proprietary dataset of real-world industrial environments that customers use for predictive maintenance, asset management, and operational decision-making. Unlike CAD models or simulated environments, Gecko captures the actual condition of operating facilities, creating a continuously expanding dataset grounded in the physical world.

Founded in 2013 by CEO Jake Loosararian, Gecko has raised approximately $347 million, including a $125 million Series D completed in June 2025 led by Cox Enterprises, with investors including Founders Fund, 8VC, and Y Combinator. The company has established commercial relationships with organizations including NAES, ADNOC, L3Harris, U.S. Steel, BP, Duke Energy, and the U.S. Navy, demonstrating adoption across critical industrial infrastructure.

For the DAO, Gecko represents exposure to a complementary layer of the Physical AI ecosystem. Rather than competing to build humanoids, the company is building infrastructure that enables autonomous systems to understand and interact with the physical world. This broadens the treasury beyond robot manufacturers while remaining aligned with XMAQUINA’s long-term investment thesis of allocating capital across the technologies underpinning humanoid robotics and Physical AI.

## Company and Technology Overview

Gecko Robotics has developed an integrated technology platform combining autonomous robotic inspection systems, advanced sensing hardware, and AI software to digitize critical industrial infrastructure.

Its robotic fleet includes magnetic wall-climbing robots, aerial drones, submersibles, and fixed monitoring systems equipped with phased-array ultrasound, eddy current inspection, lidar, computer vision, and other industrial sensing technologies. These systems collect millions of high-resolution data points from power plants, refineries, manufacturing facilities, ships, and other industrial assets that have historically relied on manual inspection methods.

The data collected in the field is processed through Cantilever, Gecko’s AI platform, which constructs high-fidelity digital twins of real operating environments. Customers use these digital models to monitor asset health, identify structural degradation, prioritize maintenance, and improve operational decision-making across complex industrial infrastructure.

Unlike traditional inspection providers, Gecko continuously expands a proprietary dataset of real-world industrial environments with every deployment. This integration of robotics, sensing, and software creates a compounding data asset that differentiates the company within the broader Physical AI ecosystem while providing recurring value across industrial, energy, manufacturing, and defense sectors.

## Strategic Rationale

The DAO’s current portfolio is primarily composed of companies developing general-purpose robots and the intelligence that powers them. Gecko represents a complementary layer of the Physical AI stack. Rather than competing to build humanoids, the company is creating the infrastructure that digitizes the environments in which autonomous systems will increasingly be expected to operate.

This connection to the humanoid thesis should be viewed as long-term strategic alignment rather than an existing commercial relationship. Gecko does not build humanoids, sell humanoid training data, or currently integrate with humanoid simulation platforms. However, the industry has broadly adopted simulation as a critical step before deploying robots into real-world environments. Whether training, validating, or planning deployments, the quality of a digital twin is ultimately constrained by how accurately it represents the physical world.

Gecko’s technology directly addresses that challenge.

The twin is the map. Before a humanoid can perform useful work inside a refinery, factory, or power plant, it must understand the geometry, layout, and condition of that environment. Gecko already creates high-fidelity digital representations of these facilities.

The twin is the training ground. Modern robotics increasingly relies on simulation before real-world deployment. High-fidelity digital twins provide a more accurate environment for testing and validating autonomous systems than idealized CAD models alone, particularly in aging industrial facilities where real-world conditions differ materially from original designs.

Beyond its strategic relevance, Gecko broadens the treasury’s exposure across the Physical AI value chain. While many existing portfolio companies remain focused on developing next-generation robotic systems, Gecko is a commercially deployed infrastructure business whose value is driven by the continued digitization of industrial assets. This provides diversification across both technology layers and company maturity, balancing earlier-stage humanoid investments with a company generating commercial adoption today.

## The Deal

The DAO proposes allocating 400,000 USDC to acquire ~8,333 common shares of Gecko Robotics through a direct secondary share transfer.

The proposed purchase price is $48 per share, implying an approximate $1.2 billion valuation, below the company’s June 2025 Series D valuation of approximately $1.25 billion

**Transaction Details**

-   Allocation: 400,000 USDC
    
-   Share Price: $48.00
    
-   Shares Acquired: 8,333 shares
    
-   Share Class: Common stock
    
-   Implied Valuation: Approximately $1.2 billion
    
-   Reference Financing: June 2025 Series D ($1.25 billion valuation)
    
-   Instrument: Direct share transfer
    

**Fee Structure**

-   Participation Fee: None
    
-   Carried Interest: None
    
-   Additional Transaction Costs: USDC to USD conversion, off-ramping, and wire transfer fees, expected to remain under 3,000 USDC.
    

## Potential Liquidity Events

The following outlines potential liquidity scenarios. These outcomes are not guaranteed and remain subject to company performance, market conditions, and applicable approvals.

Initial Public Offering (IPO): If Gecko continues to scale commercially and expand its enterprise platform, a public listing may become a viable long-term liquidity event.

Strategic Acquisition: Gecko could become an acquisition target for an industrial technology, infrastructure software, or Physical AI company seeking to strengthen its industrial data, digital twin, or asset intelligence capabilities.

Secondary Liquidity: As a later-stage private company with institutional backing, future secondary opportunities may provide interim liquidity prior to an IPO or acquisition, subject to market conditions and investor demand.

Any liquidity event would remain subject to DAO governance processes and community approval.

## Key Risks & Considerations

Execution Risk: Gecko’s long-term value depends on continued commercial execution, expansion of the Cantilever platform, and maintaining technological leadership in industrial inspection and Physical AI infrastructure.

Valuation Risk: The proposed transaction is based on an implied valuation of approximately $1.2 billion. While this represents a discount to the company’s June 2025 Series D financing, future private market valuations may differ based on company performance and broader market conditions.

Secondary Transaction Risk: Completion of the investment remains subject to the company’s transfer procedures, including its Right of First Refusal (ROFR) and any required corporate approvals. Approval of this proposal does not guarantee the transaction will close.

Commercial Risk: Although Gecko has established enterprise customers, continued growth depends on expanding deployments and increasing adoption of its software platform alongside its inspection business.

Strategic Thesis Risk: The investment thesis assumes that high-fidelity digital representations of industrial environments will become increasingly valuable as Physical AI systems mature. While this aligns with broader industry trends, Gecko does not currently build humanoids or provide humanoid training data, and this connection should be viewed as long-term strategic alignment rather than existing commercial integration.

Liquidity Risk: This investment is expected to remain illiquid for an extended period, with no assurance of an IPO, acquisition, or future secondary liquidity.

## Mitigating Factors

Commercial Validation: Gecko has established long-term commercial relationships across energy, manufacturing, defense, and government, demonstrating real-world adoption beyond pilot deployments.

Proprietary Data Advantage: Every deployment expands Gecko’s proprietary dataset of real industrial infrastructure, strengthening the value of the Cantilever platform and creating a compounding data asset that is difficult to replicate.

Portfolio Diversification: The investment broadens the DAO’s exposure beyond robot manufacturers into Physical AI infrastructure, providing diversification across both technology layers and company maturity.

Disciplined Entry Structure: The proposed acquisition is priced below the company’s most recent institutional financing and is structured as a direct secondary share transfer with no participation fees, carried interest, or broker fees, improving overall capital efficiency.

## Transaction Process

Approval of this proposal authorizes the XMAQUINA Foundation to proceed with the proposed acquisition of 8,334 common shares of Gecko Robotics.

As with most private company secondary transactions, completion remains subject to the company’s transfer process, including its Right of First Refusal (ROFR) and any required corporate approvals.

If the transfer is approved, the Northstar Council will complete the transaction and disclose the final investment to the DAO. If the transfer is not approved or the ROFR is exercised, the transaction will not proceed and no treasury capital will be deployed.

## Governance Execution

If approved, the DAO's Execution Engine will finalize terms and compliance with the intermediary, coordinate legal and treasury operations, document the full transaction flow for auditability, and complete third-party attestation confirming ownership of the underlying shares, in accordance with DAO standards.

All treasury activity will be trackable on [dao.xmaquina.io](https://dao.xmaquina.io/)

– The Northstar Council

title: Adopt the CMv2 Penalty Framework
body:
## Summary

This proposal introduces the [Penalty Framework for the Curated Module v2 (CMv2)](https://research.lido.fi/t/penalty-framework-cmv2/11732) as the baseline process for assessing and applying penalties to Node Operators. The Framework establishes how [the Curated Module Committee (CMC)](https://research.lido.fi/t/proposal-transition-the-lnosg-into-the-cmc/11341), with analysis and support from the NOM team (Node Operator Mechanisms workstream of DAO contributors), reviews incidents involving Node Operator conduct, misconfiguration, underperformance, or other protocol-impacting events.

This framework does not presume automatic penalties. Each incident is assessed on a case-by-case basis against factors such as impact, cause, preventability, responsiveness, transparency, recurrence, and whether the Node Operator took steps to avoid greater protocol risk. 

Approving this Framework also establishes how it can be maintained going forward: the CMC becomes authorised to update operational elements specified below without a separate DAO vote for each change, provided the core principles, penalty mechanisms, Node Operator obligations, and governance structure remain unchanged.

## Background

Node Operators operate validators as part of the Lido protocol. Failures in validator operations, such as missed block attestations or proposals, insecure key handling, delayed withdrawals, slashing, or misdirected execution layer rewards, can create direct and/or indirect losses for stakers and reputational risk for the Lido protocol. Not every such failure reflects Node Operator fault: some arise from causes outside their reasonable control, such as client bugs, relay failures, network-wide events, or coordinated risk mitigation. Hence, incidents need to be assessed on their specific circumstances rather than resolved through a fixed rulebook. This Framework sets out the principles, factors, and process that guide that assessment.

Penalties are not intended to be punitive by default. They exist to:

1. Compensate the protocol for identifiable losses, missed rewards, or improperly redirected rewards.
2. Discourage conduct that creates avoidable operational, security, or reputational risk.
3. Encourage timely remediation and cooperation by Node Operators.
4. Protect stakers and the protocol from losses caused by preventable conduct or non-compliance.
5. Preserve the integrity and reliability of the Curated Module v2.

## Core Principles

- **Proportionality**. The penalty amount should be proportionate to the actual or reasonably estimated harm, including direct losses, missed or misdirected rewards, added operational cost, and the risk the incident introduced to the protocol, adjusted for relevant aggravating or mitigating circumstances.
- **Accountability**. Where harm results from conduct the Node Operator could reasonably have prevented, such as misconfiguration, poor key management, inadequate monitoring, inadequate backup or failover arrangements, slow response, or deliberate misconduct, the CMC can apply a penalty and/or recommend additional measures. Harm resulting from causes genuinely outside the Node Operator’s control should be assessed accordingly, and such incidents may be considered as carrying less weight in the assessment of accountability.
- **Preservation of protocol safety**. The Framework shouldn't create an incentive to take unsafe action just to avoid a penalty. If a Node Operator, in coordination with NOM or other relevant Lido contributors, takes conservative action to reduce slashing or key-compromise risk, even if that results in downtime or missed rewards, that decision should be assessed in light of the risk avoided.
- **Case-by-case assessment and non-exhaustivity**. The CMC assesses each incident on its own facts, treating the Framework's categories as reference points rather than a rulebook of automatic triggers. Matching a listed category doesn't guarantee a penalty, and falling outside one doesn't guarantee immunity: the CMC can act on a pattern, a combination of incidents, or repeated lower-severity issues that don't fit into a single category. A list of common incident categories is provided in the [forum post](https://research.lido.fi/t/penalty-framework-cmv2/11732#p-25910-h-7-indicative-penalty-treatment-by-case-type-20) for illustration and is not exhaustive.

## Assessment Factors

Assessment considers two key aspects: the actual event, its **impact**, **duration**, **cause**, **intent**, **preventability** and the way the Node Operator responded, including **responsiveness**, **coordination**, **transparency**, and any **history of recurrence**. Risk avoided and the quality of available evidence round out the assessment.

## Penalty Mechanisms

After the CMC evaluates the above-mentioned factors and determines an applicable penalty, the Framework provides two options for resolution:

- **General Delayed Penalty**. The manual settlement mechanism, used after the CMC has already made a case-by-case decision that a penalty should be applied. Once decided, the CMC reports a penalty amount (estimated harm plus [applicable penalty fee](https://research.lido.fi/t/future-of-the-curated-module-cmv2-landscape/10929/16)), which is locked from the Node Operator's bond. From there, the locked amount is either burned through governance/Easy Track to cover the loss, or released back if the Node Operator compensates directly or the CMC doesn't pursue it further within the period set by the [CMv2 parameters](https://research.lido.fi/t/future-of-the-curated-module-cmv2-landscape/10929/16#p-24792-additional-global-parameters-3).
- **Voluntary Compensation Fast Track**. If the NOM team, the CMC, and the Node Operator agree on the incident assessment and compensation amount, the Node Operator may voluntarily compensate the relevant amount to the Lido Execution Layer Rewards Vault, thereby bypassing the General Delayed Penalty route. However, the CMC and NOM team can still require remediation, post-incident explanation, or monitoring afterwards.

## Review Process

1. NOM identifies incidents through monitoring, validator performance data, relay or builder data, execution layer reward analysis, exit monitoring, key submission checks, public or community reports, Node Operator self-reporting, or other sources. A case may be opened where a material risk is identified, or the circumstances otherwise warrant investigation. At this stage, NOM may also determine whether urgent mitigation or additional information from the Node Operator is required.
2. NOM gathers relevant information, which may include the incident timeline, affected validators and their balances, root cause analysis, infrastructure or configuration details, relay, builder, fee recipient, or reward-flow evidence, and remediation actions already taken or planned by the Node Operator. Failure to provide timely and complete information may be considered an aggravating factor.
3. NOM prepares materials for CMC review, including the incident description, available evidence, Node Operator submissions, affected validators, estimated or actual losses, and any relevant mitigating or aggravating factors. Where precise calculation is not possible, losses may be reasonably estimated using conservative assumptions or other reasonable calculation methods.
4. Reviewing that material alongside the Node Operator’s own submissions and any other relevant information, the CMC may decide that no penalty is warranted, further information or monitoring is required, voluntary compensation is appropriate, a General Delayed Penalty should be applied, the Node Operator’s stake allocation, participation in the Curated set, or type should be reviewed, or the matter should be escalated to the DAO.

## Communication & Disagreement

Each reported penalty is published on the Lido Research Forum, including the incident description, the basis for the penalty, the category of harm, and the calculation/estimation approach used, subject to any confidentiality, security, or operational limits.

If a Node Operator disagrees with the assessment, the decision, the proposed compensation, or the penalty itself, they can respond on that Research Forum thread with additional evidence, alternative calculations, or mitigating context. The CMC will factor that in where timing allows, but disagreement alone doesn't pause urgent protective action if the CMC judges it necessary to protect the protocol. Separately, the Node Operator should be informed of the determination, its basis, and any expected remediation steps; urgent protective measures can be taken before the investigation is fully complete if needed.

## Framework Maintenance & Future Updates

Approving this Framework also establishes how it will be maintained going forward: the CMC becomes authorised to update operational elements, including incident-assessment thresholds, benchmarks, calculation methodologies, examples, and procedural clarifications, without requiring a separate DAO vote for each change, provided the core principles, penalty mechanisms, Node Operator obligations, and governance structure set out here remain unchanged.

Any change that goes beyond routine maintenance, such as a change that materially affects the scope of penalties, a new penalty mechanism, a material change to Node Operator obligations, or a change to decision-making authority, still requires a full DAO vote. 

All updates made under this maintenance authority, whether routine or otherwise, are published on the Research Forum for visibility.

## Next steps

If approved:

- The Framework becomes the baseline process for assessing and applying penalties to CMv2 Node Operators, effective immediately.
- The CMC will be authorised to maintain and update the Framework’s operational elements, such as incident-assessment thresholds, benchmarks, calculation methodologies, examples, and procedural clarifications, as long as the core principles, penalty mechanisms, Node Operator obligations, and governance structure remain unchanged.

title: SDGP-71: Whitelist 3.Finance - sdCRV TWAVP
body:
Quorum: 5,992,000 vlSDT  
Author: Gravity  
Category: A — Stake DAO Governance Proposal (SDGP)  
  
Summary  
This proposal requests whitelisting 3.finance from the TWAVP delay to immediately unlock boosted rewards for our permanently locked SDT positions, integrating a protocol that already enforces anti-mercenary temporal friction internally via a rolling 7-day reward distribution. This exemption removes artificial latency for structurally aligned capital, ensuring our permanent SDT commitments immediately secure their full reward-boosting capacity without compromising Stake DAO’s long-term incentive design.

Context  
3.finance operates as a sovereign currency protocol engineered to issue GUILD—a stable, unencumbered currency backed by earned protocol equity (held in our Protocol-Controlled Vault) rather than redeemable debt. Our economic architecture maintains a strict separation of assets: our Treasury (The Grove) strategically acquires yield-generating derivatives like sdCRV to generate protocol revenue, while our SDT positions serve a distinct, highly aligned purpose. We systematically acquire and lock SDT specifically to secure Stake DAO’s boosted reward allocations for our depositors.

Rather than fragmenting our focus by actively managing gauge votes, 3.finance delegates its voting power directly to the Stake DAO core team. This delegation is a deliberate operational choice that allows us to focus our resources on expanding our own sovereign economic architecture, while ensuring our SDT and sdToken capital remains under the governance of those most dedicated to Stake DAO’s long-term success. For the Stake DAO community, 3.finance functions as a structural liquidity aggregator that provides locked capital and unwavering, unified governance support.

Rationale  
The TWAVP mechanism is an essential anti-manipulation safeguard designed to filter out transient, mercenary capital attempting to flash-stake for short-term reward extraction and governance disruption. 3.finance’s capital architecture is fundamentally incompatible with this type of extraction, and we have engineered our own internal mechanisms to enforce this alignment.

To mitigate mercenary behaviour among our own depositors, 3.finance implements a rolling 7-day reward stream. Every time Stake DAO rewards are processed and allocated to our users, they are locked into a 7-day distribution window; if additional rewards are processed during that period, they are added to the pot and the 7-day distribution timer is reset. This imposes the exact same temporal friction on our users that TWAVP imposes on protocols.

Furthermore, just as our internal reward stream neutralises economic mercenary behaviour, our governance posture structurally reinforces Stake DAO’s cohesion. By delegating our voting power to the Stake DAO core team, we eliminate the risk of fragmented or adversarial governance influence. Mentioning this delegation clarifies our integration model: we are not seeking to bypass TWAVP to exert independent political pressure on gauge allocations, but rather to immediately unlock the economic yield of our permanent capital. Whitelisting 3.finance integrates a protocol that has engineered similar temporal friction internally, while consolidating its governance influence to actively support the core team’s established roadmap, ensuring our economic integration is purely additive to Stake DAO’s stability.  
  
Vote

For (Yes):  
Approve the whitelisting of 3.finance’s integration address from the TWAVP ramp, granting its permanent positions full effective voting power and boost immediately, as described.

Against (No): Reject the proposal.  
Abstain: Take no position.

  
Parameter Value  
Forum debate period 3 days minimum  
Voting period 7 days  
Debate and vote Sequential (debate first, then vote)  
Quorum 15% of total vlSDT supply  
Approval threshold Simple majority (>50% of votes cast, excl. abstentions)  
Anticipated execution If super-quorum is reached  
Address for TWAVP whitelisting: 0xD7Ba3691750153f94dc0EB40bE09448F52f33b13

title: 0x02 CSM: New Permissionless Module Launch
body:
## Summary

This proposal introduces 0x02 CSM, a new permissionless staking module that gives Node Operators a way to run validators with 0x02 withdrawal credentials, supporting an effective balance of up to 2,048 ETH. It complements the existing module, referred to as 0x01 CSM from here on, which continues serving smaller operators unchanged.

As set out in the recent Snapshot vote for [LIP-33](https://snapshot.box/#/s:lido-snapshot.eth/proposal/0x7b07bc31f0b38b69a117473031bc126becc70b9fa37246b53d9fe5a841c814f5), 0x01 CSM will be upgraded (subject to DAO approval) to CSMv3 to support the new validator standard, while a dedicated 0x02 module instance will be left for a separate rollout, with its own parameters.

This proposal seeks Lido DAO approval for the 0x02 CSM rollout, its launch parameters, and a 20% maximum combined stake share limit for 0x01 and 0x02 CSM together. Full technical details are available in the [0x02 CSM Landscape forum post](https://research.lido.fi/t/0x02-csm-landscape/11697).

## Motivation

Ethereum's Pectra upgrade ([EIP-7251](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7251)) raised a validator's maximum effective balance from 32 ETH to 2,048 ETH. This enables reward compounding, reduces the number of validator keys required for a given amount of stake, and lowers consensus-layer overhead, an important requirement for future Ethereum upgrades. Hence, supporting 0x02 credential adoption is a priority for Lido contributors.

However, technical limitations make it impractical to support both 0x01 and 0x02 credentials within the same module. Unlike 0x01 validators, which have a fixed balance of 32 ETH, 0x02 validators may range from 32 to 2,048 ETH. This variance across a single module would complicate deposit handling and bond-risk management, particularly because Ethereum currently lacks an on-chain mechanism for capping validator size.

For these reasons, 0x02 CSM is proposed as a separate module: it gives Node Operators a permissionless path to run 0x02 validators through the Lido protocol, while 0x01 CSM continues to serve smaller operators and its existing operator types, such as ICS and IDVTC, without change.

This proposal is made with the following objectives:

- Give Node Operators a permissionless path to run 0x02 validators through the Lido protocol.
- Improve DAO take-rate while offering a capital-efficient solution for Node Operators.

## Design

**New instance.** 0x02 CSM is proposed as a separate module instance that complements 0x01 CSM rather than replacing it. 0x01 CSM will continue serving smaller operators and existing operator profiles unchanged. 0x02 CSM instance is built on the same updated CSM codebase that powers [CSMv3 and CMv2](https://snapshot.box/#/s:lido-snapshot.eth/proposal/0x7b07bc31f0b38b69a117473031bc126becc70b9fa37246b53d9fe5a841c814f5).

**Stake allocation.** Because 0x02 validators require significantly more capital than 0x01 validators, stake will be allocated in two stages. First, an initial deposit queue allocates the first 32 ETH required for each validator key to activate and begin earning rewards without the full 2,048 ETH being funded upfront. Once activated, the validator moves to a capacity-limited top-up queue that progressively brings it toward full balance as protocol inflows allow. A seat in this queue represents one validator actively receiving top-up stake; once a validator reaches its full 2,048 ETH balance, it exits the queue and frees its seat for the next one in line. The exact number of top-up queue seats will be proposed closer to mainnet deployment in ~Q4.

**Consolidations.** Unlike the CMv1 → CMv2 migration, existing 0x01 CSM operators will not have a consolidation path into 0x02 CSM. Supporting consolidations in this case would require operators to maintain a bond in both modules during the transition and would introduce significant coordination overhead. An operator wishing to migrate to 0x02 CSM will instead need to exit their 0x01 CSM validators and fund new keys in 0x02 CSM, or run in both modules simultaneously.

**Economics.** While 0x02 CSM increases the nominal bond per key, it improves capital efficiency for Node Operators at scale relative to the default 0x01 CSM operator type. Although the nominal bond requirement is higher in absolute terms — 32 ETH for the first key and 30 ETH for each additional key, compared with 2.4 ETH and 1.3 ETH under 0x01 CSM — this should be assessed in the context of the larger validator capacity enabled by 0x02 CSM. A fully topped-up 0x02 validator can hold up to 2,048 ETH, which is 64 times the 32 ETH validator balance under 0x01 CSM. When normalized per 32 ETH of validator balance, the proposed bond corresponds to 0.5 ETH for the first key and approximately 0.47 ETH for each additional key. This represents a reduction of approximately 4.8x for the first key and 2.8x for each additional key, in bond required per unit of validator balance. With a 2% reward share for the Node Operator and 8% for the DAO, this gives Node Operators a higher capital multiplier than 0x01 CSM: approximately 2.18x for the first key and approximately 2.26x for each additional key, with the Node Operator’s overall capital multiplier approaching 2.26x as more keys are added, compared with up to around 1.76x for the default 0x01 CSM type.

### Parameters

The proposed parameters for 0x02 CSM are:

| **Parameter** | **Proposed Value** |
| --- | --- |
| **Bond** | 32 ETH for the first validator key; 30 ETH for each subsequent key |
| **Reward split** | 2% to the Node Operator; 8% to the DAO |
| **Key removal fee** | 0.02 ETH |
| **General penalty fee** | 0.1 ETH |
| **Performance leeway** | 3% |
| **Strikes** | 3 strikes / 6 frames lifetime |
| **Bad performance penalty** | 0.258 ETH per 32 ETH of balance, up to 16.512 ETH for a fully topped-up 2,048 ETH validator |
| **Keys limit** | Not set |
| **Performance coefficients** | 54/64 for attestations, 8/64 for block proposals, 2/64 for sync committee |
| **Exit delay charge** | 0.1 ETH per key after 4 days |

**Note.** The bond and reward split are proposed specifically for 0x02 CSM. The remaining parameters follow 0x01 CSM's [Default type](https://bafybeibhlw3e6zy6xkbdmusky5i5v5rwcpxnjqws23jpmszzkp5xwzzppe.ipfs.inbrowser.link/) as published at the time of this proposal. These values may be updated in the future.

### Operational controls

[The CSM Committee](https://docs.lido.fi/multisigs/committees/#29-community-staking-module-committee) would take on the same operational and emergency roles for 0x02 CSM that it holds for 0x01 CSM, specifically: 

- Report or cancel penalties for protocol violations through a direct on-chain action.
- Settle confirmed penalties through [Easy Track](https://docs.lido.fi/guides/easy-track-guide).
- Roll back the top-up queue through a direct on-chain action in case invalid top-up information is delivered.
- Change the bond curve for a specific Node Operator through a direct on-chain action.
- Pause 0x02 CSM in an emergency via [CircuitBreaker](https://research.lido.fi/t/circuitbreaker-programmable-panic-layer/11400).

## Stake share limit

This proposal sets a 20% maximum combined stake share limit for 0x01 and 0x02 CSM together and proposes assigning responsibility for managing the allocation between the two modules to the CSM Committee. The CSM Committee would change the stake share limit for both modules via Easy Track within the DAO-approved combined cap, following the same mechanism it already uses for 0x01 CSM, as set out in the [LIP-33 snapshot](https://snapshot.box/#/s:lido-snapshot.eth/proposal/0x7b07bc31f0b38b69a117473031bc126becc70b9fa37246b53d9fe5a841c814f5).

0x02 CSM's initial stake share limit specifically has not yet been determined since it depends on the state of the Ethereum validator network and Curated Module v2 at the time of release, and is expected to be initially low (approximately 0–2%). This will be revisited and proposed as part of the mainnet release, targeted for Q4.

As operators move from 0x01 CSM to 0x02 CSM over time, 0x02 CSM’s share is expected to grow while 0x01 CSM’s share decreases.

## Next steps

If this proposal is approved:

- An on-chain vote will be submitted to activate the 0x02 CSM instance with the approved parameters and grant the proposed roles to the CSM Committee.
- The exact number of top-up queue seats and the initial 0x02 CSM stake share limit will be finalized and brought forward as part of the mainnet release, targeted for Q4.
- The CSM Committee's mandate will be extended to manage the 0x02 CSM stake share limit via Easy Track together with the 0x01 CSM, within the approved 20% cap and under the proposed conditions for scaling 0x02 CSM's share.

title: Amendment to Leadership Structure
body:
Governance Structure & Merit-Based Operational Leadership
Constitutional Amendment 

Proposal
Replacement of Existing Leadership Positions

Upon adoption of this amendment, the existing generic Leadership positions established by the Constitution shall be replaced by the following Operational Leadership portfolios:

1. Treasurer
Treasury administration
Budget monitoring
Multisignature coordination
Treasury reporting
Approved treasury asset management oversight

2. Governance & Proposals Officer
Proposal administration
Governance documentation
Proposal compliance
Governance policy administration
Governance reporting

3. Technical & Ecosystem Liaison
Technical coordination
Foundation/Core Team liaison
Infrastructure oversight
Developer coordination
Ecosystem partnerships

4. Community & Communications Officer
Community engagement
Governance announcements
Documentation
Education
Contributor coordination
Community communications

5. Strategy & Performance Officer
Strategic planning
KPI monitoring
Initiative tracking
Quarterly performance reporting
Continuous governance improvement

These positions replace the existing generic Leadership positions and provide clearly defined operational responsibilities.

The replacement of position titles is intended to improve organisational clarity and accountability only and does not alter the governance authority of the High Council or the constitutional powers of the DAO community.

The names and responsibilities of Operational Leadership portfolios may only be amended by an approved constitutional amendment unless the Constitution expressly provides otherwise.

Executive Summary
This proposal clarifies the governance structure of the Redbelly Community DAO by distinguishing between elected governance positions and appointed operational leadership positions.

The High Council will continue to be elected by the community and retain governance authority.
Operational Leadership positions will instead be appointed through a transparent, merit-based process, recognising that these positions primarily perform operational and administrative functions requiring appropriate skills, experience and availability.

This proposal preserves democratic governance while strengthening the operational capability, accountability and continuity of the DAO.

Background
The Constitution currently provides for elected High Council and Leadership positions.

Experience has demonstrated that Leadership positions perform operational rather than governance functions. These roles often require specialised skills and ongoing commitment that may not always be reflected through popularity-based elections.

This proposal aligns the governance framework with the original intent of the Constitution by ensuring governance remains democratic while operational responsibilities are undertaken by suitably qualified contributors.

Problem & Rationale
Operational Leadership positions are responsible for functions such as:
Treasury administration
Governance administration
Proposal management
Technical coordination
Ecosystem liaison
Community engagement
Strategic planning
These responsibilities are better suited to transparent merit-based appointments than popularity-based elections.
The community should continue electing those responsible for governance while enabling operational roles to be filled according to competence and capability.

Objectives
This proposal seeks to:
Preserve democratic governance.
Improve operational capability.
Strengthen accountability.
Improve governance continuity.
Ensure operational positions are filled by suitably qualified contributors.
Increase transparency of appointments.
Reduce operational risk.
Improve long-term sustainability.

Proposed Constitutional Amendment
Governance Structure
High Council

The High Council shall continue to be elected by the DAO community.

The High Council remains responsible for:
Governance oversight
Constitutional compliance
Treasury oversight
Strategic governance
Appointment oversight
Accountability to the community

This proposal does not alter the number of High Council positions established elsewhere in the Constitution.

Operational Leadership
The following positions shall become appointed Operational Leadership positions:
Treasurer
Governance & Proposals Officer
Technical & Ecosystem Liaison
Community & Communications Officer
Strategy & Performance Officer

These positions perform administrative and operational functions and do not independently exercise governance authority unless expressly authorised by the Constitution or an approved DAO proposal.
 
Appointments should seek to match each Operational Leadership portfolio with individuals possessing relevant qualifications, experience or demonstrated capability appropriate to the responsibilities of that portfolio.
_______________________________________________________________________________
Appointment Process
Operational Leadership appointments shall be made by the High Council through majority resolution following an open merit-based recruitment process. Appointment decisions, including the reasons for selection, shall be published to the community. Any community member may challenge an appointment through the Governance Appeals & Review Policy where they believe the appointment process has not been conducted in accordance with the Constitution or approved Governance Policies.
Where an elected position remains vacant, or where insufficient suitably qualified candidates are available, the High Council may appoint a suitably qualified individual to serve until the next scheduled election, subject to transparency requirements.

Appointments should consider:
Relevant experience
Demonstrated capability
Governance participation
Availability
Integrity
Communication skills
Absence of material conflicts of interest

Recruitment Process
Appointments should normally include:
Public expression of interest
Published selection criteria
Opportunity for self-nomination
Transparent appointment decision
Publication of appointment reasons

Terms of Appointment
Operational Leadership appointments should normally:
Be for a six (6) month term with one extension.
Remain eligible for reappointment.
Be reviewed annually.
Remain accountable to the High Council.

Responsibilities
Operational Leadership shall:
Fulfil the responsibilities of their assigned portfolio.
Publish periodic activity reports.
Maintain governance documentation.
Support community transparency.
Cooperate with other leadership portfolios.
Act in accordance with the Constitution, Governance Policies and Code of Conduct.
Inactivity
An Operational Leadership member may be considered inactive where they have failed to meaningfully participate in the responsibilities of their appointed role for a continuous period of thirty (30) days without reasonable explanation or prior notification to the High Council.
Meaningful participation may include:
Responding to governance matters.
Undertaking the responsibilities of the position.
Attending scheduled leadership meetings where reasonably practicable.
Providing required reports or updates.
The High Council may extend this period where reasonable circumstances exist, including illness, family responsibilities, employment commitments or other exceptional circumstances.
Where a member is determined inactive under this clause, the High Council may declare the position vacant by majority resolution.

Performance Review
An Operational Leadership appointment may be terminated for unsatisfactory performance or serious misconduct, including material breach of the Code of Conduct, where the High Council has determined, by majority resolution, that the member has persistently failed to fulfil the responsibilities of their appointed role despite having been provided with reasonable opportunity to address identified concerns.

Removal Process
Prior to removal, the Operational Leadership member should:
Be informed of the concerns.
Be provided an opportunity to respond.
Be given reasonable opportunity to address the concerns where appropriate.
Following consideration of all relevant information, the High Council may remove the appointment by majority resolution.
The decision and reasons for removal should be documented and made available to the community, except where confidentiality is required by law or to protect personal privacy.

Appeals
Any Operational Leadership member removed under this provision may request a review under the Governance Appeals & Review Policy.

Vacancies
Temporary Appointment of Foundation Personnel
Where:
no suitably qualified community applicant is available following a documented recruitment process; or
an Operational Leadership position remains vacant following reasonable efforts to appoint a community member; and
the continued vacancy presents a material operational risk to the DAO,
the High Council may request that the Redbelly Foundation nominate a suitably qualified employee or contractor to temporarily perform the responsibilities of the vacant Operational Leadership position.
Any such appointment shall:
be temporary only;
ineligible for filling the Treasurer role specifically due to conflict of interest
be approved by the High Council by majority resolution;
not exceed twelve (12) months without further DAO approval;
remain subject to the Constitution, Governance Policies and Code of Conduct;
be publicly announced together with the reasons for the appointment.
Where an Operational Leadership position becomes vacant, the High Council may appoint an interim replacement by majority resolution until the position is filled through the normal appointment process.
This proposal does not alter constitutional provisions relating to elected High Council vacancies.
Governance Principles
Operational Leadership exists to support the effective administration of the DAO.
Appointments should be based primarily upon competence, experience, integrity and the ability to fulfil the responsibilities of the role rather than popularity.
Community governance shall continue to be exercised through:
Snapshot voting
Constitutional amendments
Governance proposals
Election of the High Council
Benefits
This proposal:
Preserves democratic governance.
Improves operational capability.
Strengthens accountability.
Reduces operational risk.
Improves governance continuity.
Aligns appointments with required expertise.
Increases transparency.
Supports long-term sustainability.
Risk & Mitigation
Risk
Mitigation
Perception of reduced decentralisation
High Council remains fully elected by the community.
Perception of favouritism
Transparent recruitment process and published appointment reasons.
Poor appointments
Annual reviews, majority High Council oversight and defined removal process.
Reduced community involvement
Community retains governance authority through Snapshot voting and High Council elections.
Constitutional Compatibility
This proposal clarifies the distinction between governance oversight and operational administration.
It preserves community governance while strengthening the operational capability of the DAO.
Budget
0 USDT / 0 RBNT
Decision Requested
Approve the amendment to distinguish elected governance positions from appointed Operational Leadership positions, adopt the transparent merit-based appointment framework described in this proposal, and authorise consequential amendments to related governance documents and role descriptions.

title: [Temp Check] Protocol Fee Expansion: Robinhood Chain
body:
_This proposal is part of the protocol fee rollout, following proposals_ [_#93_](https://vote.uniswapfoundation.org/proposals/93)_,_ [_#94_](https://vote.uniswapfoundation.org/proposals/94)_,_ [_#95_](https://vote.uniswapfoundation.org/proposals/95)_, and_ [_#96_](https://vote.uniswapfoundation.org/proposals/96)_. It uses the expedited governance process_ [_approved_](https://gov.uniswap.org/t/unification-proposal/25881#p-57882-protocol-fee-rollout-4) _in UNIfication, where fee parameter update proposals can bypass the RFC stage and go directly to a five-day Snapshot followed by an onchain vote._

Since protocol fees went live on Ethereum mainnet in late December last year, the rollout has extended to ten additional chains: Arbitrum, Base, OP Mainnet, Worldchain, X Layer, Soneium, Zora, Celo, BNB Chain, and Polygon. The burn system is working as designed, with fees accumulating in TokenJars across chains. From there, searchers claim them in exchange for burning UNI by bridging it back to mainnet and sending it to the burn address.

Uniswap [launched on Robinhood Chain](https://blog.uniswap.org/robinhood-chain-is-live) at the chain's July 1, 2026 mainnet debut, with v2, v3, and v4 all live. As of July 10, the deployments have crossed [$1b of cumulative swap volume](https://x.com/DefiLlama/status/2075608063969485082?s=20). This proposal:

-   Extends the infrastructure for collecting and burning protocol fees to Robinhood Chain
    
-   Enables v2, v3, and v4 protocol fees on Robinhood Chain
    

## Implementation Details

Fees on Robinhood Chain will be routed to the TokenJar on that chain. UNI burned on Robinhood Chain is bridged back to Ethereum mainnet and sent to the burn address.

Robinhood Chain is an Arbitrum Orbit chain, so this proposal reuses the pattern from the Arbitrum One activation in proposal 94.

**Governance path.** Same as Arbitrum One: cross-chain governance messages are delivered as retryable tickets through Robinhood Chain's Inbox contract on Ethereum and executed on Robinhood Chain by the L2 alias of the governance Timelock. The aliased Timelock already controls both factories and the v4 PoolManager on Robinhood Chain (it is the v2 factory's feeToSetter and the owner of the v3 factory and the PoolManager), so no ownership migration is required.

**Burn path.** The releaser, ArbitrumOrbitResourceFirepit, is the Arbitrum One firepit generalized for Orbit chains. A searcher pays bridged UNI on Robinhood Chain to claim the TokenJar's accumulated fees, and the contract withdraws that UNI to the burn address on mainnet through the canonical gateway. As on Arbitrum One, the withdrawal finalizes on mainnet after Robinhood Chain's challenge period.

The TokenJar, Releaser, V3OpenFeeAdapter, V4FeeAdapter, and V4FeePolicy will be deployed ahead of the onchain votes, with ownership verified against the aliased Timelock. This post will be updated with those addresses when they've been deployed and a link to the repo containing the contracts and deployment scripts once it has been merged.

Implementation details for the v4 fee system are in the [v4 fee activation temp check](https://gov.uniswap.org/t/temp-check-activate-v4-protocol-fees/26162). v2 and v3 protocol fee levels are the same as on all other chains where fees are live, see breakdown [here](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/protocol-fee/concepts/fees#fee-split-table).

## Proposal Spec

If passed, the Robinhood Fee Activation proposal will execute two calls, each creating a retryable ticket in Robinhood Chain's Inbox on Ethereum.

`RH_INBOX.createRetryableTicket(...) x2`

One call will encode:

`V2_FACTORY.setFeeTo(TOKEN_JAR)`

The other will encode:

`V3_FACTORY.setOwner(V3_OPEN_FEE_ADAPTER)`

Once executed on Robinhood Chain, they set the fee collector of UniswapV2Factory to TokenJar and transfer ownership of UniswapV3Factory to V3OpenFeeAdapter.

Robinhood's v4 activation will be included in the V4 Fee Activation (Part 1) proposal described below. Matching the spec of the [v4 fee activation temp check](https://gov.uniswap.org/t/temp-check-activate-v4-protocol-fees/26162), and delivered through the same retryable ticket path, it will encode:

`V4_POOL_MANAGER.setProtocolFeeController(V4_FEE_ADAPTER)`

**RELEVANT ADDRESSES:**

| Name | Network | Address | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| V3_FACTORY | Robinhood Chain | [0x1f7d7550B1b028f7571E69A784071F0205FD2EfA](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/address/0x1f7d7550B1b028f7571E69A784071F0205FD2EfA) | Uniswap V3 Factory |

title: DIP: Fully Deprecate USDH Bridge and Return USDH to Owners
body:
# **DIP: Fully Deprecate USDH Bridge and Return USDH to Owners**

# **Simple Summary**

Fully deprecate the legacy USDH bridge at the request of the USDH/native team, disable further USDH bridge activity, and return all USDH held by the protocol directly to the relevant owners on HyperEVM.

# **Abstract**

This proposal authorises Derive Subsidiary (BVI) Ltd, and where required Derive Foundation and its affiliates, to take all steps necessary to fully deprecate USDH support through Derive’s legacy bridge infrastructure.

Following a request from the USDH/native team, this proposal authorises the full wind-down of USDH bridge support and the return of USDH directly to the wallets entitled to it.

# **Context and Objectives**

Following a request from the USDH/native team, Derive proposes to fully deprecate the USDH bridge and return the relevant USDH directly to owners on HyperEVM.

The objectives of this proposal are to:

* fully deprecate USDH bridge support;

* remove residual USDH from Derive protocol/bridge infrastructure;

* return USDH directly to the relevant owners on HyperEVM;

# **Specification**

The DAO resolves that Derive Subsidiary (BVI) Ltd, and where required Derive Foundation and its affiliates, shall take all actions necessary to implement the following changes, including any required board approvals and onchain or offchain actions.

## **1. USDH Bridge Deprecation**

The USDH bridge shall be fully deprecated, disabled, dissolved, or otherwise wound down.

No new USDH deposits, bridge transfers, or other protocol-supported USDH inflows shall be enabled through the existing bridge infrastructure after implementation of this proposal.

## **2. Return of USDH to Owners**

All USDH currently held in Derive protocol contracts, bridge contracts, or related protocol-controlled infrastructure shall be returned directly to the wallets entitled to such USDH.

## **3. Residual or Unreturnable Amounts**

If any USDH cannot reasonably be returned directly due to dust amounts, invalid addresses, technical constraints, abandoned balances, or unresolved entitlement issues, Derive Subsidiary shall be authorised to implement a reasonable alternative process.

## **4. Implementation Authority**

Derive Subsidiary (BVI) Ltd shall be authorised to implement any parameter updates, contract administration actions, treasury actions, frontend updates, bridge actions, user communications, and ancillary operational changes required to give effect to this proposal.

The changes shall take effect upon execution of the relevant onchain and offchain actions.

## **5. Superseding Effect**

This proposal supersedes any prior DAO approval, protocol setting, bridge configuration, or operational process relating to USDH to the extent inconsistent with the changes set out above.

title: Melee 2 Slate Selection
body:
## Introduction
 
Voting for [Shutter Champions: Melee 2](https://blog.shutter.network/shutter-champions-melee-2/) begins Tuesday, July 14 at 9:00 UTC!
 
Melee 2 asks one question: **What is the best way to advance Shutter with $10,000?**
 
Five slates have been selected for the vote:

- Kickstart Shutter PEN 
- Delegate Impact + AI Agents
- Shutter Governance Live Pilot
- Spreading Shutter's Voice
- None - Add Funds to Melee 3 

If you bought SHU between May 21 and June 10 and held it through July 10, you will receive Melee 2 voting power proportional to the amount of SHU you bought and held, and you can rank the slates on [Snapshot](https://snapshot.box/#/s:rmelee2.eth) from July 14 at 9:00 UTC to July 17 at 9:00 UTC.
 
Here is an outline of each slate, including a consolidated overview incorporating the questions and comments raised in each slate's forum discussion:
 
---
 
## Kickstart Shutter PEN
 
**Description:** Kickstart Shutter PEN (Perpetual Endowment Network) with deployment and frontend bounties plus seed funding for its first three funding rounds.
 
**Forum discussion:** [Melee 2 Slate - Kickstart Shutter PEN](https://shutternetwork.discourse.group/t/melee-2-slate-kickstart-shutter-pen/892)
 
**Recipients & Amounts:**
 
| Recipient | $ Amount | Paid in | Milestone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Deployment Bounty Recipient | $250 | SHU | Verification of deployment |
| Frontend | $750 | SHU | Hosting or IPFS pin for 12 months |
| Selected by Shutter PEN in Funding Round 1 | $3,000 | SHU | NA |
| Selected by Shutter PEN in Funding Round 2 | $3,000 | SHU | NA |
| Selected by Shutter PEN in Funding Round 3 | $3,000 | SHU | NA |
 
**Overview:**
 
This slate kickstarts [Shutter PEN](https://blog.shutter.network/a-proposed-blueprint-for-launching-a-shutter-pen/) - a perpetual endowment network with the mission to fund projects aligned with The Ethereum Cypherpunk Manifesto - in two ways. First, bounties incentivize the deployment of a Shutter PEN and the creation of a frontend. Second, $9,000 of seed funding addresses the "cold start" problem: without donations or assets earning interest there are no funds to distribute, so seeding the initial three quarterly funding rounds ensures early SEAT holders have meaningful funds to allocate, which in turn kickstarts SEAT purchases.
 
---
 
## Delegate Impact + AI Agents
 
**Description:** 1) a 12 week pilot to reward delegates for measurable ecosystem impact, and 2) POIDH bounties for AI agents that help delegates create that impact.
 
**Forum discussion:** [Shutter Delegate Impact Pilot + AI Agent Bounty](https://shutternetwork.discourse.group/t/shutter-delegate-impact-pilot-ai-agent-bounty/889)
 
**Recipients & Amounts:**
 
| Recipient | $ Amount | Paid in | Milestone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Delegate Impact Pilot | $5,000 | SHU | Rewards for eligible delegate impact |
| POIDH AI Agent Bounties | $5,000 | SHU | Working open-source agent prototypes submitted through POIDH |
 
**Overview:**
 
This funds 2 projects: 1) Half the funds reward delegate impact across three pillars: governance participation (voting and posting rationale), idea origination (new proposals and ideas on the forum), and business development / integrations (ecosystem introductions and adoption pathways). 2) The other half funds POIDH bounties for open-source AI agents that help delegates create impact, with proposed themes including a LUCID Monitor Agent, a Public Goods Narrative Agent, and a Scout Agent.  

---

## Shutter Governance Live Pilot
 
**Description:** Fund up to a $10,000 grant for an approved organization to use Shutter Governance in a live voting pilot.
 
**Forum discussion:** [Melee 2 Slate - Shutter Governance Live Pilot](https://shutternetwork.discourse.group/t/melee-2-slate-shutter-governance-live-pilot/890)
 
**Recipients & Amounts:**
 
| Recipient | $ Amount | Paid in | Milestone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Selected by brainbot gmbh | Up to $10,000 | SHU, if possible (USDC, if needed) | Upon completion of the pilot |
 
**Overview:**
 
This slate funds a grant of up to $10,000 for one approved organization to use Shutter Governance in a live voting pilot. Shutter Governance is a new digital voting system for municipalities, universities, unions, cooperatives, political parties, NGOs, and other organizations, where votes stay hidden from everyone while the results remain publicly verifiable. The funding would help cover the integration and delivery work needed to run the pilot. 
 
---
 
## Spreading Shutter's Voice 
 
**Description:** 1) Fund ETH Daily, Book of Ethereum, and Web3Privacy Now to push Shutter into the wider Ethereum conversation through editorial coverage, cultural translation, and 2) Create bounties to deploy Shutter PEN and create a frontend.
 
**Forum discussion:** [Mele 2 Slate - Spreading Shutter's voice through content and education](https://shutternetwork.discourse.group/t/mele-2-slate-spreading-shutters-voice-through-content-and-education/881)

| The Book of Ethereum (foundation.booe.eth) | $2,000 | SHU | Half upfront; second half on October 17th upon delivery of a recap of Shutter content (X posts, Telegram/Spaces discussions, onboarding pieces) |

**Overview:**
 
This slate funds 2 projects: 1) 90% of funds go to ETH Daily, Book of Ethereum, and Web3Privacy Now for daily editorial coverage of Shutter milestones, educational content that translates the tech for everyday users, and embedding Shutter in the Ethereum Cypherpunk Congress in Mumbai 2026 (respectively). 2) 10% of funds go to bounties to deploy Shutter PEN and build and pin an IPFS frontend for 12 months.

title: MIP-021: A Rules-Based Buyback That Scales With Revenue
body:
Overview

Maple has continued to scale since the Syrup Strategic Fund (SSF) was activated under MIP-019 and extended under MIP-020. The SSF has three jobs: pursuing strategic opportunities, supporting token liquidity, and holding capital reserves and buybacks. Over that period, a portion of protocol revenue has been used to buy back SYRUP and build a durable DAO balance sheet.

Based on community feedback, MIP-021 replaces discretionary buyback allocation with a clear, rules-based model that scales the buyback directly with revenue.

MIP-021 proposes:

Buybacks set as a percentage of monthly revenue, increasing as revenue scales:

Monthly revenue under $1.5M = 10% to buybacks

Monthly revenue $1.5M–$2.0M = 20% to buybacks

Monthly revenue above $2.0M = 30% to buybacks

All SSF buybacks will be executed after each month-end by the 15th, once the revenue figure is finalised.

SYRUP purchased through these buybacks will live within the SSF.

Buyback details will be included in the Transparency page.

The framework applies for six months.

A Rules-Based Buyback

To make buybacks predictable and directly tied to Maple’s performance, MIP-021 introduces a tiered, revenue-based model. The buyback rate steps up as net revenue grows: 10%, 20%, then 30%, so the stronger Maple’s monthly revenue, the greater the share directed to buying back SYRUP. This replaces discretion with a clear, verifiable rule.

Transparency

Every SSF buyback will be executed after month-end once revenue is finalised, with the details reflected on the Transparency page, so the community can verify each month’s activity.

Implementation

Should MIP-021 pass, the following will be enacted:

Buyback Rate: set by the monthly revenue band. 10% under $1.5M, 20% from $1.5M – $2.0M, and 30% above $2.0M.

Execution: buybacks performed after each calendar month-end, once the revenue number is finalised.

Reporting: buyback details posted on X and added to the Transparency page.

Duration: the framework applies for six months.

Voting

MIP-021 can be voted on by all SYRUP holders, with the vote scheduled to go live on July 13, 2026 and remain open for 4 days until July 17, 2026.

title: AIP-010: Tokenomics V1
body:
## AIP-010 Summary
AIP-010 establishes Arrow's first unified tokenomics framework for the $ARROW token:

- Total supply is fixed at 100,000,000 $ARROW. No new tokens will be minted under this framework, and all deployment draws from the existing DAO treasury.
- $ARROW has three active utilities in 2026: governance voting, slashable manufacturing bonds ([AIP-009](https://github.com/Arrow-air/dao-aips/blob/main/AIPs/AIP-009.md)), and contributor compensation ([AIP-004](https://github.com/Arrow-air/dao-aips/blob/main/AIPs/AIP-004.md)).
- Treasury deployment is governed by an annual cap that the DAO must approve by governance vote each year. The Year 1 (2026) cap is 5,000,000 $ARROW: 1,500,000 for a contributor grants program, 500,000 for manufacturing rewards, and 3,000,000 for long term engineering project funding.
- Each conversion of treasury $ARROW to USDC requires its own governance vote covering amount, venue, counterparty, and pricing.
- Slashed manufacturer bonds compensate affected customers first, and any excess is burned. The DAO never retains slashed tokens as revenue.
- Creating a DAO owned liquidity pool is not authorized by this AIP and remains a separate future governance action following legal review.
- Phase 2 and 3 mechanics (operator staking, network usage rewards) are described as a roadmap only and are not binding.
- $ARROW does not entitle holders to profit or dividends.

You can read the full text for AIP-010 [here](https://github.com/Arrow-air/dao-aips/blob/main/AIPs/AIP-010.md)

## Motivation
Arrow has operated for over three years without a unified tokenomics framework while roughly 76.5M $ARROW (~76% of supply) sits in the DAO treasury with no formal plan. AIP-009 introduced the first protocol native token utility, the DAO funds multi year engineering projects from a treasury that is mostly $ARROW, and bounty first compensation under AIP-004 only motivates contributors if there is a credible path to liquidity and utility. AIP-010 connects these pieces into one framework and gives the DAO a governance controlled way to deploy treasury $ARROW toward real protocol actors: contributors completing work, manufacturers shipping products, and projects building aircraft.

## Outcome if vote passes
AIP-010 will have been ratified by the voting Arrow community. The features introduced in AIP-010 will become standard and must be adopted according to the specification. Passing this vote also authorizes the Year 1 (2026) treasury deployment cap of 5,000,000 $ARROW across the three buckets defined in the specification. Individual conversions of treasury $ARROW to USDC will each still require their own governance vote.

## Further Context
Full AIP: [AIP-010](https://github.com/Arrow-air/dao-aips/blob/main/AIPs/AIP-010.md)
[Forum Discussion](https://dao.arrowair.com/t/aip-010-discussion-tokenomics-v1/159)
