title: DIP080 - Proposal: Oracle Migration & Asset Parameter Adjustments on Conflux eSpace
body:
## Summary

This proposal includes:

1. **Oracle Migration** – Switch Unitus pricing from Pyth Oracle to the official Conflux Foundation price feed following the Pyth Core upgrade.
2. **Asset Parameter Updates** – Adjust selected asset caps to better align with current protocol usage and risk management.

---

## Background

Following the Pyth Core upgrade, Pyth price feeds will no longer be supported on Conflux eSpace by the end of **July 2026**.

To ensure continuous oracle availability, Unitus will migrate to the official Conflux Foundation price feed. Existing users do not need to take any action.

References:

- Pyth Core Upgrade: https://www.pyth.network/blog/the-pyth-core-upgrade
- Conflux Oracle Contracts: https://github.com/conflux-fans/oracle-contracts

---

## Benefits to the Community

- Ensures continuous and reliable oracle support.
- Improves protocol security with an officially maintained oracle.
- Optimizes risk parameters based on current market conditions.
- No impact or action required for existing users.

---

## Proposed Asset Parameter Adjustments

| Asset | LTV | LT | Reserve Ratio | Caps | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| USDT0 | 85% | 88% | 10% | 10m, 10m **⇒ 4m, 4m** |  |
| CFX | 70% | 80% | 15% | 15m, 15m **⇒ 3m, 3m** |  |
| USDC | 85% | 88% | 10% | 2m, 2m **⇒ 100k, 100k** |  |
| ETH | 85% | 88% | 15% | 500, 500 **⇒ 50, 50** |  |
| WBTC | 80% | 85% | 20% | 35, 35 **⇒ 5, 5** |  |
| USDT | 85% | 88% | 10% | 2m, 2m **⇒ 0, 0** | Paused already |
| AxCNH | 0% | 0% | 10% | 50m, 50m | no change |
| USX | 80% | 85% | 20% | 0, 0 | no change |

---

## Expected Impact

- Seamless oracle migration with no user action required.
- Improved protocol resilience and risk management on Conflux eSpace.

title: OCP-17: Deprecation of EDULand
body:
# Abstract

This proposal requests approval to retire the EDULand verifier node product and cancel the remaining undistributed earmark of $EDU from the 150,000,000 token node operator rewards allocation (OCP-8, amended by OCP-14). The unused portion was never disbursed and stays in the Open Campus Treasury.

EDULand was an early piece of EDU Chain's learn to earn program, letting the community earn $EDU by running nodes, and it served that purpose. As Open Campus turns toward its next chapter as a consumer, AI-native learning platform, it is bringing everything into one place so the project can focus on reaching learners at scale. Open Campus services and credential issuance continue to run intact. The Foundation will communicate separately on Yuzu and $EDU staking.

# Motivation

EDULand launched alongside the EDU Chain Principal Node program so the community could take part in the $EDU economy by operating verifier nodes. OCP-8 set 150,000,000 $EDU as rewards over three years; OCP-14 made the distribution non linear. EDULand did its job, helping bootstrap EDU Chain's early ecosystem. OCP-8 set a three year distribution period ending in 2027. This proposal ends the program ahead of that original term, in line with Open Campus's move to consolidate around one platform now rather than waiting for the full period to run out.

# Benefits

1.  One Open Campus platform for what is next.
    
2.  The unused $EDU earmark is cancelled rather than emitted for a product whose job is done, since it was never disbursed and never left the Treasury.
    
3.  Full focus on building for learners at scale, instead of maintaining a legacy product.
    
4.  A cleaner, forward-looking ecosystem as the ecosystem matures.
    

# Specification

**1. EDULand deprecation:** All EDULand node operations wind down. New rentals are paused now; existing rentals run to their natural expiry and are not extended. A transition window runs to end of July 2026, during which node renters can claim outstanding rewards or balances in a claim only state. After that, surfaces are disabled or archived, dependencies terminated, costs wound down.

**2. Amendment to OCP-8 and OCP-14:** Both are amended to cease all further $EDU node operator reward emissions immediately upon approval, ending the program roughly ten months ahead of the three year term set under OCP-8. This also formally supersedes the OCP-14 provision permitting undistributed EDU to be used for TVL, loan collateral, or dApp liquidity after the three year term. Of the 150,000,000 $EDU allocated, 11,897,280.27 has been distributed to date. The remaining 138,102,719.73 $EDU was never disbursed and never left the Treasury. This proposal cancels the earmark for that unused portion. No tokens move and no new circulating supply is created.

**3. User migration:** Active EDULand users will be kept informed throughout the transition via social media platforms.

# Budget

No new funding requested. The proposal produces cost savings from removing EDULand infrastructure, hosting, and operating expenses.

# Risks and drawbacks

1.  **Loss of EDULand:** The product is permanently retired. Current indicators suggest little strategic loss.
    
2.  **Community sentiment:** Ecosystem members who expected ongoing rewards may react negatively. Clear communication and a fair claim window mitigate this.
    
3.  **Token supply:** No tokens move as a result of this proposal. The unused earmark was never disbursed, so cancelling it does not change circulating supply or the Foundation's discretionary holdings.
    
4.  **Early termination:** This ends the program roughly ten months before the three year term set under OCP-8.
    

# Goals

1.  Authorise the deprecation of EDULand and the wind-down of node operations.
    
2.  Amend OCP-8 and OCP-14 to stop further $EDU node rewards and cancel the undistributed earmark, which was never disbursed and never left the Treasury.
    
3.  Formally supersede the OCP-14 provision allowing undistributed EDU to be used for TVL, collateral, or liquidity, replacing it with cancellation.
    
4.  Set a transition window with clear timelines for community, ending end of July 2026.
    

# Timeline

Following the DAO's approval of OCP-17, EDULand's node operations will begin winding down immediately, with the amendment to OCP-8 and OCP-14 taking effect upon approval. New rentals are already paused, and existing rentals will run to their natural expiry. A transition window remains open through end of July 2026, during which node operators can claim any outstanding rewards or balances. After that, EDULand surfaces will be disabled or archived and the program formally closed.

# Appendix

-   **OCP-8:** [Further $EDU Rewards Allocation to EDU Chain Principal Node Operators](https://dao.opencampus.xyz/t/ocp-8-further-edu-rewards-allocation-to-edu-chain-principal-node-operators/21)
    
-   **OCP-14:** [Amendment to OCP-8 Rewards Distribution](https://dao.opencampus.xyz/t/ocp-14-amendment-to-ocp-8-rewards-distribution/28)
    
-   **OCP-1:** [Proposing the DAO](https://dao.opencampus.xyz/t/ocp-1-proposing-the-dao/15)

title: PIP #27 - Discontinue Future PNP Emissions
body:
## Abstract

This proposal seeks to discontinue all future PNP emissions across the Penpie protocol, realign Penpie’s incentive structure, and support a more sustainable long-term token economy for PNP.

## Motivation

The current PNP emission model no longer fully aligns with Penpie’s long-term direction or the current needs of the ecosystem.

Discontinuing future PNP emissions would help reduce ongoing token dilution, realign incentives, and support a more sustainable token economy for PNP holders and the broader Penpie ecosystem.

For clarity, this proposal applies only to future, unaccrued PNP emissions. It does not affect any PNP rewards that have already accrued, vested, or become claimable before implementation.

## Specification

We ask vlPNP holders to vote on whether to approve the discontinuation of all future PNP emissions across the Penpie protocol.

If approved, future PNP emissions will be discontinued from the implementation date determined by the Penpie team in accordance with the protocol’s technical requirements and governance process.

**Voting Options**

-   FOR - Approve the discontinuation of all future PNP emissions across the Penpie protocol.
    
-   AGAINST - Maintain the current PNP emission model.

title: MIP #98 - Determine Magpie’s Stance on Penpie’s PIP #27
body:
## Abstract

This proposal seeks to determine Magpie’s stance on Penpie’s PIP #27, which proposes discontinuing all future PNP emissions across the Penpie protocol, realigning Penpie’s incentive structure, and supporting a more sustainable long-term token economy for PNP.

For clarity, PIP #27 applies only to future, unaccrued PNP emissions. It does not affect any PNP rewards that have already accrued, vested, or become claimable before implementation.

## Motivation

According to PIP #27, the current PNP emission model no longer fully aligns with Penpie’s long-term direction or the current needs of the ecosystem.

Supporting PIP #27 would discontinue future PNP emissions from an implementation date determined by the Penpie team in accordance with the protocol’s technical requirements and governance process. This would help reduce ongoing token dilution, realign incentives, and support a more sustainable token economy for PNP holders and the broader Penpie ecosystem.

Voting against PIP #27 would maintain the current PNP emission model.

This proposal allows Magpie users to determine how Magpie should vote on Penpie’s PIP #27.

## Specification

Magpie will vote on Penpie’s PIP #27 according to the outcome of this proposal.

**Voting Options**

-   FOR - Direct Magpie to vote FOR Penpie’s PIP #27, approving the discontinuation of all future PNP emissions across the Penpie protocol.
    
-   AGAINST - Direct Magpie to vote AGAINST Penpie’s PIP #27, maintaining the current PNP emission model.

# **Summary**
This proposal seeks to onboard syrupUSDC — a USDC-based yield-bearing token issued by Maple Finance — as a collateral asset on Aave V3 Core Instance. syrupUSDC is built on top of Maple’s infrastructure and offers access to overcollateralized, fixed-rate institutional loans, providing high and consistent yields to DeFi users.

Maple, launched in 2021, is an on-chain Asset Manager with decades of traditional finance and crypto experience. 
# **Motivation**
Onboarding syrupUSDC to Aave V3 Core Instance provides:
New Token Type: A new collateral option backed by real yield from fixed-rate institutional lending strategies
AAVE TVL: Maple has a large network of institutional capital allocators, ready to allocate $500M+ USDC/USDT into syrupUSDC if it is available on Aave as collateral to loop it and get to their hurdle rates.
Higher Rates and Utilization: Increases USDC rates and utilization due to strong expected borrower demand.
Growth Incentives: Maple has $250k of incentives available to bootstrap the growth for Aave users.

The Aave and Maple partnership will enable:
New Yield Opportunities: Commercial alignment with Maple’s large institutional network, unlocking additional yield generation opportunities for Aave.
GHO Adoption: Maple can help with growing other strategic priorities for Aave, including GHO adoption. Eg GHO lending to institutions.
Future Collaboration: Future asset listings, including the Maple liquid yielding Bitcoin asset.

title: SAEP-17: Update Spark Savings Artifact Section
body:
# SAEP-17: Update Spark Savings Artifact Section - July 20, 2026

Spark's Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Phoenix Labs.

## Review

The Spark community can hereby express support or opposition to the following changes, as described by the author of the proposal:

> ### Summary
>
> This proposal is submitted by Phoenix Labs in its role as a nested contributor, as defined in section [A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1.1](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1.1) of the Spark Artifact. The proposal recommends that Spark governance update the Spark Savings section of the Spark Artifact to revise the Spark Savings USDT rewards rate framework and to add current configuration entries for recently launched Spark Savings vaults.
>
> ### Background
>
> Previously, Spark used the Aave Core USDT deposit rate as the benchmark rate for setting the Spark Savings USDT rewards rate. This was a suitable benchmark as Aave Core was broadly considered to be the dominant USDT yield venue in defi, and provided high liquidity which allowed the SLL to deposit excess USDT into this venue. Now that Aave's USDT market has declined in size and liquidity, and is no longer a part of the Spark Liquidity Layer allocation strategy, we submit that Spark governance should adjust the rewards rate framework for Spark Savings USDT to better reflect current market conditions and Spark's evolving liquidity objectives.
>
> Separately, Spark has recently launched several new Spark Savings vaults: Spark Savings PYUSD on Ethereum, Spark Savings USDG on Robinhood Chain, Spark Savings USDT on Arbitrum, and Spark Savings USDT on X Layer. The Spark Artifact's current configuration sections should be updated to record the onchain parameters and operational parameters of these vaults. In addition, several existing current configuration entries have become out of date relative to the onchain state of the vaults (updated Setter role addresses on all five existing vaults, and an increased supply cap for Spark Savings USDC on Avalanche), and one entry contains a typographical error; these should be corrected so the Spark Artifact remains an accurate record.
>
> ### Proposal Details
>
> We propose that Spark governance approve the following changes to the Spark Savings section of the Spark Artifact:
>
> - Replace the existing benchmark-based rewards rate framework for Spark Savings USDT on Ethereum with a governance-bounded operational rate-setting framework.
> - Update the existing Onchain Parameters Current Configuration entries to reflect the current onchain configuration of each vault (updated Setter role addresses on all five existing vaults, and an increased supply cap for Spark Savings USDC on Avalanche).
> - Add Onchain Parameters Current Configuration entries for Spark Savings PYUSD on Ethereum, Spark Savings USDG on Robinhood Chain, and Spark Savings USDT on X Layer.
> - Correct a typographical error in the Target Liquidity Current Configuration entry for Spark Savings USDT on Ethereum.
> - Add Target Liquidity and Rewards Rate Current Configuration entries for Spark Savings USDG on Robinhood Chain, Spark Savings USDT on Arbitrum, and Spark Savings USDT on X Layer.
>
> ### Justification
>
> The proposed update is intended to ensure that the Spark Savings USDT rewards rate framework remains aligned with current market conditions and Spark's broader liquidity strategy.
>
> The prior framework referenced the Aave Core USDT deposit rate because Aave Core was, at the time, a highly relevant benchmark for USDT yield in DeFi. It represented a large, liquid, and broadly utilized venue where excess USDT liquidity could be deployed by the Spark Liquidity Layer. As a result, referencing the Aave Core USDT deposit rate provided a practical basis for setting a competitive Spark Savings USDT rewards rate.
>
> Market conditions have since changed. The Aave Core USDT market has declined in size and liquidity, and it is no longer part of the Spark Liquidity Layer allocation strategy. As a result, continuing to reference the Aave Core USDT deposit rate may cause the Spark Savings USDT rewards framework to rely on a benchmark that is no longer representative of Spark's actual liquidity deployment opportunities or strategic objectives.
>
> The proposed framework replaces a fixed external benchmark with a governance-bounded operational rate-setting framework. Rather than relying on a single third-party reference rate, the Rewards Rate may be determined pursuant to the governance-bounded operational rate-setting framework established for the applicable Spark Savings vault, subject to the applicable Onchain Parameters. This allows the framework to respond to evolving market conditions while preserving governance oversight.
>
> The rewards rate should support Spark's liquidity objectives, rather than mechanically referencing a venue that may no longer be relevant to Spark's allocation strategy. By moving to a more flexible framework bounded by governance-approved onchain parameters, Spark can maintain competitiveness while preserving appropriate controls over rate-setting authority.
>
> In addition, this proposal performs routine maintenance of the Spark Artifact's current configuration sections. Spark has recently launched Spark Savings PYUSD on Ethereum, Spark Savings USDG on Robinhood Chain, Spark Savings USDT on Arbitrum, and Spark Savings USDT on X Layer. Adding these vaults to the Onchain Parameters, Target Liquidity, and Rewards Rate current configuration sections keeps the Spark Artifact an accurate record of the current state of Spark Savings. Because Spark Savings USDG on Robinhood Chain, Spark Savings USDT on Arbitrum, and Spark Savings USDT on X Layer use the flexible rewards rate strategy, their Rewards Rate entries follow the same governance-bounded operational rate-setting framework proposed for Spark Savings USDT on Ethereum in Change 1.
>
> The proposal also corrects existing current configuration entries that have drifted from the onchain state of the vaults. The Setter role on all four existing Spark Savings vaults has been migrated to the freezable ALM proxy on the respective chain ([0xe5c6318456a7Cb6f74f93B4eee4616dB5fcef699](https://etherscan.io/address/0xe5c6318456a7cb6f74f93b4eee4616db5fcef699) on Ethereum, [0x93c81ADc7F98FdBC8C7a15eCBeD312c8F6adbcB3](https://snowtrace.io/address/0x93c81ADc7F98FdBC8C7a15eCBeD312c8F6adbcB3) on Avalanche), and the supply cap for Spark Savings USDC on Avalanche has been increased from 150 million to 500 million. Finally, the proposal corrects a typographical error in the Target Liquidity entry for Spark Savings USDT on Ethereum, which referenced "1 million USDC" rather than "1 million USDT". These corrections ensure the Spark Artifact accurately reflects the live configuration of Spark Savings.
>
> Overall, this proposal updates the Spark Artifact to reflect the current state of the USDT yield market, the Spark Liquidity Layer's allocation strategy, and the current set of live Spark Savings vaults. It removes reliance on an outdated benchmark and replaces it with a framework that better balances operational flexibility, market responsiveness, and governance oversight.

The proposed Spark Artifact changes can be found in the following pull request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/281

## Outcomes

- If "For" receives the most votes, the proposal will be approved. The associated pull request will be merged into Spark's artifact. When required, the listed changes will proceed to implementation by the relevant actors.
- If "Against" receives the most votes, the proposal will be rejected. No changes will be implemented.

title: SAEP-18: Update Spark Liquidity Layer Freezer Multisig
body:
# SAEP-18: Update Spark Liquidity Layer Freezer Multisig - July 20, 2026

Spark's Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Phoenix Labs.

## Review

The Spark community can hereby express support or opposition to the following changes, as described by the author of the proposal:

> ## Summary
>
> This proposal is submitted by Phoenix Labs in its role as a nested contributor, as defined in section [A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1.1](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1.1) of the Spark Artifact. The proposal recommends that Spark governance update the Spark Artifact section documenting the Spark Liquidity Layer Freezer Multisig.
>
> ## Background
>
> The Spark Liquidity Layer Freezer Multisig has the ability to deauthorize ("freeze") an address with the `Relayer Role`, which improves the safety of the Spark Liquidity Layer by allowing a compromised or faulty relayer to be rapidly removed without needing to wait for a Sky spell to be executed. Previously, the Spark Liquidity Layer Freezer Multisig was composed of 1 signer from Spark Assets Foundation (SAF), 2 signers from Phoenix Labs (PL), and VoteWizard, with a 1-of-4 signing requirement.
>
> While low signer thresholds allows for rapid action in response to emergencies, it also created increased operational risk of the Freezer Multisig itself, as any single compromised signer could remove the other signers and deauthorize addresses with the `Relayer Role`, resulting in the Spark Liquidity Layer being unable to take action or reallocate funds until the situation was resolved with a Sky spell.
>
> ## Proposal Details
>
> We propose that Spark governance approve the following changes to the Spark Artifact:
>
> - Remove the SAF signer and replace it with an additional signer from PL
> - Increase the required number of signers from 1-to-4 to 2-to-4
>
> ### Justification
>
> This proposal improves the safety and operational resilience of the Spark Liquidity Layer by reducing the risk that the Freezer Multisig itself becomes a source of disruption.
>
> The Freezer Multisig serves an important emergency function within the Spark Liquidity Layer. Its ability to rapidly freeze an address with the Relayer Role allows Spark to respond quickly if a relayer is compromised, malfunctioning, or otherwise presents an operational risk. This capability reduces reliance on the slower Sky spell process for urgent defensive actions and helps protect funds allocated through the Spark Liquidity Layer.
>
> However, the previous 1-to-4 signing threshold also created a meaningful operational risk. Because any single signer could independently execute Freezer Multisig actions, the compromise or malfunction of a single signer could result in inappropriate changes to the relayer set, including the removal of other signers or the deauthorization of active relayers. In an adverse scenario, this could impair the Spark Liquidity Layer's ability to take action, reallocate funds, or maintain normal operations until governance intervened through a Sky spell.
>
> Increasing the signing requirement from 1-to-4 to 2-to-4 better balances emergency responsiveness with signer-level security. A 2-signature threshold preserves the ability for the Freezer Multisig to act quickly when needed, while materially reducing the likelihood that a single compromised signer or operational error can disrupt Spark Liquidity Layer operations. This provides a stronger control environment for a role that is intentionally designed to have rapid-response authority.
>
> Replacing the SAF signer with an additional Phoenix Labs signer is also consistent with the current operational structure of the Spark Liquidity Layer. Phoenix Labs is responsible for key operational and technical work supporting the Spark Liquidity Layer, and consolidating signer responsibility with PL and VoteWizard simplifies operational coordination while preserving redundancy across multiple signers. The updated signer composition maintains a 4-signer set, while the increased threshold ensures that no individual signer can unilaterally exercise the Freezer Multisig's authority or remove other signers.

The proposed Spark Artifact changes can be found in the following pull request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/282

## Outcomes

- If "For" receives the most votes, the proposal will be approved. The associated pull request will be merged into Spark's artifact. When required, the listed changes will proceed to implementation by the relevant actors.
- If "Against" receives the most votes, the proposal will be rejected. No changes will be implemented.

title: [ARFC] Aave App Launch
body:
### [ARFC] Aave App Launch

### Author: Aave Labs

### Date: 2026-07-21

***

# **1. Aave for Everyone**

Aave App is designed to meet the usability bar of leading fintech apps: the [Fintech Test](https://aave.com/blog/aave-app-reimagines-defi-experience). It gives anyone, anywhere, a self-custodial way to access Aave Protocol's lending infrastructure through an interface as simple as the apps they already use.

Aave App allows anyone with a smartphone to use Aave's institutional-grade lending infrastructure without setting up a digital asset wallet, managing gas, or understanding the complexities of DeFi. Users transfer fiat from their bank account via Aave Push's regulated fiat-conversion rails and earn yield generated by Aave Protocol's lending markets, with all net revenue directed to the DAO treasury. Aave Labs provides the user interface and the self-custodial infrastructure behind it, through Aave Accounts and ERC-6900 smart accounts.

At launch, the Aave App will introduce four new innovations (Stable Vaults, Balance Protection, Aave App Accounts and Aave Push), with more product additions arriving through 2026 to increase revenue, lower costs, and expand the App's user base.

This proposal asks the DAO to approve the following:

- The initial vault allocation configuration for the Aave App, as specified in Section 5
- The RPUR (Revenue Parameter Update Request) framework described in Section 7, under which the DAO may propose changes to Aave App's core revenue parameters
- A launch campaign for the Aave App, as detailed in Section 8
- The use of the entire Milestone 1 funding from the Aave Will Win proposal to fund the first-loss tranche of the Balance Protection captive structure
- The addition of Stable Vaults to the scope of the Aave App Stack bug bounty program, as described in the [Aave Protocol Bug Bounty Programs Restructure ARFC](https://governance.aave.com/t/arfc-aave-protocol-bug-bounty-programs-restructure/24816) and specified in Section 5

# **2. User & Balance Projections**

Aave App's iOS waitlist comprises approximately 50,000 registered users, each of whom completed a multi-step onboarding process: app download, account setup, and profile completion with a subset of users also completing applicable KYC screening (only available to US users while on the waitlist). This required multi-step process filters for higher intent users relative to those present in email-only waitlists. The Android version of the Aave App is expected to be released in Q3 2026, expanding the non-US user base.

By the end of the Aave App's first 12 months, we estimate three scenarios for combined iOS and Android success metrics by varying three assumptions together for each case: conversion rate from waitlist to funded user (a user who has made an initial deposit), average balance per funded user, and month over month user growth:

![Projections](https://europe1.discourse-cdn.com/flex013/uploads/aave/original/2X/7/7c324017baf9f58f0b6005c90781319ba94f4d1c.webp)

The above metrics are purely indicative, based on current waitlist numbers, assumed conversion rates, and projected month-over-month growth, and should not be taken as a guarantee of future performance.

# **3. Revenue Opportunities**

Aave App is projected to generate over $15M in annual revenue by the end of year two (indicative), across the four revenue streams outlined below, with additional streams under evaluation. Stream 1 (yield spread fees) and Stream 2 (reserve factor attribution) are expected to be active at launch. Streams 3 and 4 (card fees, swaps and FX), are expected to phase in throughout 2026, pending product availability and regulatory clearance. The $15M figure includes illustrative contributions from Streams 3 and 4; as these products have not yet been built or cleared for launch, their revenue contribution should not be treated as a projection the DAO is asked to rely on.

## **Yield Spread**

This fee is derived from the spread between the yield earned by the assets deployed in the vault and the yield payable to users.

![Yield Spread](https://europe1.discourse-cdn.com/flex013/uploads/aave/original/2X/a/a88ee50938ba8a8863b077118a043cc9a8283a63.jpeg)

For example, total user deposits of $1B with a 0.2% yield spread could result in $2M in annual revenue within 24 months.

## **Reserve Factor Attribution**

Because the Aave App uses Aave Protocol for earning on the vault's balances, an increase in deposits via the app results in an increase in deposits into the protocol markets. Assuming unchanged protocol utilization rates and reserve factor, an increase in user balances would increase the reserve factor revenue for the DAO.

![Reserve Factor Attribution](https://europe1.discourse-cdn.com/flex013/uploads/aave/original/2X/1/173f530d59cffc146254d07db86431338e672986.jpeg)

Within 24 months, deposits of $1B flowing into Aave Protocol via the Aave App could generate approximately **$4.5M in annual reserve factor revenue accruing to the DAO treasury at a 6% borrow rate**, calculated as:

- $1B × 75% utilization × 6% borrow rate × 10% reserve factor = $4.5M

The above calculation is a projection that assumes stable protocol utilization, borrow rates, and reserve factor allocation. The actual figure depends on protocol-wide activity, the stability of the above noted factors, and DAO governance.

## **Card Fees**

Card fees (including interchange, FX, network incentives, signing bonuses, etc) are expected to be a major revenue driver. The Aave App is expected to enable worldwide card issuance, letting users spend directly from their vault balances. This creates a high-margin, transaction-based revenue stream opportunity that can scale independently of yield or user balances.

The table below includes projections assuming a 1.0% blended card fee. Savings-first users tend to have higher card spend because their vault balance functions as a spending account, similar to debit card behavior at neobanks. Card adoption rates are benchmarked against major fintechs.

![Card Fees](https://europe1.discourse-cdn.com/flex013/uploads/aave/original/2X/e/ea917f6a78d16f974882ca14a24b4135f691a2e3.jpeg)

If Aave Cards launch, the calculation above illustrates how card revenue could scale with adoption; it is not a revenue target and is not part of what this proposal asks the DAO to approve.

## **Swap Fees**

Future additions to the Aave App could include volume-based fees on swaps between assets. Example use cases could include:

- Non-Stablecoin Deposits: Users that want to exit a crypto asset position and enter into stablecoins that pay a yield before they make their next move.
- Foreign Exchange Swaps: With the introduction of savings in additional fiat currencies as well as the ability to spend the Aave App balance internationally with the upcoming card, Aave App would be able to charge FX swap fees.

The chart below is illustrative only. Swap fees depend on both the FX swap capability and the card product described above, neither of which currently exists, and the figures shown should not be treated as a projection the DAO is asked to rely on:

![Swap Fees](https://europe1.discourse-cdn.com/flex013/uploads/aave/original/2X/8/8cf2602f0117d9be199f0bfa7fa64f6b97a6865f.webp)

# **4. The Four Aave App Innovations**

At launch, Aave App will introduce four breakthrough innovations, each one necessary to pass the Fintech Test.

## **Stable Vault**

Stable Vault is a vault tailor-made for retail consumer savings and provides a step-function improvement for stablecoin-powered savings applications. While being a DeFi innovation, it mirrors the user experience of traditional savings accounts while allowing for maximum cost and liquidity scalability. The core features that make this possible are:

- **Per-user stable rate:** Stable Vault depositors' assets are placed in a yield bucket (for example, earning 5%, with the rates being influenced by underlying variable DeFi markets) from the vault's allocation rather than guaranteed by any actor. This innovation allows for a smoother, more predictable yield experience. Certain users may be eligible to obtain yield boosts by completing in-app activities such as inviting friends or setting up automated deposits.
- **Multi-strategy connectivity:** Stable Vault is able to earn by supplying liquidity to protocols with any ERC-4626 compatible strategy, meaning Aave App can earn with Aave V3, V4 and sGHO.
- **Multi-chain earning:** Stable Vault is able to earn on any supported chain, enabling for the accounting (processing of deposits & withdrawals) to happen on a gas-efficient chain, while accessing the deepest pools of liquidity on Ethereum and capturing incentives on select other chains.
- **Multi-stablecoin deposits:** Stable Vault allows deposits & withdrawals in any number of whitelisted stablecoins, further allowing Aave App to abstract away individual stablecoin balances behind a reported dollar value. Stablecoins inside of the Stable Vault are rebalanced toward the target allocation automatically and uniformly across pooled balances, without discretionary per-user management.

Stable Vault's multi-chain IOU bridging functionality is guarded by an M-of-N bridge quorum. Rate limits are enforced on asset bridging globally and per lane (a route per asset, bridge provider and chain) to mitigate risk of bridge compromises or down time. Stable Vaults have been audited by Certora, Chain Security, Josselin, Stermi, and Recon. You can find the code and more information in the [Stable Vault GitHub repository](https://github.com/aave/stable-vault). Stable Vaults will be available to fintechs and partners as part of Aave Kit.

![Stable Vault](https://europe1.discourse-cdn.com/flex013/uploads/aave/original/2X/5/51400ef08767f4093de6227bcbc9068dc1f82a28.webp)

***


Due to the Snapshot character limit, the remainder of this proposal can be viewed on the Aave Governance forum.

title: ROBO Brand Direction — Phase 1 Temperature Check
body:
**Summary**
As ROBO Governance Phase 1 launches, we want to hear from token holders on the overall brand direction for ROBO. This is a non-binding temperature check — results will be reviewed by the Foundation Security Council and used to inform the Foundation's approach to brand development.

**Background**
ROBO is building toward a fully decentralised robotics economy. As the protocol grows, the brand will play a key role in how ROBO is perceived by the community, partners, and the broader market. Your signal here helps the Foundation understand what resonates most with token holders.

**Question**
What brand direction should ROBO pursue?

**Options**

A — Technical & Institutional: Clean, minimal, engineering-focused. Positions ROBO as a serious infrastructure protocol.
B — Bold & Community-First: Vibrant, expressive, community-driven. Positions ROBO as an accessible, energetic ecosystem.
C — No preference

**Important Notes**
This vote is non-binding. 
No action will be taken solely on the basis of this Snapshot vote.
Results will be reviewed by the Foundation Security Council before any decision is made.

*[Please NOTE: TWO clones for the DAO-Governance-SIGPROP for the three-tier Quorum Framework are issued simultaneously today. They are identical to the SIGPROP that failed to reach quorum last week. From each other they differ solely regarding their voting-duration: 
one is running for 25 days ("25-day-clone"), the other for 32 days ("32-day-clone")
This measure shall address the risk of quorum failure due to voter apathy. The two proposals will run concurrently. Once any clone reaches quorum and concludes, the remaining active clone will be removed to prevent duplication. This staggered-duration approach ensures that this Signal Proposal — a matter of material importance — has the maximum opportunity to achieve a decisive outcome without any additional delay.]*

Author: Nestor (5583)
Vote Duration: 25 days 
Quorum Requirement: 7.2M GHST (~25%)

**[SIGPROP] DAO Governance Evolution - Three-Tier Quorum Framework - [25-day-clone]**
(2nd attempt re-post)

Summary:
Replacing a single over-calibrated threshold with a stake-proportionate tier system, considering current organic quorum and including community input via three polls to decide key parameters.

The Impasse - One Threshold Fits None :
AavegotchiDAO currently applies a single quorum threshold of 7,200,000 VP to every proposal regardless of stakes, scope, or time-sensitivity. The data shows this is broken in both directions.
Recent evidence:
Important Treasury proposals which ran for a month failed. Despite representing the considered will of the active community the proposals closed below quorum with approximately two-thirds of necessary VP.
These proposals (among others) did not fail for lack of support. They failed because the quorum threshold is structurally misaligned with organic participation levels. The 7.2M bar requires roughly 27% of all eligible VP to participate: this is a figure the active community cannot sustain without exceptional effort on every single proposal.
The mandate of AGIP-145 is clear:
it established the 7.2M threshold particularly under the condition that the figure "will need to be monitored and could be adjusted via a new proposal, especially if it becomes inadequate after migration of most ecosystem assets and functions to Base network."
That migration is complete. The number is evidently inadequate. The revision is due.

Proposed solution - A Quorum Framework with three tiers:
Replace the single universal threshold with three tiers, each calibrated to the stakes of the proposal type. Thresholds follow a clean 2× progression: each tier is 50% of the tier above it. The issues listed in the overview below are examplary and not exhaustive.

**Galaxy Tier >>> 20 % ** Constitutional amendments, Director elections, Treasury allocations above the threshold defined in Poll B, governance framework changes.
**Medium Tier >>> 10% ** Protocol parameter changes, strategic partnerships, multi-month operational mandates (e.g. Officers), Significant grants (Poll B)
**Smol Tier >>> 5% ** Community events, minor parameter adjustments, short-term incentive programmes like Hackathons, Small grants (Poll B);
(Poll C gauges the intent to secure the tiers additionally by adjusting Vote Differentials)
Tier assignment: The proposal author self-classifies, using both the scope criteria above and the dollar-amount ranges decided in Poll B below. Where the tier is not clear from established criteria, the classification is discussed and confirmed during the Signal Proposal phase before the Core Proposal is posted.

Vote Differential for the Smol and Medium tiers is decided by the community in Poll C:
the Galaxy tier retains the existing COCOON baselines (10% / 15% / 20% by option count) which already provide strong abuse protection on their own.

Polls:
Launching with the Signal Proposal, running for 10 days and closing together, leaving one week of the SigProp window for additional polls, if the poll-results should require further calibration.
Please visit the seperate Snapshat-Polls for details, here the overview:

Poll A >> Quorum methodology:
fixed quorum or continuously calculated? (as it has been before AGIP-145)

Poll B >> Funding range per tier:
definition of the Medium tier's range fixes the Smol-tier ceiling, and the Galaxy-tier floor.

Poll C >> Vote Differential calibration for Medium and Smol tiers:
prevention of abuse through adjusting of Vote Differentials

*[Please NOTE: Polls (A to C) have concluded (no quorum mandate). Please find the results on the respective snapshot-poll-page:
A: https://snapshot.box/#/s:aavegotchi.eth/proposal/0x740178f597983ee522290095f947f6806e89c7923c2f3f48d22741d28e8c270f
B: https://snapshot.box/#/s:aavegotchi.eth/proposal/0xb7daa8100923890b6318a0fc122c9b2f1166f23ed2506a7929be5906eca8f837
C: https://snapshot.box/#/s:aavegotchi.eth/proposal/0x9ed40cabec658dbe0b9f22e753c77564f312a7536d47ffe75becf8c873ab9f89
The discussions about relevant details are thus extended until the finalization of the Sigprop.
Additional polls could be created, if deemed necessary to inform the final CoreProp about any further details.]*

Deferred to a future Phase 2 of Governance Evolution :

Trigger definition - when and how quorum thresholds are reviewed, if Poll A returns "Fixed."
Voting period durations per tier - to be determined after community reaction to the tier structure.
Wallet-count layer - a minimum-distinct-wallets requirement per tier, displayed alongside the VP-weighted result for transparency (collapsed bicameral design).
Vote:
Do you support replacing the current single-threshold quorum system with a three-tier quorum framework (Galaxy / Medium / Smol) for AavegotchiDAO governance, with implementation parameters to be finalised in AGIP-160 based on the results of the concurrent community polls?

✓ YES >>> I support tiered quorum governance
✗ NO >>> I prefer the current single-threshold system
○ ABSTAIN >>> I acknowledge the vote but take no position

Author: Nestor (5583)
Vote Duration: 25 days 
Quorum Requirement: 7.2M GHST (~25%)

**[SIGPROP] Transfer of Aavegotchi Intellectual Property to the AavegotchiDAO Foundation - [25-day-clone]**
(2nd attempt re-post)

Motivation:
The Aavegotchi brand is among the most distinctive identities in on-chain gaming. Currently the Aavegotchi identity is held by Pixelcraft Studios as corporate IP. Transferring that IP to the AavegotchiDAO Foundation aligns legal ownership with the envisioned economic and governance reality. The community has carried this brand. The GHST and asset holders govern this protocol. Accountable to on-chain governance via its Constitution, the Foundation is the appropriate custodian of the IP, serving as the DAO's off-chain legal agent, enabling the DAO to license, enforce and commercialise its own brand.

Summary:
This Signal Proposal asks the AavegotchiDAO community to express its support for the transfer of Pixelcraft Studios' Aavegotchi-related intellectual property to the AavegotchiDAO Foundation. This intellectual property includes core trademarks, brand assets, and related IP over which Pixelcraft holds transferable rights. An affirmative signal here authorises the Foundation to commence formal coordination with Pixelcraft Studios on the legal mechanics of transfer, contingent on the passage of the subsequent Core Proposal.
This proposal is scoped strictly to intellectual property. Operational stewardship during and after any transition is addressed in a separate, forthcoming Signal Proposal.
Any obligtions between the DAO and Pixelcraft, especially any previous revenue sharing agreements, like in AGIP133, remain entirely unaffected by this proposal and the outcomes thereof.
Final recipience of the IP and full completion of the transfer are contingent on the review of the transition documents by a counsellor familiar with legal matters regarding Intellectual Property.

Assets in Scope:
IP and Brand Assets
• Core Aavegotchi intellectual property, including the Aavegotchi name, visual identity, and associated lore assets (particularly: the two primary trademarks currently held by Pixelcraft: the original Aavegotchi word/logo mark and the original Aavegotchi pixel art character (“main Gotchi”);
• Principal Aavegotchi trademarks, in all jurisdictions where registrations are held or pending;
• Related brand assets — logos, character designs, iconography — over which Pixelcraft Studios holds transferable rights (including: "to assign to the Aavegotchi DAO Foundation any unregistered or common-law rights it holds in later stylized Aavegotchi wordmarks, game logos, icons, character designs, and other source-identifying brand assets, together with the associated goodwill arising from their use in commerce.").

DAO Signal - Outcomes:
If This Proposal Passes
A vote of Yes on this proposal communicates that the AavegotchiDAO community:
• Supports the transfer of core Aavegotchi IP and principal trademarks from Pixelcraft Studios to the AavegotchiDAO Foundation;
• Accepts that Pixelcraft Studios will cover the currently estimated legal and registrar costs of the trademark transfer (approximately USD 4,000) as a contribution to the transition;

title: Proposal: Transition Symmio from Staking Fee Distribution to Buyback & Burn
body:
Executive Summary
Currently Symmio allows staking to earn 100% of protocol settlement fees. This proposal shifts to using 100% of fees for automated $SYMM buybacks from open markets, followed by permanent burns. This creates deflationary pressure, reduces sell pressure from reward claims, and better aligns long-term value with protocol growth. SYMM Holders also now have the option to stake SYMM in Vibe (45-50% APR).


Current Model
Stakers receive proportional share of all settlement fees.
Proposed Model
Redirect 100% of fees to on-chain buyback contract → purchase $SYMM → burn to dead address.
Key Benefits
Deflationary supply — Reduces circulating tokens 
Lower sell pressure 
Better alignment for all parties (solvers, front ends, liquidity providers, holders)
Simpler & sustainable — Proven in projects like BNB/Hyperliquid.
Competitive positioning — Enhances $SYMM appeal in DeFi derivatives space.
Implementation Roadmap
Submit as Symmio Improvement Proposal (SIP) → community discussion 
Vote → deploy → monthly transparency reports (fees, buys, burns).

Conclusion
This shift moves Symmio toward sustainable, supply-driven value accrual as the protocol matures. It positions $SYMM for stronger deflationary dynamics amid expected growth in RFQ-based derivatives. Recommend governance vote to decide. Feedback welcome via official channels.


Note: Staking will remain for the distribution of early claim penalties and for ex-aero bribes. Only protocol settlement fees will be burned.

Please vote for your preferred outcome 

For : Symmio Platform fees will be used to buyback and burn Symm, Claiming and burning of all platform fees needs to be automated  before the end of 2026. A Dashboard showing total fees Used to buyback, total Symm burnt and bought along with any other useful information requested should be made when possible.

Against : Symmio will continue to buyback and distribute platform fees to stakers, Claiming and distribution of all platform fees needs to be automated before the end 2026. A Dashboard showing total fees Used to buyback, total symm bought and total fees distributed along with any other useful information requested should be made when possible.

title: Proposal: Buyback Strategy Using Symmio platform fees (~66K$ )
body:
Executive Summary
This proposal outlines how to deploy the approximately $66,000 in accumulated protocol revenue/reserve to initiate $SYMM buybacks. Three options are presented for community consideration:
Option 1: 1000$ daily
Option 2: Keep at current 350$ daily
Option 3: Dynamic buyback of 2× protocol revenue (matching model)
The community is invited to vote on their preferred option.

Background & Motivation
Symmio has accumulated roughly $66,000 in revenue.
Buybacks from the treasury reserve represent an additional powerful tool to create value for token holders.

Goal: Maximize the impact of the $66K reserve while ensuring the strategy remains sustainable and scalable as the protocol grows.

Proposed Options
Option 1: Fixed Buyback
Mechanism: Use the reserve to $1000 worth of $SYMM every day
Pros:.
SYMM holders get their owed revenue reliably and reasonably quickly.
Buyback and burn a lot at this current low price (if burn vote passes)
Meaningful impact relative to the current market cap (~$6M).
Cons:
Limited duration.
Some traders could extract value.

Option 2: keep the buybacks at the current daily of $350

Option 3: Dynamic Buyback at 2× Protocol Revenue 
Mechanism: For every $1 of revenue generated by the protocol, perform a total buyback of $2 worth of $SYMM:
$1 funded directly by protocol revenue.
$1 funded from the treasury reserve.
Examples:
If the protocol generates $200 in daily revenue → Total buyback of $400 ($200 from revenue + $200 from reserve).
If daily revenue reaches $1,000 → Total buyback of $2,000.
Pros:
Scalable: Impact automatically grows with protocol adoption and revenue.
More sustainable over the long term.
Better aligned with actual protocol growth.
Lower risk of prematurely exhausting the reserve.
Hard for traders to take advantage of it
Cons:
Less predictable in the short term (depends on actual revenue).
Slightly less aggressive signalling at the very beginning compared to a fixed amount.
With current revenue (around 10$ per day) the buyback will be low even with the boost.

Please vote for you preferred outcome

1000 daily : 1000 USDC daily will be used to buyback Symm form the open market using the 66k USDC mentioned in executive summary without fail until the funds run out. This is to start within 24h of the conclusion of the vote.

350 daily :  350 USDC daily will be used to buyback Symm form the open market daily using the 66k USDC mentioned in executive summary without fail until the funds run out. This is to start within 24h of the conclusion of the vote.

2x daily revenue : For every $1 of revenue generated by the protocol, perform a total buyback of $2 worth of $SYMM on the open market using the 66k USDC mentioned in executive summary without fail until funds run out. This is to start within 24h of the conclusion of the vote.

title: [Temp Check] - Four for V4
body:
## Summary

GFX Labs/Oku Trade proposes deploying Uniswap V4 on four EVM-compatible networks: **Sei, Etherlink, Pharos, and 0G**. These deployments expand V4's footprint, generate protocol fees across new chains, and give hook developers new environments to build on. With Morpho deployed on these networks, the addition of V4 provides a playground for unique financial applications to be developed. V3 is deployed on all chains and acts as the main liquidity hub for the networks.

No treasury spend is requested — GFX Labs covers all costs.

---

## Background

Since 2022, GFX Labs has deployed Uniswap V3 to 30+ EVM chains through Oku Trade, funding and executing the majority of deployments independently. With Oku's V4 interface complete, we are positioned to continue this expansion.

This proposal covers four chains where the community, liquidity environment, or emerging technical primitives create meaningful opportunities for the Uniswap DAO.

---

## Upside for the DAO

The four networks in this proposal collectively represent a meaningful and growing source of protocol fee revenue for the DAO. Sei recorded $1.5B in DEX volume in Q1 2026 with TVL holding steadily above $50M. With limited competition outside of Sei's native DEX Saphyre, V4 is well positioned to carve out meaningful market share. Pharos adds further upside — with mainnet recently live and over $100M committed to RWAs on the network, V4 has a clear opportunity to become the primary trading protocol on a chain purpose-built for institutional liquidity.

Applying a 5bps protocol fee across anticipated V4 pool activity at common 5bps and 30bps LP fee tiers, even conservative volume assumptions produce meaningful accrual. If V4 captures 15-20% of Sei's quarterly DEX volume, that represents roughly $300M flowing through V4 pools and an estimated $150,000 in quarterly protocol fees from a single chain at current activity levels. With Uniswap's fee switch now active following the UNIfication proposal, every incremental deployment directly contributes to protocol revenue, making low-cost (zero in this case), high-conviction expansions like this the most efficient path to growing the DAO's fee base.

![V4_draft_image|690x392](upload://9YsP4Pq9de7me21sXw9eTo8sZaQ.jpeg)

## Proposed Deployments

### Sei

Sei is a Layer-1 blockchain built specifically for trading and financial applications. With over $300M in minted stablecoins, predominantly through Ondo's multi-chain U.S. treasury product, Sei has established a strong and growing foothold in EVM DeFi. The network's ongoing full EVM migration plan aims to enhance network performance and further position itself as the backbone for institutional-grade onchain infrastructure.

### Etherlink (Tezos EVM)

Etherlink is the EVM-compatible Layer 2 of the Tezos ecosystem, backed by the Tezos Foundation, one of crypto's most established and consistently funded foundations since 2014. Etherlink has developed a notable presence in novel onchain RWA markets, specifically for metals, as exemplified by tokenized uranium (xU308), which can be leveraged as collateral for USDC-backed loans on Morpho. With a focus on bringing unique assets onchain, V4 adds another layer to Etherlink's growing suite of financial markets. Etherlink is currently undergoing a rebranding to TezosX - a consolidation effort to strengthen and reunify the Tezos brand and act as the primary EVM DeFi environment for the network.

### Pharos

Pharos is an EVM Layer 1 focused on RWA tokenization, high-throughput DeFi, and institutional-grade infrastructure. Built and incubated by Ant Group with over $50M in raised capital from investors including Sumitomo, Chainlink, and Flow Traders, Pharos heads into its 2026 mainnet after an exceptional testnet that processed 4.3B transactions across 200 million wallets, with its inaugural RWA vault reaching $50M capacity within days of opening. With Morpho live on the network, combining V4’s programmable liquidity layer gives Pharos the most capable DeFi stack available for institutions looking to move, lend, and trade tokenized assets in a compliant environment at scale.

### 0G

0G is a modular Layer 1 built for AI and autonomous applications, backed by $290M in funding, with mainnet launching in September 2025. It offers decentralized storage with 2 GB/s throughput and a data availability layer that is significantly faster and cheaper than Ethereum's. As AI agents and autonomous DeFi protocols grow in prevalence, they'll need reliable onchain liquidity infrastructure. V4's hooks to enable dynamic fees, TWAMM, and programmable pool behaviors are a strong fit for AI-driven strategies that require more nuanced market infrastructure than standard AMMs offer. Deploying V4 on 0G positions Uniswap as the default DEX for the emerging agentic economy. 0G is currently **incentivizing three V3** pools with $40,000 $0G distributed monthly.

---

### **Benefits to the DAO**

**More protocol fee revenue.** Four additional chains means four more sources of fees accruing to the DAO as V4 adoption grows.

**Expanded V4 footprint.** Each deployment grows the total addressable market for Uniswap — more users, more LPs, more developers interacting with V4 infrastructure.

**No cost.** GFX Labs handles all technical deployment, maintenance, and Oku interface support. No treasury expenditure, no token subsidies.

---

### **Requested Action**

GFX Labs requests that the Uniswap DAO:

* Grant GFX Labs a Uniswap V4 BSL

This proposal continues Oku's role as a reliable execution partner for the DAO — handling the operational lift of the V4 expansion so the DAO can capture the upside without the overhead. More chains, more hooks, more fee generation.

We welcome feedback on the networks, deployment process, or integration timelines.

— GFX Labs / Oku.Trade

title: SDGP-73: Activation of Revenue Sharing on OnlyBoost vaults, Inverse Finance as First Partner
body:
**Author:** Stake DAO Association  
**Category:** A — Stake DAO Governance Proposal (SDGP)

## **Summary**

As anticipated in the Stake DAO roadmap, this proposal activates the fee-sharing framework on Stake DAO's OnlyBoost vaults, carved exclusively out of the treasury portion of the performance fee. OnlyBoost vaults currently charge a total performance fee of **16.1%**, of which **5.5%** accrues to the Stake DAO treasury.

Under this framework, up to the full treasury share, 5.5 percentage points of the 16.1% performance fee, generated by TVL originated by an approved partner may be redirected to that partner's treasury. Fees accruing to sdTKN stakers and vlSDT holders are **not affected**. For clarity: no new fee is introduced. This proposal only re-routes part of an existing protocol fee via a governance-set parameter, and creates no entitlement, offer, or contractual obligation for any party (see the Legal Annex).

As the first application of this framework, the proposal approves a revenue share to **Inverse Finance** equal to the full treasury portion, 5.5 percentage points of the 16.1% performance fee (~34% of total performance fees collected), on TVL originated through FiRM markets using Stake DAO escrows (Stake DAO OnlyBoost vaults).

## **Motivation**

### **1. Redeploying part of the treasury fee to support protocol integrations**

OnlyBoost vaults performance fees are currently split as follows:

| Allocation | Share |
| --- | --- |
| Distributed to sdTKN stakers (e.g., sdCRV) | 5% |
| Distributed to vlSDT holders | 6% |
| Treasury | 5.5% |
| Harvester | 0.1% |
| **Total performance fee** | **16.1%** |

The treasury share is the only component the DAO can deploy strategically without diluting stakers or lockers. Redirecting part of it to integration partners allocates a portion of protocol-level fees to protocols that bring additional TVL to Stake DAO. The allocation is calculated solely from the performance fees that the partner-originated deposits themselves generate; it is a protocol fee parameter set by governance, not a promise of profit, yield, or return to any person.

### **2. Attracting new TVL and making Stake DAO the preferred yield source**

Protocols choosing a yield venue for their collateral, treasury, or LP strategies compare net yield, boost quality, and alignment. A revenue share tips this comparison in Stake DAO's favor: building on top of Stake DAO becomes a decision that also reflects the protocol-level fee allocation available to integrating partners. The framework is designed to incentivize protocols to integrate Stake DAO as their preferred yield source, and to make each new integration self-reinforcing: the more TVL a partner routes, the larger the fee allocation calculated from that partner's originated TVL.

This fee sharing aims to only incentivise liquidity that would otherwise not be deployed on Stake DAO, so that it doesn't ever destroy value for the DAO.

Because the share is carved solely out of the treasury portion, every dollar of partner-originated TVL remains strictly accretive to sdTKN stakers and vlSDT holders. Revenue the treasury "gives up" applies only to TVL that would otherwise be going to the competition.

### **3. Inverse Finance and FiRM**

[Inverse Finance](https://www.inverse.finance/) is the issuer of DOLA, a decentralized stablecoin, and the developer of **FiRM** (Fixed Rate Market), a fixed-rate lending protocol where borrowing costs are paid via DBR (DOLA Borrowing Rights) and each borrower's collateral is held in an isolated, per-user escrow contract. This escrow architecture is what makes FiRM uniquely compatible with Stake DAO: collateral can remain productive while securing a loan.

Inverse has already taken the first step. [Proposal #363](https://www.inverse.finance/governance/proposals/mills/363) re-onboards the sDOLA/scrvUSD Curve LP as FiRM collateral using **Stake DAO's OnlyBoost escrow**, the first FiRM market to do so. For depositors, this means optimized boost between Stake DAO and Convex, improved reward capture, instant reward crediting after harvest, and continued reward accrual while the LP is used as collateral. For Inverse, the revenue share approved in this proposal is the fee-share benefit referenced in that proposal.

What this partnership can bring to Stake DAO:

-   **Immediate TVL:** the sDOLA/scrvUSD market launches with a 5,000,000 DOLA supply ceiling, with looping demand expected given the LP's combined sDOLA, scrvUSD, and boosted CRV yields (a forward-looking expectation only, not a commitment or assurance — see the Forward-Looking Statements notice in the Legal Annex).
    
-   **Potential migration of all FiRM Curve LP markets to OnlyBoost:** if the first market performs as expected, Inverse may, at its sole discretion, route additional current or future Curve LP collateral markets through Stake DAO OnlyBoost escrows. This is a possibility only; neither Inverse nor Stake DAO commits to it.
    
-   **A public reference integration** demonstrating the "build on Stake DAO, share the revenue" model to other lending markets, stablecoin issuers, and yield aggregators.
    

## **Specification**

### **1. Activation of the revenue-sharing framework**

Revenue sharing is hereby enabled on Stake DAO OnlyBoost vaults, subject to the following constraints:

-   The revenue share is carved **exclusively out of the 5.5% treasury portion** of the performance fee. The allocations to sdTKN stakers (5%), vlSDT holders (6%), and the harvester (0.1%) are unchanged.
    
-   The revenue share applies **only to performance fees generated by TVL originated by the partner** (deposits routed through the partner's contracts, escrows, or integrations), not to the vaults' total TVL.
    
-   Each partner allocation (partner, rate, scope) must be approved by Stake DAO governance, either through this proposal or a subsequent SDGP.
    
-   Partner terms are recorded on-chain in the **PartnerRegistry** contract, owned by Stake DAO governance. The registry stores each partnership's parameters (fee share in bps, payout recipient, active status), either per vault or per integrator/referrer, and holds no funds. Terms can only be set, updated, or paused by governance.
    
-   **Compliance condition.** Activation of, and each distribution under, any partner allocation is conditional on the payout recipient not being a Restricted Person (as defined in the Legal Annex) and on the distribution being lawful. Stake DAO governance may pause or revoke any allocation, and its PartnerRegistry entry, if the recipient becomes subject to sanctions or if distribution would otherwise be unlawful.
    

### **2. Inverse Finance revenue share**

-   **Partner:** Inverse Finance
    
-   **Rate:** **5.5 percentage points of the 16.1% performance fee** (i.e., 100% of the 5.5% treasury share, or ~34% of total performance fees collected) generated by TVL originated through FiRM markets using Stake DAO escrows
    
-   **Scope:** the sDOLA/scrvUSD FiRM market ([0xC45E9c231ab5D9Bd3F1131E7901B100D8D236C4d](https://etherscan.io/address/0xC45E9c231ab5D9Bd3F1131E7901B100D8D236C4d)) and any future FiRM market using a Stake DAO OnlyBoost escrow
    
-   **Recipient:** Inverse Finance Treasury (0x9D5Df30F475CEA915b1ed4C0CCa59255C897b61B), such address to be verified and recorded in the PartnerRegistry by Stake DAO governance before any amounts accrue or are made claimable. No amounts will be made claimable to any address not so recorded, and no Released Party (as defined in the Legal Annex) shall be liable for amounts directed to an address confirmed through that process.
    

### **3. Payment mechanics**

Revenue-share amounts are computed autonomously by Stake DAO's keeper infrastructure from on-chain harvest data attributable to partner-originated TVL, based on the terms recorded in the PartnerRegistry. Accrued amounts are made claimable through a **Merkle-claim contract (Universal Rewards Distributor)**, updated **monthly**, in the reward tokens collected (e.g., CRV). Inverse Finance will be able to claim its accrued share each month to its treasury. Stake DAO will publish the methodology for transparency.

The StakeDAO Association does not custody or take title to these tokens at any time; amounts are made available for the partner to claim on a pull basis directly from the smart contract. All amounts are gross: the partner is solely responsible for any taxes arising on amounts it claims, no amount will be grossed up, and Stake DAO neither withholds nor accounts for any tax.

### **4. Duration and termination**

The revenue share remains in force as long as the corresponding partner integration is live. The revenue-share allocation is an on-chain governance parameter, not a contract: it confers no vested or contractual right on any partner, and Stake DAO governance may amend, pause, or revoke it at any time by SDGP or other authorized governance action. It may also cease automatically if the underlying integration is discontinued. As an operational courtesy only, and not as a binding obligation, Stake DAO will endeavour to give 30 days' notice before any discretionary discontinuation where practicable. Rates may be revised by a subsequent SDGP.

## **Fee structure after this proposal (partner-originated TVL)**

| Allocation | Share |
| --- | --- |
| Distributed to sdTKN stakers | 5% |
| Distributed to vlSDT holders | 6% |
| Partner (Inverse Finance) | 5.5% |
| Treasury | 0% |
| Harvester | 0.1% |
| **Total performance fee** | **16.1%** |

Non-partner TVL keeps the current split (5% / 6% / 5.5% / 0.1%).

## **Vote**

-   **For (Yes):** Activate the OnlyBoost vaults revenue-sharing framework on the treasury fee portion, and approve a revenue share to Inverse Finance equal to the full 5.5% treasury share (5.5 percentage points of the 16.1% performance fee) as described.
    
-   **Against (No):** Reject the proposal.
    
-   **Abstain:** Take no position.
    

| **Parameter** | **Value** |
| --- | --- |
| Forum debate period | 3 days minimum |
| Voting period | 7 days |
| Debate and vote | Sequential (debate first, then vote) |
| Quorum | 15% of total vlSDT supply |
| Approval threshold | Simple majority (>50% of votes cast, excl. abstentions) |
| Anticipated execution | If the quorum and approval threshold set out above are met |

## **References**

-   Inverse Finance Proposal #363 — Re-Onboard sDOLA/scrvUSD LP as Collateral [[Inverse Governance](https://www.inverse.finance/governance/proposals/mills/363)]

-   FiRM documentation [[docs.inverse.finance](https://docs.inverse.finance/)]
