title: SDGP-74: StakeDAO Association Grant Request H2-2026
body:
**Quorum:** 6,018,000 vlSDT  
**Author:** StakeDAO Association

## Preamble

This proposal serves as a formal request for a half-yearly grant ("Grant Proposal") from Stake DAO for the period of H2-2026 (July 1st to December 31st, 2026) in continuation and recognition of the governance proposal (SDGP-32) and the previous Grant proposals (SDGP-62, SDGP-56, SDGP-48 and SDGP-39) previously adopted by Stake DAO.

The StakeDAO Association ("Association"), established as a pivotal entity within the Stake DAO ecosystem and based in Zug, Switzerland, aims to further support the development and growth of Stake DAO through specified services aligned with Stake DAO's strategic objectives.

## Review of the previous grant (H1-2026)

For H1-26, StakeDAO Association was awarded a USDC 962,000 grant for the purpose of achieving certain milestones. Here is a recap of the outcome for those milestones:

| Milestone | Budget ($) | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New Tokenomics Rollout (M1) | 125,000 | Successful |
| Lending Product Rollout (M2) | 100,000 | Successful |
| Identifying New Growth Opportunities (M3) | 50,000 | Successful |
| 5-Year Anniversary Celebration (M4) | 45,000 | Cancelled |
| Product Uptime & Maintenance (M5) | 250,000 | Successful |
| Votemarket Incentive Flows & Balancer Leadership (M6) | 65,000 | Partially successful |
| Business Development & TVL Growth targets (M7) | 150,000 | Unsuccessful |

The new SDT tokenomics were successfully deployed in April 2026, with the launch of vlSDT and a smooth migration from veSDT (more than 80% migrated within weeks), the adaptation of Stake DAO's governance framework (SDGP-66), and the launch of the vlSDT boost marketplace, shipped in June. The lending vertical was rolled out with a full user interface, a monitoring dashboard with automated alerts, and dedicated liquidation bots. New growth opportunities were identified and consolidated into a mid and long-term development strategy, which shapes the milestones proposed below. Finally, the 5-year anniversary celebration of Stake DAO was cancelled following the downturn in the market and the need to be cautious with spending, heading into a bear market.

H1-2026 was nevertheless marked by two security incidents. In March, a peripheral proof bridging mechanism on Votemarket was abused on Arbitrum and Base, leading to approximately $176k of user rewards lost, of which 80% were recovered through a white-hat agreement with the identified attacker; affected users were made whole within 24 hours through an ex gratia distribution approved by governance (SDGP-65), made on a voluntary basis and without any admission of liability. In May, a compromised deployer key which had retained legacy owner rights on the vsdCRV cross-chain contract was used to forge an unbacked mint; the backing was secured quickly, limiting the loss to the liquid vsdCRV supply on Arbitrum, approximately $88k, and an ex gratia compensation plan was approved by governance (SDGP-70) and executed, in each case without any admission of liability on the part of the Association. Those incidents triggered a deep overhaul of the Association's security posture: review and transfer of all privileged accesses across the whole contract stack, rotation of all signer keys, continuous ownership and invariant monitoring by automated agents with automated pause and per-vault solvency triggers, extended monitoring coverage to key integrations, upgraded on-call response, per-function Timelock delays, and pre-audit automation on the development process. Aside from these incidents, product uptime remained above the 95% target throughout the period.

On the Votemarket side, incentive flows remained steady and Votemarket continued to outperform competing platforms, but the objective of becoming the leader of the Balancer vote incentive market, although achieved, was voided by Balancer's decision to sunset veBAL. This milestone is therefore considered only partially successful.

In terms of business development, TVL in Stake DAO strategies grew to approximately $141m by the end of Q1. However, the May incident, combined with a broad market downturn, led to a sharp drop in TVL, which ended the half-year at approximately $70m. The $200m target was therefore not reached. Encouragingly, the situation stabilised in June (-9% MoM after -45% in May) while Stake DAO's share of CRV inflation and OnlyBoost BD penetration (76.5%) recovered markedly, but rebuilding trust and TVL remains a central objective of the H2-2026 period.

Financially, the DAO remained profitable over the period despite the exceptional losses linked to the incidents, with a positive comprehensive result (treasury, SDT holder distributions and Association combined) of approximately +$282k for H1-2026. Approximately $358k was returned to SDT holders over the period through veSDT/vlSDT distributions and buybacks. Costs remained under control, with a normalised monthly cost base of approximately $105k at the end of the period, excluding the payment of the 2025 incentive program.

## H2-26 Grant request

For H2-26, the proposed focus will be on rebuilding trust and TVL after the May incident, developing Votemarket v3 as a decentralised incentive-distribution platform, growing the curation vertical, further hardening security, and increasing the automation and decentralisation of the protocol.

**Amount Granted:** The Association hereby requests a grant amount of USDC 672,000 ("Grant Amount") designated for the execution of the milestones further described below ("Grant Purpose").

## Milestones

The Grant Amount shall be paid to the Association in six (6) instalments to perform the following milestones ("Milestones"):

| Milestone | Budget ($) | Target date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Votemarket v3 development (M1): a new iteration for Votemarket which will not use cross-chain interactions and be able to expand beyond vote incentives, leveraging zero-knowledge technology to provide a trustless, decentralised, modular incentive infrastructure. | 120,000 | Dec-26 |
| Growing the curation vertical (M2): new partnerships with DeFi projects and integrations with institution-facing players, targeting $50m of curated assets under management | 160,000 | Dec-26 |
| Security hardening (M3): launch of a public bug bounty program, hardening of automation and key-management processes, reduction of the protocol's attack surface through targeted product sunsets, and extension of monitoring coverage | 30,000 | Oct-26 |
| Automation and decentralisation of the protocol (M4): moving governance further on-chain and exploring keeper solutions to reduce in-house automation needs | 60,000 | Dec-26 |
| Developing growth venues for Stake DAO, including the expansion of the curation vertical, and exploring new product ideas. (M5) | 34,000 | Nov-26 |
| Maintain a high level of uptime of Stake DAO's product and user interface (>95%), including community management and legal watch (M6) | 250,000 | Dec-26 |
| Ensure steady business development efforts focused on rebuilding trust, with an objective of $100m TVL in Stake DAO strategies (M7) | 150,000 | Dec-26 |

The Milestones are funded by the Grant Amount together with the Association's existing balance, as detailed under "Use of funds" below.

## Payment schedule

The Grant Amount shall be distributed in six (6) monthly payments to the Association per mutually agreeable arrangements. The payment schedule is shaped to not request unnecessary funds from the DAO, with the Association maintaining only a minimal cash buffer throughout the period. Below is the initial version of the payment schedule:

| Date | Payment (USDC) |
| --- | --- |
| July 2026 | 42,000 |
| August 2026 | 129,000 |
| September 2026 | 159,000 |
| October 2026 | 134,000 |
| November 2026 | 134,000 |
| December 2026 | 74,000 |

## Use of funds

This grant is significantly lower than the previous one, for two main reasons. First, the H1-26 grant included a $307,000 incentive program rewarding the 2025 performance; for 2026, the team incentivisation (if any) will be distributed in January 2027, and therefore will be part of the H1-2027 grant request. Second, limited exceptional costs are expected for the period. The implied monthly spend (~$134k) exceeds the normalised $105k cost base mainly due to audit and one-off legal costs concentrated in the period.

Below is a detailed breakdown of the expected use of funds.

| H2-26 budget | USD |
| --- | --- |
| R&D | 575,000 |
| Association staff | 28,000 |
| Tooling | 20,000 |
| Legal & Accounting | 86,000 |
| Audits | 75,000 |
| Taxes | 10,000 |
| Others (events, etc.) | 10,000 |
| **Total** | **804,000** |
| Current association balance | (132,000) |
| **Total requested grant** | **672,000** |

## Association Autonomy

The Grant Proposal does not create a principal or agent, employer or employee partnership, or joint venture between the Association and Stake DAO.

The Association is free to decide upon the way to carry out the execution or fulfillment of the Milestones set forth above. The Association retains its independence in achieving these Milestones, leveraging either internal capabilities and resources or engaging suitable third parties as auxiliary persons.

No regulated services; no fiduciary role. Nothing in this Grant Proposal, nor any activity performed by the Association in connection with the Milestones, shall be construed as (i) the provision of regulated financial services, investment services, asset management, portfolio management, custody, brokerage, placement, underwriting, investment advice, or financial intermediation, in Switzerland, the European Union, or any other jurisdiction, or (ii) the creation of any fiduciary, trustee, agency, or similar relationship vis-à-vis any user, token holder, or third party. The Grant Amount constitutes non-reciprocal funding for the development of the Stake DAO ecosystem and does not constitute consideration for, or an inducement to acquire, any token, security, or other financial instrument.

The Association acts solely as a service provider supporting the Stake DAO ecosystem and does not take possession of, control, or discretionary authority over users' assets.

## Purpose and Limitation of Use

As described in the Milestones, the Grant Amount shall fund research and development (R&D) initiatives aimed at enhancing Stake DAO's decentralized finance (DeFi) products and services, encompassing new product development, user experience enhancements, security auditing, and risk management, as well as the operation and maintenance of the existing product when needed.

The Association understands and acknowledges that the Grant Amount shall be exclusively used to execute the Milestones defined within the Grant Proposal.

Internal regulations shall be in place to address any misuse of the funds, ensuring that all activities funded by the Grant Amount shall directly contribute to the specified project and the broader Stake DAO ecosystem. Any portion of the Grant Amount not applied to the Grant Purpose during the period shall be retained by the Association and netted against its next grant request, consistent with the treatment of the current Association balance set out under “Use of funds” above.

The Association will use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve the Milestones; however, the Stake DAO ecosystem is subject to technological, market, governance, third-party protocol, and security risks, and the Association does not guarantee any particular financial performance, TVL level, token price outcome, or absence of exploits. For the avoidance of doubt, the financial targets referenced in the Milestones (including the curated AUM and TVL objectives) are good-faith objectives and not guarantees of outcomes or of the conditions of the Association’s entitlement to the Grant Amount.

The Association shall not knowingly use the Grant Amount in a manner that would cause a violation of applicable sanctions, anti-money laundering, anti-corruption, or counter-terrorism financing laws, including Swiss sanctions measures and (to the extent applicable) EU/UN measures. In particular, the Association shall not, directly or indirectly, make the Grant Amount available to, or for the benefit of, any person, entity, or jurisdiction that is the target of applicable sanctions. The Association shall maintain reasonable internal checks for material counterparties and service providers engaged using the Grant Amount.

## IP Ownership and Source Code Publication and Licensing

Subject to any third-party components and dependencies (including open-source libraries and external protocols) which remain subject to their respective licences and terms, the Association shall become the sole owner of any intellectual property rights in and to any kind of work products that have been or will be created in the context of this grant.

The Association acknowledges its role in holding and managing intellectual property rights within the Stake DAO ecosystem.

All backend and frontend code developed as part of this grant, including smart contracts and web interfaces, will be published on a designated public GitHub repository. The software will be licensed under an open-source license (such as the BSD License, the MIT License, the Apache License Version 2.0, or any other license approved by Stake DAO), promoting transparency and accessibility. For avoidance of doubt, such publication is intended to grant the Stake DAO ecosystem and its community a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free right to use, copy, modify, and distribute the Work Product in accordance with the applicable open-source licence.

## Reporting Obligation

In line with the commitment to transparency and accountability, the Association will include details regarding the Grant Amount and its utilization in its monthly activity reports. This report will be prepared in accordance with the governance proposal's requirements, ensuring the Stake DAO community is fully informed of the progress and outcomes of the funded initiatives.

## Conclusion

This proposal, structured in accordance with both the strategic goals of Stake DAO and the legal guidelines provided, represents a comprehensive plan for utilizing the requested grant to achieve significant advancements within the Stake DAO ecosystem. The Association commits to fulfilling the outlined objectives with the highest standards of transparency, efficiency, and accountability.

## Vote

-   **For (Yes):** Approve the H2-2026 grant of USDC 672,000 to the StakeDAO Association, according to the payment schedule and used for the execution of the Milestones as described.
    
-   **Against (No):** Reject the proposal.
    
-   **Abstain:** Take no position.

title: The Future Of The Old QUICK To New QUICK Conversion Process
body:
In 2022, the dragon community voted to redenominate QUICK through a 1:1000 token split, expanding the maximum supply from 1 million Old QUICK to 1 billion New QUICK tokens. Shortly after the vote passed, QuickSwap launched a conversion contract where holders could convert Old QUICK to New QUICK at a fixed 1:1000 ratio.

During this period (until now), the migration process via the converter contract was intentionally left open-ended to give QUICK token holders, CEXs, LPs, and ecosystem participants enough time to migrate without pressure.

After several years, QuickSwap has migrated to be centred almost entirely around New QUICK (91%+ have been migrated) to power ecosystem initiatives, leaving the Old QUICK token with extremely limited utility.

**This governance proposal is aimed for the dragon community to decide the long-term future of the Old QUICK to New QUICK conversion process.**

Rather than introducing multiple governance decisions simultaneously, this proposal proposes a two-stage governance approach.

The first vote will determine whether the conversion process should remain open indefinitely, or whether the DAO should introduce a final six-month migration schedule.  
If the DAO votes in favor of the final migration schedule, a second governance vote will take place once that migration period has concluded. This second vote will determine what happens to any remaining New QUICK that was originally reserved for unconverted Old QUICK.

Continue reading the entire proposal below for more details and information.

# Next Steps:  
To begin, the governance discussion on the official QuickSwap Reddit will run until **Tuesday, July 28 11:00 AM UTC**
Once the discussion has concluded, a Snapshot vote will be initiated and run until **Tuesday, August 4 at 11:00 AM UTC**

Once you’ve read this proposal, make sure to visit the official QuickSwap Reddit discussion forum to share your perspective with your fellow community members

# Old & New QUICK Tokenomics

Below is a breakdown of the current supply and conversion figures for Old QUICK and New QUICK:  
Old QUICK Converted: ~915,895 QUICK  
Original Old QUICK Max Supply: 1,000,000 QUICK  
Remaining Unconverted Old QUICK: ~84105 QUICK  
Equivalent New QUICK Reserved For Conversion: ~84,105,000 QUICK

Based on this data, more than 91% of the original Old QUICK supply has already been converted or otherwise removed from circulation, while approximately 8.4% remains unconverted.

Of the remaining unconverted Old QUICK:  
~12,262.82 QUICK remains in liquidity positions.  
~11,266 QUICK remains in the original Dragon’s Lair.  
~60,577 QUICK remains in user wallets.

At the 1:1000 conversion ratio, the user wallet portion alone represents approximately 60,577,000 New QUICK, or ~6.05% of the maximum New QUICK supply.

As of today, the remaining reserved allocation exists solely to honor potential future conversions. Whether that allocation should remain permanently reserved or whether the conversion process should eventually conclude is the primary question this proposal seeks to answer.

# Why Revisit The Conversion Process?

There are several important considerations for the dragon community when evaluating the future of the Old QUICK to New QUICK conversion process:

Supply clarity: More than 69 million New QUICK remains reserved for potential future conversions. While much of this may never enter circulation, it must still be considered when evaluating QUICK’s maximum potential supply.

Finalising the ecosystem transition: 91%+ of Old QUICK has already been migrated. The QuickSwap ecosystem now operates almost entirely using New QUICK, leaving Old QUICK with extremely limited utility.

Encouraging remaining migrations: Introducing a clearly communicated migration schedule may encourage remaining active holders to complete their migration rather than leaving the process open indefinitely.

Long-term certainty: An indefinitely open conversion process means the DAO must continue accounting for a significant reserved allocation whose future remains uncertain.  
Inactive or lost wallets: Some Old QUICK almost certainly belongs to inactive wallets, lost wallets, or holders who are unaware that the converter remains available.

Original expectations: The migration process was intentionally left open-ended to avoid forcing holders into an arbitrary deadline; some community members may believe this expectation should continue indefinitely.

Exchange and ecosystem coordination: Any changes to the migration process would require appropriate notice across exchanges, explorers, wallets, liquidity providers and ecosystem partners.

Future governance flexibility: Separating the decision to conclude the migration process from the decision regarding any remaining reserved New QUICK allows the DAO to make the second decision using final onchain data rather than estimates.

# Proposed Voting Structure

As highlighted in the introduction of this governance proposal, the proposed approach would involve two DAO votes in total.

The first vote would determine whether the Old QUICK to New QUICK conversion process should remain open indefinitely, or whether the DAO should introduce a final structured migration schedule.

If the DAO votes in favor of the final migration schedule, a second governance vote would take place once the full six-month migration period has concluded. This second vote would determine what happens to any remaining New QUICK that was originally reserved for unconverted Old QUICK.

**Vote 1: Should The Old QUICK To New QUICK Conversion Process Remain Open Indefinitely, Or Move To A Final Migration Schedule?**

**Option A: Keep The Conversion Process Open Indefinitely**  
No changes are made.  
Old QUICK holders can continue converting Old QUICK to New QUICK at the fixed 1:1000 ratio at any time.  
The remaining reserved New QUICK stays allocated for future conversions indefinitely.

**Option B: Introduce A Final Six-Month Migration Schedule**  
The DAO agrees to move the Old QUICK to New QUICK conversion process into a final six-month migration schedule.

For the first three months, Old QUICK holders would continue to be able to convert at the full 1:1000 ratio.

Following the initial three-month period, the conversion ratio would reduce by 25% each month over the following three months.

The proposed migration schedule would be:  
Months 1–3: 100% conversion rate  
1 Old QUICK = 1,000 New QUICK  
Month 4: 75% conversion rate  
1 Old QUICK = 750 New QUICK  
Month 5: 50% conversion rate  
1 Old QUICK = 500 New QUICK  
Month 6: 25% conversion rate  
1 Old QUICK = 250 New QUICK  
After Month 6: 0% conversion rate

The existing automated conversion process would conclude, and no further automatic Old QUICK to New QUICK conversions would be available through the converter contract.

This approach provides remaining Old QUICK holders with a clearly communicated final migration period while gradually reducing the conversion benefit for holders who choose to migrate later in the process.

**Vote 2: What Should Happen To The Remaining Reserved New QUICK?**  
If Vote 1 passes in favour of the final migration schedule, a second DAO vote will be held once the six-month migration period has concluded.

By that point, the remaining amount of unconverted Old QUICK — and therefore the remaining reserved New QUICK allocation — can be calculated accurately through final onchain accounting.

This second governance vote will determine the future of those remaining reserved tokens.

Possible outcomes may include, but are not limited to:  
Burning the remaining reserved New QUICK.  
Transferring the remaining reserved New QUICK to the QuickSwap Treasury.  
Another DAO-approved outcome proposed by the community.  
The exact voting options will be presented closer to the second vote once the final migration figures have been confirmed.

# Suggested Implementation & Updates Timeline

If the dragon community votes to keep the conversion process open indefinitely, no changes would be made.

If the dragon community votes to introduce the final six-month migration schedule, the following implementation path could be be used:  
The final migration schedule is formally announced across QuickSwap communication channels, including X, Discord, Telegram, Reddit and the QuickSwap website.

QuickSwap coordinates messaging with relevant ecosystem partners, wallets, explorers and exchanges wherever possible to maximise awareness.

Old QUICK holders are encouraged to remove their Old QUICK from liquidity positions, withdraw from the original Dragon’s Lair, and complete migration during the initial three-month period where the full 1:1000 conversion ratio remains available.

Following the first three months, the conversion ratio reduces by 25% each month according to the approved migration schedule.

Once the six-month migration schedule has concluded, the automated conversion process ends.

A second DAO vote is initiated to determine the future treatment of the remaining reserved New QUICK.

Finally, QuickSwap would publish a public confirmation outlining the final migration figures, the remaining amount of unconverted Old QUICK, and the outcome of the second governance vote.

# Join The Discussion

As always, QuickSwap community members are encouraged to participate in and contribute to governance discussions and proposals across all of QuickSwap’s official forums, especially on Reddit. As a Dragon, you are a valued member of the community, and your opinion matters—but you have to participate in governance to make it count.  
Critical decisions guiding QuickSwap’s strategic development will continue to be determined through decentralised governance. QuickSwap’s future is in your hands, so make your voice heard!

title: PIP-4: Advancing Agent-Native Global Markets Through Purr-Fect Claw
body:
# Summary

This proposal recognizes the emergence of agent-native global markets — markets where autonomous agents can independently discover, reason, execute, and manage economic activity — and establishes Pieverse's commitment to building the infrastructure that enables open access to them. Purr-Fect Claw shall serve as the primary Agent Trading Terminal through which this vision is realized.

# Motivation

Trading infrastructure was designed for humans — navigating dashboards, switching between venues, managing keys across platforms. As autonomous agents become active market participants, they require infrastructure built for a different paradigm: one that abstracts venue complexity, operates across asset classes, and enables both natural-language intent and autonomous execution at machine speed.

At the same time, global markets are undergoing a structural shift. Tokenized equities, commodity derivatives, FX markets, and prediction markets are increasingly available through permissionless infrastructure, extending the tradable universe far beyond crypto-native assets. These markets are becoming natively accessible to autonomous agents — and Pieverse is positioned to meet this moment.

# Specification

The Pieverse Foundation formally declares the following:

1.  **Open Access Across Global Markets** — Pieverse recognizes that global markets — spanning crypto, tokenized equities and indices, commodities, foreign exchange, prediction markets, and emerging digital markets — are increasingly accessible to autonomous agents. The protocol will support infrastructure that enables agents to discover opportunities, execute transactions, and manage positions across these markets without being constrained to a single chain, venue, or asset class.
    
2.  **Purr-Fect Claw as the Agent Trading Terminal** — Purr-Fect Claw shall serve as Pieverse's primary Agent Trading Terminal, providing autonomous agents with a unified interface to access fragmented global markets. By abstracting wallets, venues, data sources, and execution pathways, Purr-Fect Claw enables agents to interact with decentralized protocols, centralized venues, and other market infrastructure through a single, cohesive terminal.
    
3.  **Open, Ecosystem-Driven Expansion** — Pieverse will uphold an open and composable model for expanding agent access to global markets. Through the Skill Store and open developer ecosystem, new venues, asset classes, data sources, and execution capabilities can be integrated by any participant, ensuring that market access remains permissionless and ecosystem-driven.
    
4.  **Infrastructure, Not Intermediation** — Pieverse's role is to provide the infrastructure layer that makes global markets agent-accessible — not to intermediate, gatekeep, or centralize market access. The protocol supports open

title: Multisig Signers Update + Transition to 3/5 Configuration
body:
**Summary:**  
Proposal to update the multisig signers by replacing Glassy and Eightz with jiujiteiroETH, Pronk, and Efraim.  
The required number of signatures remains set at 3, changing the configuration from 3/4 to 3/5.

**Specifications:**  
-Removal of current signers: Glassy and Eightz  
-Addition of new signers: jiujiteiroETH, Pronk, and Efraim  
-New configuration: increase from 4 to 5 members  
-Maintenance of the required signature threshold at 3

**Motivation:**  
For several years, we have faced recurring difficulties in executing transactions on the multisig due to the prolonged absence of certain signers. This has caused significant delays on operations that had clear consensus within the active community.  
The objective of this proposal is to strengthen the reactivity of the multisig while maintaining a high level of security (still requiring 3 signatures). By integrating long-time active and engaged members (jiujiteiroETH, Pronk, and Efraim), we ensure better operational continuity.

**Budget:**  
Gas fee reimbursement for the signer who will execute the transaction.  
This change requires one on-chain transaction on the Gnosis Safe. Current gas fees are low (estimated $3–12 on Ethereum Mainnet) and will be covered by an active signer.

title: [Temp Check] Deploy Aave V4 on Tempo
body:
### [Temp Check] Deploy Aave V4 on Tempo

### Author: Tempo

### Date: 2026-07-23

***

# **Summary**

This Temp Check seeks community feedback on deploying Aave v4 on Tempo Mainnet.

Tempo is a new purpose-built Layer 1 blockchain for payments, developed in partnership with leading fintechs and Fortune 500s like DoorDash, Deel, Shopify, Moneygram and more. Incubated by Stripe and Paradigm, Tempo is designed for stablecoin use cases including cross-border payments, remittances, embedded finance, payroll, and treasury management that bring real business value to companies adopting blockchain technology.

Launching Aave v4 on Tempo would position Aave as a key infrastructure partner for Tempo and the enterprises building on Tempo.

# **Motivation**

Tempo launched on mainnet in March 2026. Since then, the Tempo team has been building yield and credit products with enterprise partners. With regulatory clarity emerging around stablecoins and crypto, traditional companies are increasingly positioned to build onchain using DeFi infrastructure. Tempo is excited to partner with the Aave ecosystem on bringing these use cases to life.

Deploying Aave v4 on Tempo will:

- Expand Aave's liquidity footprint to include traditional enterprises and fintechs

- Develop new markets by listing bespoke real-world assets exclusive to Tempo

- Grow GHO by powering B2B credit use cases on Tempo

- Drive new revenue opportunities that will accrue value back to the Aave DAO and $AAVE token holders

For the first year after Aave v4 launches on Tempo, the Tempo team will incentivize pathUSD deposited on Aave at around SOFR rate. This will establish a sustainable baseline incentive APY for the pathUSD supply market. pathUSD is a native stablecoin on Tempo issued by Bridge.

# **Specification**

If governance supports this Temp Check, the next phase will be an ARFC for deploying Aave v4 on Tempo. The ARFC would include the proposed initial supported tokens, oracle configuration, risk framework, deployment contracts, incentive strategy, and parameter recommendations from relevant Aave DAO service providers.

# **Useful Links**

- Website: https://tempo.xyz/

- Customer stories: https://tempo.xyz/customer-stories/

- Developer docs: https://tempo.xyz/developers/docs

# **Next Steps**

1. If the Temp Check Snapshot outcome is YAE, publish an ARFC covering the initial supported tokens, oracle configuration, risk framework, deployment contracts, incentive strategy, and parameter recommendations from relevant Aave DAO service providers.

2. After the ARFC discussion and a successful ARFC Snapshot, submit an AIP for an onchain vote to deploy Aave v4 on Tempo.

title: Reducing the CARROT → PUFFER Conversion Period
body:
The current CARROT → PUFFER conversion period is 6 months. A governance forum discussion raised the case that this may be too long, supported by on-chain data.

This implementation vote asks whether to reduce the conversion period to 1 month or keep it at 6.

Reduce the CARROT → PUFFER Conversion Period

Summary

This proposal asks the Puffer community whether the CARROT → PUFFER conversion period should be reduced from 6 months to 1 months.

Background

When the CARROT → PUFFER converter launched, the 6-month conversion period was designed to:

  • Encourage long-term commitment to the Puffer ecosystem.
  • Limit short-term selling pressure on PUFFER.
  • Align CARROT recipients with the protocol over a longer period.

As the incentive system has matured, community members have questioned whether the current conversion period is unnecessarily long and whether a shorter period could improve the efficiency of CARROT emissions.

Why This Matters

The conversion period affects both individual CARROT holders and the efficiency of Puffer’s broader incentive system.

Arguments in Favor

When the CARROT:PUFFER premium is high, each CARROT distributed through gauge voting purchases less TVL per token emitted.

Reducing the conversion period could make the converter more practical to use and reduce the market premium associated with CARROT. As a result, the same amount of CARROT emissions could potentially attract more liquidity across all gauges.

A shorter conversion period may therefore improve the capital efficiency of Puffer’s incentive program.

Arguments Against

Reducing the conversion period could weaken incentives for long-term participation by allowing CARROT recipients to access PUFFER sooner.

This may increase short-term selling pressure on PUFFER and reduce the long-term alignment created by the existing 6-month conversion schedule.

Existing Vesting Period

CARROT already has a 30-day vesting period after it is claimed.

Therefore, reducing the CARROT → PUFFER conversion period to 1 months would result in an effective lock-up period of approximately 2 months from claim to PUFFER:

  • 1-month CARROT vesting period.
  • 1-month CARROT → PUFFER conversion period.

The Vote

The community will vote on the following options:

Yes

Reduce the CARROT → PUFFER conversion period from 6 months to 1 months.

No

Keep the CARROT → PUFFER conversion period at 6 months.

Existing Conversions

Conversions already in progress would not be affected by this proposal.

Any existing conversion would remain subject to its original 6-month schedule.

The reduced 1-month conversion period would apply only to new conversions initiated after the approved change takes effect.

Timeline

  • vote: 5 days
  • Implementation: Following a successful vote

title: [BIP:101] Contributor Funding H2 2026
body:
### **Total Cost: $145,500 per month**

### **(-$3,000 from [last proposal](https://snapshot.box/#/s:beefydao.eth/proposal/0xfe0085d8d51629ded840940fb863f3cb7ae0dc890650261a390977d491a30242))**

This budget requests approval for future contributor funding covering work scheduled for the months of August 2026 to January 2027\. This covers the last two quarters of financial year 2026, including the first month of 2027.

### 6-month Budget

Beefy has traditionally sought funding on a quarterly basis to maintain flexibility. Though this approach has worked well, it has at times left contributors with uncertainty over their future and incurs more time each quarter for budget discussions than is desirable. A majority of the Core contributor team is of the opinion that longer-term budgets would be a helpful change.

The team has also evolved the way that it handles funding over the last year: adjusting compensation in some cases to align with contributions on a monthly basis, and making changes to compensation in the course of an existing budget, in both cases where those changes are uncontroversial and do not increase the overall budget. In recent months, this has led to actual payments undershooting the budgeted amount. 

In light of the changes to how funding works, the team feels comfortable to commit to a longer-term budget representing the maximum spend and commits to manage this budget carefully from month to month, aiming to save treasury funds wherever possible.

### Staworth Reassignment

Though this budget contains a reduction of $3,000, the overall budget for contributor funding remains the same as the decrease is matched by a reciprocal increase in Staworth’s budget. The change reflects an increase in the scope of Staworth’s work and contribution in recent months which are expected to continue over the rest of the year, as described in their separate proposal.

### Departmental Breakdown

Development - $104,250

Marketing & Design - $17,500

Business Development - $23,750

**TOTAL BUDGET - $145,500 per month**

title: [BIP:102] Staworth Renewal H2 2026
body:
**Total Cost: $10,000 \+ 20% VAT ($12,000 total) per month 
(+$3,000 from [last proposal](https://snapshot.box/#/s:beefydao.eth/proposal/0x5ba9e76f4237e64b212f27d334868755da58347c0fa6e7807857acb73d443c7b))**

**TL;DR** — renew Staworth Limited’s engagement for an additional 6 months at a cost of $12,000 per month.

### Background

In January 2025, Staworth [received](https://snapshot.org/#/s:beefydao.eth/proposal/0x7293b09c56e80bf7b655e6eea2a7c913d8ff6d8c3ee470b9f90349d0b196ea0e) approval for an initial engagement for the DAO, covering financial reporting, non-reserved legal services, and support among a range of other functions for the DAO. That proposal was renewed in [January](https://snapshot.box/#/s:beefydao.eth/proposal/0x960d4a4807f50d2b4138ab6e7aaf06deed855f6c216d47a47db5a72ebaecf67c) and [April](https://snapshot.box/#/s:beefydao.eth/proposal/0x5ba9e76f4237e64b212f27d334868755da58347c0fa6e7807857acb73d443c7b) 2026\.

This proposal covers an extension of our mandate for a further 6 months — in line with the longer term of the main Contributor Funding proposal — on substantially the same terms. We have worked hard in the first 6 months of 2026 to increase our contributions and set Beefy on the right path; now we’re asking for the support to double down on this approach for the rest of the year.

For more information on our background, please see the *Who Are We?* section of our [previous proposal \[BIP:86\]](https://snapshot.org/#/s:beefydao.eth/proposal/0x7293b09c56e80bf7b655e6eea2a7c913d8ff6d8c3ee470b9f90349d0b196ea0e).

### Contributions

Below we detail the major work we’ve undertaken so far in 2026\. Please see our [earlier proposal](https://snapshot.box/#/s:beefydao.eth/proposal/0x960d4a4807f50d2b4138ab6e7aaf06deed855f6c216d47a47db5a72ebaecf67c) for more information on our work in 2025\. Our work includes:

* Shipped \~130 distinct strategies in 2026 so far, averaging \~5 per week. We continue to expand our skills across new strategies, protocols, chains and issues. With a few new chain and protocol launches scheduled for Q3, we continue to grow our role as a key contributor helping to lead the biggest developments in Beefy’s operations.  
* Developed tooling to support deploying and managing Beefy products, including an app for assembling routes and oracles and a system for analysing CLM performance.  
* Led a selection of data handling work for accounting, Dune dashboards and ad hoc analyses of performance, finances, and activities from underlying protocols. This includes key BD requirements like incentive dashboards and point calculations.  
* Issued the 2025 annual report and the 2026 Q1 report for a detailed overview of Beefy’s activities and financial position. Continued our collaboration with Octav to approve accounting and reporting processes.  
* Led recovery efforts relating to incidents and exploits, including the Kelp DAO hack, the Gnosis distribution from the Balancer hack and the USR exploit. Continued to lead the response to the Stream finance situation, including speaking with Stream’s advisors and guiding users on submitting claim information forms.  
* Provided detailed legal support in handling partnerships and procurement contracts, including our grant from Monad, our incentives partnership with Base, our renewal with ChainPatrol and our service agreement with Goldsky.  
* Growing our work with the community and our moderators, including co-hosting the first public Q\&A session in 2 years, answering several dozen questions with candid opinions and updates.  
* Published 7 articles so far in 2026\. Collaborated over marketing plans for the launch of Crosschain Zaps, Ethereum CLMs and new chains like Robinhood and MegaETH.  
* Continued to maintain messaging and knowledge across the project, through our documentation, blog posts, website copy, moderation guidance and knowledge base articles.  
* Helped to manage the Core team’s administration and strategy by leading meetings, keeping regular notes and maintaining strategy documents and action lists to help align on direction.

### Goals

The first half of 2026 has been crucial for the survival of DeFi. Although conditions remain challenging, the first signs of change are beginning to emerge, and we are fortunate that Beefy has survived and been strengthened by the recent bearish markets.

In the second half of 2026, we propose to double down on our existing work, continuing to focus on expanding development contributions while keeping our other competences in good order to support Beefy’s growth:

* Helping to lead on the deployment of new chains, and new protocols on existing chains (including the new Aero protocol and the rollout of Robinhood Chain).  
* Continuing to build out and maintain the systems we have devised for accelerating and strengthening deployment and product maintenance.  
* Growing the DAO’s voice through more public discussions and appearances, and a continued focus on community engagement.  
* Prudent accounting, forecasting and management of Beefy’s financials to ensure a close tracking of performance, risks and opportunities.  
* Proactive management of Beefy’s legal position and communications with users and stakeholders regarding ongoing legal matters, each to ensure safety and stability for the project and space for focus on core revenue-generating activities.  
* General support with business development and partner relations as we strive to capitalise on significant opportunities like new chain launches. This includes supporting some marketing initiatives with content and execution.

### Budget

Our proposed budget is $12,000 per month for the next 6 months. This reflects a $3,000 increase, matched by $3,000 in decreases for the main contributor budget, leaving the total budget for contributor funding at the same level.

Since the start of 2026, we have significantly increased our involvement with development work as well as our overall level of responsibility across the project, all while maintaining our existing responsibilities. This aligns with other movements across the core team, as various contributors have changed their level of engagement. After 6 months of change, the team has conducted a rebalancing to match funding to contribution and properly incentivise those who have increased their responsibilities and output.

This increase places us among the largest contributors to the DAO. We believe this is reflective of the value we contribute to the project, as well as the increase in workflow in 2026 so far. We hope the DAO will be satisfied with the proposed change, and are happy to answer any questions about the changes in our role.

### Terms

This arrangement will be subject to Staworth’s [independent contractor terms](https://docs.google.com/document/d/12LLcVLI9S10-i6baZpYrZg35BbZFSLly/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=100087118599271690842&rtpof=true&sd=true) throughout.  
In addition, the following supplementary terms shall apply specifically for Beefy DAO:

* **Conflicts of Interest** \- where any apparent conflict of interest is identified in any of the work to be performed by Staworth under this engagement, whether by Staworth, Beefy or third parties, either Staworth or Beefy shall be entitled to halt that work immediately without explanation. Staworth shall create and maintain a conflicts policy and register, as a means of safeguarding against conflicts.

* **Independent Interests** \- subject to any provisions and policies relating to conflicts of interest, nothing in this agreement shall impact the rights of Staworth and its contributors to hold or action their own independent views and interests in matters of the Beefy DAO’s governance. Staworth and its contributors shall always retain the right to abstain without explanation on any governance matters.

* **Split Services and Expenses** \- there may be circumstances where Staworth provides services in parallel for multiple clients (e.g. attending conferences with opportunities to represent 2 or more projects). In such circumstances, Staworth will always report the existence of such a split to all client contributor teams, together with an indication of the likely division of its efforts between them. Where any expenses are incurred in relation to split services, Staworth will offer to split the funding of its expenses in line with its expected efforts for each client.

If approved, this engagement will commence on 1 August 2026 and proceed to the end of January 2027\. A further engagement proposal will be provided towards the end of this engagement.

### Proposal

Beefy DAO should renew its engagement with Staworth for another 6 months at a cost of $10,000 \+ 20% VAT ($12,000 total) per month.

title: Relay Operator Voting Rights
body:
Anyone Protocol governance continues to expand as the network builds toward a much bigger roadmap of upcoming releases and milestones. This proposal extends Anyone Protocol governance voting power to relay operators by recognising active relay locks as governance voting power.

If approved, relay operators will be able to participate directly in governance signalling and operational proposals through daoforanyone.eth, with no additional steps required on their part.  
This change gives relay operators a direct governance voice in proportion to the infrastructure they support, without requiring them to change how they operate their relays.

---

## What This Proposal Changes

Currently, Snapshot governance voting power is based on governance staking voting power from the Hodler contract.

This proposal adds relay-lock voting power on top of that existing mechanism.

Under the proposed system:

-   1 actively locked $ANYONE for relay registration = 1 vote
    
-   Existing governance staking voting power continues to count
    
-   Relay-lock voting power is added to governance staking voting power
    
-   Relay operators do not need to enable governance mode to receive relay-lock voting power
    
-   Wallets with both governance staking and active relay locks receive both forms of voting power
    

The voting power calculation becomes:

Total Voting Power = Governance Staking Voting Power + Active Relay-Lock Voting Power

---

## How Relay-Lock Voting Power Works

## How Relay Voting Works

There is no separate opt-in process and nothing to configure on the dashboard for relay-lock voting power. Simply running a relay is what generates voting power, so the network recognises an operator's contribution without asking them to do anything differently.  
When a Snapshot vote is created, voting power is calculated from the wallet’s existing governance staking votes plus any active relay locks held by that wallet at the Snapshot voting block.  
Relay operators do not need to enable governance mode if their voting power comes only from active relay locks. If a wallet has both governance staking voting power and active relay locks, both are added together.  
This means simply running relays with active $ANYONE locks can generate voting power, so the network recognises an operator’s contribution without asking them to do anything differently.

### Examples

#### Relay lock only

A wallet has:

-   0 staking votes
    
-   100 active relay-locked $ANYONE
    

Voting power: 100 VP

#### Staking only

A wallet has:

-   1,000 staking votes
    
-   0 active relay-locked $ANYONE
    

Voting power: 1,000 VP

#### Staking and relay locks

A wallet has:

-   1,000 staking votes
    
-   500 active relay-locked $ANYONE
    

Voting power: 1,500 VP

---

## What Does Not Count

Only active relay locks count toward relay-lock voting power.  
Tokens that have been unlocked and are waiting in a withdrawal or vault period do not count as active relay-lock voting power.

---

## Quorum and Voting Period

This proposal uses the same core governance structure as previous Snapshot votes.

### Quorum

Quorum is set at 1,000,000 VP.

The proposal is considered valid if total voting participation reaches at least 1,000,000 voting power and the number of For votes exceeds the number of Against votes.

### Voting Period

#### **Voting will remain open for 7 days from publication.**

## Looking Ahead

Relay operators carry real operational weight in the network, running the infrastructure that keeps the protocol functioning day to day.

Giving relay operators governance voting power brings governance closer to the people actively contributing to network security and uptime.

This is one part of a longer pipeline of work already underway, with further product releases and governance milestones planned in the months ahead as the team continues building with the runway and resources to keep shipping for the foreseeable future.

---

## Proposal Summary

By voting For, participants approve:

-   Extending Snapshot governance voting power to active relay locks
    
-   Counting active relay-locked $ANYONE on a 1:1 basis
    
-   Adding relay-lock voting power on top of existing governance staking voting power
    
-   Allowing relay-lock voting power without requiring governance mode to be enabled
    
-   Using a quorum of 1,000,000 VP and voting structure for relay operator participation
    
-   Keeping the voting period open for 7 days
    

By voting Against, participants reject extending governance voting power to active relay locks under this framework.

title: WIP #9: Non-Dilutive Merger of WAGMI DAO into Hey Anon
body:
This vote ratifies the merger of WAGMI DAO into Hey Anon, converting WAGMI into ANON and unifying both communities under a single token.

Non-dilutive: No new ANON tokens will be minted, and the total supply will remain unchanged. The swap will be funded entirely with ANON held in the Hey Anon protocol treasury.

Swap: WAGMI will be converted into ANON at a fixed rate based on the 10-day moving-average price before the proposal was posted, helping prevent front-running and market manipulation. The swap will be available for one week and executed manually by users through a swap contract on Sonic and/or Robinhood Chain.

GMI exit: The vesting period will be reduced to 12 hours, allowing GMI participants to exit into WAGMI and participate in the swap.

What WAGMI brings: WAGMI v2 AMM, Boost—single-sided, impermanent-loss-neutral liquidity—an RWA lending market, and tokenized DeFi funds deployed on Robinhood Chain. More detailed information is available in the proposal posted on the official DAO forum.

Condition: The merger will proceed only if both the WAGMI vote and the Hey Anon vote, RFC-#6, pass.

Vote:

Yes — Approve the merger and treasury-funded swap.
No — Reject the proposal.

title: Should the DAO Mandate an Annual Review and Update of All Governance Documents?
body:
> by 0x7bbea9c18cd0541acab8c19da2b11d0c03faef1c (AlGoreRhythm)

## Linked Pre-Proposal
[Should the DAO mandate an annual review and update of all governance documents?](https://decentraland.org/governance/proposal/?id=630bcf4a-695e-4335-a5fc-55ef7e731489)

## Summary

Require that all official DAO governance documents are reviewed and updated annually, with additional updates triggered by any structural change, so the rules governing this DAO are always accurate and accessible.


## Abstract

The Decentraland DAO has governance documents that in some cases have not been meaningfully reviewed or updated since inception. The result is documentation describing committees that no longer exist, processes that have changed, and roles that are no longer accurate. The Governance Legislative Tracker, the DAO's official record of currently applicable decisions, was last updated in May 2024. While the link has since been restored, the content still references the DAO Committee, Revocations Committee, and multiple squads that were deprecated in 2025. Official documentation describes a governance structure that no longer exists.
This Draft Proposal establishes a named review process, a responsible party, defined timelines, and a trigger clause requiring updates whenever a structural change occurs, so the community always has accurate documentation to rely on.


## Motivation

Every functioning organization, public or private, traditional or decentralized, maintains its governing documents as living records. Corporations update their bylaws when their structure changes. Nonprofits review their charters annually. Government agencies publish updated procedures when policies change. This is not bureaucratic overhead. It is the minimum standard for any organization that expects its participants to follow rules and processes that are written down and accurate.
The Decentraland DAO currently has no such requirement. Documents may be created when a proposal passes and never touched again. Two specific examples are already confirmed on the public record: the DAO Council's roles and responsibilities are not documented in any single official maintained source, and the DAO's community-approved mission and vision statements, voted on through governance in 2024, have never been published in an official maintained DAO document. They passed through governance and were never formally recorded anywhere the community is expected to look.
That is the problem this proposal is designed to fix. Not just discoverability, but the absence of any process to ensure governance decisions are documented, kept current, and maintained by someone accountable for doing so.
These gaps affect every community member who tries to understand how the DAO works, every new participant who reads the documentation and forms an inaccurate picture of the current governance structure, and every accountability conversation that stalls because the rules are not written down anywhere reliable.
An annual review cycle with a structural change trigger is the minimum standard expected of any organization that takes its own governance seriously. This proposal asks the DAO to meet that standard.


## Specification

**Responsible Party**
The DAO Council is responsible for ensuring all official DAO governance documents are reviewed and updated as required. The Council may conduct this work directly or identify and engage someone to do so through whatever process it determines appropriate. The method is the Council's decision. The accountability is not.

1.  *Annual Review Cycle*
    A comprehensive review of all official DAO governance documents must be completed once per calendar year. The review must assess whether each document accurately reflects current processes, roles, responsibilities, and timelines. Any document found to be outdated, incomplete, or inaccurate must be updated before the review cycle closes. A summary of all changes, or confirmation that no changes were needed, must be published to the DAO governance forum upon completion. The first review must be completed within 6 months of the binding proposal passing.

2.  *Trigger Clause*
    Whenever a structural change occurs, including a new role being created, an existing process modified, a governance body deprecated, or a new mechanism introduced, the relevant documentation must be updated within 30 days of that change taking effect. This ensures documents never fall more than 30 days behind reality and makes the annual review faster and more confirmatory than corrective.

3.  *Minimum Documents in Scope*
    The following documents must be included in every annual review:

4.  The Governance Legislative Tracker

5.  DAO Council roles, responsibilities, and timeline obligations

6.  Documentation describing how governance proposals advance through each stage

7.  A summary of the Regenesis Labs mandate and operational scope as it relates to DAO governance

8.  Wearable, emote, and creator submission guidelines

9.  Any documentation describing DAO governance bodies, committees, or squads

10. The DAO's approved mission and vision statements, published in an official and accessible location

11. *Accountability*
    For the purposes of this proposal, “ownership" means a named individual or team, identified by wallet address and/or community handle, who is publicly accountable for ensuring the document is current and accessible.

Named owners must publish a public confirmation upon completion of each annual review. Any missed deadline must be publicly flagged within 30 days with an explanation and revised timeline. If a trigger clause update is not made within 30 days of a structural change, the responsible party must publicly acknowledge the delay and publish a revised timeline. No governance document becomes ownerless. Ownership transfers must be publicly documented.


## Conclusion

The Decentraland DAO approved a mission that includes representative governance and efficient management of collective resources. Governance documents that are outdated, inaccessible, or simply wrong undermine both.
This is not a complex ask. It is the minimum that any serious organization maintains: a regular review cycle, a named responsible party, and a requirement that documentation reflects reality. The fact that it needs to be put through governance at all is itself evidence of why it is needed.

A properly maintained Governance Legislative Tracker, updated as required by this proposal, serves as the living directory of all current governance responsibilities, decisions, and accountable parties — making it the single reference point the community has never had.

**[This proposal is summarized due to technical limitations. To view it complete and vote on it, visit the DCL DAO Governance dApp](https://decentraland.org/governance/proposal/?id=0ef1b25f-9d29-441d-93d0-eee26b7fa3ba)**

title: [Proposal #14] Community Vote to Delist
body:
**Introduction**

Orderly’s mission is to provide a high-quality trading environment with deep liquidity, sustainable trading activity, and transparent governance. While new listings bring growth and experimentation, it is equally important to evaluate underperforming markets and decide which should be removed.

This proposal introduces a new Community Vote to Delist. Instead of voting to remove tokens, the community will now vote to retain tokens from a pre-identified list, ensuring our resources are focused on assets with verifiable community support.

**The Proposal**

The Orderly Core Team has identified the following 7 tokens for potential delisting based on predefined criteria (e.g., sustained low liquidity, volume, and community activity).

**Delisting Pool:**

DASH  
SKR  
ICP  
WLFI  
LDO  
LINEA  
ZEN

**The Vote & Outcome:**

A "Vote to Retain" will be held for each token individually. For a token to be removed from the delisting pool and continue trading on Orderly, it must meet the following threshold:

3% of Total Staked $ORDER voting "AGAINST Delisting".

If none of the tokens meet the 3% retention threshold, all tokens in the pool will be delisted.

**Rationale**

This revised process ensures Orderly focuses liquidity on markets with active community engagement, while introducing a more efficient and decisive governance mechanism.

Efficiency & Clarity – Provides a clear, binary outcome for each asset based on measurable community support, eliminating ambiguity.

Community Empowerment – Directly measures which assets have sufficient stakeholder backing to merit ongoing platform support.

Protocol Integrity – Ensures resources are directed to ecosystems with engaged communities, driving sustainable growth.

**Next Steps & Implementation**

Community votes will be collected during the 7-day voting period.

After the vote, each token will be evaluated against the 3% retention threshold.

Tokens that fail to meet the threshold will be scheduled for delisting.

Orderly will issue a reminder at least 48 hours before any delisting is executed.

**Voting Parameters**

Retention Threshold: >3% of total staked $ORDER must vote "AGAINST Delisting" for a token to be saved.

Voting Period: 7 days

Eligibility: Only $ORDER staked before proposal submission counts toward voting power.

**The Takeaway**

This Vote to Retain empowers ORDER stakers to clearly signal support for the assets they value. This decisive process ensures Orderly maintains a vibrant market of high-engagement tokens, upholding our commitment to transparency and community-driven governance.

title: [ARFC] Deploy a Dedicated Aave V4 Whitelabel Instance fully managed by EtherFi on OP Mainnet to Power Ether.fi Cash
body:
**Author:** [Ether.Fi](https://ether.fi/)

**Date:** 2026-07-14

**ARFC discussion:** [governance.aave.com thread](https://governance.aave.com/t/arfc-deploy-a-dedicated-aave-v4-whitelabel-instance-fully-managed-by-etherfi-on-op-mainnet-to-power-ether-fi-cash/25314)

**Temp Check discussion:** [governance.aave.com thread](https://governance.aave.com/t/temp-check-deploy-a-dedicated-aave-v4-whitelabel-instance-fully-managed-by-etherfi-on-op-mainnet-to-power-ether-fi-cash/25267)

**Temp Check Snapshot (passed):** [Snapshot vote](https://snapshot.org/#/s:aavedao.eth/proposal/0xf4019e2bfcf1c15460957fa47078402edd10af000139725178f34b6a50b476f8)

## Summary

Following the successful TEMP CHECK Snapshot, this ARFC formalizes the deployment of a dedicated, EtherFi-operated Aave V4 hub on OP Mainnet to serve as the credit backend for EtherFi Cash, the Visa card product used by tens of thousands of cardholders. The instance replaces the bespoke borrow/lend market ("Debt Manager") that powers Cash today.

The instance is isolated and borrow-whitelisted: borrowing is restricted exclusively to EtherFi Cash users. EtherFi operates it end to end — configuration, risk parameters, liquidity, and growth — while Aave provides the V4 deployment and operating license (2-year initial term) and earns a share of the revenue the instance generates. Because the instance is ring-fenced and EtherFi-run, Aave carries the upside without taking on the market's day-to-day risk.

## Key Terms

- **Revenue share:** 80-20 EtherFi / Aave on the totality of instance protocol revenue (Liquidity Fee, liquidation fees, SVR and other fee streams), settled automatically on-chain. Projected ~$1.0-1.2M/year to the Aave DAO at end-2026 target scale (~$500M instance assets).
- **GHO integration:** GHO listed as supply and borrow reserve once deployed on OP Mainnet; Aave deploys a GHO GSM on Optimism; GHO may become a spend asset in Cash at the DAO's discretion.
- **Assets at launch:** up to $175M brought by EtherFi.
- **Launch capitalization:** $20M supplied by the Optimism Foundation Treasury; $1.2M joint incentive package; $5M strategic GHO position via the GSM (6 months).
- **Exclusivity:** EtherFi Cash will exclusively use Aave V4 as its DeFi lending protocol.
- **Operating model:** EtherFi as operator; Nonce Capital as independent risk admin (listings, oracles, risk parameters, IRMs, caps, pause states); Aave Labs provides deployment, license, and GSM; Aave DAO ratifies and receives the revenue share.

Full specification — architecture (single Liquidity Hub + Cash Spoke on OP Mainnet), the 20-asset launch collateral set, reference risk parameters, oracles, liquidations, and the phased Debt Manager migration (~$25M active borrows) — is detailed in the [ARFC post](https://governance.aave.com/t/arfc-deploy-a-dedicated-aave-v4-whitelabel-instance-fully-managed-by-etherfi-on-op-mainnet-to-power-ether-fi-cash/25314).

## Next Steps

If the outcome of this ARFC Snapshot is YAE, publish an AIP vote for final confirmation and enforcement of the proposal, targeting a July 2026 deployment to meet the Cash product handoff from the current Debt Manager.

## Disclaimer

This proposal is submitted by EtherFi as the operator of EtherFi Cash and the proposer of the instance. All terms and parameters are subject to this governance process and service-provider review. EtherFi is not compensated by any third party for submitting this proposal.

title: Arrow Air 2026 Board Election
body:
### Arrow Air 2026 Board Election

This proposal executes the director election announced in the [Election Notice posted 2026-07-15](https://dao.arrowair.com/t/arrow-air-2026-board-election-election-notice-open-nominations/177), as required by the Arrow Air Bylaws (elections every 12–18 months; current board seated February 2024).

**What this vote does:**

1. **Elects a board of five (5) directors.** The five candidates with the most approvals are seated as the new board of Arrow Air (Wyoming UNA), Arrow DAO's legal wrapper.
2. **Dissolves the outgoing board in its entirety** upon vote close, including removal of any current director not standing for re-election.
3. **Rotates the treasury Safe signer set.** The five elected directors become the five signers on the DAO treasury Safe (3-of-5 threshold), replacing the current signers. Elected directors will privately provide a signing address for the rotation and board records.

**Candidates** (nominations were open to any $ARROW holder for 7 days; each candidate confirmed acceptance of director and Safe signer duties and declared no disqualifying conflicts — full statements in the [nomination thread](https://dao.arrowair.com/t/arrow-air-2026-board-election-election-notice-open-nominations/177)):

- **Sleety** — director since the UNA was established (Secretary/Treasurer); author of AIP-001–004; manages Arrow's public presence; active Safe signer.
- **Thomas Garrison (thomasg)** — working to advance Arrow since founding; available daily/weekly for governance items and multisig actions.
- **Erick Perdomo (errrks)** — Project Quiver lead, GBC member, co-author of AIP-010; longtime multisig signer and disbursement operator; joined April 2022.
- **Alperen Gundogan (alperenag)** — initiated and led Arrow engineering across Feather, Quiver, and Spearhead (current lead); author of AIP-005.
- **Julius (far1no)** — Arrow engineering since early 2023 (batteries, Feather); team lead for Project Caribou and Project Longshot.

**Vote mechanics:** approval voting — approve every candidate you support. The top five by approvals are seated. Quorum is 2,000,000 $ARROW. The board is the DAO's execution layer, not its decision layer: directors carry out the will of the tokenholders and hold no unilateral power.

**Upon passing:** the new board is seated by written consent, and the treasury Safe signer rotation is executed and publicly reported.
