title: [Fast Track] [1IP-103] Aqua Launch Framework: Aqua Interface Authorization, Protocol Fee Activation
body:
## Simple Summary

Degensoft requests authorization from 1inch DAO to deploy and launch Aqua and SwapVM and to operate the official Aqua interface for the 1inch Network; activates 100% of protocol fees, accruing to the DAO Treasury

## Abstract

Aqua and SwapVM are live at the protocol layer following the November 2025 developer release, and the DAO has approved the surrounding framework: the Aqua Revenue Stream Incubator \[1IP-93\] and the Aqua/SwapVM operational license confirmation under the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1 \[1IP-102\]. This proposal completes the launch by settling, in one governance action, the protocol's production deployment, who operates the user-facing layer, how protocol fees are handled, and how the DAO supports initial liquidity. The DAO’s liquidity incentive budget is deliberately kept out: it runs as a separate, standard-track proposal posted in parallel.

## Motivation

The DAO has funded Aqua's audits, confirmed its operational license, and incubates strategies on it, but no protocol fees currently accrue to the Treasury, and no official interface exists to bring it users. Meanwhile, operating a global non-custodial interface requires 24/7 coverage, incident command, and continuous iteration, responsibilities suited to a single accountable operator, as established in the dApp transfer proposal \[1IP-88\].

## Specification

### 1. Protocol Deployment & Interface Authorization

The 1inch DAO consents to and authorizes Degensoft Ltd (BVI) ("Degensoft") to deploy and launch the production Aqua and SwapVM protocol contracts, and to build, deploy, operate, and maintain the official Aqua interface of the 1inch Network, covering LP onboarding and position management, strategy discovery (including a listing track for Incubator strategies), virtual-balance management, analytics, and access to Aqua/SwapVM liquidity.

**Protocol deployment:** the DAO expressly consents to Degensoft deploying and launching the production Aqua and SwapVM contracts; deployments made under this consent are DAO-authorized deployments for the purposes of the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1 and DAO governance. The DAO gives this consent with knowledge of the DAO-funded audit program and of the inherent risks of smart-contract systems.

**Risk allocation:** this authorization allocates defined operational responsibilities to the operator, as set out below; it does not make Degensoft or any contributor a guarantor of protocol performance. The underlying protocols are source-available under the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1 and run as DAO-authorized deployments, and the interface is non-custodial: users retain full control over their keys and on-chain interactions. Protocol-level risks of DAO-authorized deployments are borne by participants, who acknowledge and assume such risks as set out in the Guidelines' risk disclosures (Sections 5.3.2 and 5.6.2), and nothing here limits the DAO's governance authority over the deployments.

The 1inch.com domain and the 1inch dApp belong to the 1inch Network. Under the network structure set out in the 1inch DAO Guidelines, operation and management of these assets rested with the 1inch Foundation, acting on behalf of the 1inch DAO; pursuant to the DAO's authorization in 1IP-88 and the transfer documentation executed by the Foundation, that role now rests with Degensoft. Degensoft holds and manages the domain and the dApp in this capacity, and operates the official Aqua interface of the 1inch Network under the same authorization. The interface will be hosted on the Network's domain (e.g. 1inch.com/aqua), and 1inch.network, the DAO's governance hub, will reference and link to it. Aqua operates under the 1inch brand as part of the broader 1inch ecosystem, and its users participate in the 1inch Network.

Degensoft's underlying right to build and operate Aqua front-ends already exists under the operational license confirmation \[1IP-102\]. This proposal designates the interface Degensoft operates as the official Aqua interface of the 1inch Network; it confirms status rather than granting new rights.

* The interface remains fully non-custodial; users retain control of keys and assets at all times.
* As operator, Degensoft is responsible for interface-level operations and risks, including terms of use, restricted-jurisdiction access controls, sanctions screening, user disclosures, and interface security.
* This authorization does not restrict third parties from building alternative Aqua interfaces under the existing license and ecosystem protections.

### 2. Protocol Fee Activation — Fees Accrue to the DAO Treasury

Acting within its authority over DAO-authorized deployments of Aqua and SwapVM, made available under the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1, the DAO activates protocol-level fees. In plain terms: every Aqua trade pays an LP fee, which goes to the maker whose liquidity filled it. The protocol fee is a slice of that existing fee, redirected to the DAO Treasury (converted to USDC on the way) — a quarter of it on low-fee pools, a sixth on high-fee pools. Worked example: a $10,000 trade in a 0.30% pool generates a $30 LP fee — $5 goes to the DAO, $25 stays with the maker; the same trade in a 0.05% pool generates $5 — $1.25 to the DAO, $3.75 to the maker.

| Parameter | Value |
|----|----|
| **Protocol fee** | A slice of the LP fee on each strategy, taken from the maker's earnings; taker quotes are unchanged. One quarter on low-fee tiers, one sixth on high-fee tiers, per the initial fee schedule below; custom fees are treated like the nearest standard tier. All parameters, including the tier boundary, are adjustable by governance. |
| **Beneficiary** | 1inch DAO Treasury — the DAO's main Treasury wallet (100% of collected protocol fees) |
| **Collection** | Routed on-chain to the DAO Treasury's main wallet (`eth:0x7951c7ef839e26F63DA87a42C9a87986507f1c07`) via the fee-collector configuration and the fee exchanger described below, published for review with contract addresses prior to activation. Later changes to fee parameters or collection routing require DAO governance approval. |
| **Conversion** | Collected fees are converted through a fee exchanger operated and supported by Degensoft as part of protocol operations, with an initial target composition of 100% USDC delivered to the Treasury's main wallet. The DAO may change the target composition at any time by governance signal to Degensoft, and Degensoft implements the updated composition promptly. Degensoft charges no service fee for operating the exchanger; ordinary market execution costs apply. |
| **Timing** | Firm activation gate: no protocol fees are collected before this proposal is approved. Upon approval, fees activate at, or promptly following, the production interface launch — whichever occurs later. Parameters remain reviewable by governance at any time, including adjustment or suspension for legal or operational reasons. |

**Initial fee schedule** — the protocol fee as a fraction of the LP fee:

| LP fee tier | Protocol share | Protocol fee (of trade amount) |
|----|----|----|
| 0.01% | 1/4 | 0.0025% |
| 0.05% | 1/4 | 0.0125% |
| 0.30% | 1/6 | 0.05% |
| 1.00% | 1/6 | \~0.1667% |
| Correlated presets (0.01% / 0.04% / 0.10% / 0.20%) | 1/4 · 1/4 · 1/4 · 1/6 | 0.0025% / 0.01% / 0.025% / \~0.03333% — per the same boundary rule; confirmed in the published fee schedule |
| Custom fees | 1/4 or 1/6 | Treated like the nearest standard tier. The dividing line sits at ≈0.1225% (the geometric midpoint of 0.05% and 0.30%): below it → 1/4, at or above → 1/6. One constant, retunable by governance. |

Three edge rules, stated plainly: a strategy with a zero LP fee pays no protocol fee; tiny derived values round up to the smallest unit the system can record; and right at the dividing line the absolute take steps down slightly (a 0.13% pool pays \~0.0217% versus 0.030% for a 0.12% pool) — a known property of any tiered rule, accepted by design. Exact encodings for all presets are pinned in the fee schedule published by the core team prior to activation.

**Boundaries:** the protocol fee is independent of (i) the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1 and any license fees thereunder, and (ii) the revenue-share obligations of Incubator teams to the DAO, both of which remain unchanged. Degensoft Ltd, as Licensor under the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1, acknowledges that protocol fee configuration on DAO-authorized deployments falls within the permitted operational use confirmed in \[1IP-102\].

**Execution:** to give the confirmed license arrangement contractual form, the DAO authorizes and directs the 1inch Foundation, as the DAO's off-chain representative, to execute the operational-use terms of the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1 with Degensoft Ltd, exercising the DAO's authority to direct the Foundation under the Guidelines (Section 4.3.2). This changes nothing in \[1IP-102\]: the license and the DAO's confirmed operational rights are unchanged — the Foundation's signature converts an on-chain confirmation into a bilaterally executed agreement, a clearer contractual bond for both sides.

**Foundation position:** the Foundation's directors have confirmed this in writing — by email to the proposer and in a published Foundation page linked from this proposal \[[link](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yjDqCno6zM00KBOfDSITo3SiRqvZUpTf/edit)\] — endorsing the framework as a whole (the interface authorization, the license execution, the fee activation, and the incentive program) as serving the interests of the 1inch Network. Consistent with its neutral role in day-to-day governance, the Foundation expresses its support through this written confirmation rather than by voting.

### 3. Interface & Protocol Development — Service Fee Framework (Separate Proposal)

Developing, maintaining, and servicing Aqua, SwapVM, and the official interface is ongoing work that Degensoft currently carries at its own cost. Compensation for that work is deliberately kept out of this proposal. Degensoft intends to bring a dedicated Development & Service Fee framework to the DAO as a separate proposal, so the launch decision and the operator's compensation are each judged on their own merits.

The follow-up proposal should define, at minimum: the scope of services and deliverables (protocol development, interface operations, security and incident response); term and renewal; budget and payment mechanics, including whether part of the compensation is denominated in 1INCH with vesting, to align long-term incentives and support token utility; reporting obligations; independent review of terms before the vote; and the DAO's rights to adjust or terminate the arrangement.

Sequencing matters. Before recurring service payments begin, the DAO should have its treasury and organizational structures in place, including operational finance groups and defined budget and reporting standards, so a standing service relationship can be administered, accounted for, and reviewed properly.

## Rationale

This framework gives the launch a clear structure and confirms existing contributor roles. The Network keeps its domain and dApp; production deployment proceeds under the DAO's express consent; a single accountable operator carries the interface and its operating obligations; protocol fees accrue to the DAO Treasury, where governance directs them to audits, development, security, and ecosystem programs. Keeping all spending on the standard track means this proposal changes rights and responsibilities, not balances — the money follows the full process.

## Considerations

### Security

The interface introduces no new smart contracts and interacts exclusively with Aqua/SwapVM deployments covered by the DAO-funded audit program, including the fee logic activated under Section 2. Later changes to fee parameters or collection routing require DAO governance approval; the fee exchanger and its target composition follow the same rule, with composition changes by governance signal as set out in Section 2. The interface is non-custodial throughout. Interface-layer security, including penetration testing, monitoring, and incident response, is Degensoft's responsibility as operator.

### Team Qualifications

Degensoft Ltd (BVI) is the developer of Aqua and SwapVM and operates the 1inch dApp for the 1inch Network — one of the most widely used non-custodial interfaces in DeFi.

### Legal & Risk Management

This proposal falls within the risk-review triggers in Guidelines Section 5.6.2 (a new product or feature with changes to the DAO's financial arrangements), and the independent review contemplated there is being completed before the temperature check. The interface is non-custodial, and Degensoft, as operator, is responsible for interface-level risk management, including terms of use, restricted-jurisdiction access controls, sanctions screening, and user disclosures.

Protocol fees accrue to the DAO Treasury as community resources allocated through governance. They are not distributions to tokenholders, and none are proposed. Fee parameters, collection routing, conversion composition, and activation status remain under DAO governance control at all times, including suspension for legal or operational reasons, and deployment of fee proceeds follows the DAO's treasury processes. The interface authorization confirms the official status of an interface Degensoft is already licensed to operate; it does not create new rights or transfer intellectual property. The express deployment consent records that production deployment occurs at the DAO's direction, with informed acceptance of the inherent risks of smart-contract systems disclosed in the Guidelines (Section 5.3.2, 5.6.1, 5.6.2); it allocates operational responsibility without making any party a guarantor of protocol performance. The Foundation's execution of the license terms on the Network's behalf follows the DAO's authority to direct the Foundation (Guidelines Section 4.3.2).

### Conflict of Interest

This proposal is submitted by a @daoplomats  who have received no compensation for authoring it. It was developed with technical input from the Degensoft team, disclosed here for transparency.

**Degensoft Ltd's interests:** it is the developer of Aqua and SwapVM, the Licensor under the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1, the deployer of the protocol and the operator of the official interface under Section 1, the administrator of the incentive program under Section 4, and the intended proposer of a future Development & Service Fee framework under Section 3.

**Mitigants:** all protocol fees accrue to the DAO Treasury, and fee parameters, collection routing, and the exchanger's target composition sit under exclusive DAO governance control; no Treasury funding for interface operations is requested here, and any future service fee will be a separate governance decision with independent review of terms; incentive funds flow to makers primarily through Merkl's claim mechanism, under a published methodology, Degensoft takes no compensation from that budget, and unspent funds return to the Treasury automatically; fee accrual to the Treasury is on-chain and independently verifiable; and Degensoft reports on the incentive program within 60 days of its end.

## Summary

This proposal sets the launch framework for Aqua in a single governance action: the DAO authorizes the production deployment of Aqua and SwapVM and recognizes the official Aqua interface, operated by Degensoft for the 1inch Network on the Network's own domain; protocol fees on Aqua and SwapVM are activated and accrue to the DAO Treasury under governance-controlled parameters; the operator's development and service compensation is deferred to a separate, properly structured proposal. Governance holds the protocol economics; the operator carries the interface and its obligations.

*Note: This proposal follows the fast-track governance process to align its approval with the upcoming public launch of Aqua, ensuring protocol fee activation is in place from day one of production availability. This proposal contains no Treasury spending and requires no on-chain execution; the DAO’s liquidity incentive budget is posted in parallel as a separate, standard-track proposal and takes effect only through that vote.*

title: FIRST COMMUNITY FIELD PROJECT-INTERNET & TRAINING CENTRE
body:
Proposal for first community fields project

Strategic Partnership with VOOS Technology and Launch of the Blockchain Internet Block Initiative
![Y_Internet_DAO_Compressed_0_9MB.jpg](ipfs://bafybeifl5f4sgziyufuy252cjkb7zzq7mkg45vavcaetfhocujngehrh4i)
Executive Summary

The Executive Team of Global Web3 Academy respectfully submits this proposal to the DAO members for consideration and approval.

The purpose of this proposal is to establish a strategic partnership with VOOS Technology Company Limited to launch a real-world blockchain infrastructure initiative known as the Blockchain Internet Block Program.

This initiative is designed to bridge blockchain technology with physical internet infrastructure while creating practical educational opportunities, generating sustainable business revenue, and strengthening the long-term value of the Global Web3 Academy ecosystem.

The Executive Team requests approval from the DAO before proceeding with the partnership and implementation.

Background

Global Web3 Academy was established to empower communities through education in Blockchain, Artificial Intelligence, Web3, Digital Entrepreneurship, and emerging technologies.

As our community grows, there is an opportunity to move beyond education by participating in real infrastructure projects that demonstrate how blockchain technology can solve practical challenges while creating sustainable income-generating assets.

One such opportunity is the deployment of affordable community internet centers through a strategic partnership with VOOS Technology.

Proposed Partnership

The Executive Team proposes that Global Web3 Academy enter into a strategic partnership with VOOS Technology Company Limited.

VOOS Technology specializes in internet infrastructure and telecommunications solutions.

Through this collaboration, both organizations will jointly establish Y Internet Community Centers, providing affordable high-speed internet while creating educational, technological, and business opportunities for our members.

The Blockchain Internet Block Concept

The proposed system introduces Blockchain Internet Blocks.

Each Internet Block represents the minimum capital required to establish one fully operational Y Internet community internet center.

Minimum Capital Per Internet Block

USD 8,000

Once fully funded, the Internet Block will be deployed to establish a new internet center capable of delivering affordable high-speed internet services to its surrounding community.

Each completed Internet Block becomes a real operating business supported by recurring internet subscription revenue.

Expected Annual Performance

Based on the proposed business model and under favorable operating conditions, each operational Internet Block is designed with a target annual performance (APY) of approximately 100%–150%, generated from business revenue after operational expenses.

These projections assume:

Successful completion of the Internet Block.
Timely deployment of the internet center.
Strong subscriber adoption.
Stable operational performance.
Effective management and maintenance.
The Executive Team acknowledges that actual performance may vary depending on market conditions, subscriber growth, operating costs, competition, regulatory requirements, and other business factors. Regular financial reporting will be provided to the DAO to ensure transparency.

Integration with Web3 Pocket (Web3Kibubu)

The proposal further recommends integrating the Blockchain Internet Block initiative with Web3 Pocket (Web3Kibubu).

Members who choose to participate may contribute funds through Web3 Pocket.

These contributions will be pooled until the required USD 8,000 is reached to establish one Internet Block.

Once the funding target is achieved, the Internet Block will be deployed to establish a new Y Internet Community Center.

As the center generates revenue, eligible participants may receive distributions in accordance with the approved DAO policies and the actual financial performance of the project.

Educational Benefits

One of the major objectives of this proposal is to provide students with practical learning opportunities.

Approved participants will have opportunities to:

Visit operational Y Internet centers.
Observe internet infrastructure deployment.
Learn network management and telecommunications operations.
Study blockchain governance in practical environments.
Participate in monthly educational tours organized jointly by Global Web3 Academy and VOOS Technology.
This transforms learning from theory into practical experience.

Governance Through NFTs

Following the successful deployment of each Internet Block, the DAO proposes issuing one Blockchain Internet Block Governance NFT.

The NFT will serve as a transparent digital record of participation and may provide governance rights, including:

Voting on future Internet Block deployments.
Participation in DAO governance.
Access to operational and financial reports.
Participation in future ecosystem proposals.
Community decision-making on expansion and development.
The NFT represents governance participation within the ecosystem and does not automatically represent legal equity unless approved under future DAO policies.

Expected Benefits to the Academy

Approval of this proposal is expected to provide long-term value through:

Practical blockchain implementation.
Real-world infrastructure development.
Sustainable revenue-generating assets.
Increased educational opportunities.
Expansion of affordable internet access.
Stronger partnerships with industry.
Greater DAO participation.
Long-term ecosystem sustainability.
Increased visibility of Global Web3 Academy across Africa and beyond.
Risk Considerations

The Executive Team recognizes that every infrastructure project involves risks.

Potential risks include:

Slower-than-expected subscriber growth.
Infrastructure deployment delays.
Regulatory changes.
Technical failures.
Market competition.
Operational costs.
These risks will be managed through transparent governance, professional project management, partnership with VOOS Technology, and regular reporting to the DAO.

Resolution

The Global Web3 Academy DAO is requested to vote on the following resolution:

"Shall Global Web3 Academy enter into a strategic partnership with VOOS Technology Company Limited to develop and implement the Blockchain Internet Block Program, integrate the initiative with Web3 Pocket (Web3Kibubu), and authorize the deployment of Y Internet Community Centers under the governance framework approved by the DAO?"

Voting Options

☐ YES – Approve the proposal and authorize implementation.

☐ NO – Reject the proposal.

☐ ABSTAIN – Neither approve nor reject.

Closing Statement

This proposal represents an opportunity for Global Web3 Academy to extend blockchain education into real-world infrastructure, creating practical learning experiences while supporting the development of affordable internet access.

By approving this proposal, the DAO will authorize the Executive Team to pursue this partnership, establish Blockchain Internet Blocks, and develop a governance framework that aligns technological innovation with community participation and sustainable growth.

Together, we can transform blockchain knowledge into real infrastructure that connects communities, empowers learners, and builds lasting value for the Global Web3 Academy ecosystem.

title: Proposal for Engagement as the DAO’s Master of Coin extension #4
body:
**TLDR**

This proposal suggests extending my engagement as the DAO’s “Master of Coin” for another 6 months, following the DAO’s compensated contributor guidelines. The proposal is valid from July 1st to December 31st, with a monthly compensation rate of $3,500 in SSV. I dedicate approximately 10 hours weekly and regularly report activities and recommendations to the DAO.

## **Proposal**

### **Objectives**

Objective 1: Ensure that the Multisig committee operates to the highest standard

Key Results:

-   Ensure that all members remain engaged and aware of current DAO proposals
    
-   Help the multisig committee execute in a timely manner
    
-   Ensure security best practices
    
-   Promote continuous improvement of the committees processes
    
-   Propose two transaction batches a month on the 2nd and the 17th of the month.
    
-   Report on multisig performance and MoC activity on an evergreen forum post
    

Objective 2: Help the DAO make informed decisions through documentation and tooling

Key Results:

-   Create runway calculations and related documentation
    
-   Community Treasury Sheet updated every week to ensure that documentation is complete, up-to-date and easily understandable/accessible
    
-   Continued development and maintenance of the community Dune Dashboard
    

Objective 3: Drive Financial Transparency and Budget Managemen**t**

Key Results:

-   Track the DAO Budget (Actual vs. Target)
    
-   Track the spendings of the various programs that the DAO runs, e.g., Lido SDVT, IMP, and future proposals
    
-   Regularly report updates on the DAO Budget and Protocol economics to the DAO.
    
-   Verify numbers presented by the SSV Foundation
    

**About Me**

[image], I’m Sp00kyG (#Sp00kyG on Discord). I have been a DAO contributor since the inception of the SSV DAO. As the “Master of Coin” I lead the multisig committee, review DAO approved proposals, and work with related parties to ensure that proposals get properly translated to the multisig committee. I also help committees and the broader SSV community with multisig committee related questions and proposals.

Past Key Results

-   Helped write and implement DIP-55, getting the DAO to the [top of ENSAwards](https://ensawards.org/leaderboards/dao) (DAO received $6,000 prize at time of [transfer](https://etherscan.io/tx/0x3e7eb84d762df97d25d037278e1afc5b6fdc60a99632dd0fc13639bbd6dc7019))
    
-   Published DAO Budget tracking [report](https://forum.ssv.network/t/moc-report-update-on-the-4-year-dao-budget-evergreen/2113)
    
-   Proposed and executed more than 700 transactions on behalf of the DAO over the past four years
    
-   Helped the multisig committee achieve a flawless track record
    
-   Coordinated and proposed the resolution of several distinct detrimental situations
    
-   Ensured my availability for the above detrimental situations and any other enquiries
    

Some of my other contributions include the development and maintenance of the community [Dune Dashboard](https://dune.com/ssv_network/ssvnetworktoken) and the community [Treasury sheets](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/12cWougs1YjTd6gnsEvIZJMd0PXg_R3e7VkWyFXsmzbo/edit#gid=732582404). I am an operator and validator on the SSV Network, and have helped shape the DAO as part of the genesis committee. I have a computer science background that I leverage to help the DAO in whichever way I can.

Responsibilities

As the DAO’s “Master of Coin”, I will undertake the following responsibilities (in addition to any responsibilities outlined in the [DIP-2] Multi-Sig Committee proposal):

-   Lead the Multisig Committee and inform the DAO regularly on the committee's activity.
    
-   Attend weekly meetings with Labs, Foundation and DAO
    
-   Review DAO-approved proposals and initiate signature requests (including any research, calculation, coordination, etc. required for initiating the said requests).
    
-   Ensure accessibility in case of emergencies
    
-   Ensure proper public documentation of past and future multisig committee activity.
    
-   Calculate and document committee expenses on behalf of the DAO
    
-   Work with committees and related parties on budgeting frameworks
    
-   Propose two transaction batches a month on the 2nd and the 17th of the month. This allows me as the MoC to refuse to propose transactions that do not fall into these two time slots. This does not pertain to Emergency Procedures as outlined in [DIP-2], where a new transaction can be requested for Emergency and Detrimental situations, as described in [DIP-2].
    

## **Terms of contribution**

I shall act under the established [compensated contribution guidelines](https://ssvnetwork.notion.site/Contributor-Guidelines-f2d16e93ff864e1498437b3296d5269f). Logistics and mechanics follow the same guidelines if this proposal does not state otherwise.

**Validity**

This proposal is valid for 6 months, starting from July 1st and ending on the 31st of December 2026.

**Compensation**

For my time and effort, I’m asking for a monthly rate of $3,500. All payments will be denominated 100% in SSV based on a 30-day trailing price average calculated on the 1st day of the following month. According to the compensated contributor guidelines, I will not receive any additional compensation from working groups, circles, or committees I work with as part of this mandate.

Any committee compensation I have received during the validity period of this proposal and the actual date it passes shall be deducted from my first monthly compensation.

Any past or future transaction execution costs incurred while executing transactions on behalf of the DAO will be reimbursed “in-kind” (ETH) by the treasury.

**Commitment**

This is a part-time engagement with an estimated weekly demand of ~10 hours. Over the last three years, I have shown engagement beyond that level in times of high workload or crisis. My primary area and preferred time zone for the length of this engagement is Central Europe (CET).

**Reporting**

I will report the activities I perform per my objectives and responsibilities. Reporting shall be done publicly to the DAO on an evergreen MoC post on the forum. The reporting should include the main objectives for the upcoming month(s), a recap of the activities worked on in the past month(s), ongoing work, and any side objectives, including recommendations to improve the DAO’s efficiency and governance. These objectives are subject to change based on the DAO’s needs.

**Acknowledgment and clarifications**

_As an applicant for a role within the DAO, I acknowledge and understand the effective compensated contributor guidelines and their impact on my role. I appreciate the DAO’s commitment, and I am aligned with the DAO’s values and mission. I acknowledge that these guidelines can be changed at any time, are subject to the DAO’s voting and consensus process, and that continuous refinement is a key aspect of the DAO’s governance structure._

_This engagement is not an employment agreement and does not create an employment relationship. As such, the contributor must cover their own tax, healthcare, and workspace expenses, and they shall not be entitled to any benefits such as a pension or health insurance associated with an employment relationship._

_The contributor warrants that all activities in the context mentioned in this proposal shall be put to the service of the DAO and the ssv.network and not to any of its members to whom the contributor has no direct relationship or obligation. The contributor does not have the power to commit on behalf of the DAO and shall not present themselves as having such power._

**Closing**

Thank you for reading my proposal! Let me know if you have any questions or comments, as usual you can always reach out to me on Discord #sp00kyg

title: TELIP16: The TEL Token Upgrade
body:
Activating TEL as the Native Token of Telcoin Network  
Abstract  
This TELIP proposes the development, third-party security assessment, and deployment of the native TEL token contract and its supporting upgrade contracts across Ethereum, Polygon, Base, and Telcoin Network, in coordination with Telcoin Network mainnet launch.

In exchange for approving this upgrade, the ecosystem receives the following:

A standards-compliant, 18-decimal TEL token that every exchange, decentralized exchange, lending market, aggregator, bridge, and institutional custodian in the EVM ecosystem can list and integrate by default, with no bespoke engineering.

TEL activated as the native gas token of Telcoin Network at genesis, creating recurring, structural, on-chain demand for TEL for the first time.

A single, unified contract address across all supported chains, with mint and burn capability and clean cross-chain liquidity, using Telcoin Network as the source of truth for total supply.

A direct community voice in the upgrade, through ratification of the downstream constitutional amendment that records the upgraded TEL as the canonical TEL going forward.

The upgrade preserves every holder's position one for one. Balances do not change. The TEL ticker does not change. No token is removed from any wallet. Holders upgrade directly on the chain where they already hold TEL, in a single click, with no requirement to bridge first.

This TELIP is the primary proposal and is decided first, through the standard TELIP process: Platform Council approval, then Treasury Council approval, then the Compliance Council veto window. Its approval is what authorizes the upgrade. Two downstream instruments follow. A TGIP, voted by the full Miner Assembly, amends the Telcoin Association Constitution to record the upgraded TEL contract in the preamble.

Motivation  
For eight years, TEL has paid a tax that almost no other token pays. Every exchange that wanted to list it, every protocol that wanted to integrate it, and every custodian that wanted to hold it has had to build something custom to do so, because TEL does not behave the way the EVM ecosystem expects a token to behave. The cost of that friction is not theoretical. It is the listings that never happened, the lending markets TEL was never added to, the liquidity pools that required special handling, and the institutional integrations that quietly declined rather than take on the engineering. TEL has been structurally excluded, by default, from the integration surface that the rest of the market has used to grow for years.

The cause is a single architectural detail. The current TEL token uses 2 decimals. The EVM ecosystem standardized long ago on 18, and it has standardized with increasing rigidity. A token's decimal count is one of the first three attributes any exchange or protocol checks when assessing an asset, alongside its address and its supply. A 2-decimal token signals non-standard behavior immediately, and non-standard behavior is friction, cost, and risk that most counterparties simply route around.

This is the moment to remove that constraint, permanently, because the network TEL was built for is now here.

Telcoin Network is launching, and TEL is its native gas token. A blockchain's native token must express value in fractions finer than 0.01, and it must bridge cleanly without destroying value on the way out. A 2-decimal token can do neither. Launching the network on a legacy token architecture would embed that limitation into the foundation of the chain and into every downstream system, and would make any future correction far more disruptive than doing it now.

This upgrade marks TEL taking its native form: the standards-compliant, finely-divisible, cleanly-bridgeable token that powers its own Layer 1 and that the entire market can finally integrate without exception. The constraint that has capped TEL for eight years comes off at the exact moment the network switches on. That alignment is the opportunity this proposal asks the Councils to seize.

What the Upgrade Unlocks  
The case for this upgrade is not relief from a problem. It is the expansion of everything TEL can do, where it can trade, and who can hold it. Each item below is a capability TEL gains, tied directly to network usage and value accrual.

The full EVM integration surface, by default. An 18-decimal TEL is a token every exchange listing pipeline, every decentralized exchange pool template, every lending market, every yield aggregator, every cross-chain bridge, and every institutional custody platform can support out of the box. The integration work that was a custom engineering project for each counterparty becomes a standard onboarding. The set of venues where TEL can live, trade, and be used expands from a constrained subset to the entire ecosystem.

TEL live as native gas on Telcoin Network. At genesis, TEL becomes the fuel of its own blockchain. Every transaction on Telcoin Network requires TEL for gas. As mobile network operators validate the chain and build applications that drive subscriber activity, that activity converts directly into demand for TEL. For the first time in TEL's history, the token has structural, recurring, on-chain demand tied to real usage rather than to speculation alone.

Clean cross-chain liquidity and a single source of truth. A unified contract address across Ethereum, Polygon, Base, and Telcoin Network, deployed deterministically, means partners identify TEL by the same address everywhere. Mint and burn capability replaces the lock-and-release model that constrains liquidity today, so TEL can move between chains without the bottlenecks and dust losses that legacy bridging imposes. Telcoin Network serves as the canonical source of truth for total supply across all chains. The result is dramatically simpler integration and far easier market-making.

A functioning on-chain TEL economy. Validator staking, TELx liquidity mining, TAN application-developer fees, and Treasury harvesting all assume a standards-compliant, finely-divisible token. The upgrade is the precondition for the full Miner economy to operate at scale. It is what allows the four Miner Groups to produce, earn, and govern on the infrastructure the network was designed around.

Taken together, these are not incremental fixes. They remove the single largest structural suppressor of TEL's market access and replace it with the native foundation for a global, institutionally adoptable token standard for the telecommunications industry.

Why the Current Architecture Caps TEL  
The following details what the upgrade removes. Each is a real constraint on TEL today, and each maps directly to a capability gained above.

Non-standard decimals exclude TEL from the integration surface. TEL's 2-decimal configuration deviates from the 18-decimal standard that virtually every tool, protocol, and exchange in the EVM ecosystem relies on. In practice, every integration with a 2-decimal token requires custom handling. Exchanges must build bespoke deposit and withdrawal pipelines. Decentralized exchanges cannot use standard pool templates. Lending markets, yield aggregators, launchpads, bridges, and custody platforms that assume 18-decimal conformance must either special-case TEL or decline to support it. For a meaningful number of counterparties, the answer has been to decline. The cumulative cost, measured in foregone listings, integrations, and liquidity over eight years, is difficult to overstate, and it is fundamentally incompatible with the adoption trajectory TEL requires.

Non-standard decimal handling is also a security liability. Custom scaling logic is a recurring source of catastrophic precision-loss vulnerabilities across DeFi. The November 2025 Balancer exploit, which drained roughly 128 million dollars across six chains, originated in a precision-loss and rounding inconsistency in the scaled-balance invariant math of its stable pools, exploited by driving balances into very small unit ranges across many swaps in a single transaction. The broader lesson is direct: wherever a token forces custom decimal and scaling logic, it widens the attack surface. A standards-compliant token removes an entire class of this risk.

Inconsistent addresses across chains. TEL's contract addresses differ across chains today, which complicates integration for exchanges, mobile network operators, and data services. A unified address across all supported chains simplifies onboarding at scale.

No mint and burn, which constrains bridging. The current contract lacks mint and burn capability, which limits bridges to lock-and-release. That model creates liquidity bottlenecks that can prevent tokens from moving cleanly between chains. Mint and burn capability enables robust cross-chain supply management and gives the Association the ability to add, replace, or revoke bridge partners over time without further token changes.

Unviable as gas on Telcoin Network. Gas pricing requires denomination in fractions far smaller than 0.01 TEL. With only 2 decimals, the minimum unit is too coarse. As TEL appreciates and network demand rises, fees would become prohibitively expensive relative to competing networks, and TEL could not function as a unit of account on its own chain without value leakage.

Value destruction on outbound bridging. Converting TEL from 2 decimals to 18 when bridging onto Telcoin Network is straightforward. The reverse is not. When a user bridges TEL from Telcoin Network to a chain where TEL has only 2 decimals, any value beyond the second decimal place is truncated and permanently lost as dust. At small sizes this looks negligible, but it compounds across millions of transactions and grows as TEL appreciates. A token that silently destroys value on every outbound bridge transaction cannot serve as a credible medium of exchange.

A clean upgrade to a properly configured 18-decimal token is the only solution that fully, permanently, and verifiably resolves all of the above. Since assuming stewardship of the project, the team has evaluated every reasonable alternative, including wrapper contracts, proxy upgrade patterns, and decimal-adapting middleware. None eliminates the underlying incompatibility. Each only adds layers of abstraction that enlarge the attack surface and reduce confidence in security assessments. For a token destined to sit at the center of a global, institutionally adopted network, residual ambiguity in how decimal handling behaves under adversarial conditions is a systemic risk no responsible engineering team should accept. TEL has been upgraded cleanly once before, when the contract was last updated in January 2020. The team knows how to execute this, and the discipline applied to evaluating the alternatives is the same discipline that will govern the upgrade itself.

Specification and Technical Strategy  
Deployment Plan  
Telcoin Network. A LayerZero native adapter locks and releases native TEL. Genesis includes the total off-chain supply. As holders upgrade and bridge to Telcoin Network, these tokens unlock and serve as native gas. To bridge off Telcoin Network, users lock native TEL, which is then minted on the destination chain.  
Ethereum, Polygon, and Base. The upgraded TEL contract is deployed using CREATE3 for deterministic, identical addressing across chains. Each deployment integrates a mint and burn adapter to support bridging to and from Telcoin Network.  
Upgrade contracts. Dedicated upgrade contracts are deployed on Ethereum, Polygon, and Base. Each accepts legacy TEL and mints upgraded TEL to the holder in the same transaction, ensuring liquidity is always available for the upgrade. After the primary upgrade window closes, the contract stops accepting deposits and stops minting. Legacy TEL remains locked in the contract until all upgrade windows close, enforced at the contract level by a timestamp that any holder can verify by reading the contract directly.  
Legacy token deprecation. To help holders distinguish the two, the legacy TEL logo is updated to gray. The upgraded TEL retains the familiar blue logo as the canonical TEL going forward.  
Recovery of abandoned legacy tokens. Following the primary window, the schedule in the Upgrade Window and Governance section governs the recovery of permanently abandoned legacy tokens to the community-governed TEL Treasury, administered by the Compliance Council. The upgrade contracts permit withdrawal of legacy TEL only after all windows close, again enforced by an on-chain timestamp.

Integrate with LayerZero DVNs. The final step is to register the new TEL with LayerZero DVNs using best practices, diverse clients, and multi-signature threshold. LayerZero is the initial bridge partner that supports flat-fee bridging between chains. The bridge authority is fully customizable and can be revoked any time by a multisig safe controlled by TAO.

TAN and TELx Updates. The councils will update relevant contracts once the upgraded TEL becomes available.

Upgrade Mechanics  
Holders call the upgrade function on the official contract for their chain. The Telcoin Association provides an official upgrade page. Holders connect their wallet, approve the transfer, and complete the upgrade with a single click. The operation is one-way. Upgraded TEL cannot be reverted to legacy TEL.

The contract locks the holder's legacy TEL and mints an equivalent amount of upgraded TEL to the holder in the same transaction. One human-readable legacy TEL equals one human-readable upgraded TEL.

After the primary window, the official page draws from a one-way reserve for holders upgrading late. The holder experience is identical across all windows.

The only recommended upgrade method is the official Telcoin Association page. Holders should verify official contract addresses independently and should never trust unofficial upgrade links.

Bridge Partner Flexibility  
Because the upgraded TEL uses a mint and burn model on EVM chains, the Telcoin Association retains the ability to revoke mint authority from any bridge provider and to onboard new or additional bridge partners. This eliminates long-term vendor lock-in and strengthens the security posture of cross-chain operations.

Upgrade Window and Governance: Suggested Schedule and Compliance Council Mandate  
The upgrade gives every holder a full, generous, and heavily communicated window to upgrade one for one, and it provides a long tail of additional opportunity for anyone who cannot act in time. It does not take tokens from holders. What it does, after a long period, is return permanently abandoned and provably lost tokens to the productive, community-governed TEL Treasury, rather than leaving that value stranded and unusable forever.

This framing is deliberate and it is accurate. A large share of unclaimed legacy TEL will be permanently lost or abandoned: sent to burn addresses, trapped in dead contracts, or stranded as dust in expired liquidity pools. Leaving that value permanently unrecoverable serves no member of the ecosystem. Recovering it, slowly and transparently, returns it to the Treasury that the four Miner Groups govern, for allocation through the TELIP process to ecosystem purposes such as network growth, liquidity, security, and incentives. Recovered TEL does not accrue to any company. It returns to the community.

The schedule below is a suggested framework, not a final policy. This proposal empowers and requires the Compliance Council to establish, finalize, and implement policies through a CCIP within nine months of the commencement of the TEL upgrade to manage unminted TEL3.

Suggested schedule:

Months 1 to 12, primary upgrade window. 100% of legacy TEL is upgradeable on a one-for-one basis, available to every holder for the full period.

Month 12 checkpoint. 50% of the remaining unminted reserve is minted and secured under Compliance Council administration.

Months 12 to 24, extended upgrade window. Upgrades continue on a one-for-one basis from the remaining reserve, first come, first served.

Month 24. The upgrade window closes, and any remaining reserve is secured under Compliance Council administration.

Compliance Council authority and mandate:

Upon approval of this TELIP and the proceeding TGIP, the Compliance Council is empowered and required to create and implement the final policies, through a CCIP, which govern:

The upgrade periods, including the final duration and structure of the primary and extended windows.

The upgrade schedule, including whether, when, and in what proportions TEL3 is minted into reserve.

The process by which holders may upgrade tokens after the upgrade window closes.

The minting and custody of upgraded TEL, held for future use through Compliance Council processes.

TEL3 reserve is stored and administered solely under Compliance Council authority. It is not administered by the Platform Council or the Treasury Council, and it is not transferred to the TEL Treasury unless the Compliance Council determines via CCIP. Only in that case may the Compliance Council allocate those tokens to the TEL Treasury, where any use is governed through the public TELIP process.

The Compliance Council must publish and ratify these final policies through a CCIP within nine months of the commencement of the TEL upgrade. Because the first suggested checkpoint occurs at month 12, this means the final rules will be established, published, and in force before any unminted TEL is minted into reserve.

Risks and Mitigations  
A token upgrade of this scope carries real, ecosystem-wide impact. Each material risk below is paired with its mitigation.

Ecosystem-wide coordination. Every participant must act, including centralized exchanges, decentralized exchanges that will redeploy liquidity pools, wallet providers, and data services such as CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko. Mitigation: a dedicated coordination effort with early, direct outreach to every affected exchange, market maker, and infrastructure provider, ample lead time, a defined exchange contingency path, and supported TELx pools for liquidity providers to upgrade into.

Security. New token and upgrade contracts must meet the highest standard. Mitigation: rigorous third-party security assessments of all new contracts before deployment, with findings addressed and re-assessed as needed, funded as a defined line item in this proposal.

Market confusion during transition. Legacy TEL and upgraded TEL may trade separately for a period. Mitigation: clear deprecation of legacy TEL, the gray-versus-blue logo distinction, consistent identification of the upgraded token as the canonical TEL, and continuous communication. Some transitional confusion is possible, and the communications plan is built to minimize it.

Exchange non-cooperation. An exchange may be slow to support the upgrade. Mitigation: a published contingency path. Depending on the exchange, holders may withdraw legacy TEL to a self-custody wallet and upgrade directly through the official page.

Phishing. Upgrade events attract impersonation and fraudulent sites. Mitigation: official contract addresses published through multiple channels, prominent anti-phishing guidance, and clear instruction that holders verify addresses before approving any transaction and never trust unofficial links.

Adoption friction. Despite a chain-native, one-click upgrade, some holders will not act in the primary window. Mitigation: the 24-month extended window and the front-loaded recovery schedule are designed to protect genuine holders while still reaching ecosystem finality.

Rationale  
Strategic Alignment with Association Mission  
The Telcoin Association's mission is to align GSMA mobile network operators and a global user base around common blockchain infrastructure, with TEL and Telcoin Network as the blockchain and token standard for the telecommunications industry. A token standard cannot be a token the industry's exchanges, custodians, and protocols cannot integrate by default. This upgrade is the precondition for TEL to function as that standard. It is also the precondition for the network's economic model, since validator staking, liquidity mining, application-developer fees, and Treasury harvesting all depend on a standards-compliant, finely-divisible native token. The upgrade does not sit beside the mission. It is required to achieve it.

Proportional Equivalence Between Costs and Benefits  
The cost of this upgrade is a defined, one-time engineering and security investment plus a coordinated communications effort. The benefit is the permanent removal of the single largest structural constraint on TEL's market access, at the exact moment the network goes live. The integration surface expands from a constrained subset of the market to the entire EVM ecosystem. TEL gains structural on-chain demand as native gas. Cross-chain liquidity becomes clean and unified. Set against the eight years of foregone listings, integrations, and liquidity that the 2-decimal architecture has cost, and against the systemic risk of launching a global network on a legacy token, the investment is small and the return is asymmetric.

Risk and Reward Profile  
Holders are protected. Every position upgrades one for one. Balances do not change. The ticker does not change. No token is removed from any wallet. The upgrade is chain-native and one-click, with a twelve-month primary window and a 24-month total horizon.

The upside is unlocked. TEL gains the full EVM integration surface, native gas demand on its own Layer 1, and clean cross-chain liquidity, all of which compound with network adoption.

Principal is preserved, and recovered value returns to the community. The upgrade does not dilute holders or alter the economic supply. Recovered abandoned TEL returns to the community-governed Treasury, never to any company, and is allocated transparently through the TELIP process.

Feasibility  
The upgrade requires no unproven technology. CREATE3 deterministic deployment, mint and burn adapters, and LayerZero native bridging are established patterns. The team has evaluated and ruled out every non-upgrade alternative on security grounds. TEL has been upgraded cleanly once before. Execution is coordinated with mainnet readiness, exchange readiness, bridge readiness, and communications readiness, and the timeline is generous and telegraphed well in advance. If mainnet timing shifts, the Councils reassess the upgrade timeline accordingly, since the two are deliberately coordinated.

High-Level Phases  
Development  
Develop the upgraded TEL token contracts and the upgrade contracts for Ethereum, Polygon, and Base.

Security Assessment  
Engage third-party security researchers to review all new contracts. Address findings and re-assess as needed.

Deployment  
Deploy the upgraded TEL and the upgrade contracts across all target chains. Include upgraded TEL in Telcoin Network genesis configuration.

Ecosystem Coordination  
Notify and support exchanges, wallet providers, data services, and community members ahead of and throughout the upgrade.

Primary Window Opens  
Begin the twelve-month primary upgrade window. Monitor participation and provide ongoing support.

Extended Windows and Recovery  
Maintain extended upgrade opportunity through month 24, with the front-loaded recovery schedule returning abandoned legacy TEL to the community Treasury.

Completion  
After 24 months, conclude upgrade support. Recover abandoned liquidity from obsolete legacy pools, with proceeds to the community Treasury.

Costs  
165k USD for integration costs with exchanges  
250k-500k USD worth of TEL for trading liquidity (this is not lost - TA retains the value)  
120k USD for third-party security assessments  
Conclusion  
TEL was built for a network that did not exist yet. That network is now here, and this upgrade is TEL taking its native form: the standards-compliant, finely-divisible, cleanly-bridgeable token that powers its own Layer 1 and that the entire market can finally integrate without exception. The constraint that has quietly capped TEL for eight years comes off at the precise moment the network switches on, and the two events reinforce each other into a single, positive catalyst.

This is not a discretionary change, and it is not a defensive one. It is the foundation for everything the token standard is meant to do: to let GSMA operators validate and build, to let the four Miner Groups produce, earn, and govern, and to connect every mobile user to digital money through infrastructure the world's exchanges, custodians, and protocols can adopt by default. Approving this upgrade does not just fix a contract. It activates TEL as the native token of the telecommunications blockchain and opens the door to the on-chain TEL economy the network was designed to host.

title: [Treasury Management] - Cash Management for August 2026
body:
## Intro
This proposal relates to the management of our treasury's stablecoin income over August 2026.

## Description
Since our treasury regularly receives stablecoins (for example, from contributions), this vote is related to the way we're going to invest/use these stablecoins.

#### Currently, our treasury holds the following stablecoins
- 263.39 USDC on Venus ($263.39)
- 194.58 USDC on Aave ($194.58)
- 1.27 BUSD ($1.27)

**Totalling $459.24**

#### As well as the following RPTR-denominated assets
- 24,170,984.54 RPTR
- 999,779.00 RPTR in the RPTR-USDC pool

**Totalling 25,170,763.54 RPTR worth $1,015.18**

In addition to :
- 0.003965364349 WBETH worth $8.36 
- 0.0007899865202 Binance-Peg BTC worth $51.03 
- 0.01425228341 Stader BNBx worth $9.05
- 676.5300285 Klima kVCM worth $16.99

### **For a grand total of $1,559.86**

## Consequences
The stablecoins received by the Raptor Treasury over August 2026 will be used/invested following the results of this proposal :
- "Lend them on Venus" => we'll lend them on Venus
- "Lend them on Aave" => we'll lend them on Aave
- "Buy BTC" => we'll hold it as Binance-Peg BTC on BNB Chain
- "Stake ETH" => we'll buy WBETH on BNB Chain
- "Stake BNB" => we'll stake it through Stader
- "Stake SOL" => we'll stake SOL on Solana, then bridge the mSOL to the Treasury through Wormhole
- "Leave them here for now" => we'll leave them uninvested
- "Buy Toucan Protocol CHAR on Base" => We'll buy CHAR tokens on the secondary market on Base
- "Buy Klima Protocol kVCM on Base" => We'll buy kCVM on the secondary market on Base

Please note that this doesn't apply to the interests accruing on our Venus/Aave positions, since it would require scooping up the yield manually, and paying gas fees. Thus, we're going to let these compound over time.

Additionally, we won't claim the fees from the RPTR-USDC liquidity position every time, since it also requires gas fees, which might be counterproductive (e.g. if the gas fees exceed the claimable amount).

title: [Fast Track] [1IP-103] [Revote] Aqua Launch Framework: Aqua Interface Authorization, Protocol Fee Activation
body:
## Simple Summary

Degensoft requests authorization from 1inch DAO to deploy and launch Aqua and SwapVM and to operate the official Aqua interface for the 1inch Network; activates 100% of protocol fees, accruing to the DAO Treasury

## Abstract

Aqua and SwapVM are live at the protocol layer following the November 2025 developer release, and the DAO has approved the surrounding framework: the Aqua Revenue Stream Incubator \[1IP-93\] and the Aqua/SwapVM operational license confirmation under the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1 \[1IP-102\]. This proposal completes the launch by settling, in one governance action, the protocol's production deployment, who operates the user-facing layer, how protocol fees are handled, and how the DAO supports initial liquidity. The DAO’s liquidity incentive budget is deliberately kept out: it runs as a separate, standard-track proposal posted in parallel.

## Motivation

The DAO has funded Aqua's audits, confirmed its operational license, and incubates strategies on it, but no protocol fees currently accrue to the Treasury, and no official interface exists to bring it users. Meanwhile, operating a global non-custodial interface requires 24/7 coverage, incident command, and continuous iteration, responsibilities suited to a single accountable operator, as established in the dApp transfer proposal \[1IP-88\].

## Specification

### 1. Protocol Deployment & Interface Authorization

The 1inch DAO consents to and authorizes Degensoft Ltd (BVI) ("Degensoft") to deploy and launch the production Aqua and SwapVM protocol contracts, and to build, deploy, operate, and maintain the official Aqua interface of the 1inch Network, covering LP onboarding and position management, strategy discovery (including a listing track for Incubator strategies), virtual-balance management, analytics, and access to Aqua/SwapVM liquidity.

**Protocol deployment:** the DAO expressly consents to Degensoft deploying and launching the production Aqua and SwapVM contracts; deployments made under this consent are DAO-authorized deployments for the purposes of the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1 and DAO governance. The DAO gives this consent with knowledge of the DAO-funded audit program and of the inherent risks of smart-contract systems.

**Risk allocation:** this authorization allocates defined operational responsibilities to the operator, as set out below; it does not make Degensoft or any contributor a guarantor of protocol performance. The underlying protocols are source-available under the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1 and run as DAO-authorized deployments, and the interface is non-custodial: users retain full control over their keys and on-chain interactions. Protocol-level risks of DAO-authorized deployments are borne by participants, who acknowledge and assume such risks as set out in the Guidelines' risk disclosures (Sections 5.3.2 and 5.6.2), and nothing here limits the DAO's governance authority over the deployments.

The 1inch.com domain and the 1inch dApp belong to the 1inch Network. Under the network structure set out in the 1inch DAO Guidelines, operation and management of these assets rested with the 1inch Foundation, acting on behalf of the 1inch DAO; pursuant to the DAO's authorization in 1IP-88 and the transfer documentation executed by the Foundation, that role now rests with Degensoft. Degensoft holds and manages the domain and the dApp in this capacity, and operates the official Aqua interface of the 1inch Network under the same authorization. The interface will be hosted on the Network's domain (e.g. 1inch.com/aqua), and 1inch.network, the DAO's governance hub, will reference and link to it. Aqua operates under the 1inch brand as part of the broader 1inch ecosystem, and its users participate in the 1inch Network.

Degensoft's underlying right to build and operate Aqua front-ends already exists under the operational license confirmation \[1IP-102\]. This proposal designates the interface Degensoft operates as the official Aqua interface of the 1inch Network; it confirms status rather than granting new rights.

* The interface remains fully non-custodial; users retain control of keys and assets at all times.
* As operator, Degensoft is responsible for interface-level operations and risks, including terms of use, restricted-jurisdiction access controls, sanctions screening, user disclosures, and interface security.
* This authorization does not restrict third parties from building alternative Aqua interfaces under the existing license and ecosystem protections.

### 2. Protocol Fee Activation — Fees Accrue to the DAO Treasury

Acting within its authority over DAO-authorized deployments of Aqua and SwapVM, made available under the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1, the DAO activates protocol-level fees. In plain terms: every Aqua trade pays an LP fee, which goes to the maker whose liquidity filled it. The protocol fee is a slice of that existing fee, redirected to the DAO Treasury (converted to USDC on the way) — a quarter of it on low-fee pools, a sixth on high-fee pools. Worked example: a $10,000 trade in a 0.30% pool generates a $30 LP fee — $5 goes to the DAO, $25 stays with the maker; the same trade in a 0.05% pool generates $5 — $1.25 to the DAO, $3.75 to the maker.

| Parameter | Value |
|----|----|
| **Protocol fee** | A slice of the LP fee on each strategy, taken from the maker's earnings; taker quotes are unchanged. One quarter on low-fee tiers, one sixth on high-fee tiers, per the initial fee schedule below; custom fees are treated like the nearest standard tier. All parameters, including the tier boundary, are adjustable by governance. |
| **Beneficiary** | 1inch DAO Treasury — the DAO's main Treasury wallet (100% of collected protocol fees) |
| **Collection** | Routed on-chain to the DAO Treasury's main wallet (`eth:0x7951c7ef839e26F63DA87a42C9a87986507f1c07`) via the fee-collector configuration and the fee exchanger described below, published for review with contract addresses prior to activation. Later changes to fee parameters or collection routing require DAO governance approval. |
| **Conversion** | Collected fees are converted through a fee exchanger operated and supported by Degensoft as part of protocol operations, with an initial target composition of 100% USDC delivered to the Treasury's main wallet. The DAO may change the target composition at any time by governance signal to Degensoft, and Degensoft implements the updated composition promptly. Degensoft charges no service fee for operating the exchanger; ordinary market execution costs apply. |
| **Timing** | Firm activation gate: no protocol fees are collected before this proposal is approved. Upon approval, fees activate at, or promptly following, the production interface launch — whichever occurs later. Parameters remain reviewable by governance at any time, including adjustment or suspension for legal or operational reasons. |

**Initial fee schedule** — the protocol fee as a fraction of the LP fee:

| LP fee tier | Protocol share | Protocol fee (of trade amount) |
|----|----|----|
| 0.01% | 1/4 | 0.0025% |
| 0.05% | 1/4 | 0.0125% |
| 0.30% | 1/6 | 0.05% |
| 1.00% | 1/6 | \~0.1667% |
| Correlated presets (0.01% / 0.04% / 0.10% / 0.20%) | 1/4 · 1/4 · 1/4 · 1/6 | 0.0025% / 0.01% / 0.025% / \~0.03333% — per the same boundary rule; confirmed in the published fee schedule |
| Custom fees | 1/4 or 1/6 | Treated like the nearest standard tier. The dividing line sits at ≈0.1225% (the geometric midpoint of 0.05% and 0.30%): below it → 1/4, at or above → 1/6. One constant, retunable by governance. |

Three edge rules, stated plainly: a strategy with a zero LP fee pays no protocol fee; tiny derived values round up to the smallest unit the system can record; and right at the dividing line the absolute take steps down slightly (a 0.13% pool pays \~0.0217% versus 0.030% for a 0.12% pool) — a known property of any tiered rule, accepted by design. Exact encodings for all presets are pinned in the fee schedule published by the core team prior to activation.

**Boundaries:** the protocol fee is independent of (i) the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1 and any license fees thereunder, and (ii) the revenue-share obligations of Incubator teams to the DAO, both of which remain unchanged. Degensoft Ltd, as Licensor under the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1, acknowledges that protocol fee configuration on DAO-authorized deployments falls within the permitted operational use confirmed in \[1IP-102\].

**Execution:** to give the confirmed license arrangement contractual form, the DAO authorizes and directs the 1inch Foundation, as the DAO's off-chain representative, to execute the operational-use terms of the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1 with Degensoft Ltd, exercising the DAO's authority to direct the Foundation under the Guidelines (Section 4.3.2). This changes nothing in \[1IP-102\]: the license and the DAO's confirmed operational rights are unchanged — the Foundation's signature converts an on-chain confirmation into a bilaterally executed agreement, a clearer contractual bond for both sides.

**Foundation position:** the Foundation's directors have confirmed this in writing — by email to the proposer and in a published Foundation page linked from this proposal \[[link](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yjDqCno6zM00KBOfDSITo3SiRqvZUpTf/edit)\] — endorsing the framework as a whole (the interface authorization, the license execution, the fee activation, and the incentive program) as serving the interests of the 1inch Network. Consistent with its neutral role in day-to-day governance, the Foundation expresses its support through this written confirmation rather than by voting.

### 3. Interface & Protocol Development — Service Fee Framework (Separate Proposal)

Developing, maintaining, and servicing Aqua, SwapVM, and the official interface is ongoing work that Degensoft currently carries at its own cost. Compensation for that work is deliberately kept out of this proposal. Degensoft intends to bring a dedicated Development & Service Fee framework to the DAO as a separate proposal, so the launch decision and the operator's compensation are each judged on their own merits.

The follow-up proposal should define, at minimum: the scope of services and deliverables (protocol development, interface operations, security and incident response); term and renewal; budget and payment mechanics, including whether part of the compensation is denominated in 1INCH with vesting, to align long-term incentives and support token utility; reporting obligations; independent review of terms before the vote; and the DAO's rights to adjust or terminate the arrangement.

Sequencing matters. Before recurring service payments begin, the DAO should have its treasury and organizational structures in place, including operational finance groups and defined budget and reporting standards, so a standing service relationship can be administered, accounted for, and reviewed properly.

## Rationale

This framework gives the launch a clear structure and confirms existing contributor roles. The Network keeps its domain and dApp; production deployment proceeds under the DAO's express consent; a single accountable operator carries the interface and its operating obligations; protocol fees accrue to the DAO Treasury, where governance directs them to audits, development, security, and ecosystem programs. Keeping all spending on the standard track means this proposal changes rights and responsibilities, not balances — the money follows the full process.

## Considerations

### Security

The interface introduces no new smart contracts and interacts exclusively with Aqua/SwapVM deployments covered by the DAO-funded audit program, including the fee logic activated under Section 2. Later changes to fee parameters or collection routing require DAO governance approval; the fee exchanger and its target composition follow the same rule, with composition changes by governance signal as set out in Section 2. The interface is non-custodial throughout. Interface-layer security, including penetration testing, monitoring, and incident response, is Degensoft's responsibility as operator.

### Team Qualifications

Degensoft Ltd (BVI) is the developer of Aqua and SwapVM and operates the 1inch dApp for the 1inch Network — one of the most widely used non-custodial interfaces in DeFi.

### Legal & Risk Management

This proposal falls within the risk-review triggers in Guidelines Section 5.6.2 (a new product or feature with changes to the DAO's financial arrangements), and the independent review contemplated there is being completed before the temperature check. The interface is non-custodial, and Degensoft, as operator, is responsible for interface-level risk management, including terms of use, restricted-jurisdiction access controls, sanctions screening, and user disclosures.

Protocol fees accrue to the DAO Treasury as community resources allocated through governance. They are not distributions to tokenholders, and none are proposed. Fee parameters, collection routing, conversion composition, and activation status remain under DAO governance control at all times, including suspension for legal or operational reasons, and deployment of fee proceeds follows the DAO's treasury processes. The interface authorization confirms the official status of an interface Degensoft is already licensed to operate; it does not create new rights or transfer intellectual property. The express deployment consent records that production deployment occurs at the DAO's direction, with informed acceptance of the inherent risks of smart-contract systems disclosed in the Guidelines (Section 5.3.2, 5.6.1, 5.6.2); it allocates operational responsibility without making any party a guarantor of protocol performance. The Foundation's execution of the license terms on the Network's behalf follows the DAO's authority to direct the Foundation (Guidelines Section 4.3.2).

### Conflict of Interest

This proposal is submitted by a @daoplomats  who have received no compensation for authoring it. It was developed with technical input from the Degensoft team, disclosed here for transparency.

**Degensoft Ltd's interests:** it is the developer of Aqua and SwapVM, the Licensor under the Degensoft Aqua Source License 1.1, the deployer of the protocol and the operator of the official interface under Section 1, the administrator of the incentive program under Section 4, and the intended proposer of a future Development & Service Fee framework under Section 3.

**Mitigants:** all protocol fees accrue to the DAO Treasury, and fee parameters, collection routing, and the exchanger's target composition sit under exclusive DAO governance control; no Treasury funding for interface operations is requested here, and any future service fee will be a separate governance decision with independent review of terms; incentive funds flow to makers primarily through Merkl's claim mechanism, under a published methodology, Degensoft takes no compensation from that budget, and unspent funds return to the Treasury automatically; fee accrual to the Treasury is on-chain and independently verifiable; and Degensoft reports on the incentive program within 60 days of its end.

## Summary

This proposal sets the launch framework for Aqua in a single governance action: the DAO authorizes the production deployment of Aqua and SwapVM and recognizes the official Aqua interface, operated by Degensoft for the 1inch Network on the Network's own domain; protocol fees on Aqua and SwapVM are activated and accrue to the DAO Treasury under governance-controlled parameters; the operator's development and service compensation is deferred to a separate, properly structured proposal. Governance holds the protocol economics; the operator carries the interface and its obligations.

*Note: This proposal follows the fast-track governance process to align its approval with the upcoming public launch of Aqua, ensuring protocol fee activation is in place from day one of production availability. This proposal contains no Treasury spending and requires no on-chain execution; the DAO’s liquidity incentive budget is posted in parallel as a separate, standard-track proposal and takes effect only through that vote.*

title: Strategic Asset Empowerment and Ecosystem Value Protection / 战略资产赋能与生态价值护航
body:
Strategic Asset Empowerment and Ecosystem Value Protection 🚀

We are excited to announce the commencement of a new strategic journey regarding the "RBS Price Stabilization Mechanism" 🌟. To deeply empower the core interests of all consensus holders and ensure continuous, healthy ecosystem growth, we are actively optimizing our asset allocation strategies.

In the face of market volatility or external irrational challenges, we recognize that maintaining the stability of the secondary market is a critical component of our shared mission. Therefore, we propose the strategic allocation of a portion of idle capital from our substantial Treasury reserves, converting it into high-value "defensive liquidity" to be injected into the RBS Price Stabilization Mechanism. This is not merely a transfer of funds but a manifestation of our commitment to the long-term value of the ecosystem! 💪

Through this strategic initiative, we will construct a robust official liquidity reservoir. When the market faces downward pressure or concentrated sell-offs, the RBS algorithmic defense mechanism will automatically activate, executing intelligent buyback and accumulation strategies to effectively hedge risks and provide solid support for the price. This serves not only as protection for the market but also as a key driver for token price appreciation and deflationary feedback. 📈

🔥 Vision Scenario:
When facing systemic risks or panic-driven corrections, the RBS engine will respond instantly, utilizing strategic reserve funds to build a powerful buy-side defense line. This will rapidly stabilize the market, ensuring the asset security of all token holders and jointly resisting the impact of irrational crashes.

🗳 We invite everyone to exercise their governance rights (vIBS) to help shape our future:


✅ Approve: Fully support the strategic transfer of funds from the Treasury to inject into the RBS, initiating the price stabilization protection mechanism to co-create ecosystem prosperity!

❌ Reject: Maintain the status quo and temporarily refrain from fund allocation.

⚪️ Abstain

All allocations of defensive funds will be subject to strict auditing and on-chain public tracking via blockchain smart contracts, ensuring 100% transparency. Every contribution will be precisely utilized to defend ecosystem value and price stability. Let us join hands to move towards a new chapter that is more robust and holds greater growth potential! 🚀🤝

在面临市场波动或外部非理性挑战时，我们深知维护二级市场的稳健性是我们共同使命的关键一环。因此，我们提议从我们充足的国库（Treasury）储备中，战略性地调配部分闲置资本，将其转化为高价值的“防御性流动性”，注入 RBS 价格稳定机制。这不仅是资金的划转，更是我们对生态长远价值承诺的体现！💪
