title: Shiba ecosystem direction proposal
body:
This proposal asks the SHIB community to decide the fundamental direction of the Shiba ecosystem.
After reading a lot of "suggestions" 
The community must choose whether to:

Option A:  Preserve and Rebuild the Shiba Vision

Continue building the multi-token Shiba ecosystem in which SHIB, BONE, LEASH, TREAT and SHI each have separate purposes, beginning with launch of LEASH V2 (it is ready to be launched).

Option B Simplify and Consolidate the Ecosystem

Move away from the existing multi-token structure and develop a plan to consolidate BONE, LEASH, TREAT and other ecosystem functions into one unified token or governance asset alongside SHIB.

This proposal selects a direction and if there is any change **needed** in future then it will happen. 

Current Starting Position

Regardless of which option is selected, the community must proceed under the following assumptions and reality:

There is no access to an existing Shiba treasury. In case they did then it should be transferred here 0x8FF0A8B2229041eb098A5D59455D5DB803e475CE
There is no guaranteed transfer of funds or holdings from previous ecosystem controllers.
**There is no guaranteed liquidity available for LEASH V2 so whoever wants to add liquidity anyone is free to do so. **
There is no development budget. Any product will be created will have fees (should be explained why and where and how much, everything on chain transparent nothing hidden) as explained before. Any products that will be launched will be owned by me  currently since I do not not see any other proper solution for now and an action should be taken rather than waiting or doing nothing. **Some have reached but I repeat any developer is free to reach me out.**  Any product should be audited before launch. 
The community is effectively rebuilding from zero just how we started in shiba before.

Any development, liquidity or operational support must therefore come from transparent voluntary participation, new contributions, community builders or future revenue.



Option A Preserve and Rebuild the Original Shiba Vision

Under Option A, the community affirms that the Shiba ecosystem should continue as a collection of assets with distinct purposes.

The proposed structure would remain generally aligned with:

SHIB: The flagship ecosystem token.
BONE: N/A for now
LEASH V2: A rebuilt version of LEASH and same utility as before such as exclusivity for early access and store of value and govern over SHI. 
TREAT:  to be discussed later but a reward token with unlimited supply (producing more when it is needed only controlled by a known multisig and known people in community not random voted by DAO to be part of that multisig and same goes for the management of future treasury but this is early to happen at current stage). 
SHI: A future Shiba ecosystem stablecoin.
new chain: super far in future and very early to even think about now 
Keep in mind a lot of supply of current bone and treat is still controlled under shy and kaal and they keep dumping it until now even recently.  So future migration is highly possible especially TREAT at current stages.

You can imagine all tokens move as a flywheel that benefit each other directly or indirectly such as burns (not fan of but many do think it is a must) or buybacks or whatever through products what will be built or rebuilt **for example** shibaswap (I will not accept launching just a random useless swap, it should be unique or something that can compete with others in the market at least a lesser fee for swapping for example, this is just an example when a project or product will be built to benefit shiba). The best focus now is to launch products that give utility for shiba and generate revenue for it. It is a step by step and need a lot of patience.  

First Step: LEASH V2

If Option A is selected, LEASH V2 will be launched first rebuilding project. 
It will be same as original supply 107646.4693.
How it works? 
This contract is a non-rebasing wrapper for the original LEASH token. When you wrap your legacy LEASH, the contract locks your tokens and mints an equivalent amount of the new LEASH based on the legacy token's underlying gons accounting system. It is a separate ERC20 that can be traded anywhere just like any other token such as SHIB. Because the conversion is based on gons rather than the displayed token balance, your proportional ownership is preserved even if the legacy token rebases. 

The wrapped LEASH itself never rebases. Your wallet balance stays fixed, making it much easier to use with wallets, exchanges, and DeFi protocols that expect a standard ERC-20 token.

Example 1: If you wrap 100 legacy LEASH today, those 100 tokens are locked in the wrapper contract and you receive the equivalent amount of new LEASH. Your new LEASH balance remains constant, it will not automatically change because of future rebases from legacy LEASH.

Example 2: If the legacy LEASH supply later doubles due to a rebase or other supply change, your wrapped LEASH balance still stays exactly the same. If you decide to unwrap later, the contract calculates the redemption using the new current legacy supply, ensuring the conversion reflects the latest state of the underlying token.

You are free to move between the two versions whenever you choose. You can wrap legacy LEASH into the new token or unwrap back into the legacy token** at any time** for example because there is a better liquidity in legacy leash you can move there and sell at any moment or when you want to buy, provided the wrapper contract holds your deposited legacy LEASH. No one is forced to migrate, and no one is required to burn their legacy tokens. Wrapping is entirely optional and they can move on or back anytime they want and the contract will do the calculation by itself regardless if you move now or in the future you will not have any advanatge on anyone.

The contract is intentionally simple and has no owner, no admin controls, no transfer taxes, no blacklist, and no hidden mint function. The only way new wrapped LEASH can be created is by depositing legacy LEASH into the wrapper, and the only way wrapped LEASH is removed is when it is redeemed for the underlying legacy LEASH that was previously locked in the contract.

**Auditing (suggest which company) it can be funded by the community to this current address**
0x8FF0A8B2229041eb098A5D59455D5DB803e475CE
 
Benefits of Option A
Preserves the established Shiba ecosystem vision.
Gives existing ecosystem communities a possibility of continued utility.
Avoids abandoning the identities of the tokens.
Allows specialized tokens to support different ecosystem functions.
Provides a path to begin rebuilding through LEASH V2.

Risks of Option A
Multiple tokens may divide liquidity and attention.
Each token requires a credible purpose, developers and adoption.
Existing reputational problems may continue especially after the hacks and other previous histories. People should not expect refunds or any kind of that because it does not seem realistic at all if we are all being honest about it. 
New liquidity may be insufficient.
The ecosystem may become too complex and a burden. 

Option B: Simplify and Consolidate the Ecosystem

Under Option B, the community agrees that the existing multi-token structure should not be rebuilt in its current form.
In case B vote wins then
A later restructuring proposal would evaluate combining the intended functions, communities and possible obligations of BONE, LEASH, TREAT and related ecosystem assets into one unified token or governance asset. Which means there would be a direct forced burn migration except for SHIB since it is pure and no need to do anything with it. 

SHIB would remain the central Shiba token. The consolidated token could potentially provide governance, network incentives, access, ecosystem rewards or other functions 

The exact structure and supply % and how much, would require another discussion.

Benefits of Option B
Simplifies the ecosystem.
Concentrates development and community attention.
Reduces competition between ecosystem tokens.
May concentrate available liquidity.
Could provide one clear governance and utility structure.
Allows the community to redesign the ecosystem from zero.

Risks of Option B
Abandon the original Shiba ecosystem vision.
Could damage existing BONE, LEASH and TREAT holders who refuse to move.
Fair conversion ratios may be impossible to determine.
A new token could appear to be an unnecessary fundraising mechanism to many.
Consolidation cannot automatically eliminate existing liabilities.
Lack of treasury access would still remain.
Creating another token does not guarantee demand, liquidity or adoption.

title: Outsourcing of Development, Marketing, Support, and Cryptocurrency Management to BLUEBELT Co., Ltd
body:
## **DAO Resolution Proposal**  

**Background**  
To ensure the continued operation and development of the DAO’s services, the DAO proposes outsourcing certain technical, marketing, support, and cryptocurrency management functions to BLUEBELT Co., Ltd. as an independent service provider.  
This proposal is submitted for transparency and formal approval of the outsourcing arrangement and its applicable fee structure.

**Scope of Services**

1.  Development  
    Outsource to BLUEBELT Co., Ltd. the development, maintenance, testing, infrastructure management, security support, and other technical services required for the DAO’s products, platforms, systems, smart contracts, and related services.
    
2.  Marketing  
    Outsource to BLUEBELT Co., Ltd. the marketing and promotion of the DAO’s services, including cryptocurrency-, token-, blockchain-, and digital asset-related services.  
    Such activities shall be conducted in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and platform policies.
    
3.  Support  
    Outsource to BLUEBELT Co., Ltd. customer support, community support, technical support, and other operational support services relating to the DAO’s services.
    
4.  Cryptocurrency Management  
    Outsource to BLUEBELT Co., Ltd. the administrative and operational management of the DAO’s cryptocurrency holdings, including wallet administration, transaction execution, balance reconciliation, record keeping, and coordination with exchanges or other service providers.  
    BLUEBELT Co., Ltd. shall only execute transactions duly authorized under the DAO’s applicable governance and approval procedures and shall not acquire any ownership or beneficial interest in the DAO’s assets.
    

**Outsourcing Fees**  
The fees payable to BLUEBELT Co., Ltd. shall be calculated as follows:  
Actual and reasonable costs incurred in providing the outsourced services; plus  
A service fee equal to ten percent (10%) of such costs.  
No additional management fee, commission, markup, or other compensation shall be charged unless separately approved by the DAO.

**Cost Disclosure**  
BLUEBELT Co., Ltd. shall disclose the costs incurred in providing the outsourced services and provide reasonable supporting documents upon request.  
The disclosed costs may include personnel, contractors, development, infrastructure, marketing, support, professional services, transaction fees, and third-party vendor expenses.  
The DAO or its appointed accountants, auditors, or advisers may review and verify such costs and the calculation of the 10% service fee.

**Resolutions**  
The DAO hereby resolves:

-   To approve the outsourcing of development services to BLUEBELT Co., Ltd.
    
-   To approve the outsourcing of marketing services to BLUEBELT Co., Ltd., including marketing relating to cryptocurrency, tokens, blockchain technology, and digital assets.
    
-   To approve the outsourcing of customer, technical, community, and operational support services to BLUEBELT Co., Ltd.
    
-   To approve the outsourcing of administrative and operational cryptocurrency management services to BLUEBELT Co., Ltd., subject to the DAO’s applicable authorization procedures.
    
-   To approve outsourcing fees calculated at actual cost plus ten percent (10%).
    
-   To require BLUEBELT Co., Ltd. to disclose the underlying costs and provide reasonable supporting documentation.
    
-   To authorize the appropriate DAO representatives to negotiate, execute, and administer the relevant service agreement with BLUEBELT Co., Ltd.
    
-   To confirm that BLUEBELT Co., Ltd. shall not obtain any ownership, governance, voting, or beneficial interest in the DAO or its assets solely as a result of this outsourcing arrangement.
    

**Effective Date**  
This resolution shall become effective upon approval in accordance with the DAO’s applicable governance and voting procedures.  
Nothing in this resolution shall limit any claim arising from fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, unauthorized transactions, misappropriation of DAO assets, or material breach of the applicable service agreement.

title: Unlock Rules Adjustment: Revenue / Principal New Policy / 解锁 收益 / 本金 新政策
body:
🗳 Unlock Rules Adjustment: Revenue / Principal New Policy

📖 Proposal Background

As the POTS ecosystem continues to grow, in order to further enhance protocol stability, strengthen long-term liquidity, and align the unlocking mechanism more closely with the philosophy of long-term co-building, we are putting forward this DAO proposal.

This proposal adjusts the unlocking rules for revenue and principal, allowing long-term holders to enjoy lower unlocking costs while encouraging the community to remain engaged in the long-term development of the ecosystem.

POTS is committed to transparency, community governance, and DAO decision-making. Every key parameter is determined through community voting.

⸻

📋 Proposal Details

The unlocking adjustments for revenue and principal are as follows:

· Immediate unlock (0 days): 30%  
· Linear unlock over 30 days: 20%  
· Linear unlock over 60 days: 10%  
· Linear unlock over 90 days: 1%

Additionally, the unlocking rules are adjusted as follows: for members who have already applied for the 30-day linear unlock, the remaining unlock period will be automatically extended to 2× the original duration under the new mechanism.

⸻

🎯 Proposal Objectives

· Reduce unlocking costs for long-term holders.  
· Encourage longer lock-up periods and reduce short-term selling pressure.  
· Improve overall ecosystem capital stability.  
· Optimize the protocol model to support the long-term healthy development of the ecosystem.

⸻

✅ Voting Options

👍 YES: Approve the new unlock policy for revenue and principal.

👎 NO: Maintain the current unlock rules without changes.

—————————————-

🗳 解锁 收益 / 本金 新政策

📖 提案背景

随着 POTS 生态持续发展，为进一步提升协议稳定性、增强长期流动性，并让 解锁机制更加符合长期共建理念，现提出本次 DAO 提案。

本次提案将调整 收益 / 本金的解锁规则，让长期持有者享有更低的解锁成本，同时鼓励社区长期参与生态建设。

POTS 坚持公开透明、社区治理、DAO 决策，每一项重要参数都由社区共同投票决定。

⸻

📋 提案内容

解锁 收益 / 本金解锁调整如下：

· 0 天立即解锁：30%  
· 30 天线性解锁：20%  
· 60 天线性解锁：10%  
· 90 天线性解锁：1%

同时调整 解锁 规则，已經申請30天線性解鎖之會員，剩余天数將由原机制自动调整为 x 2 的时间。

⸻

🎯 提案目的

· 降低长期持有者的解锁成本。  
· 鼓励长期锁仓，减少短期卖压。  
· 提升生态资金稳定性。  
· 优化协议模型，促进生态长期健康发展。

⸻

✅ 投票选项

👍 YES：同意采用新的 解锁收益 / 本金政策。

👎 NO：维持现行 解锁规则不变。

title: (IDEATION) SCP219: Move rFOX to Mainnet
body:
SCP219: Move rFOX to Ethereum
Move rFOX from Arbitrum to Mainnet on October 1st. Most FOX already lives on Mainnet, so this puts the program where the tokens are. Rewards temporarily go from 25% to 50% of revenue for the first three months to get people to move quickly.
Abstract
rFOX is on Arbitrum today, so if you hold FOX on Mainnet you have to bridge before you can stake. Most people hold on Mainnet.
This deploys the same audited rFOX contract to Ethereum Mainnet, live October 1st. Stakers get 25% of DAO revenue in USDC and the 5% burn keeps running exactly as it does now. Arbitrum stops earning rewards that day, and the Arbitrum contract’s unstaking cooldown drops to 0 so nobody is stuck waiting to move.
For October 2026, November 2026, and December 2026, Mainnet rFOX pays 50% of revenue instead of 25%. It goes back to 25% automatically on January 1st.
Motivation
The biggest chunk of FOX is on Mainnet. Meeting FOX holders where they are currently. Also matches where the DAO is headed. We're consolidating liquidity and programs onto Mainnet, and our flagship revenue share program shouldn't be sitting on a different chain.
Engineering already audited the contract and is confident it ports over cleanly.
Specification
• Go live: October 1st, 2026. Mainnet only after that.
• Contract: Same audited rFOX contract, no functional changes.
• Boost: October, November, and December pay 50% of revenue. Back to 25% automatically on January 1st, 2027.
• Arbitrum: Cooldown drops to 0 days immediately so people can move. Rewards go to 0% once Mainnet is live. Anything accrued before then still gets paid.
Cost: The boost runs about $5,000/month, roughly $15,000 total, based on 2026 revenue. It moves with revenue since it's a percentage. Dropping the Arbitrum Snapshot voting strategy saves around $6,000/year per GK on an ongoing basis.
Benefits
• Puts rFOX where the most liquidity and FOX already is.
• Lines up with the DAO's move to simplify and conslidate
• Opens the program to every Mainnet holder who wouldn't bridge.
• Potential ongoing cost savings from not having to pay for advanced snapshot strategies of $6k/year
Drawbacks
• 27M FOX can unlock at once. Dropping the Arbitrum cooldown to 0 means a lot of FOX becomes available at the same time. If people sell instead of migrating to the new contract, there could be massive sell pressure.
• Mainnet gas is more expensive. Staking costs more than on Arbitrum, which hurts smaller stakers most.
• Three months of reduced treasury revenues. Roughly $15,000 in extra payouts.
• Some people won't move due to lack of paying attention. Anyone who misses it stops earning October 1st.
• There's a cliff in January for rewards, could trigger unstaking.
• This will require work on the Engineering side to launch contract, adjust revenue dashboards, and update the interface to include both contracts for withdrawing on the old one if a user is staked into it, and then also to bridge and stake into the new one.
Vote
For: Move rFOX to Ethereum Mainnet on October 1st, 2026, with a 28 day cooldown, 25% of revenue paid in USDC. This would get a temporary bump to 50% of revenue for October through December. Once mainnet contract is launched, a 0 day Arbitrum cooldown, and Arbitrum rewards ending at go live.
Against: rFOX stays on Arbitrum.
For, with changes: Please comment the changes you’d like to see.

title: Temporary Revenue Reallocation to Accelerate QuickSwap Protocol Expansion
body:
**The purpose of this proposal is to provide the QuickSwap Foundation with additional resources and operational flexibility to pursue an aggressive period of protocol expansion, product development, integrations, partnerships, and revenue growth.**

  
One of the primary areas of expansion will be QuickSwap’s new CLOB-based DEX and white-label exchange infrastructure, although the funding and authority provided under this proposal will support the broader growth of the QuickSwap protocol and ecosystem.

This proposal seeks DAO approval to temporarily adjust the distribution of QuickSwap’s protocol revenue from:

  
30% to the QuickSwap Foundation  
70% to the QuickSwap DAO  
to:

  
80% to the QuickSwap Foundation  
20% to the QuickSwap DAO

  
This temporary allocation would remain in effect for a period of 3 months from the date of implementation.  
Continue reading the entire proposal below for more details and information.

**Next Steps:**  
To begin, the governance discussion will run on the official Telegram and Discord community chats until Thursday, August 6 at 12:00 PM UTC  
Once the discussion finishes, a Snapshot vote will be initiated and run until Monday, August 10 at 12:00 PM UTC

  
Once you’ve read this entire blog post, make sure to visit the community chats to share your perspective with your fellow community members  
Motivation

  
QuickSwap is entering an important phase of growth.  
The protocol has an opportunity to expand beyond its existing AMM products, enter new markets, launch additional infrastructure, establish new partnerships, and develop products capable of generating meaningful new revenue streams.

  
To capitalize on these opportunities, QuickSwap must be able to move quickly and deploy resources aggressively.

  
The current 30% Foundation revenue allocation supports the protocol’s existing operations. However, it limits the Foundation’s ability to simultaneously maintain current products while funding significant expansion across development, business operations, infrastructure, marketing, liquidity, integrations, partnerships, and new product launches.

  
The proposed temporary allocation is intended to give the Foundation the resources required to accelerate the protocol’s growth rather than operating under a constrained maintenance-focused budget.

  
This is a temporary reinvestment of protocol revenue into QuickSwap’s expansion, with the objective of increasing the protocol’s long-term competitiveness, adoption, revenue, and value to the DAO and QUICK holders.

##   
**Protocol Expansion Strategy**

  
The additional revenue would be used to pursue a broad protocol expansion strategy.

  
This may include:  
Developing and launching new QuickSwap products.  
Expanding QuickSwap across additional chains and ecosystems.  
Pursuing integrations with wallets, protocols, exchanges, applications, and infrastructure providers.

  
Increasing business development and partnership activity.  
Strengthening QuickSwap’s engineering, operations, and contributor capacity.  
Expanding marketing, communications, and user-acquisition efforts.  
Supporting liquidity, incentives, and market-making arrangements.  
Funding smart contract development, security audits, infrastructure, and hosting.

  
Developing additional protocol revenue streams.  
Supporting legal, corporate, compliance, and operational requirements.  
Responding quickly to strategic opportunities that benefit the protocol.  
The Foundation would have discretion to allocate resources between these areas based on expected impact, urgency, cost, and the evolving needs of the protocol.

##   
**CLOB DEX and White-Label Expansion**

  
A major focus of the expansion strategy will be the development and commercialization of QuickSwap’s new central limit order book, or CLOB, decentralised exchange infrastructure.

  
The CLOB initiative is intended to expand QuickSwap’s product offering beyond traditional AMM-based trading and create infrastructure that may be deployed through both QuickSwap-branded and white-label exchange solutions.

-   This expansion may provide QuickSwap with opportunities to:  
    Enter new trading markets.
    
-   Offer more advanced trading functionality.
    
-   Serve projects, protocols, chains, and institutions seeking exchange infrastructure.
    
-   Launch customized or branded exchange deployments.
    
-   Generate revenue from trading, licensing, infrastructure, integrations, and commercial partnerships.
    
-   Expand QuickSwap’s presence across multiple blockchain ecosystems.  
    Strengthen QuickSwap’s position as a broader decentralized exchange and trading-infrastructure provider.
    

  
Launching and scaling this initiative will require meaningful investment across engineering, infrastructure, security, liquidity, business development, legal work, marketing, integrations, and commercial operations.

  
While the CLOB and white-label solution will be one of the main areas supported by this proposal, the temporary revenue increase is intended to fund the growth of the QuickSwap protocol as a whole.

##   
Temporary Revenue Allocation

  
For 3 months, applicable protocol revenue would be distributed as follows:  
Recipient  
Current Allocation  
  
QuickSwap Foundation  
30% QuickSwap Foundation  
70% QuickSwap DAO  
  
80% QuickSwap Foundation  
20% QuickSwap DAO

This proposal does not change the amount of protocol revenue generated or the mechanisms through which it is collected. It only temporarily changes how that revenue is distributed between the Foundation and the DAO.

##   
**Continued QUICK Buybacks**

  
The DAO’s temporary 20% share of protocol revenue will continue to be used for QUICK buybacks under the existing or applicable DAO-approved buyback process.

  
This means that QUICK buybacks will continue throughout the 3-month expansion period.

  
QUICK staking rewards will also continue unaffected by this vote.  
The proposal is therefore intended to balance two priorities:  
Directing the majority of short-term protocol revenue toward aggressive expansion and growth.

  
Continuing to return value to the QUICK ecosystem through ongoing buybacks funded by the DAO’s 20% revenue allocation.

## **  
Delegated Operational Authority**

  
To execute an aggressive expansion strategy effectively, the Foundation is also requesting delegated authority to make operational, commercial, and strategic decisions without requiring a separate governance proposal for each individual action.

  
This authority is intended to allow the Foundation to:  
Act quickly when opportunities arise.

-   Negotiate and enter into commercial arrangements.
    
-   Hire contributors, developers, contractors, advisors, and service providers.
    
-   Approve product-development and infrastructure expenditure.
    
-   Establish partnerships and integrations.
    
-   Negotiate confidential commercial terms.
    
-   Allocate resources between products and strategic initiatives.
    
-   Adjust priorities in response to market conditions, technical requirements, and business opportunities.
    
-   Take other reasonable actions intended to support QuickSwap’s growth and competitiveness.
    

  
This delegation is necessary because major product development and commercial expansion frequently require rapid decisions, confidential negotiations, and the ability to commit resources within commercially relevant timeframes.

  
Requiring individual governance approval for every operating decision, expense, integration, or partnership could materially slow execution and cause QuickSwap to lose opportunities to faster-moving competitors.

  
The delegated authority is intended to benefit the protocol and would apply only to decisions reasonably connected to QuickSwap’s operations, development, expansion, and commercialization.

##   
**Limitations**

  
This proposal does not authorize the Foundation to:

-   Permanently change the protocol revenue allocation.
    
-   Extend the temporary allocation beyond three months without further DAO approval.
    
-   Change the supply of QUICK.
    
-   Materially alter the governance rights of QUICK holders.  
    Transfer ownership or control of core DAO assets without appropriate authorization.
    
-   Make permanent changes to the DAO’s governance structure.  
    Use the DAO’s 20% revenue allocation for purposes other than the applicable DAO-approved process, including the continuation of QUICK buybacks or Treasury expansion.
    

  
Any action that would ordinarily require a specific DAO governance vote will continue to require DAO approval.

  
**Duration and Automatic Reversion**

  
The temporary allocation will apply for exactly 3 months from the date it is implemented.  
After the 3-month period, protocol revenue will automatically return to:  
30% to the QuickSwap Foundation  
70% to the QuickSwap DAO  
Any extension, renewal, or permanent change must be approved through a separate governance proposal.

##   
**Expected Benefits**

  
Approval of this proposal is expected to provide QuickSwap with:  
Greater capacity to fund protocol growth.  
Faster product development and execution.  
Increased ability to compete with rapidly expanding protocols.  
Greater flexibility when negotiating partnerships and integrations.  
The resources needed to develop and commercialize the CLOB and white-label solution.  
Increased engineering and operational capacity.  
Additional opportunities to expand onto new chains and into new markets.  
The potential to create meaningful new sources of protocol revenue.  
Continued QUICK buybacks during the temporary expansion period.  
Greater potential long-term value for the QuickSwap DAO and QUICK holders.  
Although the DAO will temporarily receive a smaller percentage of protocol revenue, it will continue receiving 20%, which will support ongoing QUICK buybacks.  
The broader objective is to aggressively reinvest protocol revenue into initiatives that can increase QuickSwap’s future revenue, market presence, product offering, and long-term value.  
Risks and Mitigations  
Temporary Reduction in DAO Revenue  
The DAO’s revenue share will temporarily decrease from 70% to 20%.  
This is mitigated by the limited 3-month duration, the automatic reversion to the existing allocation, and the continuation of QUICK buybacks using the DAO’s 20% share.  
Increased Foundation Discretion  
The Foundation will have greater authority to allocate resources and make operational decisions.  
This is necessary to support faster execution and is mitigated by the temporary duration, the defined purpose of protocol expansion, the stated limitations, and the commitment to provide a high-level report.  
Execution Risk  
Not every investment, product, partnership, or expansion initiative will necessarily produce immediate results.  
However, maintaining the existing allocation may limit QuickSwap’s ability to pursue growth opportunities and compete effectively. The Foundation believes that the potential long-term benefits justify a temporary period of increased investment.

##   
**Implementation**

  
If approved, the relevant contracts, wallets, multisig instructions, payment processes, or revenue-distribution mechanisms will be updated so that:

  
The QuickSwap Foundation receives 80% of applicable protocol revenue.  
The QuickSwap DAO receives 20% of applicable protocol revenue.  
The DAO’s 20% allocation continues to support QUICK buybacks.  
The temporary allocation begins as soon as reasonably practicable following approval.  
The revenue allocation automatically returns to 30% Foundation and 70% DAO after three months.  
The Foundation, DAO contributors, relevant multisig signers, and technical service providers are authorized to take the administrative and technical actions reasonably required to implement this proposal.

##   
**Voting Options**

  
For: Approve the temporary three-month allocation of 80% of protocol revenue to the QuickSwap Foundation and 20% to the QuickSwap DAO, with the DAO allocation continuing to support QUICK buybacks, together with the delegated authority required to accelerate QuickSwap’s protocol expansion.

  
Against: Retain the current allocation of 30% to the QuickSwap Foundation and 70% to the QuickSwap DAO.

title: Should DAO Council members have term limits ?
body:
> by 0x247e0896706bb09245549e476257a0a1129db418 (DCLCars)

**What is this poll about?**

The DAO Council has important responsibilities. It oversees the Executive Arm, approves plans and budgets, and helps guide the DAO.

The current rules explain how Council members are elected and removed, but they do not say how long a member can stay in the role. This means Council members do not need to face a new election after a fixed period.

This poll asks the community if we should change that.

**Suggested term limits**

My suggested starting point is:

*   One term lasts **2 years**.
*   A member can serve a maximum of **2 terms in a row**.
*   After 2 terms, the member must take a **2-year break** before running again.
*   How current members move into the new system should be discussed in the next step.
*   Council members can still resign or be removed early through the existing DAO process.

**Why set term limits ?**

Term limits would give the community a regular chance to review Council members and choose who should represent the DAO.

They could also:

*   stop the same people from staying in power for too long;
*   create more chances for new candidates and new ideas;
*   make Council members ask the community for support again; and
*   keep useful experience, because a member could still serve for up to 4 years in a row.

This poll is **not binding**. Its purpose is to understand what the community wants. If the community supports term limits, a later Draft Proposal can work out the details, including the rules for current members. ***The rules would change only if a final binding Governance Proposal also passes.***

**Context**

*   [Proposal that created the DAO Council](https://decentraland.org/governance/proposal/?id=3a499895-35c7-45fe-ac9e-918e3248fc7b)
*   [Decentraland DAO User Guide](https://docs.decentraland.org/dao/dao-userguide)

**VOTING OPTIONS**

1.  **Yes — 2 year terms, maximum 2 terms in a row, then a 2-year break.**
2.  **Yes — but I prefer different term limits(COMMENT).**
3.  **No — DAO Council members should not have term limits.**
4.  **Abstain / I need more information.**

- 1. Yes — 2 year terms, maximum 2 terms in a row, then a 2-year break
- 2. Yes — but I prefer different term limits(COMMENT)
- 3. No — DAO Council members should not have term limits
- 4. Abstain / I need more information
- Invalid question/options


**[This proposal is summarized due to technical limitations. To view it complete and vote on it, visit the DCL DAO Governance dApp](https://decentraland.org/governance/proposal/?id=de9c27e4-976b-4412-97a5-b94bb1f9e15e)**
choices: 1. Yes — 2 year terms, maximum 2 terms in a row, then a 2-year break
2. Yes — but I prefer different term limits(COMMENT)

title: Transition to an Independent Structural Governance Engine and Complete Separation of Powers
body:
This proposal outlines a structural overhaul of GnosisDAO governance to eliminate the systemic liabilities associated with centralized concentration of voting power (de facto GbR partnership liability) under the fully enforced Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulatory environment.

We propose the complete separation of powers via a Lean Leadership Service Provider (Executive) and a 5-Seat Independent Supervisory Board. To protect the integrity of the network from insider dominance and regulatory perimeter failures, the activation of this model is strictly bound to programmatic, data-driven decentralization triggers that completely disqualify concentrated, hostile voting blocks and collusive cartel formations.

1. Structural Architecture
To establish a resilient and compliant organization, the current monolithic and founder-dominated execution model will be unbundled into two distinct bodies:

A. The Leadership Service Provider (The Executive / CEO Role)
Mandate: Manages daily technical roadmaps, platform-level integration pipelines, and ecosystem coordination.

Limitation: Holds zero administrative control over treasury keys or arbitrary spending. Operates purely on an explicit, milestone-bound contract.

Execution Pathway: The ultimate structural objective is to transition from human-managed intermediate steps to a (semi-)automated on-chain enforcement module. While the strict architectural parameters, safety sandboxes, and rollouts of this automated system will be defined in the Operational Framework and Risk-Control Charter, the constitution formally commits to binding this execution pathway programmatically.

B. The Independent Supervisory Board
Structure: Consists of five (5) distinct seats held by independent companies or industry experts elected by the community.

The Independence Mandate: No elected board member may have a current or historic structural, financial, or personal relationship with the Leadership Service Provider, core venture arms, or affiliated insider foundations (no overlapping cap tables, shared multi-sigs, or proxy entities).

Role: Acts as the strategic circuit breaker. The board is responsible for vetting asset-acquisition due diligence, reviewing technical audits, verifying portfolio user metrics, and holding veto power over treasury outlays.

Execution Pathway: Mirroring the Executive mandate, the ultimate structural objective of the Board is to transition its oversight from manual human review to programmatic, trustless verification. The goal is to eventually replace human multisig latency with automated circuit breakers, utilizing smart contract risk guards, zero-knowledge proofs for metrics verification, and algorithmic vetoes triggered by on-chain telemetry. The specific parameters and safe transition into this (semi-)automated oversight model will be rigorously defined in the Charter.

Cycle: Appointed via token vote for a fixed 4-year cycle.

2. Mandatory Framework Pre-Requisite
To prevent capital misallocation and the extraction of treasury funds before operational boundaries are established, a strict provision is mandated:

Zero-Funding Clause: Neither the elected Leadership Service Provider nor the Independent Supervisory Board shall receive any compensation, operational funding, or treasury streaming until they have co-defined, published, and passed a secondary, binding community vote on the Operational Framework and Risk-Control Charter.

3. MiCA-Aligned Decentralization Trigger & Hostile Block Disqualification
To ensure the validity of this model and protect participants from joint and several liability under regional civil partnership laws (e.g. GbR), the activation of this governance structure is bound to objective distribution metrics.

While European frameworks (MiCA) do not define an absolute binary percentage for “full decentralization”, regulatory multi-factor assessments look directly at structural concentration of control, administrative key dominance, and voting asymmetry. A concentration exceeding 10% by a single actor represents a definitive failure of decentralization, while a 5% threshold defines the absolute boundary for an individual operator.

To enforce this reality, the governance engine will apply a strict programmatic rule on active voting weight:

The 5% Anti-Dominance Threshold: The maximum permissible voting weight allocated to any single entity, natural person, corporate organization, or coordinated cluster of addresses is strictly capped below 5% of the total active votes cast in any specific governance action.

Total Hostile Vote Invalidated: If an entity, founder wallet, or coordinated proxy cluster deploys a block of tokens representing 5% or more of the total active votes cast, their entire vote is classified as a hostile centralization action and is rendered completely invalid. The aggregation layer will programmatically drop their voting weight to 0%.

4. Anti-Collusion Rules: Disqualifying Cartel Formations
To prevent the subversion of the 5% threshold through backroom deals, private alliances, or hidden corporate coordination, strict anti-cartel provisions are woven into the aggregation layer.

The Collective 5% Cartel Cap: If multiple distinct addresses or entities exhibit sufficient evidence of coordinated voting alignment, including but not limited to: parallel voting history, shared funding origins, overlapping venture cap tables, off-chain execution pacts, or documented backroom agreements, the entire cluster will be legally and programmatically treated as a single unified Cartel Entity.

Hostile Disqualification for Collusion: If the aggregate voting weight of an identified cartel reaches or exceeds the 5% threshold, the entire group’s votes are deemed hostile and invalidated (dropped to 0%).

Shifting the Game Theory: By penalizing collusion while permitting distributed, independent voting, the system fundamentally changes the game theory of the DAO. It dismantles the traditional Web3 paradigm of raw capital accumulation and forces a battle of open information distribution. Actors are structurally disincentivized from building secret cartels, as doing so explicitly strips them of their governance power. To pass initiatives, they must instead openly coordinate, persuade, and distribute information to the wider, decentralized community.

The Anti-Accumulation Forcing Function: Because accumulating or centralizing tokens past the 5% limit results in the total destruction of voting power rather than a simple haircut, concentrated insiders are stripped of their ability to dictate terms. This structures a powerful economic incentive forcing them to distribute and sell down their massive blocks into the open market, naturally flattening the token topology.

5. Systemic Exclusion of Opaque Intermediaries & Identity Standards
Recognizing that delegated voting structures and off-chain execution environments present severe compliance vectors and personal liability risks under MiCA, GnosisDAO establishes a clear boundary on identity and network transit:

Direct Key Validation: Votes must be cast directly by the sovereign key holders. Any address cluster identified as operating a centralized proxy or acting as a de facto organizational delegate block will be evaluated as a single collective entity and subject to the 5% hostile block disqualification.

The Identity and Infrastructure Reality: While emerging on-chain agent standards (such as ERC-8004 or ERC-8217) offer elegant cryptographic verification of identity, GnosisDAO recognizes that on-chain records remain functionally centralized if the underlying peering, DNS, and physical routing layers are centralized. If network gateways or RPC endpoints can be administratively gated, the trustless nature of the identity collapses.

The Physical Layer Mandate: To achieve true censorship resistance, the DAO’s long-term roadmap must address the physical transit layer, including motivating the community toward establishing direct p2p fiber peering and sovereign communications. Therefore, the strategic transition from on-chain identity abstractions to physical-layer network resilience is formally designated as a core pillar to be researched and executed within the Charter.

6. Election Safeguard Framework
The 80% Verification Benchmark: The formal election process for the Leadership Service Provider and the Independent Board seats may only begin once a data-driven audit confirms that the token and voting weight distribution is at least 80% of the way toward the target decentralization standard (i.e. insider dominance is effectively neutralized and floating supply distribution is sufficiently flat).

The Active Snapshot Kill-Switch: If, during the open governance voting process or Snapshot period, a concentrated entity or cartel attempts to swing the outcome, thereby dropping the distribution metrics below the 80% threshold, the entire election process must be instantly halted and invalidated.

System Freeze: The governance process will remain frozen until the raw distribution data naturally corrects or steps are taken to adjust the voting rails programmatically.

title: TGIP2: Recording the Upgraded TEL Contract in the Telcoin Association Constitution
body:
## Abstract

This TGIP proposes a single amendment to the Preamble of the Telcoin Association Constitution, replacing the legacy TEL contract address `0x467Bccd9d29f223BcE8043b84E8C8B282827790F` with the upgraded TEL contract at `0x7E13B43065380aCdeC1c2d138c579cbBbafA0731`, so that the founding document of the Association names the token the Telcoin Platform actually runs on. It is the constitutional-choice instrument contemplated by [TELIP16: The TEL Token Upgrade](https://forum.telcoin.org/t/telip-the-tel-token-upgrade/847), which was affirmed by the Platform and Treasury Councils. It is the only part of that upgrade which no Council may decide. Amending these Statutes is an inalienable power of the Miner Assembly under Article 12.1. The amendment is limited to the identification of TEL and changes nothing else: not the total supply of 100,000,000,000 TEL, not any Miner's staked balance or voting power, not the upgrade window, and not the recovery schedule, each of which is governed by its own process. Voting opens Thursday 6 August at 22:30 UTC, 17:30 CDT and closes Thursday 13 August at 22:30 UTC, 17:30 CDT, simultaneously in all four Miner Group Snapshot spaces, and requires 80% approval and a 20% quorum in each of them.



---

## Motivation

The Preamble of our Constitution does something unusual for a founding document. It identifies the native resource unit of the Telcoin Platform not by name but by contract address:



**WHEREAS,** TEL, an ERC-20 token on the Ethereum Network at contract 0x467Bccd9d29f223BcE8043b84E8C8B282827790F, "TEL", is the native resource unit created, stored, and generated as flows by the Telcoin Platform, and



That was the correct choice in August 2023 and it remains the correct choice now. A common property system needs to be exact about the resource it governs. Every rule that follows in these Statutes, and every collective-choice and operational rule the Councils have made underneath them, refers back to TEL as the Preamble defines it. When Article 14 provides that Members vote via their staked TEL tokens, with one TEL equaling one vote, the TEL it means is the one named in the Preamble. The same is true of harvesting, of issuance from the TEL Treasury, and of the pro-rata share that determines each Miner's political power within their Miner Group.



The consequence is that the identity of TEL is a constitutional question and not a technical one. Upon implementation of **TELIP16: The TEL Token Upgrade**, the upgraded, 18-decimal TEL becomes the canonical TEL of the Telcoin Platform, deployed at a single deterministic address across Ethereum, Polygon, Base, and Telcoin Network. If the Preamble is left as it stands, our founding document will name a contract that the Platform no longer runs on, and every downstream rule will inherit that ambiguity.



This is an exciting moment for the Association, and it is worth being clear about why. The Councils have decided, within their mandates, that the upgrade happens. They cannot decide what the Constitution says TEL is. Under Article 12, the General Assembly, which is to say the Miner Assembly composed of all Members, retains the adoption and amendment of these Statutes as an inalienable power that cannot be delegated to the Board or to any Council. *The Councils authorize the upgrade; the Miner Assembly alone determines the constitutional identity of TEL.* In other words, this is the part of the TEL token upgrade that belongs to all of us collectively, and it is the second TGIP in the history of the Association, following [TGIP1: Establishing the Telcoin Platform and Association](https://forum.telcoin.org/t/tgip1-establishing-the-telcoin-platform-and-association/135) in December 2023.



---

## Specification

### 1. Amendment to the Preamble

The second WHEREAS clause of the Preamble to the Statutes of Telcoin is deleted in its entirety and replaced with the following:



**WHEREAS,** TEL, an ERC-20 token deployed at contract `0x7E13B43065380aCdeC1c2d138c579cbBbafA0731` on the Ethereum Network, the Polygon Network, and the Base Network, and existing as the native token of Telcoin Network, "TEL", is the native resource unit created, stored, and generated as flows by the Telcoin Platform, and



No other provision of the Statutes is amended, and no other clause of the Preamble is altered.

### 2. Legacy TEL

The token deployed at 0x467Bccd9d29f223BcE8043b84E8C8B282827790F on the Ethereum Network, and its corresponding legacy deployments on other networks, are hereafter referred to as "legacy TEL". Legacy TEL is not the native resource unit of the Telcoin Platform for the purposes of these Statutes from the date this amendment takes effect. Holders of legacy TEL retain the right to upgrade their holdings 1:1 through the official upgrade contracts on the terms set out in **TELIP16: The TEL Token Upgrade** and in the policies to be established by the Compliance Council through the [TIP process](https://www.telcoin.org/documentation/association-governance/association-rules/collective-choice-rules/miner-council-decision-making-rules/telcoin-improvement-proposal-tip-rules).

### 3. Condition precedent and effective date

The upgraded TEL contract is deployed at `0x7E13B43065380aCdeC1c2d138c579cbBbafA0731` on the Ethereum Network, the Polygon Network, and the Base Network, with its source verified on each network's block explorer..

### 4. Scope limitation

For the avoidance of doubt, this TGIP does not authorize, modify, ratify, or extend any of the following, each of which is decided through its own process and on its own record:



* The authorization of the TEL token upgrade itself, which is decided by TELIP16 through the Platform Council, the Treasury Council, and the Compliance Council guard.



* The duration of the primary or extended upgrade windows.



* The schedule for the recovery of abandoned legacy tokens to the TEL Treasury, which TELIP16 assigns to the Compliance Council to implement through a TIP.



* Any rule concerning staking, harvesting, issuance, or the composition of any Miner Council.



---

## Rationale

**The Preamble should name the token the Platform runs on.** This is the whole of the proposal. A constitution that identifies its resource unit by an address which no longer carries that resource unit is a document that has to be read against a footnote, and a common property system whose members must consult a footnote to know what they are governing is weaker for it.



**A conditional effective date protects the Miner Assembly from voting on an outcome.** Members are not being asked to trust that a suitable contract will exist. They are being asked to ratify a specific, pre-computable address, with the amendment taking effect only if that exact address is what is deployed. This is the same discipline the Association applies elsewhere in tying constitutional-choice decisions to verifiable facts rather than to intentions.

title: TGIP2: Recording the Upgraded TEL Contract in the Telcoin Association Constitution
body:
## Abstract

This TGIP proposes a single amendment to the Preamble of the Telcoin Association Constitution, replacing the legacy TEL contract address `0x467Bccd9d29f223BcE8043b84E8C8B282827790F` with the upgraded TEL contract at `0x7E13B43065380aCdeC1c2d138c579cbBbafA0731`, so that the founding document of the Association names the token the Telcoin Platform actually runs on. It is the constitutional-choice instrument contemplated by [TELIP16: The TEL Token Upgrade](https://forum.telcoin.org/t/telip-the-tel-token-upgrade/847), which was affirmed by the Platform and Treasury Councils. It is the only part of that upgrade which no Council may decide. Amending these Statutes is an inalienable power of the Miner Assembly under Article 12.1. The amendment is limited to the identification of TEL and changes nothing else: not the total supply of 100,000,000,000 TEL, not any Miner's staked balance or voting power, not the upgrade window, and not the recovery schedule, each of which is governed by its own process. Voting opens Thursday 6 August at 22:30 UTC, 17:30 CDT and closes Thursday 13 August at 22:30 UTC, 17:30 CDT, simultaneously in all four Miner Group Snapshot spaces, and requires 80% approval and a 20% quorum in each of them.



---

## Motivation

The Preamble of our Constitution does something unusual for a founding document. It identifies the native resource unit of the Telcoin Platform not by name but by contract address:



**WHEREAS,** TEL, an ERC-20 token on the Ethereum Network at contract 0x467Bccd9d29f223BcE8043b84E8C8B282827790F, "TEL", is the native resource unit created, stored, and generated as flows by the Telcoin Platform, and



That was the correct choice in August 2023 and it remains the correct choice now. A common property system needs to be exact about the resource it governs. Every rule that follows in these Statutes, and every collective-choice and operational rule the Councils have made underneath them, refers back to TEL as the Preamble defines it. When Article 14 provides that Members vote via their staked TEL tokens, with one TEL equaling one vote, the TEL it means is the one named in the Preamble. The same is true of harvesting, of issuance from the TEL Treasury, and of the pro-rata share that determines each Miner's political power within their Miner Group.



The consequence is that the identity of TEL is a constitutional question and not a technical one. Upon implementation of **TELIP16: The TEL Token Upgrade**, the upgraded, 18-decimal TEL becomes the canonical TEL of the Telcoin Platform, deployed at a single deterministic address across Ethereum, Polygon, Base, and Telcoin Network. If the Preamble is left as it stands, our founding document will name a contract that the Platform no longer runs on, and every downstream rule will inherit that ambiguity.



This is an exciting moment for the Association, and it is worth being clear about why. The Councils have decided, within their mandates, that the upgrade happens. They cannot decide what the Constitution says TEL is. Under Article 12, the General Assembly, which is to say the Miner Assembly composed of all Members, retains the adoption and amendment of these Statutes as an inalienable power that cannot be delegated to the Board or to any Council. *The Councils authorize the upgrade; the Miner Assembly alone determines the constitutional identity of TEL.* In other words, this is the part of the TEL token upgrade that belongs to all of us collectively, and it is the second TGIP in the history of the Association, following [TGIP1: Establishing the Telcoin Platform and Association](https://forum.telcoin.org/t/tgip1-establishing-the-telcoin-platform-and-association/135) in December 2023.



---

## Specification

### 1. Amendment to the Preamble

The second WHEREAS clause of the Preamble to the Statutes of Telcoin is deleted in its entirety and replaced with the following:



**WHEREAS,** TEL, an ERC-20 token deployed at contract `0x7E13B43065380aCdeC1c2d138c579cbBbafA0731` on the Ethereum Network, the Polygon Network, and the Base Network, and existing as the native token of Telcoin Network, "TEL", is the native resource unit created, stored, and generated as flows by the Telcoin Platform, and



No other provision of the Statutes is amended, and no other clause of the Preamble is altered.

### 2. Legacy TEL

The token deployed at 0x467Bccd9d29f223BcE8043b84E8C8B282827790F on the Ethereum Network, and its corresponding legacy deployments on other networks, are hereafter referred to as "legacy TEL". Legacy TEL is not the native resource unit of the Telcoin Platform for the purposes of these Statutes from the date this amendment takes effect. Holders of legacy TEL retain the right to upgrade their holdings 1:1 through the official upgrade contracts on the terms set out in **TELIP16: The TEL Token Upgrade** and in the policies to be established by the Compliance Council through the [TIP process](https://www.telcoin.org/documentation/association-governance/association-rules/collective-choice-rules/miner-council-decision-making-rules/telcoin-improvement-proposal-tip-rules).

### 3. Condition precedent and effective date

The upgraded TEL contract is deployed at `0x7E13B43065380aCdeC1c2d138c579cbBbafA0731` on the Ethereum Network, the Polygon Network, and the Base Network, with its source verified on each network's block explorer..

### 4. Scope limitation

For the avoidance of doubt, this TGIP does not authorize, modify, ratify, or extend any of the following, each of which is decided through its own process and on its own record:



* The authorization of the TEL token upgrade itself, which is decided by TELIP16 through the Platform Council, the Treasury Council, and the Compliance Council guard.



* The duration of the primary or extended upgrade windows.



* The schedule for the recovery of abandoned legacy tokens to the TEL Treasury, which TELIP16 assigns to the Compliance Council to implement through a TIP.



* Any rule concerning staking, harvesting, issuance, or the composition of any Miner Council.



---

## Rationale

**The Preamble should name the token the Platform runs on.** This is the whole of the proposal. A constitution that identifies its resource unit by an address which no longer carries that resource unit is a document that has to be read against a footnote, and a common property system whose members must consult a footnote to know what they are governing is weaker for it.



**A conditional effective date protects the Miner Assembly from voting on an outcome.** Members are not being asked to trust that a suitable contract will exist. 3. Coordinate with the TAN Council and the TELx Council on the updates to staking, issuance, and liquidity contracts that reference the TEL contract address, each through that Council's own decision-making process.

**WHEREAS,** TEL, an ERC-20 token deployed at contract `0x7E13B43065380aCdeC1c2d138c579cbBbafA0731` on the Ethereum Network, the Polygon Network, and the Base Network, and existing as the native token of Telcoin Network, "TEL", is the native resource unit created, stored, and generated as flows by the Telcoin Platform, and



No other provision of the Statutes is amended, and no other clause of the Preamble is altered.

### 2. Legacy TEL

The token deployed at 0x467Bccd9d29f223BcE8043b84E8C8B282827790F on the Ethereum Network, and its corresponding legacy deployments on other networks, are hereafter referred to as "legacy TEL". Legacy TEL is not the native resource unit of the Telcoin Platform for the purposes of these Statutes from the date this amendment takes effect. Holders of legacy TEL retain the right to upgrade their holdings 1:1 through the official upgrade contracts on the terms set out in **TELIP16: The TEL Token Upgrade** and in the policies to be established by the Compliance Council through the [TIP process](https://www.telcoin.org/documentation/association-governance/association-rules/collective-choice-rules/miner-council-decision-making-rules/telcoin-improvement-proposal-tip-rules).

### 3. Condition precedent and effective date

The upgraded TEL contract is deployed at `0x7E13B43065380aCdeC1c2d138c579cbBbafA0731` on the Ethereum Network, the Polygon Network, and the Base Network, with its source verified on each network's block explorer..

### 4. Scope limitation

For the avoidance of doubt, this TGIP does not authorize, modify, ratify, or extend any of the following, each of which is decided through its own process and on its own record:



* The authorization of the TEL token upgrade itself, which is decided by TELIP16 through the Platform Council, the Treasury Council, and the Compliance Council guard.



* The duration of the primary or extended upgrade windows.



* The schedule for the recovery of abandoned legacy tokens to the TEL Treasury, which TELIP16 assigns to the Compliance Council to implement through a TIP.



* Any rule concerning staking, harvesting, issuance, or the composition of any Miner Council.



---

## Rationale

**The Preamble should name the token the Platform runs on.** This is the whole of the proposal. A constitution that identifies its resource unit by an address which no longer carries that resource unit is a document that has to be read against a footnote, and a common property system whose members must consult a footnote to know what they are governing is weaker for it.



**A conditional effective date protects the Miner Assembly from voting on an outcome.** Members are not being asked to trust that a suitable contract will exist. They are being asked to ratify a specific, pre-computable address, with the amendment taking effect only if that exact address is what is deployed. This is the same discipline the Association applies elsewhere in tying constitutional-choice decisions to verifiable facts rather than to intentions.



**Voting power is unaffected by this proposal.** Eligibility and voting power for this TGIP are captured at the Snapshot block when the proposal opens, and are measured on staked legacy TEL and staked TELx Liquidity Provider Tokens as they exist at that moment, exactly as in every previous Association vote. No Member needs to upgrade any token to vote on this proposal, and no Member's pro-rata share within their Miner Group is changed by it.



---

## Implementation

Upon ratification by all four Miner Groups, and upon the condition in Section 3 being satisfied, the TAO will:



1. Publish the amended Statutes of Telcoin, incorporating the Preamble amendment, at [telcoin.org](https://www.telcoin.org/documentation/telcoin-association/telcoin-association-constitution) and as an updated PDF at the canonical Constitution URL, together with a redline against the version adopted under TGIP1.



2. Record the ratification, the four Snapshot results, and the deployment verification in the Association's minutes as required by Article 14, and file or register the amended Statutes as required of a Swiss Verein domiciled in the Canton of Ticino (City of Lugano).


3. Coordinate with the TAN Council and the TELx Council on the updates to staking, issuance, and liquidity contracts that reference the TEL contract address, each through that Council's own decision-making process.



4. Post the result to the Telcoin Association Discord and to this forum, and update the TGIP documentation on telcoin.org, as required by the TGIP Rules.



The implementing body is the TAO in every case. No step in this implementation is assigned to any individual.



---

## Voting

Each Miner Group votes on this identical proposal in its own Snapshot space, simultaneously, over 168 hours.

* **Voting Opens:** Thursday 6 August at 22:30 UTC (17:30 CDT)



* **Voting Closes:** Thursday 13 August at 22:30 UTC, 17:30 CDT



* **Duration:** 168 hours (7 days)



* **Eligibility Snapshot:** the block at which the proposal opens, Thursday 6 August at 22:30 UTC (17:30 CDT)



Every Miner Group must clear both the 80% approval threshold and the 20% quorum threshold. If one Miner Group falls short of either, the proposal does not pass. The vote will be resubmitted until all miner group votes pass. Quorum is measured against the total voting power held by the Miner Group, and approval is measured against the voting power that votes.



Under the TGIP Rules, where there are fewer than 10 authorized Validators producing blocks on Telcoin Network, the TAO votes on behalf of the Validator Miner Group.



Stakers should note that TEL staked in the Telcoin mobile application cannot vote on Snapshot until its voting power has been delegated to an external Polygon address through the delegate registry. If you have not completed that step, please see the [voting eligibility guide](https://forum.telcoin.org/t/tgip2-voting-guide/860). Delegation completed after the proposal opens does not apply to this vote.



---

## Next Steps

1. Members review this proposal and provide feedback in this thread before it is submitted to Snapshot.


2. The TAO submits the identical, codified proposal to all four Miner Group Snapshot spaces on Thursday 6 August at 22:30 UTC, 17:30 CDT.



3. Members ensure their voting power is correctly represented on chain before that block. Stakers stake and delegate; Liquidity Miners confirm their positions are staked on TELx or subscribed through the Uniswap v4 Telcoin Hook.



5. Upon ratification and deployment, the TAO publishes the amended Statutes.

title: Assign Voting Power to Decentraland Content Creators [GOV]
body:
> by 0x247e0896706bb09245549e476257a0a1129db418 (coalition)

## Linked Draft Proposal
[Assign VP to Content Creators [DRAFT]](https://decentraland.org/governance/proposal/?id=4393e86f-c8c8-4d33-bab6-bb0716fb4d13)

## Summary

This proposal gives content creators Voting Power (VP) based on verified publication fees they paid. The rule is **1 MANA of an eligible creator-paid publication fee = 1 VP** for eligible past and future publications.


## Abstract

Creators add value to Decentraland through Wearables, Smart Wearables, Emotes, and Linked Wearables. This proposal recognizes these contributions by creating VP from eligible creator-paid publication fees.

Creator VP may encourage more creators to publish approved content and take part in DAO governance.

This proposal does not change or refund publication fees, and it does not distribute MANA. It only creates VP.


## Motivation

Creators help build Decentraland, but publishing content does not currently give them VP.

The earlier Poll and Draft supported creator VP. The Draft excluded past submissions, but during its discussion community members asked for them to be included at the Governance stage. This proposal includes them and sets the final rules.


## Specification

### Eligible content

A publication is eligible when it:

*   was submitted through an official Decentraland publishing process;
*   was approved and published; and
*   has a creator-paid publication fee verified by official payment or publishing records.

These rules apply to past and future regular Wearables, Smart Wearables, Emotes, and Linked Wearables, with no date cutoff.

Linked Wearables are not automatically eligible. Standard and Programmatic publications qualify only for verified creator-paid amounts. Free slots and free publications create no VP. A fixed Programmatic payment is counted once, regardless of item or slot count.

### VP calculation

**1 MANA of an eligible creator-paid publication fee = 1 VP (1 MANA = 1 VP).**

*   For a MANA payment, use the exact MANA amount recorded for the publication.
*   For an official card or other non-MANA payment, use the official MANA amount recorded for that publication at payment time.
*   If no MANA amount was recorded, use the verified creator-paid USD amount and Decentraland's official MANA/USD rate at payment time. If that rate is unavailable, use the official rate at submission time. The approval-time rate may be used only as a final fallback.
*   Never recalculate an old payment using today's MANA price.
*   If the amount or creator wallet cannot be verified, the allocation remains pending until verified.

VP is added only after approval and publication. Rejected or unpublished content receives no VP.

VP goes to the submitting creator wallet in the official records. Selling or transferring the content does not transfer this VP.

Each eligible payment is counted once. If one payment covers several items or a whole collection, total VP equals the eligible MANA amount calculated under these rules and is not multiplied by the number of items. Gas and payment-service charges do not count. Later distribution of the fee does not change VP.

### Governance display and delegation

The Governance dApp must add Creator VP to own and consolidated VP totals and show it as a separate source. Creator VP uses the normal delegation system; delegation does not change its original allocation.

### Fees, subsidies, and Credits

This proposal does not change publication fees. Only the creator-paid part creates VP. Payments or subsidies from the Foundation, DAO, or others do not count. Discounts, waivers, free slots, and free publications do not count.

For publications covered by the passed 2026 fee proposal, Phase 3 sets a $25 fee. For six months, creators pay $5 and the Foundation pays $20; only the creator-paid $5 creates Creator VP. Afterward, the creator-paid amount counts under the same rule unless later governance changes the fee or subsidy.

Legacy Marketplace Credits earned in-game create no VP. Marketplace transactions do not create Creator VP. Existing VP sources (MANA, LAND, Estates, Names, and selected L1 Wearables) and delegation rules remain unchanged.

If purchasable Credits are accepted for publication fees, they may count only when official records show the submitting creator paid for them and the amount applied. Credits received without payment do not count. Calculate VP under the non-MANA rules above. If records cannot separate paid from free Credits or verify the applied amount, the allocation remains pending. Giving VP for Credits received without payment requires a separate DAO proposal.


## Impacts

The passed 2026 fee proposal reported 492 new items published by 128 unique creators during the previous 18 months: 366 Wearables, 119 Emotes, and 7 Smart Wearables. It did not list Linked Wearables separately.

The expected result is more creator representation in DAO decisions. Total governance VP will increase, and creators who paid more eligible MANA will receive more VP.

Some past records may take time to verify. The main risks are missing records, duplicate payments, incorrect wallet matching, and VP concentration among large publishers. Before the initial allocations are activated, the DAO must publish the allocation list, check for duplicate payments, test the calculation, and provide a way to correct errors.

No MANA or other token is distributed.


## Implementation Pathways

The DAO Council is responsible for oversight, public reporting, and making sure this proposal is implemented. DCL Regenesis Labs, as the DAO Executive Arm, is responsible for carrying out or arranging the technical implementation.

Both are responsible for the implementation, including reviewing pending past records.

Together, they must:

*   identify eligible past and future publications;
*   connect each publication to its creator wallet and eligible MANA amount;
*   prevent duplicate payments from creating duplicate VP;
*   build and activate the Creator VP strategy, including its Governance dApp display and delegation;
*   publish the calculation method and initial allocations for public review;
*   provide a way to report and correct errors; and
*   add pending past allocations after their records are verified.

The DAO Council and DCL Regenesis Labs may choose the technical method and correct minor technical details. They may not change the core rules of this proposal, including **1 MANA = 1 VP**, creator-paid fees only, one payment counted once, and inclusion of eligible past publications.

Implementation may happen in stages. A technical problem affecting one content or payment type does not cancel the rest of this proposal or stop other verified allocations.

If a core rule must change, the DAO Council must publish the issue and submit the required change through the DAO governance process in force at that time.

If either responsible body is replaced, its DAO-approved successor takes over these duties.


## Conclusion

This proposal gives creators **1 VP for every 1 MANA of verified creator-paid publication fees**, including eligible past and future publications.

The goal is to make creators stronger stakeholders in Decentraland governance and give them a voice that reflects their contributions. This change may also encourage more content creation and support a more diverse and engaging Decentraland for the whole community.

### References

*   [Original Creator VP Poll](https://governance.decentraland.org/proposal/?id=17f5b550-98d8-11ed-ae61-5f6dd0bf8358)
*   [Passed Creator VP Draft and discussion](https://forum.decentraland.org/t/dao-3bedba3-assign-vp-to-content-creators-draft/22385)
*   [Revised proposal for wearable publication fees](https://decentraland.org/governance/proposal/?id=50092c00-c315-11eb-ac84-1705d1ae4a66)
*   [2023 proposal setting the publication fee to 100 USD in MANA](https://decentraland.org/governance/proposal/?id=98d74360-3eae-11ee-88e6-1fe6cb69ee51)
