title: FWB H2 2026 Proposal
body:
# FWB H2 2026 Proposal 

Full proposal + H1 recap [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1So3anD_NbTmCoE8cds1nvNz1K753RbB3mcrOkqrzcz0/edit?usp=sharing).

This proposal asks to:

1. Approve a narrow mandate through December 31, 2026 focused on essential operations, post-FEST closeout, durable-asset stewardship, selective profitable partnerships, and a 2027 structural decision.  
2. Set a target all-in burn of $12,500/month and a hard ceiling of $13,000/month which is a 48% opex reduction.  
3. Preserve $20,000 for tax, legal, statutory, and orderly-transition obligations.  
4. Convert 20% of the combined liquid ETH/WETH position to USDC, with authority to convert up to 30% in order to establish a stable-liquidity buffer while retaining the majority of the treasury’s ETH exposure.

Using a working consolidated liquid treasury of approximately $111,575 before liabilities, the proposed reserve and hard burn cap preserve approximately 7.0 months of runway. At the target burn, runway is approximately 7.3 months. No uncontracted revenue is assumed.

## Governance Ask

### 1\. Approve the Mandate Through December 31, 2026

The Operating Lead is authorized to:

- complete post-FEST financial, sponsor, content, and operational obligations;  
- complete the organization’s 2025 accounting and tax filings, including all remaining coordination with FWB’s accountants and tax preparer;  
- maintain essential legal, accounting, tax, treasury, governance, website, newsletter, and communications functions;  
- steward and document FWB's durable assets, including the brand, newsletter list, social accounts, websites, archives, FEST IP, licensing agreement, treasury, and governance systems;  
- maintain a sustainable editorial/distribution cadence;  
- pursue selective partner work only under the revenue and margin rules below; and  
- prepare a formal 2027 path recommendation.

### 2\. Approve a Prospective Operating Cap

Because this proposal is being introduced after FEST and partway through Q3, the spending authority is prospective from passage through December 31 rather than a retroactive six-month blank check.

| Category | Monthly ceiling | Scope |
| :---- | ----: | :---- |
| **Operating Lead** | $6,000 | Core stewardship, governance, finance, partner closeout, transition planning |
| **Accounting, tax, and legal baseline** | $1,500 | Routine obligations; extraordinary matters use protected reserve |
| **Essential software and infrastructure** | $750 | Newsletter, domains, workspace, governance, accounting, critical web services |
| **Contracted editorial / operations support** | $1,000 | No open-ended retainer; narrow deliverables only |
| **Event Keys / member micro-programming** | $3,250 | Small, capped activity only |
| **Buffer** | $500 | Unplanned operating needs |
| **Hard monthly cap** | **$13,000** | Target actual burn: $12,500 |

### 3\. Endorse a Broader Strategic Direction for FWB

The first half of 2026—and especially the outcome of FEST26—suggests that FWB’s next phase should not be defined by trying to recreate the crypto-native market that supported earlier versions of the organization.

Crypto remains an important part of FWB’s history, network, and perspective. But the environment around FWB has changed. The speculative audience has contracted, the historical crypto sponsorship market has largely disappeared, and many of the most interesting cultural and technological questions now extend across AI, software, media, design, music, research, consumer products, and emerging creative practices.

FEST26 provided the clearest evidence that FWB can remain relevant within this wider landscape. The festival brought FWB into relationships with an almost entirely new group of partners (including Yahoo, Suno, Notion, and Feeld) and attracted a broader audience of artists, founders, researchers, musicians, designers, technologists, and cultural organizers. These partners did not engage because FWB offered access to a narrowly defined crypto audience. They engaged because FWB can convene an unusually cross-disciplinary network with taste, trust, cultural credibility, and a willingness to participate rather than simply observe.

The proposed direction is therefore to position FWB as a broader cultural and creative-technology network, with FEST as its annual tentpole rather than a separate project operating at the edge of the organization.

#### **Proposed H2 Direction**

| Workstream | H2 objective |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Network and partnerships** | Continue building bridges with aligned organizations across AI, software, media, design, music, research, consumer technology, and cultural infrastructure. Prioritize relationships that create meaningful opportunities for the FWB network and can become financially sustainable partnerships. |
| **Year-round programming** | Develop smaller talks, workshops, dinners, screenings, virtual sessions, and collaborative events with organizations and individuals connected through FEST and the wider FWB network. |
| **Editorial and media pipeline** | Establish a sustainable editorial and media pipeline spanning commissioned writing, interviews, conversations, audio, video, and documentation of projects and creative practices. |
| **Membership and audience development** | Test whether this broader positioning can attract a new cohort of members who identify with FWB’s values and interdisciplinary network, even if they do not primarily identify with crypto. |
| **FEST as the tentpole** | Use year-round programming and media to build relationships, audience, partner trust, and editorial narratives that culminate in FEST—and use post-FEST media and collaboration to extend the life of the festival beyond a single weekend. |

#### **Building a Year-Round Through Line**

Historically, many FWB relationships became visible only at FEST: a speaker appeared on the schedule, a partner created an activation, or an artist joined the lineup. But the trust and creative development that made those collaborations meaningful often happened over a much longer period. FWB should make that longer arc more intentional.

A FEST speaker might first participate in an interview or editorial feature, then host a smaller workshop or conversation, and eventually develop a larger program for the festival. A potential partner might begin with a small event or piece of media, learn how FWB works, and later support a larger FEST program. A first-time attendee might encounter FWB through an essay, workshop, collaborator, or digital program before deciding to become a member or attend the festival.

The goal is to create a reinforcing cycle:

> *Relationships → editorial and media → smaller programs and collaborations → FEST → post-FEST artifacts and follow-up → renewed partnerships, membership, and future programming*

This would allow FWB to create value throughout the year while also strengthening FEST’s programming, distribution, audience development, and partnership pipeline.

### **FEST27 Early Access**

FEST26 attendees and FWB members are invited to return to Idyllwild with access to a special [**$100 early ticket for FEST27**.](https://dice.fm/partner/tickets/event/yodn82-fwb-fest-6-30th-jul-idyllwild-arts-idyllwild-tickets?dice_id=10121997&dice_channel=web&dice_tags=organic&dice_campaign=Window+Research+Laboratory%2C+Inc.&dice_feature=mio_marketing&_branch_match_id=1612945858659363249&utm_source=web&utm_campaign=Window+Research+Laboratory%2C+Inc.&utm_medium=mio_marketing&_branch_referrer=H4sIAAAAAAAAA8soKSkottLXz8nMy9ZLyUxO1UvL1U%2B1TDI2SEs0MkmxNLKvK0pNSy0qysxLj08qyi8vTi2ydc4oys9NBQBtcf81OwAAAA%3D%3D)

## Summary of Discord Feedback

The Discord discussion produced several recurring themes:

- **FWB’s future may sit at the “edge of technology and culture.”** The discussion leaned toward broadening beyond a crypto-first identity without erasing crypto from FWB’s history or perspective. Feedback framed an opportunity for FWB to humanize emerging technology and serve as a more culturally literate touchpoint for crypto, AI, and whatever comes next.  
- **The bottleneck is execution capacity, not ideas.** Several comments emphasized the need for clearer leadership roles and better infrastructure to identify, onboard, resource, and coordinate people who want to lead work. That could include funding, team formation, production and operational support, and modestly compensated editorial or program stewardship.  
- **There is interest in more concrete member collaboration.** Ideas included collective building through shared tools and repositories, member-assembled creative and technical teams, and a possible “hive mind agency.” Members also proposed repeatable local gathering formats, including house-based pop-ups that combine building, talks, screenings, art, music, meals, and informal social time.  
- **Membership value should be tangible without becoming purely transactional.** Feedback emphasized the quality of the people, opportunities to spend time and make things together, and more “this happened because I was in FWB” outcomes. A recurring paid model would need clear value, while local programming must also account for members outside major cities.  
- **Several structural questions remain open.** Members asked how FWB could finance H1 2027, what long-term role the token and existing governance structure should play, and how leadership, member participation, and decentralization should relate in a future model.

Feedback also favored a smaller initial ETH conversion than the 50–70% originally proposed. The treasury authorization has therefore been revised to convert 20% of liquid ETH/WETH to USDC, with authority to convert up to 30%, balancing the need for stable liquidity against the risk of realizing too much of the current decline at once.

title: Treasury Multi-sig and Non Cost Proposals Constitutional Ratification
body:
Constitutional Amendment – Treasury Multisig & Zero-Value Proposal Access
Purpose
This proposal seeks to ratify two governance arrangements and incorporate them clearly into the Redbelly Community DAO Constitution:

Formalise the previously agreed structure for DAO Treasury multisignature signatories.
Allow proposals requesting no RBNT funding to be submitted at any time and without numerical submission limits.

Amendment 1 – Treasury Multisignature Signatories
The DAO Treasury shall be administered through a multisignature wallet requiring a minimum 3-of-3 multisignature approval structure, meaning no fewer than three authorised signatories and three required approvals for treasury transactions.

Up to three (3) serving High Council members and one (1) authorised Redbelly team representative may be appointed as authorised multisignature signatories, with at least one authorised Redbelly team representative included as a signatory.

Where more than three authorised signatories are appointed, the multisignature approval threshold shall never be less than three (3) approvals.

High Council signatories shall ordinarily hold signing authority for the duration of their High Council term and shall relinquish that authority following the conclusion of their term once replacement signatories have been securely appointed.

The Redbelly team representative may be replaced by another authorised Redbelly representative where required.

Operational security, wallet administration and signatory replacement procedures shall be governed by approved Treasury Governance Policies.

Rationale: This amendment formally ratifies the previously agreed treasury multisignature arrangement, establishes 3-of-3 as the minimum security standard, ensures Redbelly team representation within the multisig, and provides continuity between successive High Councils.
Amendment 2 – Zero Cost RBNT Proposals
Proposals requesting zero (0) RBNT from the DAO Treasury may be submitted at any time.

There shall also be no limit on the number of zero-RBNT proposals that may be submitted, provided each proposal otherwise complies with applicable proposal submission, eligibility, governance and evaluation requirements.

Any existing constitutional provision, policy, submission window or proposal limit that would otherwise prevent or restrict the submission of a zero cost RBNT proposal shall not apply to proposals submitted under this provision.

This exemption applies only to the RBNT proposal submission limit or submission timing restriction and does not exempt a proposal from normal governance review, voting, conflict-of-interest, documentation or other applicable requirements.

Rationale: Proposals that do not request RBNT funding do not place additional demand on the DAO's RBNT treasury allocation. Allowing these proposals to be submitted throughout the governance period, and at any other time enables governance improvements, operational changes and community initiatives to proceed without unnecessarily consuming or being restricted by funding-related, quantity or timing related proposal limits.

Upon approval, the log of Constitutional amendments shall be updated to incorporate the approved amendment(s), and changes incorporated into V1.4 of the Constitution once all amendments have been voted on and finalised during this 6 month period.

title: Quantum Biology DAO DP-33 — "Core Contributors August 2026" Proposal, v1.0
body:
This is Phase 3 of DAO governance. Voting is token-weighted using the QBIO token, which are available on Uniswap.

The following proposal is marked "fast" and as such will be in Phase 3 in Snapshot for 1 day. Votes will be taken into account if posted before 11:00pm PT | 1:00am ET | 5:00am GMT | 6:00am GMT+1 on Sun Aug 16 2026 (or Mon Aug 17 2026 for ET/GMT/GMT+1).

———

## Quantum Biology DAO “Core Contributors August 2026” Proposal, v1.0

Quantum Biology DAO Development Proposal - 033 (QBIO DP-33)

**Title:** Quantum Biology DAO “Core Contributors August 2026” Proposal

Drafted text here: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A7g0BcR4NgqkrKHjUFNuIbog3_avomAZhmv-KlepUu0/edit?usp=sharing](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A7g0BcR4NgqkrKHjUFNuIbog3_avomAZhmv-KlepUu0/edit?usp=sharing)

## Summary

This proposal changes the Core Contributors of the Quantum Biology DAO to a new set determined by popular vote in the community Discord:

-   Geoff Anders
    
-   Kyra Gardner
    
-   Yakuba Habibu (aka Cryptonurse)
    
-   Oliver Carefull
    
-   Olli Payne
    
-   Paul Ojo (aka DePaul)
    
-   Jonathan Heppner (aka Johnny Enact)
    

This new set of Core Contributors replaces the previous set of Core Contributors. The new Core Contributors will be Core Contributors for 6 months. After 6 months, Core Contributors will be chosen again; the same or different people may be chosen. Core Contributor powers are not changed, except changing Core Contributors now requires a DAO proposal.

Core Contributors who were not previously Core Contributors receive 5,000,000 QBIO from the DAO treasury, for a total of 30,000,000 QBIO, or 3% of the total token supply. This allocation comes from the “core team” pool of tokens.

## Background

**I. The Core Contributor role.**

“Core Contributor” is a special role at the Quantum Biology DAO. The position of “Core Contributor” is described in [DP-1](https://snapshot.box/#/s:qbio.eth/proposal/0xedf4358db1235da966d4fa90c1a8faef492dc307a34dfdc9631dfbb1251b0341) as follows: “Quantum Biology DAO Core Contributors are meant to comprise those who are substantially contributing to the operation of the DAO.”

**II. Core Contributor powers, prior to this proposal.**

Core Contributors have a number of powers at the DAO. To date, Core Contributor powers have focused primarily on mid-level decision-making: cases important enough for an official decision but which do not call for a DAO proposal.

At present, Core Contributor powers are:

[see [discussion](https://common.xyz/quantum-biology-dao/discussion/1313110-dp33-quantum-biology-dao-core-contributors-august-2026-proposal-v10) for list]

**III. History of this proposal.**

All three DAO co-founders participated substantially in the operation of the DAO in the period immediately after it was founded. However, in the subsequent period, concern arose that two of the co-founders (Clarice Aiello and Alessandro Lodesani) had stopped participating in the DAO and that this would impede DAO governance.

DAO member Olli Payne proposed that a vote be held for new Core Contributors. Community discussion led to it being proposed, in accordance with the spirit of progressive decentralization, that there be seven Core Contributors, rather than three. The community agreed upon a voting procedure, which involved nominations in [one thread](https://discord.com/channels/1248368139436163143/1532208092459172061) and voting in [another thread](https://discord.com/channels/1248368139436163143/1533552834438496407) in the community Discord. Any verified member of the Discord at the start of the nomination period was permitted to nominate candidates and vote. Verified members were permitted to vote for as many candidates as they wanted; votes were indicated by thumbs-up emojis.

The nomination period lasted from July 29, 2026 at 10:07pm ET through August 2, 2026 at 3:12pm ET. There were 14 nominees: Kyra Gardner, Cryptonurse, Geoff Anders, Paul Ojo (aka DePaul), Oliver Carefull, Eren Targ, Matteo (aka littleadult MiCroMacroupioer), Clarice Aiello, Alessandro Lodesani, Olli Payne, Jonathan Hepper (aka Jonny Enact), Mike Montague (aka montague.archimedesnetwork), Panaparask, and Sirisarck.

The voting period lasted from August 2, 2026 at 3:11pm ET to August 5, 3:15pm ET. Nominees were listed on their own line in the voting thread. A record of votes cast was screenshotted on August 5, 3:42pm ET. The results were: Kyra Gardner (17), Cryptonurse (15), Geoff Anders (19), Paul Ojo (aka DePaul) (12), Oliver Carefull (14), Eren Targ (7), Matteo (aka littleadult MiCroMacroupioer) (6), Clarice Aiello (5), Alessandro Lodesani (8), Olli (14), Johnny Enact (11), Mike Montague (aka montague.archimedesnetwork) (9), Panagparask (4), Sirisarck (6).

The top seven candidates are included in the proposal below.

**IV. DAO tokenomics.**

The DAO’s original tokenomics, as stated in the Quantum Biology DAO [Vision Paper](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1FCLowcfBJYEAOneG6ohlpcOL04Oym91G/view), allocated 20% of the total supply, or 200,000,000 QBIO, to “core team.” Of that, 15% was given to co-founders, 50,000,000 QBIO each, in December 2024. The remaining 5%, or 50,000,000 was reserved for future members of the “core team.”

A previous proposal, [DP-22](https://common.xyz/quantum-biology-dao/discussion/1292536-quantum-biology-dao-dp22-update-core-contributors-proposal-v11), allocated 1% of the total supply, or 10,000,000 QBIO, each to three new core contributors; however, this proposal did not pass quorum in April 2025, amidst confusion about tax implications.

At the present time, the price of the QBIO token is approximately $0.002059, which means the 0.5%, or 5,000,000 QBIO, is worth approximately $10,295.

## Proposal

**1. Core Contributors determined exclusively by DAO proposal.** Core Contributors to the Quantum Biology DAO shall be determined by a proposal which passes all phases of DAO governance. Core Contributors shall not be determined by a majority vote of Core Contributors.

Previous DAO governance on the matter of how Core Contributors are determined, including in [DP-4](https://snapshot.box/#/s:qbio.eth/proposal/0xedf4358db1235da966d4fa90c1a8faef492dc307a34dfdc9631dfbb1251b0341), section 6 and [DP-15](https://snapshot.box/#/s:qbio.eth/proposal/0x085c8d22e05852bae6c65dd14136780dff8e783abd145d4b3c281e83bfc43b14), section 8, is superseded.

**2. New set of Core Contributors.** For the six months following the passage of this proposal, the Quantum Biology DAO’s Core Contributors shall be:

-   Geoff Anders
    
-   Kyra Gardner
    
-   Yakuba Habibu (aka Cryptonurse)
    
-   Oliver Carefull
    
-   Olli Payne
    
-   Paul Ojo (aka DePaul)
    
-   Jonathan Heppner (aka Johnny Enact)
    

This list of Core Contributors replaces the previous Core Contributors. Geoff Anders continues on as a Core Contributor; Clarice Aiello and Alessandro Lodesani are no longer Core Contributors.

**3. Core Contributor term.** The term for Core Contributors lasts for six months from the date of the passage of this proposal. The DAO shall, by means of a DAO proposal, select new Core Contributors by the time six months elapses. The new Core Contributors remain Core Contributors until a DAO proposal changes the Core Contributors. Previous Core Contributors may be selected to be Core Contributors again.

**4. Powers of Core Contributors unchanged.** Apart from powers pertaining to the determination of Core Contributors, as described in section 1, the powers of Core Contributors are unchanged by this proposal.

**5. “Core team” token allocation.** Newly serving Core Contributors (i.e., who have not previously been Core Contributors), which under this proposal are Kyra Gardner, Yakuba Habibu (Cryptonurse), Oliver Carefull, Olli Payne, Paul Ojo (aka DePaul), and Jonathan Heppner (aka Johnny Enact), shall receive 5,000,000 QBIO each from the DAO’s treasury. If recipients decline this offer, the relevant QBIO will be retained in the DAO treasury.

**6. “Core team” token distribution schedule.** Tokens for newly serving Core Contributors shall be disbursed in five installments, 1,000,000 QBIO per installment per person, for a total of 5,000,000 QBIO per person. These disbursements shall happen monthly, with the first disbursement happening upon the passage of this proposal.

**7. Role of legal wrapper and multi-sig holders.** The Quantum Biology DAO Association is directed to facilitate the execution of this proposal in a timely fashion and take no steps to block it. The DAO’s multi-sig holders are directed to execute the transfers described in points 5 and 6 without delay.

## Statement

Core Contributors play an important role at the Quantum Biology DAO. In order for the DAO to be able to operate efficiently, it needs active Core Contributors, especially in cases where a majority of Core Contributors is needed to act. Since at least one of the previous Core Contributors is now inactive and the other has become much less active, it makes sense to select new Core Contributors.

The method for choosing the new set of Core Contributors was proposed by a DAO member and was approved of by the community. The elections saw substantial community participation and no issues were raised with the election process or result. The new Core Contributors put forward by this proposal have the backing of the community and are all people “substantially contributing to the operation of the DAO.”

Allocating 5,000,000 QBIO to each of the Core Contributors who were not previously Core Contributors is a suitable reward for each of them for previous and anticipated service to the DAO. The allocation of these tokens fulfills the original intention for the “core team” token pool and continues the DAO’s progress towards decentralized governance.

## Appendix I: DAO Governance on Core Contributors

title: Bring Back Collectible Culture to Decentraland
body:
> by 0x23be90335e79d3245615985d91f69814f98a0fab (SWISSVERSE)

Mistakes were made, but it is never too late to correct course.

Decentraland was built during an era when NFTs were deeply connected to scarcity, provenance, ownership, and collectibility. Wearables were part of that culture. Some were rare. Some became historically important. Some were genuinely difficult to obtain.

Over time, that culture weakened as the supply of new wearables continued to expand and the cost of creating new collections became increasingly low.

I believe it is time to consciously bring collectible culture back to Decentraland.

This Pre-Proposal asks whether the community supports exploring a permanent cap on the creation of new L2 wearable collections, while creating a path for future creators to acquire and reuse existing collections.

The idea is simple:

Decentraland already has enough wearable collections. Let us make the existing supply meaningful again.

Future creation would continue. AI-assisted creation would continue. New designs would continue.

The difference would be that creating something new would eventually require acquiring something that already exists.

Existing collections would gain a new purpose. Forgotten collections could become valuable again. Scarcity would gradually return. Ownership of a collection could itself become meaningful.

We cannot undo every decision that brought us here.

We can decide what happens next.

Should Decentraland explore permanently capping new L2 wearable collections and develop a model that allows future creators to acquire and reuse existing collections?

- Yes. Cap new L2 collections and restore value to existing ones
- No. Find another way to restore collectible value
- No. Keep wearables abundant, low-cost, and without collectible value.
- Invalid question/options


**[This proposal is summarized due to technical limitations. To view it complete and vote on it, visit the DCL DAO Governance dApp](https://decentraland.org/governance/proposal/?id=d1ee6c89-41bf-4130-ba25-88b4c0ce9204)**
choices: Yes. Cap new L2 collections and restore value to existing ones
No. Find another way to restore collectible value
No. Keep wearables abundant, low-cost, and without collectible value.

title: [Prop 989]Nouns Treasury Management - USDC
body:
## Nouns DAO Proposal 989 — Signal Vote

Source: https://nouns.wtf/vote/989  
Proposer: 0xcc4fd6e348009710404641a01b29f15703b90aed

### TLDR
Nouns DAO Treasuryが保有する484,743 USDCのうち、300,000 USDCをOrigin ProtocolのOUSDへ転換します。  
受け取ったOUSDを非リベース型のwOUSDにラップし、約5.5% APYの利回り獲得を図ります。  
約184,743 USDCは流動性として残し、想定収益は月約1,375ドル、年約16,500ドルです。

### 概要
Nouns DAO Treasuryの未運用USDCの一部を、Origin Protocolが提供する利回り付きステーブルコインOUSDで運用する提案です。

300,000 USDCをOUSD Vaultへ預け、1:1でOUSDを受け取った後、ERC-4626規格のwOUSDへラップします。wOUSDはトークン数量ではなく交換価値の上昇として利回りが反映されるため、OUSDの日次リベースによる追加トークンの発生を避けられます。

OUSDの利回りは、Curve AMOへの資金配分、MorphoでのUSDC貸付、報酬トークンのステーブルコインへの交換などから生じます。提案時点の利回りは約5.5% APYです。wOUSDにはロックアップがなく、随時OUSDへアンラップし、原資産のUSDCへ償還できるとされています。

- 運用後にTreasuryへ残る予定額：約184,743 USDC
- 想定利回り：約5.5% APY
- 想定収益：月約1,375ドル、年約16,500ドル

title: GIP-156: Should @Citrullin be banned from GnosisDAO Governance and Communication Channels?
body:
**Author:** Philipp-Alexander Blum (@Citrullin)
**Status:** Phase 3 (Direct Snapshot Referendum)
**Category:** Governance, Transparency & Contributor Rights
**Voting System:** Single-Choice Voting (YES / NO / ABSTAIN)

# Executive Summary

This proposal puts a direct question to GNO token holders and validators: 
**Should independent engineer and contributor Philipp Blum (@Citrullin) remain banned from GnosisDAO Discourse, Discord, and official communication channels?**

Following the [publication of an open-source proof-of-concept for a stateless zkEVM Account-Lattice](https://forum.gnosis.io/t/gip-xx-sovereign-reth-multi-chain-composability-poc/12412/13) and sustained critique of [GIP-153: Transition into the Ethereum Economic Zone (EEZ)](https://forum.gnosis.io/t/gip-153-should-gnosis-chain-transition-into-the-ethereum-economic-zone/12397/38), Gnosis Ltd. personnel placed the author's Discourse account on administrative hold and issued cross-platform bans under the justification of *"Threatening demeanour and unable to listen to moderator feedback".*

Taking leadership up on their public commitment to "Transparency Maximalism", this vote removes the decision from private Discord channels and places it directly on-chain.

- **A "YES" vote** requires delegates and DAO participants to publicly record their token weight in favor of administrative censorship of technical research.
- **A "NO" vote** or passive non-participation confirms the absence of a community mandate for the ban, establishing that the moderation action was an arbitrary exercise of centralized control.

# Procedural Justification & Context

This referendum is submitted directly to Snapshot, bypassing Phase 1 and Phase 2 Discourse stages because an administrative account hold makes forum posting physically impossible without creating sybil accounts.

The complete timeline and administrative statements are documented on X(formally known as Twitter):
- [Citrullin's Public Statement & Evidence Log](https://x.com/Citrullin/status/2088375732942541098)
- [0xKenk's Public Response](https://x.com/0xKenk/status/2088533161386864827)

# Addressing the Administrative Pretexts

*1. "Ignoring Governance Process and Submitting Incomplete GIPs"*
- **The Claim:** Pointed primarily at [GIP-155: Transition to an Independent Structural Governance Engine and Complete Separation of Powers.](https://forum.gnosis.io/t/gip-155-transition-to-an-independent-structural-governance-engine-and-complete-separation-of-powers/12383/17)
- **The Record:** Gnosis Ltd. personnel actively ignored community threads advocating for voting caps and independent board oversight. Meanwhile, insider proposals such as [GIP-152: Gnosis App Spin-Out](https://forum.gnosis.io/t/gip-152-should-gnosisdao-spin-out-the-gnosis-app-into-an-independent-company/12390/64) ($2.5M capital/IP transfer) advanced through governance despite community calls to restart Phase 1 and Phase 2. The standard for procedural compliance has not been applied equally.

*2. "Numerous Unfounded Accusations Against Participants"*
- **The Claim:** Characterizing critiques of delegate coordination as baseless attacks.
- **The Record:** Official delegate communications confirm that retail and minor token proposals are routinely bypassed without private lobbying. As documented in [Staworth's Delegate Platform](https://forum.gnosis.io/t/staworth-limited-delegate-platform/8770/26):
"It would also be helped to engage in some outreach to delegates or large tokenholders during the early stages of a proposal... Proposals that have festered on the forum for a few weeks with limited engagement are likely to be ignored in favour of newer topics and larger conversations."

*3. "Spamming Forum Threads Constantly"*
- **The Record:** The [Citrullin Discourse Activity Log](https://forum.gnosis.io/u/citrullin/activity) shows a three-day gap between the August 11 post and the August 14 update on the [Sovereign Reth Multi-Chain Composability PoC](https://forum.gnosis.io/t/gip-xx-sovereign-reth-multi-chain-composability-poc/12412/13). Routine technical updates do not constitute spam.

# Technical & Economic Substance

The friction leading to this ban stems from demonstrating that Gnosis Sovereign Chain does not need to abandon its L1 consensus layer to achieve multi-chain composability:
![snapshot_poc_table.png](ipfs://bafkreiadc4igfh6xjwpeccsev7paiue6cvy3qlhlwp4ftoy5ewche6pjhu)

Gnosis Chain currently maintains ~37,200 active validators ([Gnosis Metrics](https://metrics.gnosischain.com/?dashboard=overview&tab=main)). Merging this infrastructure into Ether exposes the ecosystem to extreme centralization:
- 70%+ of Ethereum Mainnet stake is concentrated in Liquid Staking Tokens (LSTs) and institutional custodians ([Dune ETH2 Staking](https://dune.com/hildobby/eth2-staking)).
- Solo stakers represent only ~6.5% of Ethers validators ([Rated Network Solo Staking Report](https://blog.rated.network/blog/solo-stakers)).
- Economies of scale consistently disadvantage small staking operations ([ArXiv: 2306.10777](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10777)).

# Legal & Regulatory Considerations

Operating a DAO through back-channel coordination while unilaterally de-platforming dissenting technical contributors introduces substantial legal vulnerabilities:
- **General Partnership Liability (Samuels v. Lido DAO):**
Federal court rulings establish that governance token holders who exercise managerial control in unincorporated DAOs operate as general partners, exposing participants and large delegates to joint and several liability.
- **EU MiCA Title VI (Market Abuse Regime):**
Evaluates economic substance over legal form (wirtschaftliche Betrachtungsweise). Coordinated treasury extraction, balance-sheet maneuvers, and the suppression of minority token holder oversight establish a clear evidentiary paper trail for supervisory authorities.

# The Precedent of Selective Moderation

Gatekeeping technical discourse under the guise of "private forum rules" replicates patterns seen elsewhere in the ecosystem, such as the Ethereum Foundation's EthResearch forum being moderated by Virgil Griffith under an explicit "our house, our rules" policy despite his federal IEEPA conviction ([Public Evidence Archive](https://x.com/Citrullin/status/2058006691698847851)). GnosisDAO must decide whether it operates as a permissionless public good or a centrally curated entity.

# Voting Options

- **YES / Ban Citrullin:** 
Ratify the administrative actions of Gnosis Ltd., confirming that Philipp Blum (@Citrullin) shall remain banned from Discourse, Discord, and official Gnosis channels, and establishing that contributor access is subject to centralized administrative discretion.
- **NO / Do Not Ban Citrullin:**
Reject the ban and direct Gnosis Ltd. administrators to immediately restore full access to all governance and communication channels, affirming that open technical dissent, validator advocacy, and alternative scaling proposals are protected within GnosisDAO.
- **ABSTAIN:**
Formally record token presence without casting a directional vote.

title: FROM FOUNDING ANGELS TO PUBLIC-COMPANY READINESS
body:
From Founding Angels to Public-Company Readiness
![1000040178.jpg](ipfs://bafybeighxtyaqoba5rqq36fqkq7zhzu3mxcdcefpzrkzlozulka4c4pmuy)
The Journey So Far

Global WEB3 Academy did not begin with thousands of investors.

It began with a small group of people who believed in the idea early.

STAGE ONE — THE FOUNDING ANGELS

The Academy originally created 100 Angel opportunities, with each opportunity requiring a contribution of $200.

The maximum capital available at this stage was:

100 × $200 = $20,000

However, only 36 Angel Investors joined.

These 36 early supporters became an important part of the Academy's foundation.

Their contribution helped the Academy develop from an early idea into the platform, community and ecosystem it is today.

In simple terms:

«36 people helped build the first house.»

They took the early risk when the Academy was still developing.

---

STAGE TWO — EXPANDING THE FOUNDATION

The next stage is much larger.

The proposal is to expand the Angel opportunity from:

100 opportunities → 10,000 opportunities

And increase the contribution from:

$200 → $5,000 per Angel position

If all 10,000 opportunities are successfully filled:

10,000 × $5,000 = $50,000,000

This means the proposed second stage could raise up to $50 million in strategic capital.

But the purpose is not simply to collect money.

The purpose is to use the capital to build the infrastructure required for the Academy's next level of growth.

---

WHAT WILL THE CAPITAL HELP BUILD?

The proposed capital can support the roadmap, including:

- Development of the Academy's blockchain infrastructure
- Stronger and more stable platform technology
- Expansion of Learning Spaces
- Digital identity and NFT Profile infrastructure
- Web3 education and professional programs
- Global community expansion
- Technology, security and infrastructure
- Business development and partnerships
- Legal, regulatory and corporate preparation
- Preparation for a possible future public share offering

In simple language:

«Stage One helped us prove that the idea could grow.

Stage Two is designed to build the infrastructure for much larger growth.»

---

WHY INCREASE THE ANGEL CONTRIBUTION?

The $200 contribution belonged to the Academy's early development stage.

At that time, the project was much smaller and the risks were much higher.

Today, the Academy has a larger vision, a developed ecosystem, an existing community and a much bigger technology roadmap.

Therefore, the proposed $5,000 Angel position represents a new investment stage, with different objectives, responsibilities and valuation considerations.

It should not be presented as simply changing the price of the original opportunity.

It represents moving from:

FOUNDING STAGE → GROWTH & INFRASTRUCTURE STAGE

---

HOW DO THE ANGELS FIT INTO THE COMPANY?

The Angel Investors are not simply contributors to a fundraising campaign.

Under the proposed structure, qualifying investors would become shareholders according to the company's approved capitalization structure.

Their investment would therefore be connected to the future value of Global WEB3 Academy.

For example, if an investor contributes $5,000, the important question is not only:

"How much money did I contribute?"

The bigger question becomes:

"What percentage of the company does my investment represent?"

That depends on the company's agreed valuation and share structure.

---

THE IMPORTANT VALUATION QUESTION

This brings us to the next major decision.

Before the Academy determines the final share allocation for the 10,000 Angel positions, the DAO needs to consider:

What should Global WEB3 Academy be valued at before the Stage Two investment?

This is called the pre-money valuation.

The valuation helps determine how much ownership the new Angel Investors collectively receive for their $50 million investment.

For example, if:

Pre-money valuation = $100M

and:

New Angel capital = $50M

then:

Post-money valuation = $150M

The new investors would collectively represent approximately 33.33% of the company, before considering other factors such as future dilution.

If the agreed valuation is higher, the percentage given to the new investors would generally be lower.

Therefore, the valuation is one of the most important decisions before the Stage Two share structure is finalized.

---

THE DAO DECISION

The DAO is therefore being asked to help determine the next step rather than simply approve a fundraising number.

Key Questions for DAO Consideration

1. What valuation should Global WEB3 Academy use for the Stage Two Angel Round?

2. What percentage of the company should be made available to the 10,000 Angel positions?

3. Should the 36 founding Angels receive a special recognition or share position because they participated during Stage One?

4. What rights should Stage Two Angel shareholders receive?

5. What share structure should be established before the company moves toward a future public offering?

6. What milestones should the Academy achieve before considering itself ready for public valuation and a public share offering?

---

THE BIGGER PICTURE

The journey can be understood very simply:

STAGE ONE

100 opportunities
→ 36 founding Angels
→ $200 each
→ Foundation built

STAGE TWO

10,000 opportunities
→ $5,000 each
→ Up to $50M capital
→ Blockchain + platform + ecosystem expansion

STAGE THREE

Valuation + corporate structure
→ Shareholder organization
→ Growth milestones
→ Public valuation preparation

FUTURE STAGE

Potential Public Company
→ Public share offering
→ Wider ownership
→ Global expansion

---

THE MESSAGE TO THE COMMUNITY

The story is not:

«"We started at $200 and now want $5,000."»

The story is:

«"We started with a small group of people who believed in the idea. Those early supporters helped build the foundation. Now we are proposing a larger Angel stage to build the infrastructure required for the next level of the Academy. Before we take that step, the DAO must help determine how the company's value and ownership should be organized."»

DAO PROPOSAL QUESTION

Should Global WEB3 Academy establish a formal pre-money valuation and share-allocation framework for the proposed 10,000 Angel positions, and use the DAO-approved framework as the foundation for organizing the company's next stage toward a future public valuation and potential public share offering?

The DAO's decision will become an important step in determining how the Academy moves from a community-founded project toward a professionally structured global company.![1000040178.jpg](ipfs://bafybeighxtyaqoba5rqq36fqkq7zhzu3mxcdcefpzrkzlozulka4c4pmuy)

title: NFT PROFILES INTO PHYSICAL WEB3 ACADEMY CARDS
body:
DAO PROPOSAL
![1000040244.jpg](ipfs://bafybeih6tvtxedpp4mfb6dfjdf7aj5brpa6ujmfn2an7ycuvyystvzbhzq)
Expanding NFT Profiles into Physical Web3 Academy Cards

Proposal Summary

As Global Web3 Academy continues developing its NFT Profile ecosystem, the Tech Team proposes expanding the profile into a premium physical NFT card that connects members' digital identities with everyday offline use.

The card would combine the member's photo, NFT Profile, membership identity, QR/NFC verification, and selected Web3 services into one physical card.

The Vision

The goal is to make the NFT Profile easier to use beyond the digital environment:

NFT PROFILE → PHYSICAL CARD → OFFLINE ACCESS → WEB3 SERVICES

The card could be designed in a premium Web3 Academy blue and yellow/gold identity, making it both a membership credential and a recognizable representation of the Academy.

Future Payment Utility

As the ecosystem develops, the Academy could explore integrating the card with Visa and Mastercard payment infrastructure through suitable partners, creating a potential bridge between crypto-based assets and traditional fiat payments.

This could eventually allow members to access supported payment services while keeping their NFT Profile as the underlying digital identity.

Key Card Features

- Member photograph and personal identity
- NFT/Profile ID
- QR code for profile verification
- NFC tap-to-access capability
- Blockchain/NFT verification
- Membership level and achievements
- Learning and community credentials
- Potential payment functionality
- Connection to selected Web3 Academy services

Why This Matters

This upgrade can transform the NFT Profile from a primarily digital identity into a physical Web3 identity that members can carry and use in everyday environments.

It can also create opportunities for:

- Greater NFT utility
- Offline member verification
- Stronger Academy branding
- Fintech and payment partnerships
- New ecosystem services
- Wider adoption of Web3 identity

Proposed Tech Team Role

The DAO would authorize the Tech Team to research, design, prototype and explore partnerships for the NFT Card expansion.

The Tech Team would then present the DAO with the proposed card design, technology, partnership model and implementation plan before full deployment.

DAO VOTE

Should Global Web3 Academy authorize the Tech Team to expand NFT Profiles into premium physical cards and explore Visa/Mastercard-compatible payment functionality and crypto–fiat connectivity through strategic partners?

YES — Approve the NFT Card expansion initiative.
NO — Do not proceed at this stage.
ABSTAIN — Request further information.

Vision

One NFT Profile.
One Physical Identity.
A Bridge Between Web3 and the Real World.

title: MENTOR–STUDENT NODES & COMMUNITY REFERENCE VALUE
body:
Building the Chain Through Learning, Participation and Community Value
![1000040291.jpg](ipfs://bafybeifva5a674jrsubzl3mgb24yhey7myk3jkcq3t4vwkb2j7kfcr45be)
Global WEB3 Academy has adopted the Mentor–Student Node and Community Reference Value framework as part of its development journey toward the 100,000 NFT Profile milestone.

The focus now is not whether the framework should exist, but how every Learning Space, mentor and learner will participate in building it responsibly.

1. OUR CURRENT MISSION

Every Learning Space is becoming part of a growing decentralized learning network.

Through learning activities, participation and voting polls, mentors and learners are contributing to:

Learning → Participation → Rewards → Records → Network → Future Token Utility

The Academy therefore asks every Learning Space to begin incorporating Community Reference Value into its relevant polls before the 100,000 NFT Profile milestone.

---

2. WHAT IS COMMUNITY REFERENCE VALUE?

Community Reference Value is the value that a Learning Space collectively assigns to its accumulated participation rewards through its own community voting process.

For example, a Learning Space may vote for:

$1 per reward

or

$10 per reward

or

$100 per reward

The purpose is to create a transparent record of how the early community valued its contribution before the future chain launch or migration.

This reference value is intended to become an important historical input when determining the future token economy.

Important:

Reference Value is not a guaranteed market price.

Once the token becomes transferable or enters wider markets, its actual market value will depend on utility, supply, demand, liquidity, adoption, market conditions and applicable regulations.

---

3. RESPONSIBILITY OF MENTORS

Mentors are now requested to include Community Reference Value as part of appropriate Learning Space polls.

Mentors should:

- Guide learners in understanding what they are voting for.
- Encourage genuine and informed participation.
- Include reference-value discussions in relevant polls.
- Record the community's agreed value transparently.
- Encourage participation from diverse communities and countries.
- Avoid manipulating or artificially influencing voting results.

The mentor's role is therefore both educational and network-building.

---

4. RESPONSIBILITY OF STUDENTS & LEARNERS

Learners are requested to:

- Participate actively in Learning Spaces.
- Vote honestly in community polls.
- Understand the value they are assigning to their participation rewards.
- Contribute knowledge and meaningful activities.
- Accumulate rewards through genuine participation.
- Help maintain diverse participation across the network.

Every genuine participant is helping create both learning history and network history.

---

5. WHY WE NEED GLOBAL PARTICIPATION

The strength of a decentralized network depends on distributed participation.

The Academy therefore invites mentors, learners, universities, associations and organizations from different countries to participate in Learning Spaces.

The objective is to prevent excessive concentration of participation within one country, institution or community.

More communities → More distributed participation → Stronger foundation for decentralization

---

6. BEFORE 100,000 NFT PROFILES

Before reaching the 100,000 NFT Profile milestone, Learning Spaces are encouraged to begin recording their Community Reference Values.

The Academy can then aggregate the results into a transparent Community Reference Value Record.

This record may include:

- Learning Space
- Number of participating members
- Community-voted reference value
- Voting date
- Voting methodology
- Governance record

This creates a historical snapshot of how the early Academy community valued its contribution before the next stage of the blockchain ecosystem.

---

7. FROM REWARDS TO FUTURE TOKEN VALUE

The intended journey is:

LEARN

↓

PARTICIPATE

↓

VOTE

↓

EARN REWARDS

↓

ACCUMULATE

↓

ESTABLISH COMMUNITY REFERENCE VALUE

↓

CHAIN LAUNCH / MIGRATION

↓

FUTURE TOKEN UTILITY & MARKET VALUE

Subject to the final blockchain design and applicable requirements, accumulated rewards may eventually gain utility within the Academy's ecosystem, potentially including transactions, platform services, chain-related fees or other approved functions.

The reference values recorded today therefore become an important part of the economic history and governance record of the ecosystem.

---

8. OUR SHARED RESPONSIBILITY

Mentors: Guide, educate, organize meaningful polls and protect the integrity of participation.

Learners: Participate, vote honestly, contribute and accumulate rewards through genuine activity.

Learning Spaces: Build communities and record their collective reference values.

Global WEB3 Academy: Preserve the records, develop the infrastructure and prepare the ecosystem for future blockchain utility.

THE MESSAGE

«Your Learning Space is not only a place to learn. It is becoming part of the network.

Your participation creates rewards.

Your community votes establish a reference for their value.

And the history we create before 100K NFT Profiles becomes part of the foundation for the future chain.»

THE TASK STARTS NOW

Mentors: Add Community Reference Value to appropriate Learning Space polls.

Learners: Participate, vote responsibly and understand the value your community is recording.

Together: Build the learning network, strengthen decentralization and establish the community's reference value before 100,000 NFT Profiles.![1000040290.jpg](ipfs://bafybeifnsoachsw5m7ojtl7ny2sm5fgtjraiiu53bfn37obnx7zckt2glu)

title: PIP-41: Restore Base V1 Deployment and Initiate Ethereum Deployment
body:
**PIP-41: Restore Base V1 Deployment, Initiate Ethereum Deployment and Compliance Role Funding**

**Proposal Summary**

This proposal seeks governance approval to:

* Restore the required **ZKP balances** to the Base V1 deployment using ZKP minted from the **rewards pool**.
* Restore the non-ZKP test asset balances required by VaultV1 to support withdrawals on Base.
* Use **DAO Council operational funding** to acquire the required non-ZKP assets.
* Initiate the build and deployment process for Panther V1 on **Ethereum**.
* Authorize the **Compliance Role funding** to be handled via DAO Grants.

---

**Motivation**

**1. Restore Base V1 ZKP balances**

To restore the Base V1 deployment to its required operational state, ZKP balances must be returned to three contracts:

* ZkpReserveController: **3,840,888.4 ZKP**
* VaultV1: **1,000,546.507790072217357505 ZKP**
* PantherPoolV1: **280,766.6906 ZKP**

This represents an exact requirement of **5,122,201.598390072217357505 ZKP**.

The required ZKP will be **minted from the rewards pool** and distributed to the respective Base V1 contracts.

**2. Restore VaultV1 test assets**

VaultV1 also requires the other test assets used by the Base deployment to be restored. Without sufficient balances of these assets in the vault, withdrawals of the corresponding tokens will revert.

The following assets are required:

* **0.000119127498140994 WETH**
* **0.434819 USDC**
* **0.100842079824413618 AERO**
* **0.066781363580384114 VIRTUAL**
* **0.018154422481002229 MORPHO**
* **0.000335444255711905 AAVE**
* **5.49509528069306407 ZORA**
* **0.00000325 cbBTC**

These assets will be acquired using **DAO Council operational funding** and transferred to VaultV1 on Base.

**3. Initiate Panther V1 deployment on Ethereum**

This proposal also seeks approval to begin the build and deployment process for **Panther V1 on Ethereum**.

The Ethereum deployment will extend the V1 architecture to Ethereum and begin the technical work required to prepare the deployment for testing and subsequent launch.

Approval of this proposal authorizes the development team to begin the necessary build, configuration, integration, testing, and deployment preparation work for Ethereum.

Exact details regarding **contract addresses, token and reward parameters, limits, token whitelist, and rewards and subsidies minting** will be prepared and presented in the next PIP.

**4. DAO Council management of Compliance Role funding**

This proposal seeks authorization for the DAO Council to manage the monthly funding of the **Compliance Role via DAO Grants**.

The DAO Council treasury has exhausted its ZKP reserves allocated for the Compliance Role. This proposal will therefore authorize DAO Grants to cover the ongoing Compliance Role costs, maintaining the intent of the funding arrangement originally approved under **PIP-24**.

---

**Proposed Changes**

**1. Restore ZKP to Base V1**

Mint **5,122,201.598391 ZKP from the rewards pool**.

The required Base balances are:

* ZkpReserveController — **3,840,888.4 ZKP**
* VaultV1 — **1,000,546.507790072217357505 ZKP**
* PantherPoolV1 — **280,766.6906 ZKP**

The exact requirement is **5,122,201.598390072217357505 ZKP**. Due to the precision supported by VestingPools, the mint is rounded up to **5,122,201.598391 ZKP**, resulting in a surplus of **927782642495 wei**.

**2. Restore non-ZKP assets to VaultV1**

Using **DAO Council operational funding**, acquire and transfer the following assets to VaultV1 on Base:

* WETH — 0.000119127498140994
* USDC — 0.434819
* AERO — 0.100842079824413618
* VIRTUAL — 0.066781363580384114
* MORPHO — 0.018154422481002229
* AAVE — 0.000335444255711905
* ZORA — 5.49509528069306407
* cbBTC — 0.00000325

These balances are required to ensure withdrawals of the corresponding assets can be processed successfully by VaultV1.

**3. Begin Ethereum deployment**

Authorize the development team to initiate the **Panther V1 Ethereum deployment**, including:

* Preparing and configuring the V1 contracts for Ethereum.
* Building and configuring the required deployment infrastructure.
* Performing integration and deployment testing.
* Preparing the Ethereum deployment for subsequent launch and governance actions where required.

Exact details regarding **contract addresses, token and reward parameters, limits, token whitelist, and rewards and subsidies minting** will be prepared and presented in the next PIP.

**4. DAO Council manages Compliance Role funding**

Authorize the DAO Council to manage the **Compliance Role monthly funding via DAO Grants**.

This will allow DAO Grants to cover the ongoing Compliance Role costs while maintaining the intent of the arrangement originally approved under **PIP-24**.

---

**Next Steps**

**Base restoration**

Following approval:

1. Mint the required **ZKP from the rewards pool**.
2. Transfer the required ZKP to the Ethereum DAO Multisig.
3. Bridge the required ZKP to Base.
4. Distribute the ZKP to ZkpReserveController, VaultV1, and PantherPoolV1.
5. Acquire the required non-ZKP assets using **DAO Council operational funding**.
6. Transfer the acquired assets to VaultV1.
7. Verify the restored balances and test Base V1 deposit and withdrawal functionality.

**Ethereum deployment**

Following approval, the development team may begin the technical build and deployment process for Panther V1 on Ethereum.

The Ethereum deployment will proceed through the required development, testing, compliance, and governance stages before being made available to users.

Exact details regarding **contract addresses, token and reward parameters, limits, token whitelist, and rewards and subsidies minting** will be prepared and presented in the next PIP.

**Compliance Role funding**

Following approval, the DAO Council will be authorized to use **DAO Grants to fund the Compliance Role**, consistent with the intent of PIP-24.

---

**Voting**

**PIP-41** will be published on Snapshot for a **3-day vote**, with voting eligibility defined in **PIP-7**.

---

**Transactions for the Snapshot**

**PIP-41: Mint 5,122,201.598391 ZKP to the Ethereum DAO Multisig to restore the Base V1 deployment**

**Addresses**

Panther contracts on Ethereum:

* DAO Multisig: `0x505796f5Bc290269D2522cf19135aD7Aa60dfd77`
* VestingPools: `0xb476104aa9D1f30180a01987FB09b1e96dDCF14B`
* ZKP: `0x909E34d3f6124C324ac83DccA84b74398a6fa173`

**Transaction Overview**

The Base V1 deployment was drained on 2026-08-06 through a compromised Reality.eth Zodiac module on the Base Safe. The contract implementations have been restored; these transactions replace the required ZKP.

A total of **5,122,201.598391 ZKP** will be minted to the Ethereum DAO Multisig. Bridging to Base and subsequent distribution to the Base V1 contracts will be performed manually afterwards and are not part of the Snapshot transactions.

Existing vesting pool #18 has **57,155 ZKP** remaining and available for release. A new vesting pool #25 will therefore provide the remaining **5,065,046.598391 ZKP**.

**Important:** Transaction #1 must execute before **2026-08-31**, otherwise it will revert because the configured pool start date would be in the past.

All four transactions are signed by the Ethereum DAO Multisig.

**Ethereum Direct Actions — 4 Transactions**

**Transaction #1 — addVestingPools**

Create vesting pool #25 for **5,065,046.598391 ZKP**, assigned to the Ethereum DAO Multisig.

* Start: 2026-08-31
* Vesting period: 1 day
* Adjustable: Yes
* Pre-minted: No
* Contract: VestingPools

**Transaction #2 — updatePoolTime**

Move vesting pool #25's start date to **2026-08-01**, allowing the full allocation to become releasable.

* Pool: #25
* New start: 2026-08-01
* Vesting period: 1 day
* Contract: VestingPools

**Transaction #3 — releaseTo**

Release **5,065,046.598391 ZKP** from vesting pool #25 to the Ethereum DAO Multisig.

* Pool: #25
* Recipient: Ethereum DAO Multisig
* Amount: 5,065,046.598391 ZKP
* Contract: VestingPools

**Transaction #4 — releaseTo**

Release the remaining **57,155 ZKP** from existing vesting pool #18 to the Ethereum DAO Multisig.

* Pool: #18
* Recipient: Ethereum DAO Multisig
* Amount: 57,155 ZKP
* Contract: VestingPools

The executable calldata for these four actions will be included directly in the corresponding Snapshot transactions.

title: SAEP-19: Remove the Spark Risk Council
body:
# SAEP-19: Remove the Spark Risk Council - August 17, 2026

Spark's Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Phoenix Labs.

## Review
The Spark community can hereby express support or opposition to the following changes, as described by the author of the proposal:

> ## Proposal Details
> 
> We propose that Spark governance remove the Spark Risk Council from the Spark Artifact and reassign its functions as follows:
> 
> - Remove the mandatory SRC review step from the Root Edit Routine Protocol. The Operational Facilitator review step remains in place unchanged as the pre-vote gate for alignment, author eligibility, and operational feasibility.
> - Remove the “Passed SRC Review” precondition from the Root Edit Token Holder Vote, so that the Operational Facilitator triggers the Snapshot poll upon a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Spark Artifact.
> - Transfer responsibility for immediate Delegate offboarding to the Spark Foundation, which already manages Delegate onboarding, identity verification, sanctions checks, and term re-approvals ([A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.1](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.1), [A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.3](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.3)) and requests the KYC whose failure is a ground for emergency removal. The existing registry-update process on offboarding ([A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.5.4](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.5.4)) is unchanged.
> - Transfer initiation of a Delegate Removal vote on disqualification grounds to the Spark Foundation, consistent with the reassignment of emergency offboarding and with the Spark Foundation’s existing role in collecting the information on which the disqualification grounds turn.
> - Transfer the Delegate compromised-key response to the Spark Foundation, which maintains the Registry of Delegates in which a compromised Delegate is flagged and through which a replacement verified address is processed.
> - Amend the Risk Curation Framework cancellation reasons so that risk-based cancellation of pending changes continues to rely on identification by the Sky Core Council. The cancellation authorities (Spark SubDAO Proxy and Guardian) and all timelock controls are unchanged.
> - Amend the Private Ecosystem Review provision so that confidential pre-activation disclosure is made to the applicable Sky ecosystem governance reviewers designated for confidential ecosystem reviews. The objection right, the bar on activation while an objection is unresolved, and the orderly wind-down requirement are unchanged.
> - Remove the Spark Risk Council section of the Spark Artifact ([A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4)) and all subdocuments, including the SRC membership registry.
> 
> If approved, any Root Edit proposal pending SRC review at the time the Artifact update takes effect proceeds under the amended Routine Protocol. Any Delegate suspension in effect under [A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.7.2](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.7.2) at the time the Artifact update takes effect continues in effect and is administered by the Spark Foundation. If approved, Phoenix Labs intends to coordinate with the Spark Foundation and the currently seated SRC members on an orderly wind-down of their engagements in accordance with the existing compensation terms approved by the Spark Foundation.
> 
> ## Justification
> 
> **Overlapping safeguards remain in place.** Each function performed by the SRC is also performed, or backstopped, by an actor whose mandate exists independently of this proposal, with the single exception identified under “What is not replicated” below. Pre-vote alignment review of every Root Edit proposal is conducted by the Operational Facilitator, who is required to prevent misaligned proposals from proceeding ([A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.3), [A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6)); the Spark Artifact already directs the Operational Facilitator to advance aligned proposals to Snapshot without an SRC conclusion when the SRC does not act within its review window ([A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.3.3](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.3.3)), so the consolidated process this proposal adopts is one the Artifact already sanctions. Downstream of any vote, every resulting Artifact update or action passes through the Operational Executor Agent, whose duty to check Prime Agent actions for Atlas alignment cannot be amended by Prime Agents or Executor Agents ([A.1.14.4.4.1](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.1.14.4.4.1)) and who may refuse to operationalize actions that are misaligned or present significant risk beyond its insured capacity ([A.1.14.4.5](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.1.14.4.5)). Core GovOps may review the Spark Artifact for Atlas compliance at any time and directly edit it to enforce conformance ([A.1.14.2.10.2.1](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.1.14.2.10.2.1), [A.1.14.2.11.1.2](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.1.14.2.11.1.2)), and the Sky Executive Vote may override any Agent Artifact provision on misalignment or safety grounds ([A.1.14.1.6.1](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.1.14.1.6.1)). These Sky Atlas-level safeguards exist independently of the Spark Artifact and are unaffected by this proposal. In addition to these codified mechanisms, ongoing risk analysis and review of Spark-related activity is performed by Sky-affiliated actors including the Sky Core Council, risk team contributors at the Sky Frontier Foundation, and the Core Council Risk Advisor(s). This proposal does not alter their mandates, and no Spark Artifact language change is required for their work to continue.
> 
> **The Root Edit Primitive continues to satisfy its Sky Core specification**. The Sky Atlas requires that the Root Edit Primitive “must specify the requirements for proposals to be included in a vote, such as any required review period or any reviews that must be conducted by other parties such as expert advisors” ([A.2.2.6.2.2.2.3](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.2.2.6.2.2.2.3)). That requirement is to specify the applicable requirements, and the examples it gives are illustrative rather than mandatory. After this change, the Spark Root Edit Routine Protocol continues to specify a seven (7) day Operational Facilitator review with a published alignment finding, the conditions under which a proposal advances, and a three (3) day token holder vote with a stated approval threshold. The Primitive therefore remains fully specified, and removing the document titled “Root Edit Expert Advisor Review” does not leave a gap against A.2.2.6.2.2.2.3.
> 
> **Process efficiency.** The SRC review is a serial step of up to seven (7) days in every Root Edit cycle, and the SRC is a compensated three-member body ([A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.6](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.6)). Removing the step shortens the path from submission to Snapshot for every future Root Edit and eliminates the ongoing compensation cost, without removing the blocking alignment gate (Operational Facilitator) or the non-amendable execution-layer check (Operational Executor Agent).
> **Each reassigned function has a named decision-maker.** After this change, the pre-vote gate for Root Edits is the Operational Facilitator; emergency Delegate removal, initiation of a Delegate Removal vote on disqualification grounds, and the Delegate compromised-key response are decided by the Spark Foundation, which already conducts the identity verification, conflict-of-interest collection, and sanctions checks on which the removal and disqualification grounds turn ([A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.1](https://sky-atlas.io/#A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.1)) and which maintains the Registry of Delegates in which a suspension is recorded; risk identification for Risk Curation cancellations rests with the Sky Core Council, which is already named in the same provision; and confidential pre-activation review of a Confidential Strategic Integration and Deployment rests with the Sky ecosystem governance reviewers designated for confidential ecosystem reviews, who are already named in the same provision and already hold the objection right that gates activation. No function is left with criteria but no decider.
> 
> **What is not replicated.** Two capabilities are narrowed rather than re-housed. The first is a structured, public, pre-vote risk analysis published for every Root Edit proposal, which is unique to the SRC and which this proposal does not re-house. Risk analysis coverage of Spark-related activity continues through the Sky-affiliated actors noted above, proposals remain open to public review on the Sky Forum throughout the governance cycle, the Operational Facilitator’s review remains a blocking gate, and token holders retain the ability to reject any proposal at Snapshot. The second is the SRC’s seat as a confidential disclosure recipient prior to activation of a Confidential Strategic Integration and Deployment, which narrows that review to the Sky ecosystem governance reviewers designated for confidential ecosystem reviews. The substance of the review is unchanged: disclosure of all relevant deployment details remains mandatory before activation, the reviewers’ objection right is unchanged, and activation remains barred while an objection is unresolved.

Additional details can be found in the [proposal forum post](https://forum.skyeco.com/t/saep-19-remove-the-spark-risk-council/28180).

The proposed Spark Artifact changes can be found in the following pull request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/302

## Outcomes

- If "For" receives the most votes, the proposal will be approved. The associated pull request will be merged into Spark's artifact. When required, the listed changes will proceed to implementation by the relevant actors.
- If "Against" receives the most votes, the proposal will be rejected. No changes will be implemented.

title: [GIP-289] Convert Treasury ETH into sfrxETH
body:
# Summary

Convert 300 WETH held by the Gearbox DAO treasury into sfrxETH to generate staking yield and strengthen alignment between Gearbox and Frax.

# Context

Frax’s [FIP-450](https://gov.frax.finance/t/fip-4xx-add-gearbox-institutional-rwa-market-to-sfrxusd-strategies/3884) proposes adding the Gearbox Institutional RWA Market to the sfrxUSD strategy whitelist with a $5 million allocation cap.

The proposal also describes a Gearbox alignment commitment involving converting ETH  into sfrxETH.

# Motivation

The ETH currently held by the treasury does not generate staking yield. sfrxETH is Frax’s yield-bearing staked ETH token and accrues rewards generated by the Frax validator system.

Converting the treasury position would:

- Generate additional yield on otherwise idle ETH.
- Maintain the treasury’s ETH-denominated exposure.
- Demonstrate Gearbox’s alignment with Frax as Frax governance voted for allocating up to $5 million to Gearbox’s institutional RWA market.

# Risks

The conversion replaces native ETH exposure with exposure to sfrxETH and Frax’s staking and redemption infrastructure, including smart-contract, validator, liquidity, and frxETH/ETH peg risks.

The frxETH/sfrxETH system has operated since 2022 without a publicly reported loss of principal caused by a protocol exploit and has undergone multiple audits. This track record provides additional confidence but does not eliminate the risks described above.

# Proposal

Authorize the Gearbox DAO treasury to convert 300 WETH into sfrxETH.

title: [SIP-58] Symbiosis X Arc: Connecting Stablecoin Finance Across Chains
body:
# Context
Arc is an EVM-compatible Layer 1 built by Circle for stablecoin-native financial applications. 

The network separates consensus and execution into two layers:
* The consensus layer uses Malachite, a Tendermint-based consensus engine that provides deterministic, sub-second finality across a permissioned validator set. Once a block is finalized, it cannot be reversed or reorganized.
* The execution layer is powered by Reth and runs the EVM, supporting Solidity and standard Ethereum development tools such as Foundry, Hardhat, and Viem.

USDC is the native gas token on Arc. Transaction fees are denominated in USDC and use an EIP-1559-based fee model designed to keep gas costs predictable. The network also natively supports stablecoin assets including EURC and USYC.

Arc plans beta support for post-quantum wallet signatures using SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s at mainnet launch. The feature will be opt-in, with additional post-quantum protections planned for later stages.

Arc is currently operating in private mainnet, with public mainnet scheduled to launch in September 2026.

# Proposal
Enable support for the Arc chain in the Symbiosis protocol.

The proposal includes the following steps:
* Deploying and configuring Symbiosis contracts on Arc to support cross-chain and on-chain operations.
* Adding Arc-based USDC to the Symbiosis AMM DEX on the Host Chain to enable cross-chain routing. 
* Leveraging DEXs on Arc to enable on-chain routing.
* Activating the Symbiosis Relayers Network to handle cross-chain messaging and verification for Arc.

# Key Points
* Supporting Arc would expand Symbiosis coverage to a stablecoin-focused Layer 1 built around USDC and other financial assets.
* The integration would enable cross-chain movement of supported assets into and out of the Arc ecosystem, connecting Arc users to additional networks and liquidity through Symbiosis.
* Arc’s EVM compatibility and use of USDC as the native gas token make it a natural fit for Symbiosis while reducing the need for users to manage a separate gas asset.

# Penalty Cap Redesign

## Simple Summary

This CIP changes the cap on penalties for unsuccessful settlements from a fixed absolute amount to a relative amount of proposed trade volume. The size of these relative caps is chosen to be as small as possible while still retaining a desired settlement success rate.

## Motivation

The auction mechanism of CoW Protocol includes a penalty for solvers whose solutions were selected as winners but whose settlements were not successfully executed. The current monetary penalties follow the same second-price logic as rewards, with penalties being capped at a chain-specific absolute value.

One issue with the current penalty is that it serves multiple purposes within the mechanism. On the one hand, the size of penalties implies a trade-off between quality of proposed prices, which improves with small penalties, and speed of execution, which improves with large penalties. On the other hand, penalties provide a form of censorship resistance since it is costly to block the execution of an order by proposing solutions which cannot be executed.

The size of the cap was originally set in [CIP-20](https://snapshot.box/#/s:cow.eth/proposal/0x2d3f9bd1ea72dca84b03e97dda3efc1f4a42a772c54bd2037e8b62e7d09a491f) and tried to address both purposes. This can lead to large caps with a negative impact on execution quality for small orders, while at the same time not providing sufficient censorship resistance for larger orders. We propose to set the cap from first principles based on the trade-off of execution quality and execution speed.

This change will impact the distribution of rewards and penalties between solvers but not the aggregate total payment to solvers, due to consistency rewards as specified in [CIP-85](https://snapshot.org/#/s:cow.eth/proposal/0xb488c343df3ba5f3857a4c7a920a74e18c13a2cdce99d27af34216803da6abff). Censorship resistance will be addressed separately in the future.

## Specification

https://github.com/cowprotocol/docs/compare/b5c361d2eaf5ac366a04258ae8128781650f77d7...12547af286d32e8875c672888f710193647140b3 ([PR](https://github.com/cowprotocol/docs/pull/655))

Each order will have a penalty cap associated with it in each auction, expressed in the native token of the chain.  
The cap for penalties for a given solver in a given auction is the sum of all penalty caps of orders which were not executed in time or not executed at all.  
For partially fillable orders, the penalty cap is scaled to the executed fraction.

Initially, the cap for each order is chosen as a fraction of the quote for an order. The fraction depends on the chain and on whether the traded tokens are correlated.  
The concrete values are as follows.

Uncorrelated tokens:

-   Ethereum mainnet: 4 bps
    
-   Gnosis: 3 bps
    
-   Arbitrum: 1 bps
    
-   Base: 2 bps
    
-   Avalanche: 2 bps
    
-   Polygon: 3 bps
    
-   BNB: 1 bps
    
-   Linea: 2 bps
    
-   Ink: 1 bps
    
-   Plasma: 1 bps
    

Correlated tokens:

-   All chains: 0.1 bps
    

Additionally, the initial cap will be bounded by the equivalent of $20.

The classification into correlated and uncorrelated token pairs follows the same logic used in determining the protocol volume fee. The quote of an order is the buy amount with all volume fees deducted for sell orders and the sell amount with all volume fees added for buy orders.

The core team has a mandate to change the penalty cap per order within the interval [0bps, 10bps], if needed, to tune the trade-off between competitive prices and fast execution. Any change to the penalty cap has to be announced in advance to solvers and will be reflected in the documentation on [docs.cow.fi](http://docs.cow.fi).

## Rational

The current cap for penalties was originally defined in CIP-20. Its size was based on a symmetry argument which neither addresses strategic implications of caps, nor censorship resistance. Subsequent changes to reward caps, e.g. in [CIP-36](https://snapshot.org/#/s:cow.eth/proposal/0x4e58f9c1208121c0e06282b5541b458bc8c8b76090263e25448848f3194df986) or [CIP-74](https://snapshot.org/#/s:cow.eth/proposal/0x0c70c8cd92accee872b52614b4fa10e3e3214f45c5b6857f7e88e910607a3c1d), did not change the general logic of the choice of penalty caps. The proposed cap in this CIP, in contrast, is derived from first principles with a focus on encouraging desirable strategic behavior of solvers.

One main driver for unsuccessful settlements is price movements of tokens. If the price moves against them enough, a solver is better off if their solution does not settle and they pay a penalty compared to their solution settling at the new price.

![image.png](ipfs://bafkreiady3pem5owmmp3beasqz4vt4jfaw42abhrmhjojztpk2eequpm4m)

For a successful protocol we want to ensure swift execution of trading intents, giving bounds on settlement success rates p_success. Given such a bound for success rates, the penalty cap for an order is set such that solvers settle with probability p_success, given estimates about price movements during the window of exclusivity, i.e., the time between the /settle notification and the deadline by which solutions to an auction need to be settled. For now, we propose to use separate fixed relative caps for two classes of token pairs, correlated and uncorrelated token pairs. Caps are fitted to achieve around 92% success rate using Binance data for price movements.

The window of exclusivity used for different chains are as follows. The value for main net is based on statistical data. All other chains follow the formula `floor((submission_deadline - 0.5) * block_time)` with values as configured in the autopilot.

-   Ethereum mainnet: 26s
    
-   Gnosis: 12s
    
-   Arbitrum: 2s
    
-   Base: 7s
    
-   Avalanche: 7s
    
-   Polygon: 11s
    
-   BNB: 2s
    
-   Linea: 7s
    
-   Ink: 4s
    
-   Plasma: 4s
    

Looking at the 10 most traded correlated and uncorrelated tokens, these exclusivity times result in the caps proposed above. A notebook containing this the computation can be found [on GitHub](https://github.com/cowprotocol/penalty-research/blob/43b751075ba62965d6d23948d99c19a2c72cf59f/notebooks/fixed_caps_from_revert_target.ipynb).

While we start with a fixed cap per class of token pair, an approach more tailored to the specific token pair could be used in the future. We have tested different approaches, e.g. based on price movements in the last 24h hours which result in a more stable success rate at the cost of additional complexity in computing penalty caps.

For caps in the proposed interval [0bps, 10bps], the expected impact on bidding is similar to the current mechanism. Solvers need to take the cap into account for optimal bidding, see [this forum post](https://forum.cow.fi/t/how-penalties-affect-bidding-of-solvers/3341).

Future initiatives of reducing settlement deadlines will reduce penalty caps, as expected price variations decrease given a shorter exclusivity window.

Note that the change to penalties is not intended to change the total payment to solvers. The aggregate of rewards and penalties is fixed to a fraction of protocol revenue, see CIP-85. This does not change with this proposal. What changes is implied solver behavior and distribution of rewards between solvers.

![counterfactual.png](ipfs://bafkreihqwmtnogucohcpumnex4ay2aunteki5gctkljn7s2zjw2cfdr3ku)

A notebook comparing current and proposed rewards can be found [on GitHub](https://github.com/cowprotocol/penalty-research/blob/43b751075ba62965d6d23948d99c19a2c72cf59f/notebooks/penalties_analysis_counterfactual.ipynb).
