title: [NMPIP 265 - Part B - Fern Re] Fern Re Formation, Capital Commitment & Governance Approval
body:
This NMPIP is broken up into two parts.

Part A - The redemption of the DAO's existing investment in Re (made ahead of the launch of Re's reUSDe token) and its reallocation, partly back into reUSDe and partly toward the Fern Re capital commitment.

Part B - The ownership, capitalization, and leadership structure of Fern Re (Cayman based entity). and Fern Speciality Ltd (UK based entity).
---

## Fern Re and Fern Specialty: Ownership, Capital & Governance

This is intended as the simplest structure to get Fern Re operational and licensed. The Foundation expects to more fully integrate Fern Re with the onchain protocol over time, and will bring further proposals to members as that integration is scoped in detail.

### 1.1 Ownership & Initial Capital

* Terrapin (on behalf of the Nexus Mutual DAO) to be the 100% equity owner of Fern Re.
* Terrapin to supply $2,500,000 of initial equity capital to Fern Re, from the Capital Pool, intended primarily to satisfy minimum regulatory capital requirements and to facilitate the writing of initial insurance policies.
* Terrapin (on behalf of the Nexus Mutual DAO) to be the 100% equity owner of Fern Specialty Ltd.
* Terrapin to supply $1,000,000 of initial equity capital to Fern Specialty, from the Community Fund, intended to primarily fund initial operational expenses to support Fern Re and other for-profit service activities.
* Both investments should be expected to be illiquid. While there is the potential for relatively early dividends due to the short tail nature of the initial business lines, its very likely the best use of profits will be to fuel further growth.

### 1.2 Surplus Note Investment

* Approval to invest up to $5,000,000 of the Mutual's existing capital pool into Fern Re via a surplus note as Fern Re requires.
* The drawing of this note is dependent on the speed of sales growth in Fern Re.
* The surplus note accrues at a rate of 12% per annum when drawn.
* Loss priority: the equity layer (Terrapin's $2.5m) bears first loss ahead of the surplus note. The surplus note is subordinated to policyholder claims but senior to equity.

Members should be aware that, should claims experience be poor, further capital injections beyond the amounts approved here may be required to keep Fern Re appropriately capitalized. Any such additional injection would be brought back to members for approval at the time.

As all investments (both equity investments and the surplus note) will be held by Terrapin, all profits from these activities will accrue to DAO members and therefore NXM holders.

### 1.3 Governance & Leadership

### Fern Re

* Hugh Karp to serve as a Director and Chairman of Fern Re.
* Jack Prenter to be appointed Director of Fern Re. Jack has driven this project from the outset and has been part of the Nexus Mutual team for over four years.
* A third, independent director is to be appointed. This individual has not yet been identified; the team will bring a nomination to the Advisory Board, (per delegated authority) once identified.
* Ania Szpak currently serves as Chief Legal Officer within the Nexus Mutual structure and will oversee the legal function of both Nexus Mutual and Fern Re structure. This shared appointment reflects the close operational and governance links between the entities and will be subject to appropriate conflict of interest, confidentiality and professional independence arrangements.

### Fern Specialty Ltd

* Jack Prenter to be appointed CEO and Director of Fern Specialty.
* Hugh Karp to serve as a Director and Chairman of Fern Specialty.
* Adam Wickens to serve as a Director of Fern Specialty. Adam joined the Nexus Mutual team recently from Relm where he has led underwriting for digital asset risks and is well known among brokers and the wider insurance community.
* Ania Szpak currently serves as Chief Legal Officer within the Nexus Mutual structure and will oversee the legal function of both Nexus Mutual and Fern Re structure. This shared appointment reflects the close operational and governance links between the entities and will be subject to appropriate conflict of interest, confidentiality and professional independence arrangements.

### 1.4 Path to Tighter Onchain Integration

This structure, a Cayman-incorporated, DAO-owned entity capitalized with equity and a surplus note, is deliberately the most straightforward way to get a licensed reinsurance vehicle operating. It is not intended as the end state. The DAO R&D and Foundation Engineering teams have launched a project to revamp the staking mechanism, which will allow the Mutual to more tightly integrate Fern Re with the onchain protocol, and will bring detailed proposals to members as that work matures.

### 1.5 Risks & Considerations for Members

* **Concentration/counterparty risk:** $2.5m initially, and up to $7.5m, of capital pool funds (equity + surplus note) will sit inside a single regulated entity rather than the onchain Capital Pool. Similar to the existing Re investment.
* **Regulatory risk:** the B(iii) licence application is submitted but not yet granted; timing and conditions of approval are outside the DAO's control.
* **Capital call risk:** poor claims experience could require further capital beyond what's approved here.
* **Key person risk:** leadership is concentrated in a small initial team (Jack Prenter, Hugh Karp for both Fern Re and Fern Specialty and Adam Wickens for Fern Specialty) pending appointment of the independent director and broader team build-out.
* **Return profile:** the 12% surplus note coupon reflects the subordinated, first-loss-adjacent position of this capital relative to policyholder obligations. Equity returns are expected to be very good on successful business growth but are illiquid and will take time to realise.

## What Members Are Being Asked to Approve

The Members are being asked in addition to the authority previously granted under Governance Votes 262, to confirm, approve and authorise the following:

## Part B

1. Terrapin to invest US$2.5 million from the Capital Pool as initial equity capital for Fern Re, becoming 100% shareholder.
2. Terrapin to invest US$1million from the Community Fund as initial equity capital for Fern Specialty Ltd, becoming the 100% shareholder.
3. Terrapin to invest up to US$5 million of Capital Pool assets into Fern Re via a 12% surplus note, subordinated to policyholder claims, with equity bearing first loss.
4. Acknowledgement that further capital injections may be required in the future if claims experience requires it (to be separately approved at that time).
5. The appointment of Jack Prenter as Director and CEO of Fern Re.
6. The appointment of Hugh Karp as Director and Chairman of Fern Re.
7. Approve the provision of Chief Legal Officer services to Fern Re by Ania Szpak under the applicable services arrangement.
8. The Advisory Board will be authorised to:

* identify and appoint a third, independent director, of Fern Re to be confirmed with members once identified;
* represent Terrapin and the wider DAO’s interests as shareholder of Fern Re and Fern Specialty Ltd;
* appoint, remove and replace directors, subject to applicable regulatory requirements and any specific member-confirmation requirement;
* exercise Terrapin’s ordinary shareholder rights; and
* approve financing and other financial matters of up to US$1 million, provided they do not change the cap table, dilute Terrapin’s ownership or otherwise fall within a matter reserved for members.

9. The authority for the Advisory Board (Foundation Council) and the directors to complete the licensing and establishment process, appoint advisers and service providers, execute the necessary documents and make any non-material changes required by CIMA or professional advisers
10. Authorise Fern Re and Fern Specialty Ltd to enter into necessary third party agreements, including but not limited to technology, intellectual property, personnel, and administrative services.
11. Authorisation for Hugh Karp, as a member of the Advisory Board, to act as Terrapin's principle representative in relation to Fern Re and Fern Specialty Ltd, including representing the Members interests, and decision making on a day to day basis including non-material changes to the structure, or documents (including where required by the regulators, legal counsel, auditors, insurance managers, or other professional advisers).
12. The respective boards of Fern Re and Fern Specialty Ltd will be responsible for:

* the day to day management and operation of the relevant company;
* regulatory compliance, risk management and the prudent operation of the relevant business; and
* determining and implementing changes to the relevant licence or expansion into additional business lines, subject to applicable regulatory approval and provided the change does not trigger a matter reserved for members.

13. Ratify actions already taken under the previous mandate (vote https://app.nexusmutual.io/governance/proposals/v1/262) including engaging advisers, preparing the business plan, identifying the structure, discussing the same with the regulators and incurring the costs associated with this process.
14. Board Independence: neither the Advisory Board nor the Members may direct the Fern Re board of directors to act inconsistently with the director's duties or regulatory obligations.
15. Matters reserved for the Members and requiring separate vote:

* any additional fundraising or capital commitment;
* any issue, transfer or cancellation of shares, change to the cap table or other transaction resulting in shareholder dilution;
* the creation of a new surplus note structure or any material amendment to the principal, interest, subordination, repayment or conversion terms of an existing surplus note; and
* the acquisition, disposal or transfer of any material shareholding interest in Fern Re or Fern Specialty Ltd.

title: [Prop 992] Fake World Assets
body:
# Fake World Assets

![](https://i.imgur.com/iYD3j6m.png)

## ⚡️ TLDR

Quick summary:

- Send 24 treasury Nouns into [fwa.fun](https://fwa.fun), the onchain gacha machine
- Each backed with ~1.28 ETH so a winner nets exactly the same whether they keep the Noun or take the ETH
- No discounts, no giveaways. Anyone who keeps a Noun turned down its exact cash value to do so
- Every listing earns an equal share of every draw fee in the protocol, paid to the treasury
- In expectation, a listing earns back its own backing in fees before it is ever drawn (math below)
- Nouns and ETH move through a reusable manager contract whose every exit is hardcoded to the treasury

*Throughout this proposal, "the treasury" means the Nouns DAO treasury, the timelock at [nouns.eth](https://etherscan.io/address/0xb1a32FC9F9D8b2cf86C068Cae13108809547ef71). Full details below...*

---

## 🙋 Background

I'm gami, Nouner since the early days (Nouns 13 and 189) and founder of [Gnars](https://gnars.com), which got started with 69 ETH from [Prop 51](https://nouns.wtf/vote/51) in April 2022 and has been proliferating Nouns ever since. You've seen my proposals before. They tend to bring voters out of the woodwork. Bring them.

In July 2026 I forked FWA onto Robinhood Chain as [StockRip](https://stockrip.com): 74,000+ draws, 1,700+ ETH of volume, 900+ players ([live stats](https://stockrip.com/secretdash)). So I know this machine from both sides of the glass, because I run one. I've also fed FWA a Noun of my own: [Noun 1382](https://nouns.wtf/noun/1382), backed with my own ETH, priced too low, gone in three hours, lol. That mistake is where this proposal's pricing rule comes from.

## 🎰 Why

The treasury holds 613 Nouns and gains one every day. Since the reserve went to 2.8 ETH in April, 101 of the 102 auctions through mid-August ended with zero bids: 26 Nouns burned, 75 swept into the treasury, one single winner. The treasury's ~4,000 ETH is mostly staked and earning. Its 604 Nouns earn nothing.

FWA is doing ~310 draws and ~25 ETH in draw fees a day across 6,400+ active listings as of 2026-08-22, down from a ~2,900-draw peak as post-emissions volume settles (measured onchain, methodology at the bottom). Nouns is already whitelisted as collection #17. The machine is running either way. This proposal puts 24 of our idle Nouns inside it, earning, and in front of people.

## ⚖️ The true decision

Each Noun is listed with backing set to floor ÷ 0.9 (~1.28 ETH at time of writing, set precisely at listing time). FWA pays a winner 90% of backing if they hand the NFT back, so at this level the choice is perfectly balanced. Draw one and you choose:

- **Keep the Noun.** You just turned down ETH worth exactly what the Noun fetches at floor. You want this.
- **Take the ETH.** Same value, none of the hassle of selling. The Noun goes straight back to the treasury.

Flippers press the ETH button. Believers keep the Noun. And while they wait to be chosen, all 24 earn draw fees for the treasury.

## 📊 The numbers

Everything here is measured from FWA's contracts onchain (latest: a full 24-hour sample ending 2026-08-22). Volume has kept settling since emissions ended, so the timeline numbers move with it; the key result in bullet three does not. Verify it, please.

- ~310 draws/day at an average price of ~0.08 ETH. 98% of every draw fee splits equally across active listings, which works out to **~0.0038 ETH per listing per day** at current volume, or ~0.09 ETH/day across our 24 (a week ago this was 4x, at the emissions peak 10x: these scale with volume)
- Draw odds scale with 1/backing. At 1.28 ETH backing, each Noun's expected time in the pool is **~11 months** at current volume (it was ~75 days a week ago; the timeline moves inversely with volume, in either direction), roughly one draw event across our 24 every couple of weeks
- The part worth checking twice: the draw fee is the pool's harmonic mean × 1.025, and draw odds are 1/backing. Those cancel, so **a listing's expected fee income before it is ever drawn ≈ its own backing**, independent of volume and of what everyone else lists
- Per-Noun branches, in expectation:
  - *Winner keeps the Noun:* ~1.28 ETH earned in fees + backing returned (minus 1% protocol cut). Treasury up ~1.3 ETH, one new Nouner who chose a Noun over cash
  - *Winner takes the ETH:* ~1.28 ETH earned in fees, 1.28 ETH of backing paid out. Roughly ETH-neutral, Noun back in the treasury
- Expectation is not a guarantee. A Noun drawn on day 2 earns less than its backing (ask me about Noun 1382). A Noun that sits earns more. That variance is why this is sized at 30 ETH and not 300
- Not modeled, pure upside: $FWA depositor rewards (30% of the protocol's fee-funded buybacks accrue to depositors)
- For calibration: across all of FWA in the sample window, winners kept the NFT in ~1.3% of settlements, because most listings are cheap NFTs backed above their value. Ours are the opposite. Keeps will still be the minority, and that's fine: a keep is a new Nouner who wanted in, a buyback is a round trip that paid us fees

## 🖼 The 24

Hand-picked from the treasury and shaped like a pyramid: the oldest Noun we have at the top, three from the early days, six from the middle years, fourteen from the no-bid era that were minted straight into the treasury. All 24 heads are different, all 24 accessories are different, and Noun 1980 is the only Noun in the entire treasury wearing the Gnars accessory.

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xigami/fwa-middleware/main/docs/img/11.png)

**11**

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xigami/fwa-middleware/main/docs/img/26.png) ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xigami/fwa-middleware/main/docs/img/82.png) ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xigami/fwa-middleware/main/docs/img/89.png)

**1957 · 1958 · 1969 · 1980 · 1983 · 1988 · 1989**

## 🔧 The middleware

The treasury can't act inside FWA's 24h settlement windows, so a small manager contract sits in between. It's the only new code in this proposal and it's deliberately boring:

- Every exit path is hardcoded to the treasury: withdrawn Nouns, returned Nouns, reclaimed backing and earned fees can go nowhere else. The operator manages listings but cannot redirect a single wei
- I'm the operator at launch. The treasury can replace the operator at any time by proposal, and the role can be opened up further later (even permissionless keeper functions) if that's where we want to take it
- It's reusable. If this experiment earns its keep, a future proposal can load more Nouns into the same audited contract without deploying anything new
- Governance stays safe: 24 Nouns in escrow shift quorum by roughly 2 votes, quorum snapshots at proposal creation so no live vote is affected, and the impact only shrinks as Nouns supply grows
- Already deployed and [verified on Etherscan](https://etherscan.io/address/0x89ec417Fa93F02926bF9c28316dA4E7d0F28089b#code): `0x89ec417Fa93F02926bF9c28316dA4E7d0F28089b`. What you audit is what executes

Attached transactions send the 24 Nouns and ~30 ETH from the treasury to the manager. I then list each one at floor ÷ the live buyback rate (90% today), priced at listing time; the contract enforces a 1 ETH minimum backing on me, and every listing tx is public and checkable against the formula.

## 🔎 Check my work

Don't trust the claims above, verify them. Everything is public in [the repo](https://github.com/0xigami/fwa-middleware):

## Nouns DAO Proposal 992 — Signal Vote

Source: https://nouns.wtf/vote/992  
Proposer: 0x387a161c6b25aa854100abaed39274e51aaffffd

### TLDR
Nouns DAO のトレジャリーから Noun 24体と約30 ETHを管理コントラクトへ送り、オンチェーン抽選プロトコル FWA に出品する。  
各Nounには出品時のフロア価格を基準に約1.28 ETHを裏付け、当選者はNounの保持または同等価値のETH受取を選択できる。  
出品中に発生する抽選手数料、未使用資金、回収されたNounとETHは、すべてトレジャリーへ返還される。

### 概要
提案者 gami が運用者となり、トレジャリー保有のNoun 24体を FWA の抽選プールへ出品する。対象は Noun 11、26、82、89、279、408、548、559、801、861、1914、1917、1929、1933、1942、1950、1954、1957、1958、1969、1980、1983、1988、1989。

各Nounの裏付け額は、出品時のフロア価格をFWAの買戻し率（現在90%）で割って設定し、コントラクト上では最低1 ETHとする。当選者がNounを保持する場合は裏付けETHがトレジャリーへ戻り、ETHを選ぶ場合はNounがトレジャリーへ戻る。

FWAでは抽選手数料の98%が有効な出品へ均等配分される。提案本文の試算では、現在の取引量を前提に1出品当たり約0.0038 ETH/日、24体合計で約0.09 ETH/日の手数料収入となる。また、各Nounが抽選されるまでに得る手数料の期待値は、おおむねその裏付け額に等しいとしているが、実際の収益や抽選時期は保証されない。

NounとETHは、デプロイ済みの管理コントラクト `0x89ec417Fa93F02926bF9c28316dA4E7d0F28089b` を通じて管理する。資産、手数料、裏付け金の送付先はNouns DAOトレジャリーに固定され、運用者は変更できない。運用者は出品管理を行い、DAOは将来の提案によって運用者を交代できる。

### 予算
- 約30 ETH：24体のNounに設定する裏付け資金
- トレジャリー保有のNoun 24体
- 各Nounの裏付け額：出品時に「フロア価格 ÷ FWAの買戻し率」で決定（提案時点の目安は約1.28 ETH、最低1 ETH）

### イベント
- FWAの決済期間：抽選後24時間
- 出品価格と裏付け額は、提案実行後の各Noun出品時に確定

title: PGP-44 l 2026-2027 Immunefi Bug Bounty Program Renewal
body:
Summary: This proposal aims to renew the Parallel bug bounty program and triaging service managed by Immunefi for an additional 24-month period from a reduced annual rate of $38,530 to $20,000 USD per year.

Rationale: One year ago, the DAO approved PGP-28, engaging Immunefi to provide an always-on, fully managed bug bounty program with 24/7 triage and one mitigation review. Since launch in July 2025, the program has been actively protecting Parallel Protocol across all deployed chains.

The bug bounty program is an essential last line of defense. Even after multiple thorough internal and external audits, vulnerabilities can remain, and bug bounty programs consistently surface critical bugs that audits miss. Across Immunefi's client base, 80% of programs have surfaced critical bugs missed in audits during their first year of operation. Immunefi remains the largest onchain security platform, having prevented over $25B of funds from being lost to hacks and currently protecting over $110B in user funds.
Program continuity: Allowing the program to lapse would create a gap in coverage that could be exploited. Renewal ensures uninterrupted protection for the protocol and its users.
Renewal terms. Immunefi is offering a significantly reduced rate for the renewal period:
- Year 2 (this proposal): $20,000 
- Year 3 (committed): $20,000 locked at the same rate
- Renewal Plan: Parallel would secure the discounted offer while upgrading to a higher level of triaging, the Immunefi Expert Assessment

Program continuity. All existing program parameters remain unchanged:
- Maximum reward: $250,000 USD for the most critical impacts
- Minimum reward: $50,000 USD for other critical bugs
- Bug validity determined by Parallel's administrators (Cooper Labs), with Immunefi mediation available for disputes
- Immunefi vault remains funded with $5,000 for bug bounty payments
- Business Days managed triage, Safe Harbor module included
- Program administrators (Cooper Labs) retain authority to transfer funds from the insurance fund without proposal, conditioned to a post detailing the bug found, the amount paid, and its resolution

Means:
- Human Resources: Cooper Labs will continue to serve as program administrators, responsible for validating bug reports and managing the program. The managed triage plan provided by Immunefi minimizes the time required from administrators by filtering invalid reports.
We propose to appoint Cooper Labs as administrators of the bug bounty program. They will be responsible for validating bug reports and will have the authority to transfer funds from the insurance fund without proposal, conditioned to a post detailing the bug found, the amount paid and its resolution. These teams will designate a representative who will sign Immunefi's standard Master Services Agreement and can also update the program at any time.
- Treasury Resources: $40,000 worth of USDC from the Parallel Insurance Fund for the Immunefi bug bounty service (Year 2 and 3 of 2-year commitment at $20,000/year). The Immunefi vault is already funded with $5,000 for bug bounty payments; no additional vault funding is required at the time of writing the proposal

Technical implementation:
On Ethereum:
- The DAO Multisig signers will transfer $20,000 worth of USDC for year 2 from (in July 2026) the Parallel Insurance Fund Multisig (0x6aF71a3723D3c0Ed69f84EE259c9De3019C2a77c) to Immunefi (0x7119f398b6C06095c6E8964C1f58e7C1BAa79E18).
- The DAO Multisig signers will transfer $20,000 worth of USDC for year 3 (in July 2027) from the Parallel Insurance Fund Multisig (0x6aF71a3723D3c0Ed69f84EE259c9De3019C2a77c) to Immunefi (0x7119f398b6C06095c6E8964C1f58e7C1BAa79E18).

Voting Options:
- For the Bug Bounty Program Renewal
- Against / Rework the Proposal
- Abstain

Author(s): Immunefi

title: Deflationary Tokenomics
body:
The tokenomics tax is currently set to the maximum of 4% (0% on buys, 4% on sells). Of that, 3% goes to the Token Fund for Foundation expenses and 1% is added to the liquidity pool.

This proposal asks the community to decide how the existing 1% liquidity pool allocation from tax should be used to introduce a deflationary mechanism.

Option A would send that full 1% to a deflationary mechanism that incrementally removes $ZYPTO from circulation (with zero LP contribution).

Option B would split it evenly: 0.5% to the deflationary mechanism and 0.5% to the liquidity pool.

title: Decentraland Shop & Marketplace Redesign
body:
> by 0xbc02db030361121dd43bbb2fcbcb4f9f98c1dc7d (Bestie)

The new Shop page UI is now a completely separate experience from the Marketplace, but it doesn’t include all of the features and asset categories that were available in the old Marketplace

I would like to see Land, Estates, and L1 Ethereum Wearables included in the new Shop. I believe these could be integrated through an on/off toggle, category filter, or separate tab, allowing users to easily switch between different asset types

I understand that the new Shop is designed to better support creators of L2 wearables and emotes, and I think that is a positive direction. However, L2 wearables and emotes don’t represent the entire Decentraland Marketplace ecosystem

Since the launch of the new Shop, I’ve noticed that trading activity for Land, Estates, and L1 wearables on the Decentraland Marketplace appears to have declined significantly. The new separation creates another hurdle for both new and existing users, who now have to navigate between different experiences to locate, search for, and purchase different types of Decentraland assets

Rather than splitting the ecosystem across separate experiences, I believe the Shop and Marketplace could be optimized to provide a more unified and intuitive experience while still giving L2 creators the visibility and support they need.

Some ideas to consider:

Include Land, Estates, L1 wearables, L2 wearables, and emotes within the same Shop experience.

Add tabs or filters that allow users to quickly switch between asset categories.

Provide a clear distinction between L1 and L2 assets without requiring users to leave the Shop.

Improve search and discovery so users can find all Decentraland assets from one place.

Make it easier for users to understand where to buy, sell, and trade each type of asset.

I’d like to hear the community’s opinions and ideas on how the new Shop and/or Marketplace could be optimized or redesigned.

What would make the experience more intuitive for both new and existing users?

- No
- Invalid question/options

title: SUSHI Tokenomics Restructure: SUSHI Reserve, Revised xSUSHI Buybacks, and Protocol-Deployed Liquidity Deployment to Robinhood Chain [Implementation]
body:
This proposal’s expectation is to produce an implementation. Full details and discussions thus far can be found at:

[https://forum.sushi.com/discussion/1313076-sushi-tokenomics-restructure-sushi-reserve-revised-xsushi-buybacks-and-protocoldeployed-liquidity-deployment-to-robinhood-chain](https://forum.sushi.com/discussion/1313076-sushi-tokenomics-restructure-sushi-reserve-revised-xsushi-buybacks-and-protocoldeployed-liquidity-deployment-to-robinhood-chain)

# TL;DR

-   Sushi’s current protocol fee model directs value primarily toward **xSUSHI buybacks**. This proposal would replace that structure with a more balanced framework supporting stakers, protocol reserves, and Sushi operations.
    
-   We propose to:
    
    1.  Allocate **1% of protocol fees**, plus **1% of all perpetuals fee revenue**, to **monthly xSUSHI buybacks**.
        
    2.  Allocate **4% of protocol fees** to **weekly SUSHI purchases** for a new **SUSHI Reserve**, with purchased SUSHI held as protocol-controlled reserves.
        
    3.  Direct **all remaining protocol fees, migration fees, and other protocol revenue to Sushi Ops** to fund development, incentives, partnerships, liquidity initiatives, security, and operations.
        
    4.  Authorize the relocation of a portion of Sushi’s **protocol-deployed liquidity currently held on EVM networks** to **Robinhood Chain**, beginning with an **ETH–USDG V3 position**.
        
-   Sushi’s initial target is approximately **$10–20 million of protocol-deployed TVL on Robinhood Chain**, with deployments executed in tranches and limited to Sushi protocol pools.
    
-   Historical LP claims established through the **MasterChef LP Migration framework remain unchanged and fully preserved**. Relocation does not increase, decrease, dilute, or otherwise modify any historical LP entitlement.
    

## Fee Scope and Effective Application

**The fee-routing framework approved by this proposal is intended to apply to both currently accrued and all future protocol revenue.**

Specifically, upon implementation, the approved allocations will apply to:

-   **all protocol fees already accrued and held by or for Sushi that have not yet been distributed under the existing fee-routing framework;**
    
-   **all accrued and undistributed perpetuals fee revenue;**
    
-   **all accrued and undistributed migration fees and other protocol revenue; and**
    
-   **all protocol fees, perpetuals fee revenue, migration fees, and other protocol revenue generated or received following implementation of this proposal.**
    

Accordingly, approval is intended to authorize the new fee-routing framework for **existing accrued and undistributed balances as well as revenue accruing on a going-forward basis**, rather than applying only to fees generated after the date of implementation.

# Proposed Fee Routing

### xSUSHI Buybacks

-   **1% of protocol fees**
    
-   **Plus 1% of all perpetuals fee revenue**
    
-   Executed **monthly**
    

This preserves a revenue-backed incentive for SUSHI holders who stake through xSUSHI while reducing the share of protocol revenue committed to buybacks.

### SUSHI Reserve

-   **4% of protocol fees**
    
-   Used to purchase SUSHI **weekly**
    
-   Purchased SUSHI would be retained as **protocol-controlled reserves**
    
-   Reserve purchases and cumulative holdings would be reported through a **public dashboard**
    

The SUSHI Reserve is a protocol treasury function and is not intended as a mechanism to support or influence the market price of SUSHI.

### Sushi Ops

**All remaining protocol fees, migration fees, and other protocol revenue** would be directed to Sushi Ops to fund:

-   Development
    
-   Incentives
    
-   Partnerships
    
-   Liquidity initiatives
    
-   Security
    
-   Operations
    

Sushi Ops may also execute additional discretionary SUSHI purchases. Any formal or recurring framework governing additional Ops-funded buybacks would be addressed through a separate proposal.

# Protocol-Deployed Liquidity

Alongside the fee-routing restructure, this proposal would authorize the relocation of a portion of the approximately **$25 million of protocol-deployed liquidity currently held on EVM networks following the MasterChef LP migration**.

The initial target would be approximately **$10–20 million of protocol-deployed TVL on Robinhood Chain**, beginning with an:

**ETH–USDG V3 position**

An initial candidate for relocation is the existing **Ethereum mainnet DAI–ETH deployed position**, currently representing approximately **$8 million in TVL**.

Additional positions may be considered where they:

-   See minimal trading activity
    
-   Contain outdated, deprecated, or migrating assets
    
-   Carry elevated asset, liquidity, migration, or technical risk
    
-   Have limited relevance to Sushi’s current liquidity infrastructure or ecosystem objectives
    

Relocation would prioritize destination pairs with **like-kind exposure** and would be executed in **tranches**.

Protocol-deployed liquidity authorized under this proposal would remain within **Sushi protocol pools** and would not be lent, leveraged, or used as collateral.

# Historical LP Claims

This proposal **does not terminate, impair, reduce, dilute, or otherwise modify historical LP claims** created through the MasterChef LP migration.

Historical LP claim entitlements remain fixed at their established basis regardless of where protocol-deployed liquidity is located.

Valid claims would continue to be fulfilled through the existing withdrawal or proportional unwinding mechanisms. If fulfilling a valid historical LP claim conflicts with maintaining a deployed position, **claim fulfilment takes priority**, and the position may be unwound to the extent required.

No historical LP claimant acquires a pro-rata economic interest in, or entitlement to the performance of, any particular protocol-deployed position as a result of this proposal.

# This Signal Covers

This Signal seeks community approval for:

-   The revised **xSUSHI buyback allocation**
    
-   Creation and funding of the **SUSHI Reserve**
    
-   Allocation of **remaining protocol revenue to Sushi Ops**
    
-   Application of the approved fee-routing framework to **currently accrued and undistributed revenue and all future revenue**
    
-   Relocation of eligible protocol-deployed liquidity to **Robinhood Chain**
    
-   An initial target of approximately **$10–20 million in protocol-deployed TVL**
    
-   An initial **ETH–USDG V3 deployment**
    
-   Continued administration of deployed liquidity under the existing MasterChef LP migration framework and its historical LP claim protections
    

_This proposal does_ **_not_** _extinguish, impair, or modify any historical LP withdrawal or claim rights established under the MasterChef LP Migration framework. It also does not guarantee any level of trading volume, fee generation, yield, protocol revenue, or token-price performance._

Full proposal details and community discussion can be viewed in the forum post attached to this Snapshot vote.

title: SIP-3 Proposal: Allocate $SOSO Tokens to Power ValueChain Ecosystem Growth
body:
# Summary
 
This proposal requests community approval for a one-time allocation of 50,000,000 $SOSO (5% of the total token supply) from the Ecosystem Fund reserve to the dedicated ValueChain Ecosystem Incentive Treasury. The allocated tokens will be migrated to the ValueChain mainnet through official channels as ValueChain-native $SOSO, and will remain in the Treasury until distributed as ecosystem incentives.

The funds will be used exclusively to accelerate the growth and enhance the security of the ValueChain ecosystem, including but not limited to:
-   User and growth incentives for ecosystem protocols, including SoDEX and Tigris Protocol;
-   Incentives to attract more protocols and builders to deploy on ValueChain;
-   Validator set expansion and staking incentives to strengthen network security.  
    This initiative aims to convert reserved tokens into productive capital that deepens the ValueChain ecosystem — the foundation of $SOSO's long-term value.  

# Background  

ValueChain began with a simple aim: to be the best place to trade and invest on-chain, with SoDEX as its flagship decentralized exchange. That aim has since grown into something larger — building ValueChain into the Layer 1 for on-chain wealth management, enabling everyone to easily access global capital markets and assets.  

Achieving this larger vision depends on one thing above all: a thriving ValueChain ecosystem. ValueChain and the protocols built on it are the cornerstone of $SOSO's value — every new protocol deployed, every new asset brought on-chain, and every new validator strengthens the fundamental demand for $SOSO as the network's gas, staking, and governance asset. To move the ecosystem from "successfully launched" to "flourishing," we need to commit further resources to ecosystem incentives.  

# Proposal  

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Allocation Amount | 50,000,000 $SOSO (5% of the total token supply) |
| Source | Ecosystem Fund Allocation |
| Destination | ValueChain Ecosystem Incentive Treasury (multi-sig) |

Total Allocation: 5% of the total token supply.  
Execution Method: The allocated tokens will be migrated to the ValueChain mainnet through official channels as ValueChain-native $SOSO, ensuring transparency and security of fund usage.  
The ValueChain Ecosystem Incentive Treasury will fund initiatives including, but not limited to:

1.  User and Growth Incentives for Ecosystem Protocols: Trading, liquidity, and adoption incentives across ValueChain-native protocols — including SoDEX (spot, perpetuals, vaults) and Tigris Protocol (community-curated asset listing) — to reward genuine usage and deepen on-chain liquidity.

2.  Ecosystem Expansion: Grants, liquidity support, and deployment incentives to attract more third-party protocols, builders, and asset issuers to ValueChain, expanding the range of applications and global assets living on-chain.

3.  Network Security and Validator Expansion: Incentives to grow the validator set and reward $SOSO staking, raising the network's security threshold and advancing progressive decentralization as the value secured on ValueChain grows.  

# Rationale  
A public chain's long-term value is determined by the vitality of its ecosystem and the security of its network. This proposal is designed to reinforce both.  

From Launch to Growth: The initial ecosystem resources approved by community governance secured ValueChain's launch and bootstrapped its early economy. The next stage of the flywheel — more users, more protocols, more assets — requires sustained incentives. This dedicated treasury provides the ecosystem with predictable, long-term growth capital rather than one-off campaigns.  

Attracting Protocols and Builders: ValueChain's vision as the Layer 1 for on-chain wealth management can only be realized by a rich ecosystem of protocols and on-chain assets. Deployment and growth incentives attract builders and asset issuers to choose ValueChain, accelerating the network effect that benefits every participant.  

Strengthening Network Security: ValueChain utilizes a Proof-of-Stake consensus mechanism, where security depends directly on the total value staked. As more assets, including real-world assets, live on ValueChain, the network's security threshold must be raised in lock-step. Expanding the validator set and incentivizing staking safeguards all users' assets and continues our progressive decentralization roadmap.  

Alignment with Long-Term Interests: The tokens will not enter circulation as a result of this allocation: they will remain in the multi-sig Treasury and be released strategically and in phases, only as incentives are actually earned and distributed.  

# Implementation  

If this proposal is passed, the Foundation will execute the following steps:
    
1.  Token Allocation: The Foundation will execute a transaction via a multi-sig wallet to allocate 50,000,000 $SOSO (5% of the total supply) from the Ecosystem Fund reserve.
    
2.  Asset Cross-Chain Migration: The allocated tokens will be migrated to the ValueChain mainnet through the official migration channel as ValueChain-native $SOSO.
    
3.  Fund Allocation: The tokens will be transferred to the ValueChain Ecosystem Incentive Treasury, a dedicated multi-sig treasury. The specific allocation plans for these funds (e.g., incentive programs, reward weights, distribution cycles) will be determined and announced through subsequent governance and official channels.
    
4.  Transparency Report: All relevant transaction hashes and addresses will be publicly disclosed to the community upon execution to ensure a fully transparent process.  

# Voting  

- For - I agree to allocate 50,000,000 $SOSO (5% of the total supply) from the Ecosystem Fund to the ValueChain Ecosystem Incentive Treasury.  
- Against - I do not agree with this proposal.  
- Abstain – I have no opinion on this proposal.

title: Snapshot 14: Expansion of tETH Strategy to Compound V3
body:
## Summary

This proposal seeks DAO approval to integrate Compound V3's WETH market on Ethereum as an additional lending venue within the tETH yield strategy.

The integration follows tETH's existing Market Efficiency Yield (MEY) approach:

-   Supply **wstETH** as collateral
    
-   Borrow **WETH** at rates below staking yield
    
-   Convert borrowed WETH back into wstETH to increase staking exposure
    

The objective is to improve yield efficiency and capital utilization of tETH by expanding access to lending liquidity, while preserving existing leverage structures, safety parameters, and risk controls.

## Motivation

As tETH's TVL grows, the protocol's ability to efficiently deploy capital across MEY strategies depends on access to sufficient lending liquidity at competitive borrow rates. Expanding to additional venues improves capital efficiency and reduces single-venue concentration risk.

Compound V3 is a lending protocol on Ethereum that structures each market around a single borrowable base asset, with multiple supported collateral assets. The Compound V3 WETH market (cWETHv3) accepts wstETH as collateral to borrow WETH, supporting the mechanism that underpins tETH's MEY strategy.

Integrating Compound V3 is expected to:

-   Expand the protocol's access to WETH lending liquidity across an additional established market
    
-   Improve capital efficiency by enabling allocation when Compound V3 offers favorable borrow rates relative to existing venues
    
-   Diversify MEY exposure across a broader set of lending protocols, reducing single-venue concentration risk
    
-   Strengthen the protocol's contribution to rate convergence across a wider portion of the Ethereum lending market
    

## Specification

If approved, this proposal will:

-   Integrate the Compound V3 WETH market (cWETHv3) as an active MEY venue  
    (Market address: 0xA17581A9E3356d9A858b789D68B4d866e593aE94)
    
    -   Supply wstETH as collateral
        
    -   Borrow WETH against it at prevailing market rates
        
    -   Convert borrowed WETH back into wstETH to maintain LST exposure
        
-   Allocate capital dynamically alongside existing venues, subject to prevailing market conditions and internal risk parameters
    

The DAO retains authority to revise allocation parameters through future governance proposals.

## Risk Considerations

The integration introduces exposure to the following risks:

-   Smart contract risk specific to Compound V3
    
-   Oracle risk within the Compound V3 WETH market
    
-   Variable borrow rate risk
    
-   Liquidity and utilization conditions within the Compound V3 WETH market
    

**Mitigations**

-   Existing collateral ratios and leverage limits are preserved across all venues
    
-   Dynamic capital allocation allows the protocol to reduce or exit exposure if borrow rates or risk conditions deteriorate
    
-   Ongoing monitoring of utilization, borrow rates, and position risk metrics across all active venues
    
-   DAO authority to adjust the Compound V3 allocation through governance
    

## Implementation

If approved, the DAO assigns Treehouse Protocol to:

1.  Finalize integration parameters for the Compound V3 WETH market, including collateral ratios, leverage limits, and initial allocation ranges
    
2.  Update strategy execution logic to incorporate Compound V3 as an active MEY venue
    
3.  Update the Proof of Reserves dashboard to reflect positions held on Compound V3
    
4.  Monitor yield performance, borrow rate dynamics, and position risk metrics across all active venues on an ongoing basis
    

No structural redesign of the tETH strategy is required.

## Voting Options

-   For — Approve the integration of Compound V3 as an active MEY venue within the tETH strategy
    
-   Against — Reject the proposal
    
-   Abstain — Record sentiment without voting for or against
    

## Vote Outcomes

**If FOR passes:**  
Compound V3 will be integrated as an active MEY venue within the tETH strategy, with capital allocated dynamically alongside existing venues under existing risk parameters.

**If AGAINST passes:**  
No changes will be made to the current tETH strategy venues.

**If ABSTAIN:**  
No direct effect; recorded for sentiment but not counted toward quorum.

title: ENA Fee Switch
body:
In collaboration with the Ethena Risk Committee, we propose the following milestones for ENA fee switch activation. These milestones will be subject to an ENA tokenholder vote, which will follow immediately after this post.

For the avoidance of doubt, these milestones would replace any suggested parameters previously suggested by the Risk Committee.

Under the proposed schedule, the share of protocol revenue directed to ENA buybacks increases at each USDe circulating supply milestone, and is set intentionally to support aggressive growth back to the heights of 2025 at ~$15b of USDe supply. This is reflected in the “growth mode” categorization in the table below.

This balances the need to continue capturing the market opportunity we see ahead by growing USDe to >$100b in the next 5 years with value accrual to the broader ecosystem.

The proposed milestones for ENA buybacks are listed in the below table:

![35 (1).png](ipfs://bafybeihvrhikyxcbq5oloza45kjlqu5ac742uj7xffuneg7nze34eq4mlm)

Ethena currently has 3 core business lines:
i) Ethena USDe savings
ii) Ethena Whitelabel stablecoins
iii) Ethena [X] - launching next week

Once the first milestone laid out above is hit, 95% of the net revenue from each of these business lines - which is paid to the Ethena Foundation - would be directed to ENA buybacks. These accumulated buybacks will be tracked in our transparency dashboard here:
https://app.ethena.fi/dashboards/transparency

The buyback rate schedule, the milestone thresholds and the buyback mechanics have all been signed off by the Risk Committee and are now live for vote and implementation.

The vote link will be posted in the replies of this post, as well as the supporting analysis by the Ethena Risk Committee. If the vote passes, ENA buybacks will begin when the above milestones are reached.

title: First Draft: 90-Day Validation Extension
body:
This proposal requests a 90-day extension of the First Draft FI at 50% of the previous budget.

After reviewing the results of the previous FI with Miriam and discussing them with Ops, we agreed that while the technology side delivered strongly, the commercial operation did not produce the expected outcomes.

The main issue identified was that distribution, lead generation, discovery, pipeline and other client-facing processes were delegated across different people without first having a single tested strategy and clear end-to-end ownership.

For the next 90 days, I will take ownership of the full First Draft process, from edition generation and distribution through outreach, discovery, pipeline and proposals. Each process will only be handed back to Ops once it has been tested, optimized and shown to work consistently.

Accountability:

* Weekly funnel scoreboard
* Day 45 checkpoint
* Final 90-day review
* Ben, and Marco as reviewers
* If meaningful acquisition signals are not present by Day 45, reviewers may recommend stopping the FI

The goal is to prove or disprove First Draft as a repeatable acquisition channel before moving into the permanent Ops role contemplated in the recently approved Snapshot.

**Full proposal:**
https://docs.google.com/document/u/1/d/1g23-KK4_RviYy_Y_tqNYOV5rR6bRMT3jX4vGtvUwheo/mobilebasic

title: CIP-13: Encumbered
body:
### Summary
The holders of Captain & Company tokens (the "Tokenholders") propose the below change to how cargo weight affects a ship at sea.

Today a hold is a hard wall in some places and no wall at all in others. Goods bought at an island tradepost and cargo loaded at the docks are both refused once the hold is full, but plunder taken at sea is not. A crew that wins a rich fight sails home carrying more than the hull was ever meant to hold, and pays nothing for it.

This choice replaces that inconsistency with a single rule that applies everywhere: a ship can always be overloaded, and an overloaded ship is slower.

### Proposal: Add the Encumbered Debuff

Cargo capacity would stop being a refusal and start being a threshold.

A ship carrying at or below its hold capacity sails exactly as it does today, with no change whatsoever. A ship carrying more than its capacity becomes Encumbered, and its top speed falls as the excess grows. The further past the line, the slower the ship.

The debuff would scale continuously rather than in steps, so there is no single unit of cargo that suddenly halves a ship's speed, and no reward for shaving one crate off a load. It would be capped at a floor speed, so an overloaded ship is always slow but never stranded.

Hold capacities are unchanged by this proposal:

* Raft, 5 units
* Dinghy, 32 units
* Freeblade Sloop, 80 units
* Clockwork Brig, 160 units
* Wraith Brig, 200 units

Doubloons continue to occupy one unit per 250 aboard. Every other commodity continues to weigh one unit each.

The hard refusals at the tradepost and at the docks would be lifted, because there is no longer a reason to refuse a load the player is willing to be slowed by. Both surfaces would show the resulting speed penalty before the player commits.

### Rationale
The current design punishes planning and ignores luck. A captain who thinks ahead and buys cargo is stopped at the hold's edge. A captain who stumbles into a large payout sails away at full speed with a hold that should be groaning. The second captain is the one the rule was written for and the one it never touches.

Making weight cost speed rather than block a transaction fixes both halves at once. The cap stops being an arbitrary wall and becomes a real decision: take the extra plunder and sail home slowly through hostile water, or leave it and run. That decision is more interesting than an error message, and it is the decision the fiction has been promising since the first hold was drawn.

It also gives the extraction run genuine tension. A heavy ship is a slow ship, a slow ship is a catchable ship, and a catchable ship makes every other captain's afternoon. Risk that the player chose is better than risk the game assigned.

### Implications
* Cargo capacity becomes a speed threshold rather than a hard limit
* An overloaded ship is slower, continuously, with a floor so it can still sail
* Buying at an island and loading at the docks would no longer be refused for a full hold
* Both surfaces would show the speed cost before the player commits
* Plunder taken at sea would carry the same weight consequence as cargo bought or loaded, which it does not today
* Hold capacities, doubloon weight and commodity weight are all unchanged
* Extraction runs become more dangerous for the crews carrying the most

### Options
1. Add the Encumbered Debuff
2. Reject

### Test Cases
n/a

https://docs.capnco.gg

title: PGP-45 | OTC Buyback & Burn of 100M PRL from Mimo Labs
body:
Summary:  
This proposal authorizes the DAO, with the support of Cooper Labs, to acquire 100,000,000 PRL (in the form of sPRL1) from Mimo Labs through an OTC swap funded by the DAO Treasury, and to burn the full amount immediately upon settlement. The swap will be priced at the average PRL market price over the 14 days preceding the publication of this proposal.  
  
Rationale:  
The DAO has committed to burning 50% of the total PRL supply (500,000,000 PRL). Three proposals have driven progress toward this milestone:  
- PGP-37 (Phase I) burned 26,371,873.81 PRL through one-time operations.  
- PIP-65 accelerated the end of the MIMO→PRL migration, resulting in the permanent burn of 370,925,853.61 PRL.  
- PGP-40 (Phase II) shifted from one-time burns to recurring, protocol-native burn flows: monthly buybacks, sPRL1 slashing burns, and unclaimed PAR recycling.  
  
A total of 435,279,031.37 PRL (39.7% of total supply) has been burned to date, leaving 64,720,968.63 PRL to reach the 50% milestone.  
Acquiring and burning (in the form of sPRL1) 100,000,000 PRL from Mimo Labs in a single transaction would bring the total burned to 564,720,968.63 PRL, or 56.47% of total supply. Combined with the recurring burn flows already in place through PGP-40 and PGP-42, this puts the 50% milestone reached.  
  
An OTC swap is the appropriate structure for a transaction of this size. Purchasing 100M PRL on the open market would have a significant price impact and would take an extended period to execute. Settling directly with Mimo Labs removes a large portion of the circulating supply in a single transaction, with zero slippage and no market disruption, and permanently retires these tokens.  
  
Pricing:  
- The swap will be priced using a 14-day TWAP: the average PRL market price over the 14 days preceding the publication of this proposal. From August 12 to August 25, 2026: 0.001278 USD  
- The resulting reference price and total settlement amount will be published in this thread before the Snapshot vote opens: 127,800.00 USD  
  
Means:  
- Human Resources: Multisigners will need to sign and execute the swap-and-burn transactions.  
- Treasury Resources: 127,800.00 worth of USDC and/or USDp from the DAO Treasury equivalent to 100,000,000 PRL at the 14-day TWAP reference price.  
  
Technical Implementation:  
- Execute the OTC swap between the DAO Treasury and Mimo Labs: the Treasury transfers the settlement amount, and Mimo Labs transfers 100,000,000 sPRL1.  
- Unstake the full 100,000,000 sPRL1 for PRL and burn them.  
  
Voting Options:  
- For the 100M sPRL1 OTC Buyback & Burn  
- Against / Rework the Proposal  
- Abstain  
  
Author(s): Cooper Labs

title: [BIP-926] Treasury Council Resignation: Xeonus, Successor Nomination of zekraken
body:
## Summary

I, @Xeonus (`0xaa5af0dd9c52c773d36cdbc509a0b2a1ded4c196`), am proposing my resignation from the Balancer Treasury Council (TC), effective as of the date this vote passes, and am nominating @zekraken (`0xBCC63E9c0a486D10Cdb8617242507733fEF1d792`) as my successor to fill the resulting seat.

## Motivation and Context

The Treasury Council was introduced in BIP-882 to ensure that, within the corporate structure of the Balancer Foundation, ecosystem interests are represented and protected. Its current 7 member, 5/7 threshold composition was most recently reaffirmed in BIP-918.

I have served as a TC member since its formation. After this period of service, I have decided to step down from the Council and am proposing @zekraken as my successor to maintain continuity of representation, community familiarity, and operational knowledge within the TC.

This proposal does not change the size of the Council (7 members) or its approval threshold (5/7); it is a like for like seat replacement.

## Specification

1. I resign from the Treasury Council effective on the date this BIP passes.
2. @zekraken (`0xBCC63E9c0a486D10Cdb8617242507733fEF1d792`) is appointed to my vacated Treasury Council seat, effective on the same date.
3. The Treasury Council composition, size (7), and threshold (5/7) remain otherwise unchanged.

## Treasury Council Composition Update

**Current (per BIP-918):**

| Member | Address |
|----|----|
| @0xDanko | `0x122AFb4667C5f80e45721a42C7c81e9140C62FA4` |
| @Xeonus | `0xaa5af0dd9c52c773d36cdbc509a0b2a1ded4c196` |
| @danielmk | `0x7984aB7e6B51A50d970b74a437BC82156753b866` |
| @mendesfabio | `0xF162D64Cab37fD3335122024f23680AF7cf067ad` |
| @gosuto | `0x11e450c72c2258ec792d5f64a263ecb18e8c0f06` |
| @Marcus | `0xb7364Fca20EEC90f51b158C05199044AD362b675` |
| @franzns | `0xA574Af018138bBC2bf065f68015687Aa67388A2A` |

**Proposed change:**

| Out | In |
|----|----|
| @Xeonus (`0xaa5af0dd9c52c773d36cdbc509a0b2a1ded4c196`) (me) | @zekraken (`0xBCC63E9c0a486D10Cdb8617242507733fEF1d792`) |

Threshold remains 5/7 post swap.

## Technical Specification

Execution consists of a single `swapOwner()` call on the Treasury Council Safe, following the same pattern used for the signer swaps documented in BIP-918:

| Chain | Safe | Old Owner | New Owner |
|----|----|----|----|
| Ethereum Mainnet | Treasury Council Safe | `0xaa5af0dd9c52c773d36cdbc509a0b2a1ded4c196` (@Xeonus) | `0xBCC63E9c0a486D10Cdb8617242507733fEF1d792` (@zekraken) |

The Safe threshold is not modified by this transaction.

## Signature Verification

@zekraken has signed a message confirming ownership and control of the new signer address, verifiable via Etherscan's Verified Signatures tool:

[Verify Signature on Etherscan](https://etherscan.io/verifiedSignatures)

## Risks and Mitigations

* **Continuity risk:** Mitigated by proposing a successor concurrently with my resignation, avoiding any period where the Council operates below its intended composition.
* **Threshold integrity:** Unaffected, the swap preserves the existing 5/7 threshold and 7 member size.
* **Address verification:** @zekraken's new signer address (`0xBCC63E9c0a486D10Cdb8617242507733fEF1d792`) has been confirmed via a verified Etherscan signature, removing any risk of address error prior to payload execution.

## References

* [BIP-882](https://claude.ai/chat/6e13156b-f5d5-4f56-9c52-c1eac9d53eac#) — Transitioning Onchain Operations of the Balancer DAO to Balancer Onchain Limited
* [BIP-918](https://claude.ai/chat/6e13156b-f5d5-4f56-9c52-c1eac9d53eac#) — Operational Restructuring for Balancer
choices: No, this is not the way

title: [BIP-927] Revoke Unused V2 Vault Permissions from Deprecated Relayers
body:
# TL;DR

On all chains, revoke leftover permissions on the V2 vault for relayers that are deprecated or no longer used. Only the latest `20231031-batch-relayer-v6/BalancerRelayer` is left intact.

# Motivation

The V2 vault still grants `swap`, `batchSwap`, `joinPool`, `exitPool`, `manageUserBalance`, and/or `setRelayerApproval` to several relayers that have been deprecated or are no longer in use. They are leftover from old frontend paths and third-party integrations. Revoking them is good security practice and falls in line with the general sunsetting of V2.

CoW Protocol has deprecated API orders that settle via Balancer's internal balances / `batchSwap` on `cow/vault_relayer`. The `CronV1Relayer` has had no onchain activity since February 2024. `20210812-lido-relayer/LidoRelayer` and the batch relayers v1/v2/v3/v4/v5 are already deprecated deployments.

# Technical Specifications

Call `Authorizer.revokeRole(actionId, account)` for any of the six roles mentioned above for the following accounts (followed by all applicable chain ids):

* `20211203-batch-relayer/BalancerRelayer` (1, 137, 42161)
* `20220318-batch-relayer-v2/BalancerRelayer` (137)
* `20220720-batch-relayer-v3/BalancerRelayer` (1, 10, 137, 42161)
* `20220916-batch-relayer-v4/BalancerRelayer` (1, 10, 100, 137, 42161)
* `20230314-batch-relayer-v5/BalancerRelayer` (1, 10, 100, 137, 8453, 42161, 43114)
* `cow/vault_relayer` (1)
* `20210812-lido-relayer/LidoRelayer` (1)
* `CronV1Relayer` (1)

# References

* [https://docs-v2.balancer.fi/reference/authorizer/](https://docs-v2.balancer.fi/reference/authorizer/)
choices: No, this is not the way

title: ether.fi DAO Proposal: Programmatic ETHFI Buybacks & Ecosystem Growth
body:
## Summary

This proposal aims to achieve two main objectives

1.  Confirm the revenue contributed to the Foundation from Labs will be used to purchase ETHFI programmatically
    
2.  Denominate all user rewards in ETHFI, primarily acquired on the open market, so that reward distributions are funded by purchases rather than new issuance.
    

The core principle of this proposal is to support the usage and adoption of the ether.fi protocol while continuing to build a sustainable treasury model for the ether.fi Foundation through a net accumulation of ETHFI.

**Revenue contribution:**

ether.fi Labs will contribute monthly protocol revenue to the Foundation, which will use this revenue to buy ETHFI on chain via automated TWAPs pending this vote. The contribution of revenue from Labs will come from a share of the following revenue streams: interchange on card, swap volume, and staking revenue, which would’ve been ~$1.33M based on last month's numbers (subject to market conditions). Borrow revenue will also be included once total borrow volume reaches $50M (currently sitting at ~$250M in supplied capital in the market with $26M borrowed), along with other revenue lines in the future, which would include perps. These streams will be additive to the total as they ramp. Execution of these buys in the Foundation will not be discretionary, they will be programmatic. They will occur on a weekly cadence, resulting in linear buybacks of ETHFI over time.

**Mechanics:**

Moving forward, every reward on ether.fi will be paid in ETHFI. Here is an illustrative example: a user makes a $10,000 swap, which pays a $50 fee (50bps). That fee splits three ways:

| Fee leg | Share | $ on this swap | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Labs | 40% | $20 | Revenue to Labs to cover operating and infrastructure expenses |
| Buyback | 30% | $15 | Buys ETHFI on market, held in the Foundation treasury |
| User cashback | 30% | $15 | Buys ETHFI on market, delivered to the user as cashback |

Net effect of that one swap: $30 of ETHFI bought on chain, $15 of ETHFI shipped to the user. With this proposal, the result is a buy back of 30bps of volume, and a reward back to the user of 15bps, two tokens purchased for every one distributed. Perps and lending will run a similar split at their own fee levels.

Card cashback will be the same mechanism at a larger scale, paid in ETHFI acquired on the open market and funded from card revenue, staking revenue, and the fee funded buyback pool above, at rates the Foundation will set to target net ETHFI accumulation. The Foundation covers any remainder of ETHFI needed. It will do this by starting with a max of 20M ETHFI backup buffer which this proposal authorizes. This buffer comes from ETHFI the Foundation already holds. No new ETHFI is minted and circulating supply does not increase from this proposal. Rewards are funded first by on market purchases, meaning the program distributes ETHFI it has purchased. This top-up shrinks over time as the fee funded legs grow with volume and revenue.

The driving target of the program will be that ETHFI purchased by the Foundation on the market through revenue contributed from Labs meets or exceeds total ETHFI sold from distributions**.** We modelled this with conservative assumptions by assuming most cashback is sold immediately (which historically has not held true when looking at WETH distributed as cashback), and it runs near neutral even under this imperfect scenario. Membership staking, which the model excludes as a margin of safety, is what pushes it well into green. If net flow drifts negative, the Foundation can revisit the levers: cashback rates, fee splits, deployment pace. The dashboard published will outline ETHFI bought and ETHFI distributed.

![Buyback flow.png](ipfs://bafkreidexlykberh5xkr65pzihcw3nzrfuhdis6rluttmbd3bapb43e454)

Interchange settles in fiat, so the flow is collect and forward rather than a switch in a contract. Each week Labs aggregates the contribution, converts it to USDC, and sends it on-chain to a published Foundation address, and the Foundation will execute the buys as TWAP orders on CoW Swap. Both addresses will be published at launch, and the dashboard ties each week together: revenue reported, amount transferred, ETHFI bought. Any mismatch between a transfer and that week's revenue is visible on chain the same week.

**Further alignment through memberships:**

Building on this, and since the launch of ether.fi summer, staking ETHFI into account vaults is becoming a core path for users to gain membership benefits. The ETHFI a user earns as cashback now has an immediate use that rewards holding it. Spending earns ETHFI, staked ETHFI improves membership, and better membership drives more spend by making the user's card top of wallet.

Since announcing the new membership structure, ETHFI staked in ether.fi account vaults has grown from roughly 21M ETHFI to 28M ETHFI, an increase of ~7.2M ETHFI in fifteen days. We see a strong correlation with users choosing to accumulate ETHFI for membership, and none of that staking demand is counted in the net flow example above.

**Summary:**

Protocol revenue now translates directly into automatic ETHFI purchases in the Foundation, and the incentive budget grows the revenue that funds it. Rewards are paid in ETHFI, largely paid from buys in market, and memberships gives that ETHFI a reason to stay within the app. Rewards are funded first by on market ETHFI purchases with a 20M ETHFI backup buffer from existing Foundation holdings, meaning no new ETHFI enters circulation. All discretionary decisions are removed: ETHFI purchase mandate is fixed, execution will be on chain, and the dashboard shows every dollar in and every ETHFI out.

**Vote**

FOR: Approve (1) ongoing Labs revenue contributions to the Foundation to be used for programmatic ETHFI buybacks via automated TWAPs, with purchased ETHFI held in the Foundation treasury or distributed as user rewards under the program described above; and (2) authorization of up to 20M ETHFI from the Foundation's existing treasury (no new ETHFI minted) to fund user rewards and ecosystem incentives, to be managed with the target of net ETHFI accumulation over time.

**AGAINST**: Do not approve.

title: Bonding Curve Protocol Upgrade Proposal (DDD-9360v3)
body:
**DDD-9360v3** is an acceleration upgrade to the **Bonding Curve Protocol v2.0 (DDD-9360v2).** The upgraded system is designed to accelerate the distribution of DNA through a controlled swap price range of **$0.10 to $0.20, with $0.01 price intervals,** while preserving the listing price established by the **final price of Bonding Curve v2.0.**

The V3.0 mechanism does not redefine, reset, or replace the listing price established under Bonding Curve v2.0. Instead, it introduces an accelerated distribution phase intended to facilitate the decentralized distribution of the remaining public DNA allocation.

**Price and Listing Mechanism**
**For clarity:**
1. If Bonding Curve v2.0 (DDD-9360v2) reaches a final price of $3.30 before the upgrade, the listing price will remain $3.30, regardless of the subsequent swap price range under Bonding Curve v3.0.
2. Under Bonding Curve v3.0, DNA swaps are accelerated through a price range of $0.10 to $0.20, with $0.01 intervals.
3. The $0.10–$0.20 range is an acceleration-phase swap mechanism and is not the market listing price.
4. The final price established under Bonding Curve v2.0 is treated as the locked listing-price reference for the subsequent market listing.
5. Bonding Curve v3.0 is designated as the “Acceleration Phase”, intended to accelerate the distribution of DNA and support the transition toward decentralized market participation.

**Reason for the Proposal**
The proposal is introduced based on the following considerations:

1. Bonding Curve v1.0 (DDD-9360) and Bonding Curve v2.0 (DDD-9360v2) have been operating for approximately six months in aggregate, yet only around 10% of the total public DNA allocation has been distributed.
2. Approximately 90% of the public allocation remains undistributed, resulting in a significant portion of the public allocation remaining within the bonding curve mechanism.
3. The maximum targeted listing date is December 12, 2027. Based on the current distribution rate and the remaining allocation, the existing mechanism is not mathematically expected to distribute the full public allocation by the target date.
4. An acceleration mechanism is therefore proposed to improve distribution efficiency and allow the protocol to progress toward its intended market-listing phase within the available timeframe.

**Developer Proposal**
The Developer proposes to upgrade the Bonding Curve Protocol to **its third version, DDD-9360v3.**

The upgrade modifies the bonding curve contract deployed at:
**0x8401A29293C5394A880856031b25C8Ee8810A2D0**

The proposed upgrade is subject to DAO approval, requiring a minimum of 50.01% YES votes within seven (7) days of the proposal, in accordance with the applicable governance requirements.

**Scope of the Upgrade**
The Bonding Curve v3.0 upgrade includes the following changes:

**1. No Reset of Bonding Curve History**
The upgrade does not reset the existing Bonding Curve v2.0 distribution history, accumulated state, or established final price.
**2. Listing Price Preservation**
The listing price remains based on the final price established by Bonding Curve v2.0 prior to the V3.0 upgrade.
**3. Acceleration Swap Mechanism**
DNA swaps under V3.0 are redirected to an accelerated price range of $0.10–$0.20, with $0.01 intervals, to encourage faster distribution of the remaining public allocation.
**4. Re-Architected Mathematical Model**
V3.0 introduces a revised mathematical model governing price progression and swap behavior during the acceleration phase.
**5. Distribution-Focused Design**
The V3.0 mechanism is designed primarily to accelerate token distribution rather than to establish a new market valuation for DNA.

**Objectives**
The primary objectives of Bonding Curve v3.0 are:

1. Accelerate DNA distribution and advance the protocol toward its market-listing phase.
2. Provide a significantly faster distribution mechanism than the existing Bonding Curve v2.0 model.
3. Preserve the V2.0 final price as the locked listing-price reference.
4. Increase the amount of liquidity that can be prepared for future market expansion.
5. Support the transition from bonding-curve distribution toward broader decentralized and centralized market participation.
6. Improve accessibility for later participants while maintaining the established V2.0 listing-price reference.
7. Establish a more decentralized distribution of the public DNA allocation before and during the market-listing phase.

**Expected Benefits**
The proposed upgrade is expected to provide the following benefits:

**1. Faster Distribution**
A lower accelerated swap range may increase participation and improve the rate at which the remaining public DNA allocation is distributed.
**2. Earlier Progress Toward Market Listing**
Faster distribution may allow the protocol to reach its intended listing phase more efficiently.
**3. Future CEX Readiness**
The liquidity structure is designed to provide a dedicated allocation for potential future Centralized Exchange (CEX) listings.
**4. Greater Accessibility for Late Participants**
The acceleration phase may provide additional access to DNA for participants who did not participate during the earlier bonding curve phases.
**5. Broader Decentralized Distribution**
Increasing the number of distributed tokens may reduce concentration of the remaining public allocation within the bonding curve mechanism and strengthen decentralized participation.
**6. Improved Governance Participation**
A broader token distribution may potentially result in wider participation in governance during the market-listing and post-listing phases.

**Risks and Trade-offs**
The V3.0 upgrade introduces several risks and trade-offs that should be considered by DAO participants:

**1. Increased Market Volatility**
A significant difference between the accelerated swap range and the locked listing-price reference may create substantial price volatility once DNA begins trading in open markets.
**2. Large Entry-Price Disparity**
Participants who acquired DNA during earlier bonding curve phases may have a substantially higher average acquisition price than participants entering during the V3.0 acceleration phase.
**3. Potential Selling Pressure**
Once DNA becomes freely tradable, participants who acquired tokens during the acceleration phase may realize significant gains relative to their acquisition price, potentially increasing selling pressure.
**4. Market Fragility During Initial Listing**
The difference between available liquidity, market depth, and potential trading demand may result in increased price impact and volatility during the initial market-listing period.
**5. CEX Listing Uncertainty**
The allocation intended for future CEX liquidity does not guarantee that a CEX listing will occur. Any CEX listing remains subject to exchange requirements, market conditions, liquidity requirements, compliance procedures, and other external factors.
**6. Liquidity Deployment Timing**
A portion of the liquidity generated through the bonding curve may remain reserved until an appropriate CEX listing opportunity becomes available.

**Liquidity Management in Bonding Curve v3.0**
Upon completion of the Bonding Curve v3.0 distribution phase and achievement of the applicable listing conditions, the generated liquidity will be allocated as follows:

**1. Initial DEX Liquidity — 40%**
40% of the available bonding-curve liquidity will be allocated toward the initial listing on one or two selected Decentralized Exchanges (DEXs). This allocation is intended to provide the initial market depth required for DNA spot trading and to establish the first open-market liquidity venue.

**2. Future CEX Liquidity Reserve — 60%**
The remaining 60% of the available bonding-curve liquidity will be reserved for potential future Centralized Exchange (CEX) listings. This allocation is intended to support future CEX expansion, including potential Spot and Futures markets, subject to applicable exchange requirements and market conditions. The 60% allocation does not constitute a guarantee of a CEX listing or a guaranteed listing date. The liquidity may remain reserved until a suitable CEX listing opportunity is secured.

**Governance and Approval**
The implementation of Bonding Curve v3.0 is subject to approval through the applicable DAO governance process. The Developer will not unilaterally activate the proposed upgrade if the required governance approval is not obtained.

**Conclusion**
DDD-9360v3 introduces an acceleration-focused modification to the Bonding Curve Protocol designed to improve the distribution efficiency of the remaining public DNA allocation and facilitate progression toward the market-listing phase.

The upgrade does not reset the Bonding Curve v2.0 mechanism and does not replace its established final price as the listing-price reference. Instead, V3.0 introduces a separate acceleration phase in which DNA may be swapped within the $0.10–$0.20 range at $0.01 intervals.

The proposed liquidity structure allocates 40% toward the initial DEX listing and 60% as a reserve for potential future CEX listings. While this structure is intended to provide both immediate DEX liquidity and future CEX readiness, it also acknowledges that CEX listings are external opportunities and therefore cannot be guaranteed.

Overall, DDD-9360v3 is proposed as a mechanism to accelerate decentralized DNA distribution, improve liquidity preparation, and advance the protocol toward open-market participation while explicitly acknowledging the increased volatility, entry-price disparity, liquidity-depth risk, and CEX uncertainty associated with the acceleration strategy.
