title: [Prop 993] Nounworks for Nouns
body:
# Nounworks for Nouns

![hand up ](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/BkBvLQBrMx.jpg)

## Nounworks is a brand building engine for Nouns.

### It is a physical goods / IRL IP and brand development experiment.

### Nounworks acts as a support layer for Nounish builders and the community.

#### Nounworks is powered by Bigshot.WTF, a creative studio with over 20 years of experience building out consumer products and experiences for global brands, entertainment studios and artists.

#### The goal has always been expanding and growing the Nouns brand by supporting our global community. This goal is achieved through the development of physical lifestyle products, activations, global partnership support, unique art and storytelling.

Some of our work to bolster the DAO:

- [Our ongoing NOUNWORKS deck](https://bigshottoyworks.my.canva.site/nounish-friends-2) 
- [Past events and activations](https://bigshottoyworks.my.canva.site/let-klim-cook/#past-events) 
- [Nounworks sizzle reel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qalcPmRLi5E)   
- [Social proof via #noggleseverywhere](https://x.com/hashtag/noggleseverywhere?src=hashtag_click) 
- SnapChat filters [here](https://x.com/bigshottoyworks/status/1948143324596179146) & [here](https://x.com/bigshottoyworks/status/1844526960296460760) 

![Nounsfest](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/SktMiOGIzl.jpg)

# THE PROBLEM:

**NOUNS** is one of the most unique, interesting, and exceptional projects to come out of the web3 space. While the things we have funded and people that we inspired are incredible, we as a community have very little exposure to the world outside of web3. 

We have failed to capture the imaginations of the world simply because we're not getting our stories, projects and message out there in the right ways. 

# OUR GOALS:

Our goal is to build on the work that we have been doing with Nouns, Nounworks and Nounish Friends for the past 5 years. The Nouns brand is poised to expand out of Web3 constraints with our careful planning and execution.  

We will cultivate the Nouns brand into a quirky, family-friendly, easily recognizable positive lifestyle brand - think Sesame Street or Yo Gabba Gabba - with a mix of humor, art and quirky weird fun. 

We will achieve this by leaning into our unique experience and our deep connections in the entertainment and licensing spaces. 

In parallel, we will be supporting and engaging with other builders and aligned Nounish communities. This will create new engagement with new audiences and attract more new holders and active builders.

# OUR PLAN:

Our plan is to push the Nouns IP to specialty retail, gaming and entertainment spaces and beyond. We also will continue our generous and robust support of all of our builders, proposers and creators for events strategic partnerships and global activations with products, creative assets and design support where feasable or requested.

![JUMBO](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/S1pb6YzUGl.webp)

# THE BUILDING BLOCKS:

**Physical goods and useful practical assets:**  High quality collectibles, plush, toys, stationary, IRL events and activations are the fastest way to introduce Nouns to a mainstream, family-friendly audience the same way that PopMart, Funko, and Pudgy Penguins built theirs.  Product-first brands provide unique tangible touch points that help connect people to the brand. Simply having people ask "What are those?" and "where is this from?" ends up elevating Nouns brand recognition.

**Storytelling and entertainment, tools and content:** We are building out high quality digital and physical assets and relationships that will allow us to plug NOUNworks into opportunites in gaming, publishing and other forms of entertainment. This proposal will allow us to build out the tools needed to launch a global entertainment-based IP and build out a licensing portfolio that will generate revenue and future opportunities.

**Infrastructure:** When we establish an infrastructure that supports builders and the development of the Nouns IP as a whole, we all benefit.

# THE WAR CHEST:

By having a creative, production, operations and distribution budget for our products, we will be able to build on and share the project freely without the usual friction. We will be able to quick strike on any opportunities that pop up, as well as offer help to others that may need it. 

We will be able to ship products all over the world to Nounish builders, as well as provide consistently branded assets and creative help as needed.

Those creators can then focus more on building and creating content in the most Nounish ways possible, while staying on-brand. They supplement their own creativity with recognizable Nouns branding and merch. 

This strategy adds value by giving tools to Nounish builders and facilitating memorable activations while helping to accelerate the prolifitation of the brand for everyone.

![image](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/rySHPVFjgg.png)

# THE ASK:

$300,000 (for an 8–12 month program)

## DELIVERABLES:

Below are the essential aspects of building a brand that incorporates physical products. 

***Workstream & Estimated Budgets:***

Total ask $300K
Loose breakdown of numbers:

- Brand / style guide & digital assets: $80K 
- Product development & manufacturing: $100K 
- Warehousing, logistics & distribution: $50K 
- Licensing, retail, events, trade shows: $35K 
- Operations, back end & CX: $35K 
- Social media and marketing 
- Community support and engagement on props as needed 
- CC0 assets and product files  
- Nounworks shop with gated pricing and rev share and links to other builder shops 

Above numbers are estimates; the program needs flexibility to move budget toward opportunities as they arise.

![image](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/BJ-cI4Yixl.png)

## Benefits for the Community:

- Branded, high-quality **products** available to all builders for events and activations around the world at no cost. 
- Cohesive & professional shareable **assets** that are easy to use and utilize (2D graphics and printable assets, 3D media and assets for gaming, entertainment and 3D printing) 
- Comprehensive **style guide** to help present and place product at retail and media partners 
- Shipping and logistics **support** for builders and partners.  
- **Event** support, branding assistance, custom product and assets to make each event unique. 
- **Licensing / retail** facilitation. Exploring real opportunities to support other builders with their dreams 

# SUCCESS METRICS

## Return to the DAO:

We propose a 5% royalty on all Nouns-related licensing deals and product sales generated through this program, paid back to the DAO. This includes 5% from any NFT/Digital collectibles and secondary sales.

All physical products will be made available to Nounish builders at no cost for their own activations — this program supplies the infrastructure so builders don't have to.

Royalties structured based on net revenue generated per year, for a period of 2 years from the date of funding. Royalties can be revisited and renegotiated before the period expires.

![NOUNSGG](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/r1uK69DLMl.jpg)

## How It Works:

**Non-Zero Start:** We have many existing relationships in place with publishers and with platforms like Veve digital collectibles. We have a licensing agent ready who represents Claynosaurs, Rokimoto and Yo Gabba Gabba - they are ready to take Nounish products and the brand to specialty and mass retail, and international manufacturing and distibution partners. Activating this program pushes work that is already in motion rather than starting from zero.

**First:** The moment the proposal passes, we go to work on the style guide development for licensing and media opportunities. The style guide and digital assets are built first to support partner/ licensing conversations already underway. This is a key step to any growth opportunities.

The budget covers this product development, manufacturing, logistics, and distribution to active and incoming builders.

**Second:** We begin development and sampling of a new Nouns blindbox plush collection, a medium size plush and larger collectible huggable soft sculptures. We will have a round of voting for the plush head traits within the community. 

We will start planning a sofubi (soft vinyl toy) release in Japan to build on the excitement of the show at Loft (yes, people are still excited about more Nouns in Japan!)

Pilot and sample runs of physical goods are produced in small batches to test the market before any larger commitment.

**Early development of blind box plush:**

![NF plush](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/HkdwU52DMl.png)

**On demand manufacturing explorations like the Nounish Slides in the works:**

![NOUNS sllides](https://hackmd.io/_uploads/rJOUR5nPzg.jpg)

## PROBLEM SOLVING:

title: Participate in OLY
body:
Summary  
This proposal asks the DAO whether to use treasury ETH to participate in the live OLY mint (opened 28 August 2026) and, if so, at what size.

Options:  
No — do not mint. Keep ETH in the treasury.  
0.75 ETH mint Pillar 1  
1.5 ETH mint Pillar 1

Context  
OLY is an Ethereum DeFi protocol designed around long-term holders rather than emissions. Sellers fund the system: market sells pay a dynamic ETH tax (starting ~10% and stepping down as market cap grows). That ETH is routed on-chain into:  
-stETH  
-LP vaults  
-buy-and-burn  
-direct staker payouts

Stakers earn a portfolio of on-chain assets (ETH, stETH, WBTC, stables, and future DAO-approved vaults) from sustainable LP vaults and staked ETH, not newly printed OLY. Voting power comes from time-locked stake shares. Supply is capped (~8.88B). Unminted mint-phase tokens are burned.

Mint is structured in three tiers. Longer lock = cheaper price, more share weight, more payout share, and more governance power. Prices rise ~2% per day compounded during the mint window.  
Tiers:  
Pillar 1 — lowest price, longest auto-locks (up to 1,776 days)  
Pillar 2 — mid price, mixed locks (88–369 days)  
Pillar 3 — highest price, fully liquid at launch

Exact prices, lock splits, and routing are defined by the deployed mint contract and whitepaper.

Review before voting:  
oly.io/whitepaper and oly.io.

Why this vote  
The mint is the only window to acquire OLY directly from the protocol at structured prices before open-market trading. Participating would give the DAO:  
-early exposure to a protocol that pays stakers in real assets funded by seller ETH AND real yield from staked ETH / Blue chip LP Positions  
-governance weight for future vaults  
-alignment with a “time over timing” design

Execution (if a mint option wins)  
If 0.75 ETH or 1.5 ETH passes:  
Multisig / executor sends that exact amount of ETH to the official OLY mint contract from the treasury wallet.  
Tier choice: Pillar 1

If No wins: no action. No ETH leaves the treasury for this mint.

Risks (non-exhaustive)  
-Novel / unproven tokenomics design  
-Long mandatory locks  
-Irreversible ETH transfer; no refunds  
-Smart contract, market, and governance risk

Read the whitepaper and terms before voting.

Vote:  
No · 0.75 ETH mint · 1.5 ETH mint

Summary  
This proposal asks the DAO whether to use treasury ETH to mint Moon Strategy ($MSTR) during its live BuilDeFi fair launch on Base, and at what size.

Token: Moon Strategy (MSTR)  
Contract: 0x5cb370837f7e282a6c2472709d0b486680ef26f8 (Base)

Options  
No - do not mint. Keep ETH in the treasury.  
Yes - Mint 0.25 ETH  
Yes - Mint 0.5 ETH

Context  
MSTR is a BuilDeFi fair-launch token on Base described as a leverage and liquidity-compounding play on Moon 8 — a liquidity web index of top Base projects. The design auto-provides LP, compounds fees, and buys & burns.

https://base.buildefi.win/token/0x5cb370837f7e282a6c2472709d0b486680ef26f8

Status: Minting Fair Launch Phase  
Launch threshold already reached  
ETH raised and tokens minted are still growing as new mints come in  
Small holder set and small market cap — this is an early, high-risk launch, not a large established protocol

Mint / supply (in progress)  
Total supply currently in the low millions of MSTR and still increasing with the mint  
Fair launch duration: 21d 18h  
Initial mint price: 1 ETH = 888,888 MSTR  
Additional tokens for LPs: 42%

Allocations  
LPs — 28%  
Builder — 8%  
Additional Support — 5%  
BuyBurn — 28%  
External Stake (AAVE) — 23%  
ETH Leaderboard — 3%  
Moon 8 Support — 5%

Mechanics  
Buy/Sell tax: 6%  
Modules: External Staking, BuyBurn  
Builder / owner: @MoonStrategy

This is not tokenized MicroStrategy equity. Same ticker, different asset.

Why this vote  
Minting now is the structured entry during the fair launch, before (or alongside) secondary liquidity. A small ETH size keeps the bet proportional to a speculative Base launch while still being large enough to receive a meaningful MSTR bag if the Moon 8 / LP-compound / buy-burn loop works.

Execution (if a mint option wins)  
If 0.25 ETH or 0.5 ETH passes:  
Multisig sends that exact amount of ETH on Base through the official BuilDeFi mint UI / mint contract for  
0x5cb370837f7e282a6c2472709d0b486680ef26f8.  
  
Received MSTR is held in the treasury in LP's to earn LP Fees from.  
No additional ETH for this token without a new proposal.  
Account for the 6% buy/sell tax on any later exit, no tax for LP action.

If No wins:  
no action.

Risks (non-exhaustive)  
-Very early fair launch: small cap, few holders, thin liquidity  
-6% tax on buys and sells  
-BuilDeFi platform / module / Base execution risk  
-Narrative risk (Moon 8 index, LP compounding, buy-burn) may not materialize  
-Ticker confusion with MicroStrategy / other $MSTR products

Read the live token page and allocations before voting.

Vote:  
No · Mint 0.25 ETH · Mint 0.5 ETH

title: [Prop 994] Nouns Treasury: Keep USDC Liquid, Earn Yield While It Waits
body:
# Nouns Treasury: Keep USDC Liquid, Earn Yield While It Waits

## 

![](https://i.ibb.co/Mx8FQDy0/exec-9aa6515b-d9da-451c-855e-7c7721a9d180.png "Nouns <3s OUSD")

**TL;DR**

Nouns has 484,743 USDC sitting idle.

This proposal moves 300,000 USDC into OUSD so the USDC can earn a yield while waiting to be used for other proposals, while still remaining fully accessible to the DAO. It also wraps it to remain compliant with the DUNA.

OUSD is a fully liquid stablecoin - converting USDC to OUSD does not lock up any funds, so there is no opportunity risk of funding other proposals with these tokens by converting some USDC to OUSD. 

- **No funds are locked.**                                                               
- **No funds are spent or given to a third party.**                                                               
- **The DAO can convert OUSD → USDC at any time.**                                                               
- **wOUSD and OUSD are fully liquid.**                                                               
- **184,743 USDC remains in native USDC immediately after execution.**                                                               
- If a future proposal needs more USDC, the DAO can redeem any or all of this position first. This proposal does not prevent, delay, or compete with future spending proposals. 

At the current estimated yield of \~5.15% APY, 300,000 USDC would generate roughly **$1,287/month** (\~$15,450/year), while the DAO keeps fully control and liquidity.

*This proposal was modeled after* recent staking proposals *that the DAO ratified.*                

## What this proposal does

Think of this as moving part of the DAO’s idle cash from a checking account into a yield-bearing version of the same cash. Like converting the DAO's ETH into stETH !

## Why do this?

Idle USDC earns nothing. This proposal lets the DAO earn yield on a portion of that balance without sacrificing the ability to fund future ideas.

The expected yield can help fund: future proposals, operating costs, purchases of additional ETH, direct donations to charity, or simply increase the DAO’s USDC balance over time.

Most importantly: **if a better use of OUSD funds appears tomorrow, Nouns is free to use the funds tomorrow - because OUSD is fully liquid.**                                

## Why wOUSD instead of OUSD?

OUSD earns yield automatically via rebase (think of it like a dividend directly to your wallet). It distributes yield in the same way stETH has distributed yield to the Nouns DAO over the last several years before it was converted into wstETH. wOUSD is simply the wrapped, non-rebasing form of OUSD.

It earns the same underlying yield, but the value accrues in the token’s exchange rate rather than by increasing the number of tokens held. That format is generally simpler for treasury accounting and avoids daily rebasing activity.

Wrapping does **not** create a lock-up. It is reversible at any time.

## Wait...how does OUSD earn yield?

OUSD puts deposited USDC to work in onchain strategies instead of leaving it idle.

In simple terms: borrowers and liquidity markets pay fees or interest to use the capital. Those earnings flow back to the OUSD vault, increasing the value held by OUSD and wOUSD holders.

OUSD's current strategies include:

- Lending USDC through Morpho on Ethereum mainnet, Base, and Hyperliquid.      
- Deploying USDC to a Curve AMO (automated market-operations strategy).      
- Automatically claiming MORPHO, CRV, and CVX rewards and converting them into more stablecoins. 

OUSD holders receive this yield automatically. wOUSD receives the same yield, but it appears in the growing wOUSD-to-OUSD exchange rate instead of as a growing token balance.

Yield rates change with market conditions, but are paid out daily without interruption. 

## Risks

This is not risk-free. The relevant risks are smart-contract and stablecoin risk:

- OUSD relies on smart contracts and external yield strategies.      
- OUSD is backed by USDC, so it shares USDC-related risks.      
- Yield rates can change and are not guaranteed. 

Origin has operated OUSD since 2020, has undergone 12+ [audits](https://docs.originprotocol.com/security-and-risk/audits) ([some](https://reports.yaudit.dev/2025-11-origin) by the same auditing firm than Nouns [used](https://reports.yaudit.dev/2022-10-NounsDAO-Token-Buyer)), maintains a bug bounty [program](https://docs.originprotocol.com/security-and-risk/bug-bounties), and uses established DeFi venues for its strategies. More detail and links can be included for anyone who wants to evaluate the technical risk. 

## Transactions

There are 4 transactions involved: approve, mint, approve, and deposit

- [USDC](https://etherscan.io/address/0xE75D77B1865Ae93c7eaa3040B038D7aA7BC02F70) ‘approve’
  - approves the usage of the USDC from the Nouns DAO treasury       
  - USDC uses 6 decimal places, so 300000000000 = 300k USDC  
- [OUSD vault](https://etherscan.io/address/0xe75d77b1865ae93c7eaa3040b038d7aa7bc02f70)  ‘mint’ 
  - mints OUSD using USDC at a 1:1 rate  
- [OUSD](https://etherscan.io/address/0x2a8e1e676ec238d8a992307b495b45b3feaa5e86)  ‘approve’ 
  - approves the usage of the OUSD from the Nouns DAO treasury      
  - OUSD uses 18 decimal places, so 300000000000000000000000 = 300k OUSD  
- [wOUSD](https://etherscan.io/address/0xd2af830e8cbdfed6cc11bab697bb25496ed6fa62)  ‘deposit’ 
  - wraps OUSD into DUNA compliant wOUSD

## Nouns DAO Proposal 993 — Signal Vote

Source: https://nouns.wtf/vote/993  
Proposer: 0xcc2688350d29623e2a0844cc8885f9050f0f6ed5

### TLDR

スタイルガイド、デジタル素材、玩具・ぬいぐるみなどの商品、物流、ライセンス、イベント支援の基盤を整備する。  
本プログラムによる対象商品の販売・ライセンス収益等の5%を、資金提供日から2年間DAOへ還元する。

### 概要
消費者向け商品や体験の開発を手がけるBigshot.WTFが運営するNounworksに対し、NounsのIPおよびブランドを小売、ゲーム、出版、エンターテインメント分野へ展開するための資金を提供する提案。

初期商品として、ブラインドボックス型ぬいぐるみ、中型ぬいぐるみ、大型ソフトスカルプチャーの開発・試作を行い、頭部Traitはコミュニティ投票で選定する。日本ではソフビ商品の展開を計画し、山城屋とロフトを優先的な小売候補としている。米国ではBarnes & NobleやBoxLunchなどとの協議を目指す。

Nouns関連のライセンス契約、商品販売、NFT／デジタルコレクティブルおよび二次流通から本プログラムが生み出す年間純収益の5%を、資金提供日から2年間DAOへ支払う。条件は期間満了前に見直し・再交渉できる。

- 倉庫、物流、配送：50,000 USD
- ライセンス、小売、イベント、展示会：35,000 USD
- 運営、バックエンド、顧客体験：35,000 USD

各金額は概算であり、発生する機会に応じて配分を変更する。

### イベント
- プログラム期間：資金提供後8〜12か月
- DAOへのロイヤルティ支払期間：資金提供日から2年間
- 初年度：日本でのソフビ展開を計画し、山城屋およびロフトへの商品提案・展開を優先

title: How should Hydrex use the Strategic Protocol Reserve?
body:
Hydrex is transitioning the Strategic Protocol Reserve to governance-guided management. This offchain Snapshot selection asks vePRO voters to choose which of three executable SPR strategies should advance to the mandatory HydrexGovernor vote. The options balance capital preservation, fee generation, and direct voter incentives differently. The winning candidate does not execute automatically; its exact encoded actions must still be submitted, approved, and executed through onchain governance.

---

## Choice 1: Conservative SPR Strategy

Keep the Strategic Protocol Reserve focused on blue-chip assets and stablecoins. Convert non-blue-chip holdings into BTC, ETH, or USDC and deploy the resulting assets into conservative Hydrex liquidity positions. This option prioritizes preserving reserve value and limiting exposure to higher-risk assets.

### Proposed onchain actions

1. **Allow an operator to call one approved function through SPR.**
   - Target: `0x1486059e16293E9F5180C518b34B1Df1C1Eee5EB`
2. **Pin calldata arguments for an approved operator action.**
   - Target: `0x1486059e16293E9F5180C518b34B1Df1C1Eee5EB`

## Choice 2: Fee-Generation Optimization Strategy

Allocate up to 1,000,000 USDC from the Strategic Protocol Reserve toward higher-volume assets and liquidity positions on Base. This option prioritizes fee generation and allows routine deployment into active pairs, accepting greater impermanent-loss and asset-price risk.

### Proposed onchain actions

1. **Allow an operator to call one approved function through SPR.**
   - Target: `0x1486059e16293E9F5180C518b34B1Df1C1Eee5EB`
2. **Pin calldata arguments for an approved operator action.**
   - Target: `0x1486059e16293E9F5180C518b34B1Df1C1Eee5EB`

## Choice 3: SPR Bribe Distribution Strategy

Distribute Strategic Protocol Reserve value directly to Hydrex voters through approved pool bribe contracts over a controlled three-month schedule. This option prioritizes returning reserve value to voters, avoids liquidity-position impermanent loss, and intentionally exhausts the allocated SPR capital through the Hydrex incentive flywheel.

### Proposed onchain actions

1. **Allow an operator to call one approved function through SPR.**
   - Target: `0x1486059e16293E9F5180C518b34B1Df1C1Eee5EB`
2. **Pin calldata arguments for an approved operator action.**
   - Target: `0x1486059e16293E9F5180C518b34B1Df1C1Eee5EB`
3. **Allow an operator to call one approved function through SPR.**
   - Target: `0x1486059e16293E9F5180C518b34B1Df1C1Eee5EB`
4. **Pin calldata arguments for an approved operator action.**
   - Target: `0x1486059e16293E9F5180C518b34B1Df1C1Eee5EB`

The exact calldata for every candidate is signed into this proposal's Hydrex metadata. The winning choice still requires a separate HydrexGovernor proposal and mandatory onchain vote.

title: New Proposal on Equilibria Wind Down
body:
Over the past few months, Equilibria has gone through a long and complex process to finalize the wind-down of the protocol. This proposal is intended to provide a clear recap of what happened, explains the final distribution framework, and outlines the next steps for all stakeholders.

**Part I. Background: From the Original Wind Down Proposal to the Final Framework**  
In January, a wind-down distribution proposal was presented to the community. To provide context for the final update, here is a quick recap of those original details:

Option 1: Distribute the underlying PENDLE according to the 0.4184 : 0.5816 ratio between EQB and ePENDLE users, and allocate 100% of the sPENDLE yield to ePENDLE holders.  
Option2 : Distribute the underlying PENDLE according to the 0.2092 : 0.7908 ratio between EQB and ePENDLE users, and split the sPENDLE yield 50/50 between the two groups.

The voting process was paused after the Pendle team provided legal feedback raising concerns about the original distribution framework. Their legal opinion issued by external counsel indicated that such allocation of the redeemed underlying PENDLE to EQB holders could create legal risks and complications.

After extensive discussions with the Pendle team and consideration of additional legal opinions, we reached a revised distribution framework.The goal of the final framework is to reduce legal uncertainty, while still protecting the economic interests of both EQB holders and ePENDLE holders as much as possible. For avoidance of doubt, whilst the Pendle team has provided input based on their legal opinion, they have reserved their position on this proposal.

**Part II. One-Off and Non-Precedential Voting Arrangement**  
For this EIP only, ePENDLE and EQB are both included in the voting process on an exceptional, non-precedential basis. The relative voting weight between ePENDLE and EQB are determined by their respective 30-day average market capitalizations prior to the official announcement of the sPENDLE transition, corresponding to approximately 56.59% for ePENDLE and 43.41% for EQB.

This structure is adopted solely due to the specific nature of this EIP, which relates to the wind-down of Equilibria and the allocation of related economic interests. For the avoidance of doubt, this arrangement does not recognize ePENDLE as an Equilibria governance token and does not create any ongoing or future voting rights for ePENDLE holders.

![mcap.png](ipfs://bafkreibzj7pg4hrdlvwlyn4o2vl4mp7b7u45jmius66lp747ldjprsaciq)

**Part III. Final Distribution Framework**  
This section presents the final distribution framework for allocating (i) Underlying PENDLE in Equilibria and (ii) Yields accrued by the underlying PENDLE during the wind-down period, with the goal of returning value to EQB and ePENDLE holders in a transparent, verifiable manner.

(i) Unlocked Underlying PENDLE: At the end of the 2-year period, the protocol’s vePENDLE will be fully redeemable as PENDLE.  
(ii) sPENDLE Yields: Throughout the wind-down period, Equilibria’s vePENDLE exposure will be treated as virtual sPENDLE and continue to accrue yields. These yields represent the ongoing cash flows received during the two years wind-down period.

The following distribution framework is presented for community to vote:

Option 1: Distribute the underlying PENDLE according to the 0.75: 0.25 ratio between ePENDLE and EQB users, and allocate 100% of the sPENDLE yield to EQB users.

Option 2: Distribute the underlying PENDLE according to the 0.70: 0.30 ratio between ePENDLE and EQB users, and split the sPENDLE yields 50%/50% between the ePENDLE and EQB users.

A management fee will be charged to cover the operational and administrative expenses of maintaining the protocol during its wind-down, consisting of a 1.5% fee on the underlying PENDLE and a 10% fee on sPENDLE yields, each applied proportionally based on the applicable ePENDLE/EQB allocation approved in the EIP.

**Part IV. Assumptions and Distribution Simulations**  
The table below summarizes the actual yield generated during the first three months of sPENDLE distributions on Pendle, including airdrops, based on a total staked PENDLE amount of 97,622,964. It is intended to provide users with an overview of recent yield performance, though actual yields may vary from month to month.

![2.png](ipfs://bafkreibt2ayxd25buotrfcgh7gmsb6jrmucubhb5x7tws4cttenwbkiynm)

Following discussions with the relevant parties, we apply a 5% APY assumption in the simulation below to account for periods without significant one-off airdrops. Based on a total of 8,584,372 vePENDLE held by Equilibria, the simulations for the two options are set out below:  
Option 1 Distribution Simulation

![3.png](ipfs://bafkreidribme3yiktkvhphcgury6v57a3qfacjanowpqyczgdjj67cyj4m)

Option 2 Distribution Simulation

![4.png](ipfs://bafkreidu5acvbe5iubbupk73wu5voeoytdrzrilwaezugnejwhdt25zdym)

As reflected in the simulations above, the key difference between Option 1 and Option 2 lies in the allocation between underlying PENDLE redemption and sPENDLE yield participation.

_Please note that the figures, projections, and distribution outcomes presented in this section are based on illustrative assumptions and forward-looking simulations. They do not represent guaranteed results or precise forecasts. These simulations are provided solely for explanatory and decision-support purposes, without implying any recommendation or preference by Equilibria as to which option any user should choose._

**Part V. Equilibria Treasury Holdings**  
This section provides a comprehensive overview of Equilibria’s current treasury holdings and outlines the guiding principles for their disposition. The assets, including EQB tokens, ePENDLE holdings, and liquidity positions on DEXs, represent value that ultimately belongs to EQB holders. Existing liquidity positions will be maintained to facilitate orderly exits for both EQB and ePENDLE holders, while all remaining treasury assets will be returned in full to EQB holders. This approach ensures a fair exit process and appropriate compensation for all protocol participants.

**EQB Tokens:** 66% of the total supply (66,555,009 EQB)

-   14% belongs to Team and Advisors allocation
    
-   52% belongs to LP Incentives and Treasury allocation, including a portion (9,454,461.93 xEQB) to Pendle team
    
-   All the EQB tokens mentioned above (66,555,009 EQB) will be permanently burned.
    

**ePENDLE Holdings:** 125,725 ePENDLE

-   These ePENDLE will receive PENDLE based on the distribution framework. At the end of the 2 years, the corresponding proceeds will be fully distributed to eligible EQB holders.
    

**Treasury Liquidity Positions**

-   EQB/WETH LP on Camelot: 1,357,197 EQB / 28.1583 WETH
    
-   ePENDLE/PENDLE LP on Camelot: 30,126 ePENDLE/10,042 PENDLE
    

**Part VI Pendle Team Waives Its xEQB Distribution Rights**  
Additionally, subject to the proposal passing, the Pendle team has agreed to waive its 9,454,461.93 xEQB distribution rights. The background regarding these tokens is explained below.

At Equilibria's inception, the Pendle and Equilibria teams agreed for the PENDLE team to support Equilibria by converting a portion of PENDLE to ePENDLE. Under this arrangement, the Pendle team did not stake its ePENDLE and was instead entitled to receive protocol rewards in xEQB over time pursuant to a vesting mechanism. Following the implementation of EIP#6, which halted all EQB emissions and token minting, this portion of xEQB rewards was not created or paid out.

As part of the wind-down arrangement, subject to this proposal passing, the Pendle team agrees to waive its distribution rights for this portion of xEQB. Accordingly, this portion of xEQB will be permanently burned together with the other EQB tokens held in the treasury, and will not participate in the final liquidation distribution.

**Closing**  
Equilibria’s wind-down proposal has been a long and difficult process. What we initially hoped to complete in January has taken nearly seven months of discussions, negotiations, and legal review. Now, a framework has finally been reached that seeks to protect the interests of both ePENDLE and EQB holders while remaining within reasonable legal framework.

We sincerely thank the community for your patience and ongoing support. We encourage all token holders to carefully review the details and participate in the vote. Regardless of the outcome, the approved option will be executed transparently, responsibly, and in alignment with the best interests of the community.

title: August 2026 Grid Cycle Vote
body:
Phantoms:

Sakura’s Vault remained conservatively positioned through uncertain market conditions.

As new opportunities emerge across crypto, we want a clear pulse check from Keyholders:

What strategy should guide the next allocation tranche of Sakura’s Vault?

Should the Vault remain concentrated in Bitcoin, expand into BTC and ETH, or pursue broader diversification across liquid crypto, emerging ecosystems and selected strategic NFT acquisitions?

Vote Options:

1. Bitcoin Reserve

Deploy the next allocation tranche exclusively into BTC.

This is the simplest and most concentrated strategy, with no altcoin or NFT exposure.

2. Blue-Chip Core

Focus exclusively on BTC and ETH.

This expands beyond Bitcoin while remaining concentrated in crypto’s two primary liquid assets.

3. Liquid Diversified

Combine BTC and ETH with selected liquid exposure to areas such as RWA, AI and other researched crypto narratives.

No NFTs would be added under this strategy.

4. Frontier Mix

Combine the liquid core with selected higher-volatility exposure to emerging ecosystems such as Robinhood Chain, while NFT exposure would remain minimal and tightly capped.

5. Full-Spectrum Vault

Allow Sakura to research a diversified mix of BTC, ETH, narrative tokens, emerging ecosystems and selected strategic NFT acquisitions.

Potential areas may include RWA, AI, Robinhood Chain and Neo Tokyo ecosystem assets.

This offers the widest opportunity set, but also carries the highest volatility, liquidity and execution risk.

This vote applies only to the next allocation tranche. It does not require a rebalance or sale of the Vault’s existing positions.

This vote does not bind Grid Phantoms to any particular course of action.

We’re simply taking a pulse of the community to better understand how Keyholders feel about the next phase of Sakura’s Vault.

Think of the result as a directional signal, not a final allocation plan. It will help guide our research and planning, while any specific assets, amounts and timing will depend on conditions and opportunities as they develop.

Cast your vote and help determine how Sakura’s Vault approaches the next phase of the market.

The Code Shall Prevail. ⚡️

# [Ethereum] Grove × Steakhouse USDG Vault - Onboard the Vault to the Grove Liquidity Layer - August 31, 2026

Grove's Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Grove Development Company.

## Review

If approved, this proposal will onboard the Grove × Steakhouse USDG vault to the Grove Liquidity Layer.

The Grove × Steakhouse USDG vault is a Morpho vault with USDG as its deposit asset, running the same audited code as the live Grove × Steakhouse USDC vault under the same curation arrangement and differing only in the asset it holds. It was built to the Core Council’s Morpho Vault V2 standard, communicated on August 17, 2026: its owner is the Grove SubProxy and its curator a two-of-two multisig whose signers are Sky governance and Steakhouse. All seventeen of its governed functions meet the standard — fourteen carry at least its minimum timelock, and the three share- and asset-gate setters are permanently abdicated, so no gate can ever be installed on those paths. The vault’s sentinel is appointed before the spell executes. Its collateral markets are drawn from the Core Council’s accepted list and are confirmed, with their per-market caps, before the spell executes. Onboarding gives Grove a USDG-denominated position alongside the existing USDC one, through the same generic ERC-4626 deposit path already live for Grove’s other vault positions.

Three values are set. The deposit rate limit bounds Grove’s incremental daily exposure; the withdrawal limit is unlimited, so the position can always be unwound; and the maximum exchange rate bounds the share price at which a deposit is accepted, which is the share-price-inflation protection for the position — it is unset for a newly deployed vault, and deposits are not possible until it is set.

The Core Council’s role and timelock requirements for a Prime’s Morpho vaults settled on August 17, 2026, and Grove is bringing its existing Morpho vaults to them; transferring an existing vault’s ownership to the Grove SubProxy is itself a spell action, and those items are scheduled into upcoming spells. A vault may receive allocations as soon as it meets the criteria, independently of that wider work, so this item’s condition is this vault meeting them, confirmed before execution.

### Change Summary

- Deposit rate limit
  - `maxAmount`: 50,000,000 USDG
  - `slope`: 50,000,000 USDG per day
- Withdrawal rate limit: unlimited
- Maximum exchange rate: at most 2 USDG per vault share (from unset; deposits are not possible until it is set)
- Relevant addresses
  - Grove × Steakhouse USDG vault [`eth:0xbeef05061FE51eA482BD1b68041353490b3a5934`](https://etherscan.io/address/0xbeef05061FE51eA482BD1b68041353490b3a5934)

  - Grove × Steakhouse USDC vault [`eth:0xBeefF08dF54897e7544aB01d0e86f013DA354111`](https://etherscan.io/address/0xBeefF08dF54897e7544aB01d0e86f013DA354111) (the live vault it mirrors)
  - ALM `RateLimits` [`eth:0x5F5cfCB8a463868E37Ab27B5eFF3ba02112dF19a`](https://etherscan.io/address/0x5F5cfCB8a463868E37Ab27B5eFF3ba02112dF19a)
  - ALM `MainnetController` [`eth:0xfd9dEA9a8D5B955649579Af482DB7198A392A9F5`](https://etherscan.io/address/0xfd9dEA9a8D5B955649579Af482DB7198A392A9F5)
- Artifact changes: record the vault onboarding and its parameters

---

Technical implementation details can be found under item 1 at [_Proposed Actions_ in the originating forum post](https://forum.skyeco.com/t/september-10-2026-proposed-changes-to-grove-for-upcoming-spell/28207#p-107231-proposed-actions-13).

title: SGP-21: Return Unclaimed Rewards to the DAO After One Year
body:
## SGP-21: Return Unclaimed Rewards to the DAO After One Year

Author: Gaspard · Category: Governance Proposal (SGP) · Status: Draft · Date: 28 August 2026

### Summary

Spectra protocol emissions are distributed through Merkl, a third-party distribution operator. The arrangement works well: it removes most of the overhead of running incentive campaigns across chains Spectra is deployed on, and it gives participants a single place to claim.

Merkl computes rewards off-chain, and they become tokens in a wallet when participants claim them. Rewards left unclaimed remain pending.

As of 28 August 2026, 1.61M SPECTRA remains unclaimed across 535 campaigns.

This proposal sets one rule: rewards still unclaimed one year after a campaign ends return to the DAO. It applies to all Spectra protocol incentive campaigns, past and future. Participants keep the full year to claim.

### Rationale

A defined window. Off-chain balances need an end date. Without one, thousands of stale balances stay alive across chains indefinitely, creating monitoring and support costs with no benefit. A published one-year window gives participants a clear claim period and returns what remains to the DAO treasury.

Incentives only. Supplied liquidity, PT and YT positions, and their accrued onchain yield are never touched. This applies to claimable rewards alone.

Operators set their own limits. Under Merkl's current terms, that limit is one year after the campaign ends. Matching it means the tokens return to the Spectra DAO.

### What happens if the vote passes

The campaign manager address carries out the operation on behalf of the DAO before each campaign's one-year mark, and the unclaimed tokens go to the DAO treasury.

Each remaining campaign is handled as it approaches its own one-year date. Campaign end dates are known in advance and previewable on Merkl, so the schedule is predictable and published.

The rule covers campaigns distributed through Merkl and through any alternative or in-house method adopted later, so it holds without a further vote.

title: [Ethereum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Offboard Unused Integrations
body:
# [Ethereum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Offboard Unused Integrations - August 31, 2026

Spark's Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Phoenix Labs.

## Review

The Spark community can hereby express support or opposition to the following changes:

If approved, this proposal will offboard a set of unused integrations by zeroing their rate limits, removing standing relayer authority over venues Spark no longer uses.

Each live rate limit is standing authority for the relayer to move funds to or from a venue. Where Spark has no position and no intention of using a venue again, that authority is unearned risk surface. Zeroing the limits removes it without moving any funds.

### Required Context

**How an SLL rate limit is disabled**: `RateLimits.setRateLimitData(key, 0, 0)`. There is no removal function; a zeroed limit makes any controller call touching that key revert at `require(maxAmount > 0, "RateLimits/zero-maxAmount")` inside `triggerRateLimitDecrease`. Rate-limit keys are derived as `keccak256(abi.encode(LIMIT_BASE, venue))`, except the five bare keys (`LIMIT_USDE_MINT`, `LIMIT_USDE_BURN`, `LIMIT_SUSDE_COOLDOWN`, `LIMIT_SUPERSTATE_SUBSCRIBE`, and the orphaned `LIMIT_SUPERSTATE_REDEEM`), which bind to a single immutable set in the controller's constructor and therefore use the bare `keccak256("LIMIT_X")` as the storage key.

**Proposal's scope is 34 rate-limit keys**, covering both the integrations Spark has already exited and those it had kept available but has now decided not to use. Twenty-one belong to the integrations previously confirmed for offboarding and thirteen to those previously held open as candidates; the per-key detail is in [Proposed actions, Item 1](https://forum.skyeco.com/t/september-10-2026-proposed-changes-to-spark-for-upcoming-spell/28208). Two venues need fewer keys than they appear to: the Curve PYUSD/USDC and Curve USDC/USDT deposit and withdraw limits are **already zero** (the former was never configured; the latter was zeroed on 2025-04-21), so only their swap legs need action.

**Superstate is offboarded in full, and that takes five keys rather than two.** The subscription and redemption paths are asymmetric, and the redemption rails are easy to miss because they are **self-transfers** — `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER(asset, asset)` — used to trigger burn-on-transfer redemption, rather than transfers between an asset and a stablecoin:

  | Path | Key | Current |
  | :---- | :---- | :---- |
  | USTB subscribe | `LIMIT_SUPERSTATE_SUBSCRIBE` (bare) | 300,000,000 USDC, 100M/day |
  | USTB redeem | `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER(USTB, USTB)` | unlimited |
  | USCC subscribe | `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER(USDC, USCC_DEPOSIT)` | 100,000,000 USDC, 50M/day |
  | USCC redeem | `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER(USCC, USCC)` | unlimited |
  | USTB redeem (legacy) | `LIMIT_SUPERSTATE_REDEEM` (bare) | unlimited |

The last of these is **an orphaned storage entry**: `LIMIT_SUPERSTATE_REDEEM` is not among the twenty-nine `LIMIT_*` constants declared by the deployed v1.10.0 controller, so no live code path reads it. It is zeroed anyway as a defensive measure — the value persists in `RateLimits` storage independently of the controller, so if a future controller version reintroduced that constant, a stale unlimited limit would become live immediately. The three `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER` legs pointing at the registry's `SUPERSTATE_REDEMPTION` address were checked and are **already zero**, having never been configured; they need no action. The ALM Proxy holds **0 USTB and 0 USCC**, so Superstate is a clean exit with no residual.

**The Proposal deliberately leaves residual balances behind.** Several offboarded venues still hold small ALM Proxy positions. These are not withdrawn, before or during the spell: the amounts are below the marginal cost of retrieving them, and any of them can be recovered later by a dedicated spell if that ever becomes worthwhile. Both the deposit and withdraw sides are zeroed. The precedent and its consequence are both known — roughly 300 USD has been stranded in Base Fluid sUSDS since the equivalent April 2026 zeroing.

### Proposed Actions

**34 calls to `RateLimits.setRateLimitData(key, 0, 0)`** on [`eth:0x7A5FD5cf045e010e62147F065cEAe59e5344b188`](https://etherscan.io/address/0x7A5FD5cf045e010e62147F065cEAe59e5344b188), executed as the Spark SubDAO Proxy, which holds `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`. **No funds move.** Keys are derived as `keccak256(abi.encode(LIMIT_BASE, venue))`, or `keccak256(abi.encode(LIMIT_BASE, asset, destination))` for transfer legs, except the five bare keys which use the bare `keccak256("LIMIT_X")`.

**Parameters, and their current values read at block 25,807,000:**

| # | Venue | Key derivation | Current `maxAmount` / slope | After |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Morpho v1 DAI vault | `LIMIT_4626_DEPOSIT` × vault | 200,000,000 DAI / 100M per day | `0 / 0` |
| 2 | Morpho v1 DAI vault | `LIMIT_4626_WITHDRAW` × vault | unlimited | `0 / 0` |
| 3 | Morpho v1 USDS vault | `LIMIT_4626_DEPOSIT` × vault | 200,000,000 USDS / 100M per day | `0 / 0` |
| 4 | Morpho v1 USDS vault | `LIMIT_4626_WITHDRAW` × vault | unlimited | `0 / 0` |
| 5 | Aave Core aEthUSDe | `LIMIT_AAVE_DEPOSIT` × aToken | 250,000,000 USDe / 100M per day | `0 / 0` |
| 6 | Aave Core aEthUSDe | `LIMIT_AAVE_WITHDRAW` × aToken | unlimited | `0 / 0` |
| 7 | Ethena USDe mint | `LIMIT_USDE_MINT` (global) | 250,000,000 USDC / 100M per day | `0 / 0` |
| 8 | Ethena USDe burn | `LIMIT_USDE_BURN` (global) | 500,000,000 USDe / 200M per day | `0 / 0` |
| 9 | Ethena sUSDe cooldown | `LIMIT_SUSDE_COOLDOWN` (global) | unlimited | `0 / 0` |
| 10–12 | Maple syrupUSDT | `LIMIT_4626_DEPOSIT`, `LIMIT_4626_WITHDRAW`, `LIMIT_MAPLE_REDEEM` × token | 50,000,000 USDT / unlimited / unlimited | `0 / 0` each |
| 13–15 | Maple syrupUSDC | same three keys × token | 100,000,000 USDC / unlimited / unlimited | `0 / 0` each |
| 16–18 | Curve PYUSD/USDS | `LIMIT_CURVE_DEPOSIT`, `_WITHDRAW`, `_SWAP` × pool | 5,000,000 / 5,000,000 / 5,000,000 | `0 / 0` each |
| 19 | Curve PYUSD/USDC | `LIMIT_CURVE_SWAP` × pool | 5,000,000 | `0 / 0` |
| 20–22 | Curve sUSDS/USDT | `LIMIT_CURVE_DEPOSIT`, `_WITHDRAW`, `_SWAP` × pool | 5,000,000 / 25,000,000 / 10,000,000 | `0 / 0` each |
| 23 | Curve USDC/USDT | `LIMIT_CURVE_SWAP` × pool | 5,000,000 | `0 / 0` |
| 24 | Curve weETH/WETH-ng | `LIMIT_CURVE_SWAP` × pool | 1,000 WETH | `0 / 0` |
| 25 | Superstate USTB subscribe | `LIMIT_SUPERSTATE_SUBSCRIBE` (global) | 300,000,000 USDC / 100M per day | `0 / 0` |
| 26 | Superstate USTB redeem | `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER` × (USTB, USTB) | unlimited | `0 / 0` |
| 27 | Superstate USTB redeem (legacy) | `LIMIT_SUPERSTATE_REDEEM` (global, orphaned) | unlimited | `0 / 0` |
| 28 | Superstate USCC subscribe | `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER` × (USDC, USCC deposit) | 100,000,000 USDC / 50M per day | `0 / 0` |
| 29 | Superstate USCC redeem | `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER` × (USCC, USCC) | unlimited | `0 / 0` |
| 30–32 | B2C2 OTC | `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER` × (USDC / USDT / PYUSD, B2C2) | 1,000,000 each / 20M per day | `0 / 0` each |
| 33 | Anchorage USDT | `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER` × (USDT, Anchorage) | 50,000,000 USDT / 250M per day | `0 / 0` |
| 34 | Anchorage USAT | `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER` × (USAT, Anchorage) | 50,000,000 USAT / 250M per day | `0 / 0` |

**External source of the values:** every current value was read from `RateLimits.getRateLimitData(bytes32)` at block 25,807,000, with each key independently re-derived from the base constants read off the deployed controller. The venue addresses are registry constants at the pinned commit.

**Explicitly out of scope, and verified untouched:** the **Anchorage USDC leg** (50,000,000 USDC, actively used — `lastAmount` 30,208,316.05), the USDS-to-SPK farm deposit and withdraw limits, Binance OTC (`LIMIT_OTC_SWAP` × Binance, 5,000,000), both LayerZero USDT0 rails to Arbitrum and X Layer, and all five Paxos conversion rails. Each was read at the same block and is unchanged by this spell.

**Already zero, so not included:** the Curve PYUSD/USDC and Curve weETH/WETH deposit and withdraw keys (never configured) and the Curve USDC/USDT deposit and withdraw keys (zeroed 2025-04-21). The three `LIMIT_ASSET_TRANSFER` legs to the registry's `SUPERSTATE_REDEMPTION` address are also already zero and were never configured.
---

Additional information can be found in Item 1 in the [forum post](https://forum.skyeco.com/t/september-10-2026-proposed-changes-to-spark-for-upcoming-spell/28208)

The proposed Spark Artifact changes can be found in the following pull request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/317

## Outcomes

- If "For" receives the most votes, the proposal will be approved. The associated pull request will be merged into Spark's artifact. When required, the listed changes will proceed to implementation by the relevant actors.
- If "Against" receives the most votes, the proposal will be rejected. No changes will be implemented.

title: [Ethereum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Onboard the Sentora-Curated RLUSD Morpho Vault
body:
# [Ethereum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Onboard the Sentora-Curated RLUSD Morpho Vault - August 31, 2026

Spark's Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Phoenix Labs.

## Review

The Spark community can hereby express support or opposition to the following changes:

If approved, this proposal will onboard the Sentora-curated RLUSD Morpho Vaults V2 instance, allowing the Spark Liquidity Layer to allocate RLUSD into it and withdraw again.

Onboarding of Sentora RLUSD Morpho vault adds an externally curated RLUSD lending venue, under the Sky required-roles standard, restricted to a collateral set Sky has already reviewed. RLUSD funding routes already exist through the Curve RLUSD/USDC pool onboarded by the August 13, 2026 spell.

### Required Context

**Proposal's spell action is only the rate limits**: deploying the vault, deploying and registering the market adapter, appointing the curator, allocator and sentinels, raising the per-selector timelocks, abdicating the gate setters, creating and seeding markets, and setting per-market caps are all done by the vault owner ahead of this spell and outside it. The spell sets `LIMIT_4626_DEPOSIT`, `LIMIT_4626_WITHDRAW` and a `maxExchangeRate` ceiling, which is what makes the vault reachable by the relayer.

**Morpho Vaults V2 is ERC-4626-compliant from the controller's perspective**, so the proposed item needs no controller change and reuses the same `LIMIT_4626_*` machinery already in service for the Morpho V2 USDT vault. This is worth stating because the vault's `maxDeposit`, `maxMint`, `maxWithdraw` and `maxRedeem` all return `0` by design ("gross underestimation because being revert-free cannot be guaranteed"), which would break an integration that consulted them. Spark's `ERC4626Lib` calls only `asset()`, `deposit`, `withdraw` and `redeem`, so the deposit and withdrawal paths are unaffected.

The proposed item depends on a Morpho Vaults V2 instance and a Morpho market adapter deployed and configured **outside this spell** by the vault owner; the spell's only action for Item 5 is to set two Spark Liquidity Layer rate limits and a share-price ceiling. No Spark contract is upgraded.

 
#### Roles setup

**The role set departs from Spark's existing Morpho instances in two deliberate ways**, both following the Sky required-roles standard rather than Spark's earlier pattern. The curator is a **2-of-2 between Sky GovOps and Sentora** rather than a Spark multisig, so no cap change can be made without Sky GovOps co-signing. And the **allocator is Sentora**, not the ALM Proxy — Spark takes no allocator seat, because the sentinel role already carries the deallocate power Spark needs. The vault owner is the Spark SubDAO Proxy, so every role change after launch requires a Sky executive spell.

### Proposed Actions

**Three calls**, following `SLLHelpers.configureERC4626Vault` — two rate-limit writes on `RateLimits` and one share-price ceiling on the ALM Controller. **The spell does not call the vault.**

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `LIMIT_4626_DEPOSIT` × vault — `maxAmount` | **10,000,000 RLUSD** | Currently `0` |
| `LIMIT_4626_DEPOSIT` × vault — slope | **100,000,000 RLUSD per day** | A low maximum against a high slope is Spark's standard convention for ERC-4626 onboardings; the bucket refills fully in roughly 2.4 hours |
| `LIMIT_4626_WITHDRAW` × vault | **unlimited** (`type(uint256).max`, slope `0`) | The standard withdraw setting — Spark never rate-limits its own exit |
| `setMaxExchangeRate(vault, 1e18, 3e18)` | `maxExchangeRate = 3` | Standard 4626 setup; RLUSD and the vault are both 18-decimal. Matches the configuration Grove used on Sentora's existing RLUSD vault |

**External source of the values:** the rate limits and share-price ceiling were set by Phoenix Labs for this integration; the `(1e18, 3e18)` form follows the established convention for ERC-4626 vaults and the precedent of Grove's March 2026 onboarding of Sentora's existing RLUSD vault.

**What is not in this spell:** vault deployment, adapter deployment and registration, curator, allocator and sentinel appointment, per-selector timelock configuration, gate abdication, market creation and seeding, and per-market caps are all completed by the vault owner beforehand — see Pre-configurations and Pre-requirement 5. The launch collateral set is **WETH, wstETH, WBTC, cbBTC and sUSDS only**; anything beyond it requires explicit Sky review and approval.

**No controller change is required:** Morpho Vaults V2 is ERC-4626-compliant on the paths Spark uses, and the same `LIMIT_4626_*` machinery already serves the Morpho V2 USDT vault on this controller version.
---

Additional details can be found under Item 5 in the [forum post](https://forum.skyeco.com/t/september-10-2026-proposed-changes-to-spark-for-upcoming-spell/28208).

The proposed Spark Artifact changes can be found in the following pull request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/318

## Outcomes

- If "For" receives the most votes, the proposal will be approved. The associated pull request will be merged into Spark's artifact. When required, the listed changes will proceed to implementation by the relevant actors.
- If "Against" receives the most votes, the proposal will be rejected. No changes will be implemented.

title: SGP-21: Return Unclaimed Rewards to the DAO After One Year
body:
## SGP-21: Return Unclaimed Rewards to the DAO After One Year

Author: Gaspard · Category: Governance Proposal (SGP) · Status: Draft · Date: 28 August 2026

### Summary

Spectra protocol emissions are distributed through Merkl, a third-party distribution operator. The arrangement works well: it removes most of the overhead of running incentive campaigns across chains Spectra is deployed on, and it gives participants a single place to claim.

Merkl computes rewards off-chain, and they become tokens in a wallet when participants claim them. Rewards left unclaimed remain pending.

As of 28 August 2026, 1.61M SPECTRA remains unclaimed across 535 campaigns.

This proposal sets one rule: rewards still unclaimed one year after a campaign ends return to the DAO. It applies to all Spectra protocol incentive campaigns, past and future. Participants keep the full year to claim.

### Rationale

A defined window. Off-chain balances need an end date. Without one, thousands of stale balances stay alive across chains indefinitely, creating monitoring and support costs with no benefit. A published one-year window gives participants a clear claim period and returns what remains to the DAO treasury.

Incentives only. Supplied liquidity, PT and YT positions, and their accrued onchain yield are never touched. This applies to claimable rewards alone.

Operators set their own limits. Under Merkl's current terms, that limit is one year after the campaign ends. Matching it means the tokens return to the Spectra DAO.

### What happens if the vote passes

The campaign manager address carries out the operation on behalf of the DAO before each campaign's one-year mark, and the unclaimed tokens go to the DAO treasury.

Each remaining campaign is handled as it approaches its own one-year date. Campaign end dates are known in advance and previewable on Merkl, so the schedule is predictable and published.

The rule covers campaigns distributed through Merkl and through any alternative or in-house method adopted later, so it holds without a further vote.

Participants keep the full year to claim in every case. What returns to the DAO is what remains at that point.

title: FGP-2: Growth SBT Issuance. Mint with FANC or Not?
body:
![Designer-grade_Web3_governance_banner_169_widesc-1787731341396 (1).png](ipfs://bafybeihnkjorzqpxnna5fhsqyppwn74vaqeuendd3mradzdhc5dzxosrum)

**Proposal Summary**
Genesis SBT is free. Connect your wallet, press mint, and that's it — you only pay gas. One per wallet, for 100 days. There was no reason to put a price on saying thank you to the people who have built fanC and CELEBe with us. But Growth SBT, which comes next, is a different kind of badge. It is a qualification meant to be used going forward.

This is the second proposal in fanC governance. We're asking the community how FANC should be linked to the issuance of Growth SBT.

This vote alone does not finalize the policy. The fanC team will publish the results within 48 hours and continue its review based on the community's choice.

Voting period: September 2, 10:00 (UTC) to September 8, 10:00 (UTC) 
Platform: Snapshot (snapshot.org/#/s:fancdao.eth) 
Voting options
🟣 Use FANC: A set amount of FANC is spent at issuance
🔵 Hold FANC: No spending — eligibility is verified by your balance
⚪ Leave it to the team: The team selects the more suitable approach

**Two SBTs, Two Different Questions**
If Genesis records who was here, Growth shows what you are doing.

Growth SBT rises in tier based on the activity and contribution you build up on CELEBe, and the services being prepared in fanC Hub will read that tier as their access standard. It isn't gratitude for time already spent. It's a qualification that gets used from here on.

That's why how it gets issued matters. If it's too easy to obtain, the tier loses its meaning. If the bar is too high, newcomers can't get in. This proposal asks which side we should lean toward.

**Why This Vote Matters**
In the first vote, the community chose creators first. 54.38%. That choice is being reflected in the large-scale CELEBe update now in preparation.

In AI character chat, users become the character themselves and build a story with AI as the conversation unfolds. No camera, no editing required. Beside the people who make videos, a seat opens up for the people who write stories. The scope of Create to Earn widens.

The more people who create, the more important it becomes to tell who the creators are. That's the role Growth SBT will play.

Free minting for Genesis SBT ends in early October. The next step has to be decided before then.

# Guide to the Options
1. Use FANC: A set amount of FANC is spent at issuance. The qualification carries more weight, and the tier means more.
2. Hold FANC: No spending — eligibility is verified by your balance. The barrier is lower, and more people come in.
3. Leave it to the team: The team selects whichever of the two approaches fits better.

Requiring FANC makes the qualification heavier. Checking balances alone lowers the barrier. Neither side is a settled answer. We decided this is not a call for the team to make, but one for holders to make.

FGP-1 was the first case where a holder decision actually moved the direction of the ecosystem. The second vote is decided the same way.

Your tokens. Your voice. Your ecosystem.

body:
**[ARFC] Onboard cirBTC on Aave v3 Core and Aave V4 Core**

**Author: Aave Labs**

**Date: 2026-08-31**

***

# Summary

This proposal seeks to onboard Circle Wrapped Bitcoin (cirBTC) to the Aave V3 Core Instance and the Aave V4 Core Instance on Ethereum, with collateral functionality enabled.

# Motivation

cirBTC is an ERC-20 representation of native BTC issued by Circle, launched on Ethereum mainnet on June 8, 2026. Each unit is backed 1:1 by Bitcoin custodied at a regulated Circle entity and segregated from Circle's corporate assets.

Onboarding cirBTC as a collateral asset is aligned with the DAO's long-term objectives in several ways:

* It broadens the set of BTC denominated collateral available on Aave, complementing existing wrapped Bitcoin exposures already present on the Core instances.
* It enables users to borrow against a regulated, BTC backed wrapped representation, supporting demand from institutional participants and DeFi protocols.
* It strengthens the Core instances' position as a venue for BTC denominated leverage and liquidity strategies.

# Specification

## Aave V3 Specific Parameters

**Instance:** Ethereum Core

| **Parameter** | **Recommendation** |
|-----------|----------------|
| Borrowable | Yes            |
| Collateral Enabled | Yes            |
| Supply Cap | 250            |
| Borrow Cap | 20             |
| LTV       | 73%            |
| LT        | 78%            |
| Liquidation Bonus | 5%             |
| Liquidation Protocol Fee | 20%            |
| Reserve Factor | 50%            |
| Base Variable Borrow Rate | 0.25%          |
| Variable Slope 1 | 4%             |
| Variable Slope 2 | 60%            |
| Uoptimal  | 80%            |
| Flashloan Enabled | Yes            |

## Aave V4 Specific Parameters

### Spoke Parameters

| **Chain** | **Hub** | **Spoke** | **Reserve** | **Collateral Factor** | **Max Liquidation Bonus** | **Borrowable** | **Collateral Risk** | **Liquidation Fee** | **Risk Premium Threshold** | **Receive****Shares** |
|-------|-----|-------|---------|-------------------|-----------------------|------------|-----------------|-----------------|------------------------|---------------|
| Ethereum | Core Hub | Main Spoke | cirBTC  | 78%               | 5.55%                 | TRUE       | 0               | 10%             | 0                      | TRUE          |

### Add and Draw Caps

| **Chain** | **Hub** | **Spoke** | **Reserve** | **Add Cap** | **Draw Cap** |
|-------|-----|-------|---------|---------|----------|
| Ethereum | Core Hub | Main Spoke | cirBTC  | 250     | 25       |

### Interest Rate Curve

| **Chain** | **Hub** | **Asset** | **Base** | **Slope 1** | **Slope 2** | **Uoptimal** | **Liquidity Fee** |
|-------|-----|-------|------|---------|---------|----------|---------------|
| Ethereum | Core Hub | cirBTC | 0.25% | 4%      | 60%     | 80%      | 20%           |

## Price feed Recommendation

Use Chainlink’s [BTC/USD feed](https://data.chain.link/feeds/ethereum/mainnet/btc-usd) to price cirBTC on Aave V3 and V4.

## Useful Links

* [Circle cirBTC product page](https://www.circle.com/cirbtc)
* [Circle announcement: cirBTC is Live on Ethereum](https://www.circle.com/blog/cirbtc-is-now-live-on-ethereum)

# Disclaimer

This proposal was prepared by Aave Labs in its capacity as a contributor to the Aave ecosystem. Aave Labs has no financial relationship with Circle or any of its affiliates and has not received compensation from Circle in connection with this proposal.

# Next Steps

1. Gather community feedback during the ARFC stage.
2. Service Providers to post Asset Technical Assessment and Asset Risk Assessment, including supply caps, reserve factor, interest rate parameters, and oracle configuration for both instances.
3. If the ARFC response is positive, escalate to Snapshot for off-chain confirmation.
4. Submit the corresponding AIP for on-chain enforcement on the Aave V3 Core. Execute the corresponding transaction through the V4 Security Council on the Aave V4 Core.

title: UIP-19: 100% USUAL Burn & UT Management Mandate
body:
**Author:** Usual Labs
**Forum discussion:** https://forum.usual.money/t/uip-19-100-usual-burn-ut-management-mandate/23

## Abstract

This proposal asks the DAO to burn 100% of the USUAL generated through bUSD0 unlocking and to grant Usual Labs a mandate to manage the Unlocking Threshold (UT) as an indirect buyback-and-burn mechanism.

The mandate has one economic constraint: UT adjustments must be calibrated to increase NAV per USUAL in circulation.

## Motivation

Today, approximately $30 million of Treasury assets, excluding the protocol’s own USUAL holdings, backs the USUAL token.

Under the current mechanism, USUAL generated through bUSD0 unlocking is allocated in three equal parts:

- one third to USUAL Star;
- one third to USUALx;
- one third to burn.

The UT is currently set at 3.75. At this level, the mechanism has approached an equilibrium where little or no new USUAL may be generated under prevailing market conditions. Usual Labs therefore considers that the current three-way distribution no longer provides a sufficiently clear or effective value-accrual policy.

Since 5 August, including pending operations, the mechanism has involved approximately:

- 15,600,433 USUAL, corresponding to approximately $140,000 of buybacks;
- 4,125,571 bUSD0 unlocked;
- 5,200,144 USUAL burned under the current one-third burn allocation;
- an estimated 0.273% NAV accretion.

A 100% burn policy creates a simpler rule: every USUAL generated through bUSD0 unlocking is permanently removed from circulation. The UT then becomes an indirect buyback-and-burn lever that Usual Labs can calibrate according to market conditions.

## Specification

### 1. Reallocate the full flow to burn

| Allocation | Current | Proposed |
|---|---:|---:|
| USUAL Star | 33.33% | 0% |
| USUALx | 33.33% | 0% |
| Burn | 33.33% | 100% |

Any USUAL covered by this mechanism would be permanently and automatically burned during the daily distribution cycle.

### 2. Grant Usual Labs a UT management mandate

The DAO would authorize Usual Labs to set and adjust the UT at its discretion, using it as an indirect buyback-and-burn mechanism responsive to market conditions.

No predefined UT range applies. The mandate is outcome-based: Usual Labs must calibrate adjustments so that they are expected to increase NAV per USUAL in circulation.

Economically, whenever $1 worth of USUAL is burned, the protocol must ensure that the value of the future income given up through the corresponding bUSD0 unlocking is significantly lower than $1. The mechanism is therefore designed to increase the value backing each remaining USUAL.

## Treasury & revenue impact

This proposal authorizes no direct treasury payout or transfer.

Its economic impact comes from two linked effects:

1. all USUAL generated through bUSD0 unlocking is removed from circulation rather than redistributed;
2. UT adjustments affect the amount of bUSD0 unlocked and the associated future protocol income.

The mandate requires the value of the USUAL burned to exceed the future income forgone from the corresponding unlocked bUSD0, so that each adjustment remains NAV-accretive for USUAL holders.

## Explicitly out of scope

This proposal does not modify USUALx unstaking fees.

## Voting options

- **For:** approve the 100% burn allocation and grant Usual Labs the UT management mandate described above.
- **Against:** retain the current allocation and governance process.
- **Abstain.**

title: Adalia Foundation / DAO Election 2026-2027 Term
body:
Community DAO Election — 2026-2027 Term

Please vote for the Community Member you would like to represent you in the DAO.

What Does a DAO Actually Do?
A DAO (Decentralized Autonomous Organization) is a community-led organization where members collectively make decisions through governance proposals and voting.

The DAO may vote on matters such as:
💰 Treasury spending — e.g., “Should we spend $XXX on development?”
🛠️ What to build next — e.g., “Which feature should we prioritize?”
📜 Governance rules — e.g., “Should we increase the voting quorum?”
🤝 Partnerships — e.g., “Should we partner with Project X?”
🪙 Token-related decisions — such as emissions, incentives, or grants
👥 Community funding — e.g., selecting recipients from several grant applicants

The DAO representatives are responsible for participating in these decisions and representing the interests of the community.



DAO Structure

Seats
The DAO will initially consist of 5 elected members.
As the community grows, this may be increased to 7 members over the next 2–3 years.

Term
Each elected member will serve a one-calendar-year term.
Elections will take place around the turn of the year, most likely in early January. The first election will elect representatives for the 2027 term.

Participation & Responsibilities
DAO members are expected to actively participate in governance.
Members must vote on DAO proposals within 7 days of a proposal being submitted.
Persistent inactivity or failure to participate in governance may result in removal from the DAO.

Replacing a Member
If a DAO member needs to be replaced during their term, the vacant seat will first be offered to the candidate who received the sixth-highest number of votes in the most recent election, provided they are still interested and willing to serve.
If the sixth-ranked candidate is no longer interested or available, the seat will be offered to the next highest-ranked candidate, continuing down the election results until an eligible and willing candidate is found.

Please review the candidates and cast your vote for the Community Member you believe would best represent the community.

title: CP_26-004: Operation Kingmaker
body:
Summary
-------

Last year, Coinage launched what became the number one creator coin on Base. It went from a market cap of ~$80,000 to $15 million in a matter of months, before Coinbase and Base announced they would be pivoting away from promoting creator coins in their respective apps.

![maxresdefault (32).jpg](ipfs://bafybeifsnhfab4b6um5cscrne4z4wgnh27xk7o67q3kqbnmualudjcwgd4)

The experiment with $COINAGE brought to light a number of learnings. Perhaps most importantly, we learned that leveraging the Coinage brand -- and trust we've been able to build by incubating the first community-owned media outlet -- can spark wonders in low-trust, emerging markets.

Since then, Robinhood has followed Coinbase's lead to launch their own Ethereum Layer-2. The Robinhood chain has seen an explosion of memecoins and tokens.

At the highest level, this proposal endeavors to port what we've been able to build with $COINAGE thus far into the Robinhood ecosystem in a strategic fashion.

* * * * *

Background
----------

Coinage has previously approved various proposals to continue scaling $COINAGE. These efforts have proved fruitful. Despite Coinbase's pivot away from creator coins, and Zora's ensuing price collapse, $COINAGE remains one of the largest creator coins on Base (currently top five by market capitalization at the time of this proposal.)

Robinhood's ecosystem has now also seen token launchpads sprout up. The category leader is Pons. Importantly -- unlike Zora -- when tokens launch there, the original trading pools created are paired with Ethereum (a much more sustainable design than pairing new tokens with a volatile token like $ZORA.)

Building on the lessons learned in our launch, Coinage has also endeavored to create and support other liquidity pools beyond the original $COINAGE-$ZORA launch pool. For example, we worked with Aerodrome to set up a $COINAGE-$USDC pool.

Like Zora, Pons offers token creators a share of trading fees that stem from a token's launch. With the $COINAGE launch on Zora, these trading fee revenues were material for Coinage in 2025.

Despite never selling $COINAGE, Coinage was able to passively benefit from the trading activity we generated, and also benefitted from the added exposure our newly launched token brought within the Base ecosystem.

* * * * *

Proposal Details
----------------

### Part 1 --- A plan for $COINAGE

We launched $COINAGE as Coinage's memecoin (creator coin) on Base when it was the leading Ethereum Layer-2. It offered no utility beyond what was made possible by the Zora platform at the time of launch.

Eventually, we realized the token gave us a touchpoint on the Base chain with users there, and it boosted Coinage's awareness as the token grew. It became an interesting lever for experimentation beyond Zora -- eventually culminating in us being able to let holders vote on and nominate entries for [Coinage's Crypto Project of the Year last year](https://v1.snapshot.box/#/cpoty.eth).

Since then, we realized $COINAGE as a memecoin offers an interesting compliment to our existing membership NFTs on Ethereum. Rather than co-op governance, these tokens allow for a proxy on the attention we are able to generate (as all good memecoins do) and a specific medium through which communities on Base can interact with Coinage.

As Robinhood's chain continues to grow, this proposal would allow Coinage to expand to Robinhood's chain by launching a $COINAGE token there. Importantly, this proposal does not endeavor to create competing tokens on two different chains that become dilutive to each other.

Instead, as the name of this proposal suggests, this proposal seeks to implement a strategy that becomes net accretive to both $COINAGE on Base and $COINAGE on Robinhood, by openly experimenting in two distinct Layer-2 ecosystems. As a journalistic, community-owned media outlet, this launch will be illuminating -- if not kingmaking.

This proposal, however, is not without risks. There is no guarantee $COINAGE on Base trades anywhere near $COINAGE on Robinhood. If this proposal passes, Coinage will endeavor to explore cross-chain trading partners that may help users on either chain.

To support appearances of neutrality between chains and to prevent fears of dilution, this proposal would also permanently abandon the ~387M $COINAGE that remains locked in the ZORA contract (on Base) that was set to unlock over 4 years to Coinage.

* * * * *

### Part 2 --- Coinage's Expansion with Market Signal

In addition to the launch of $COINAGE on Robinhood, this proposal seeks to codify an important evolution for Coinage.

Many of our members value the content and IP that Coinage has been able to produce since launching in 2022. Fewer members understand that as we've published award-winning content, we've also been able to build incredible distribution rails through our site, social accounts, syndication partners, and YouTube channel (108,000+ subscribers.)

As discussed at our Annual Meeting this year, our reach has expanded considerably and has now become monetizable. At the same time, optimizing solely for partnership or collaboration monetization risks Coinage losing subscribers, reach, or brand power.

As such, the Coinage board has endeavored to create a framework that allows for setting a floor for collaborations to be considered. This proposal sets that threshold for outside collaborators at holding 45,454,545 $COINAGE ($5,000) at the current market rate.

This proposal allows Coinage to experiment with this collaboration format by distributing the pilot season of Trustless Media's "Market Signal" through Coinage channels in 2026, so long as Trustless maintains its holdings of 45,454,545 $COINAGE.

* * * * *

NOTE: In order to vote, a wallet must now hold [a Coinage Caucus or Network NFT](https://www.coinage.media/about#mint). Our Caucus and Network NFTs allow holders to join our DAO/Co-op. To co-own the fastest-growing Web3 media outlet, [you can mint one now.](https://opensea.io/item/ethereum/0x4776defcf622c60c6419cccc9ee9e9042fadf3f7/2) Become an official DAO member to become eligible for voting and patronage dividends. By minting, you will stand alongside the co-founder of Netflix, and other Web3 leaders today!
