title: BIP-104: Aargauer Kunsthaus — Artificial Creativity Exhibition
body:
> *`Note: Snapshot is only a summary and may leave ambiguities that are covered in the full BIP in the forum which takes precedent.`*

## Summary

Botto has been invited to participate in *Artificial Creativity*, a group exhibition at the Aargauer Kunsthaus in Aarau, Switzerland, running September 26, 2026 – January 10, 2027 (~4 months), in cooperation with HEK (House of Electronic Arts). Botto has a dedicated room (E3) within the exhibition. Three works are on display — two consigned by collectors, one unsold treasury work — with no sales component. The exhibition features an interactive voting terminal that onboards visitors into Botto's governance process via VP delegation. All production costs are covered by the Aargauer Kunsthaus and the DAO receives 1,000 CHF as an artist fee to offset core team time.

## Proposal Specification

1. Botto participates in *Artificial Creativity* at the Aargauer Kunsthaus, Aarau, Switzerland, September 26, 2026 – January 10, 2027.
2. Three works displayed in dedicated room E3:
   - *Utility Stream* (Genesis period) — consigned by LeRandom
   - *Mirror Stages XII* — unsold treasury inventory, currently listed for sale on Verse
   - *Prismatic Safari* (p5.js series) — consigned by Bharat Krymo
3. No works are held back from sale. *Mirror Stages XII* remains listed on Verse as normal throughout the exhibition.
4. An interactive voting terminal is installed in E3, allowing visitors to vote on Botto's live weekly fragments via a simplified interface. Terminal votes do not count toward the main leaderboard but are recorded for the DAO's use.
5. Visitors are prompted to sign up to the Studio via a link that automatically allocates VP and join a designated Aargauer Kunsthaus VP delegation group.
6. Visitor emails are collected for follow-up outreach if they go inactive after their visit.
7. An introduction video contextualizing Botto's practice will be displayed in E3.
8. The core team monitors conversion rates after the first month and iterates on the onboarding flow if needed.
9. Museum shop magnets using LeRandom's Genesis piece may be sold pending LeRandom's approval. Proceeds support the museum foundation.

---

## Criteria of Success
- Minimum 30 new weekly voters acquired through the exhibition
- Aargauer Kunsthaus VP delegation group active with at least 20 members by end of exhibition
- Onboarding flow iterated at least once based on real conversion data
- Learnings documented and shared with the DAO at the end of the exhibition

---

## Disadvantages/Risks

- **Non-crypto-native audience:** most visitors will have no prior exposure to blockchain or wallets; mitigated by a stripped-back onboarding interface and a simplified sign-up flow requiring no prior knowledge

---

## Budget

- **Revenue:** 1,000 CHF artist fee to the DAO
- **Costs:** All production costs covered by Aargauer Kunsthaus (8,000 CHF). Core team time from existing payroll — no additional budget required.

title: SAEP-20: Update Risk Curation Framework Artifact Section
body:
# SAEP-20: Update Risk Curation Framework Artifact Section - September 7, 2026

Spark's Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Phoenix Labs.

## Review

The Spark community can hereby express support or opposition to the following changes:

## Summary

The proposal recommends that Spark governance amend the [Risk Curation Framework](https://sky-atlas.io/#78018ebc-c69d-44f6-b602-190edca11483) of the Spark Artifact to do seven things:

- Extend the framework's cancellation provisions to cover Morpho Vaults v2 instances, where the revoking role is the Sentinel rather than the Guardian and the vault owner cannot cancel directly. Add the Curator as an authorized canceller.
- Narrow the independence requirement defined in [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.3.1 - Guardian Independence](https://sky-atlas.io/#ea50c8da-008e-4f0f-b2df-ac666d5faf13), permitting overlap between the Curator and the cancellation authority, provided the holder controlled by the Operational Executor Agent uses a separate signer set and at least one holder is fully independent of every Curator entity. The Sentora RLUSD Morpho Vault meets the amended standard and not the current one.
- Rename the Guardian role used in the framework to the Cancellation Authority, covering the Morpho Vaults v1 Guardian and the Morpho Vaults v2 Sentinel as a single role, state the conditions for removing a Sentinel role holder, and restate the reporting requirement in those terms.
- Add an Allocator instance parameter to the [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.7.1 - Instance Parameter Definitions](https://sky-atlas.io/#3d1e7988-f513-4632-a653-69d420379998).
- Add the Sentora RLUSD Morpho Vault on Ethereum Mainnet to the list of [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.7.2 - Approved Instances](https://sky-atlas.io/#5f30c335-8f12-4cc7-becd-f542a7546463).
- Relabel the Guardian parameter as Cancellation Authority in the four existing approved instance records, so that every instance record uses the parameter name defined at [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.7.1.5 - Guardian](https://sky-atlas.io/#817391bd-3748-479c-846e-f8d3e3ec56f4).
- Correct the contract address recorded for the [Ethereum Mainnet Spark Blue Chip USDT Morpho Vault](https://sky-atlas.io/#5ef1e78f-e1d2-4b09-b00c-618e36ccb2d8), which names a vault that has since been replaced.

## Background

The [Risk Curation Framework](https://sky-atlas.io/#78018ebc-c69d-44f6-b602-190edca11483) governs Spark's delegation of risk parameter management to third-party Curators, and the conditions under which pending timelocked changes made by a Curator can be cancelled. The framework's cancellation provisions were written for Morpho Vaults v1. In v1 the admin role that can revoke a pending timelocked change is named Guardian, and the Spark SubProxy and the Guardian each cancel directly. Morpho Vaults v2 differs in three respects that the current text does not accommodate. First, the role is named Sentinel. Second, revocation is restricted to the Curator and Sentinel roles, so the vault owner is not itself a revoking role and the Spark SubProxy cannot cancel directly; it instead exercises cancellation authority through a Sentinel that it appoints. Third, multiple addresses may hold the Sentinel role at the same time, whereas [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.3 - Guardian Role](https://sky-atlas.io/#900c4a0d-ed93-41ad-b914-f84d50d6940e) was written on the assumption of a single holder.


For details on the Sentora-curated RLUSD Morpho Vault into the Spark Liquidity Layer, please see item 5 _[Ethereum] Spark Liquidity Layer — Onboard the Sentora-curated RLUSD Morpho Vaults V2 instance_ in the [_[September 10, 2026] Proposed Changes to Spark for Upcoming Spell_ forum post](https://forum.skyeco.com/t/september-10-2026-proposed-changes-to-spark-for-upcoming-spell/28208).

## Proposal Details

It is proposed that Spark governance approves the following changes to the Risk Curation Framework section of the Spark Artifact:

- Amend [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.1 - Authorized Cancellers](https://sky-atlas.io/#f87333c8-ec5e-4483-83a9-791e1f9f9634) to add the Curator as an authorized canceller and to extend the provision to Morpho Vaults v2.
- Retitle [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.3 - Guardian Role](https://sky-atlas.io/#900c4a0d-ed93-41ad-b914-f84d50d6940e) to Cancellation Authority, describe the v1 Guardian and the v2 Sentinel as a single role, and state the conditions for removing a Sentinel role holder.
- Replace [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.3.1 - Guardian Independence](https://sky-atlas.io/#ea50c8da-008e-4f0f-b2df-ac666d5faf13) with a requirement of a signer set separate from the Curator multisig plus at least one fully independent cancellation authority holder, in place of the current bar on any overlap between the two roles.
- Retitle [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.3.2 - Guardian Reporting](https://sky-atlas.io/#ac45b63b-3394-49d6-aab7-ff67b1d4fd0c) to Cancellation Authority Reporting and assign the reporting obligation to the acting role holder.
- Retitle the instance parameter [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.7.1.5 - Guardian](https://sky-atlas.io/#817391bd-3748-479c-846e-f8d3e3ec56f4) to "Cancellation Authority".
- Add a new Allocator instance parameter under [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.7.1 - Instance Parameter Definitions](https://sky-atlas.io/#3d1e7988-f513-4632-a653-69d420379998).
- Restate the four existing [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.7.2 - Approved Instances](https://sky-atlas.io/#5f30c335-8f12-4cc7-becd-f542a7546463), relabelling the Guardian parameter as "Cancellation Authority".
- Correct the contract address for the [Ethereum Mainnet Spark Blue Chip USDT Morpho Vault](https://sky-atlas.io/#5ef1e78f-e1d2-4b09-b00c-618e36ccb2d8) to the current Spark Blue Chip USDT Vault at [0xb0c424116172B55CbB6dD3136F5989F7959e5B91](https://etherscan.io/address/0xb0c424116172B55CbB6dD3136F5989F7959e5B91).
- Add the Sentora RLUSD Morpho Vault on Ethereum Mainnet as an approved instance.

Independence is determined by Spark governance when the instance record at [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.7.2 - Approved Instances](https://sky-atlas.io/#5f30c335-8f12-4cc7-becd-f542a7546463) is approved, on the basis of the holder identities recorded under [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.7.1.5 - Guardian](https://sky-atlas.io/#817391bd-3748-479c-846e-f8d3e3ec56f4). A change to the Curator or to the cancellation authority holder set requires a further Artifact edit to that record.

More details with exact changes for each of the above points can be found at the [_SAEP-20: Update Risk Curation Framework Artifact Section_ forum post](https://forum.skyeco.com/t/saep-20-update-risk-curation-framework-artifact-section/28221)

## Justification

This proposal addresses the following points:
- The current text does not describe cancellation on Morpho Vaults v2.
- The rename removes a collision with an existing defined term.
- The independence requirement is narrowed.
- The Allocator holds powers the Curator does not.
- The existing instance records are updated to match.

Please see the [_SAEP-20: Update Risk Curation Framework Artifact Section_ forum post](https://forum.skyeco.com/t/saep-20-update-risk-curation-framework-artifact-section/28221) for justification details.

The proposed Spark Artifact changes can be found in the following pull request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/329

## Outcomes

- If "For" receives the most votes, the proposal will be approved. The associated pull request will be merged into Spark's artifact. When required, the listed changes will proceed to implementation by the relevant actors.
- If "Against" receives the most votes, the proposal will be rejected. No changes will be implemented.

title: [BIP-1] Proximity voice chat: push-to-talk, relay-only, spectators listen
body:
**Author:** blingdawg
**Date:** 2026-09-07
**Discussion:** https://governance.bawsaq.org/t/bip-1-proximity-voice-chat-push-to-talk-relay-only-spectators-listen/33
**Temp Check:** https://governance.bawsaq.org/t/temp-check-voice-chat-so-we-can-actually-talk-to-each-other/28

*blingdawg's proposal, published on his behalf — the wallet shown as creator is the publisher, not the author. The discussion thread holds the full specification.*

## Simple Summary

Add proximity push-to-talk voice. Hold **V** (desktop) or a **TALK** button (touch), and players within 25 m hear you: full volume inside 5 m, fading to silence at 25 m, panned to the side the speaker stands on. No microphone is open unless the key is held, and the browser's mic prompt fires the first time V is pressed, never on load. Spectators hear the fighters they are watching and cannot speak. **Shift+V** mutes everyone; the scoreboard gains **MUTE** and **REPORT** per player.

Every voice connection is relayed through a TURN server run by the maintainers, so no player's IP address is ever exposed to another player. **The game will never ship a direct peer-to-peer mode, not even as a fallback.**

## Motivation

Text chat is the only way to talk to another player, and nobody types mid-kick. The Temp Check established that voice is wanted and named the risks — abuse, mobile Safari, IP leaks, the mic prompt, who pays for a relay; this BIP answers each with a rule.

## Specification

| Parameter | Today | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| Voice chat | none | proximity push-to-talk |
| Push-to-talk key | – | V (desktop), TALK button (touch) |
| Mute-all key | – | Shift+V |
| Hearing radius | – | 25 m |
| Full-volume radius | – | 5 m |
| Peers heard at once | – | 8 nearest |
| Spectators one fighter feeds at once | – | 6 |
| Server-side range check | – | about 40 m, by the server's own positions |
| Relay credential lifetime | – | 1 hour or less |
| Reports per player | – | 5 per hour |
| Transport | – | WebRTC, relayed only, never direct |
| Spectators | – | listen-only, enforced server-side |
| Audio through the game server | – | none |
| Voice-banned wallets | – | none to start; a moderators' list |

Rules that are privacy and cost decisions, not build choices:

- **Audio never goes through the game server.** Voice is browser to browser; the server passes only the setup messages, and only between players it sees within about 40 m.
- **Every connection is relayed.** Direct peer-to-peer would put each player's IP address into the other player's browser. A build that ships direct peer-to-peer, even as a fallback, fails this BIP.
- **The server enforces what it can without hearing anything:** range, spectators listen-only, a rate limit on setup messages, the ban list. Relay credentials expire within an hour. With no relay there is no mic prompt at all; a voice-banned wallet gets no voice either way.

## What this vote settles

- Voice ships with the player-facing behaviour and the parameters above.
- Every voice connection is relayed. The game never ships a direct peer-to-peer mode.
- Spectators listen and never speak.
- The maintainers run the relay and may switch voice off if it is abused or the bill is out of line, posting why on the forum within 24 hours.
- Changing any value in the table is a new BIP.

## What it does not settle

- Where the relay is hosted, or how any of this is built — the maintainers'.
- Whether any individual is voice-banned. That is moderation, under the moderators' own rules.
- Team channels, a global channel, private-room voice beyond these radius rules, and recording. Not in this BIP.

## Effect on the money

Buy-in, payout split, burn, round length, what a player ends a round with, ArenaPool and anything the operator key signs, and what the server reports as a kill: **all unchanged.**

One new recurring cost: the relay — a few dollars a month for a small machine running an open-source TURN server, plus bandwidth of roughly 24 kbps per person you are talking to while the key is held (under 2 GB an hour at 50 concurrent players). Paid from whatever pays for the game server today.

## How we will know it worked

Checked 14 days after it ships, by anyone, and posted in the thread:

1. Two players together in a live round on arena.bawsaq.org both see "1 nearby" and hear each other — Chrome, Firefox and Safari on desktop, and one iPhone.
2. Voice stayed up the 14 days with no outage posted, and nobody has published a way to see another player's IP address through it.
3. A REPORT has been tested and a moderator has confirmed in the thread it reached them.

## Voting

- **For** — ship it.
- **Against** — do not ship it.
- **Abstain** — counts toward quorum, not toward the result.

Single choice, 3 days. Passes on more than 50% of For + Against, with quorum of 29,842,021 BAWSAQ. Voting is gasless message signing — no transaction, no gas. Voting power is your BAWSAQ balance on Robinhood Chain, frozen at the block this proposal was created. Nothing executes on Ethereum; the space's network setting is a formality, since Snapshot does not support Robinhood Chain.

title: Strategic Protocol Reserve Temp Check
body:
## Intent & Overview

As shared in the original [Hydrex Voting Expansion](https://paragraph.com/@hydrex/hydrex-voting-expansion) article, the purpose of this Temp Check is to decide which option will be proposed for a formal onchain vote. This temp check has no quorum and its voting outcomes have no onchain impacts. The most popular option, weighted by votes, will be placed into an onchain proposal where onchain specifics will be voted upon and executed.

For a full understanding of the governance process, please read the aforementioned article or the [Hydrex Governance Documentation](https://docs.hydrex.fi/#governance).

## SPR Reminder: A High-Level Performance Snapshot

Currently sitting at $1.45M in value, the vast majority is held in bluechips and stablecoins, with nearly all liquidity provisioned into Hydrex gauges. At a current snapshot, the SPR is averaging approximately 8% APR, which contributes ~$2,200 in weekly fees generated split across Hydrex Account voters.

To date, the SPR has experienced around 11.8% in net losses vs USDC inputs as a result of holdings price changes and impermanent loss. Specifics about the SPR and its current capital structure are readily available on the [Hydrex Analytics page](https://www.hydrex.fi/analytics).

The options below purely address the proposed actionable items, and do not get into any nuances on justifications or rationale, in order to remain unbiased. For further details, including breakdowns of the options below, please read the original [Hydrex Voting Expansion](https://paragraph.com/@hydrex/hydrex-voting-expansion) article or the dialogue captured in the [Hydrex Discord](https://discord.gg/hydrexfi).

---

## Option 1: Conservative

Prioritizes retaining value in the SPR. All existing liquidity would remain in the SPR and be deployed across the Hydrex protocol in the following proportions:

| Allocation | Deployment |
|---|---|
| 50% | Bluechip Crypto LPs |
| 30% | Lending Gauges (Bluechip & Stables) |
| 20% | Bluechip RWA LPs |

## Option 2: Fee-Gen Optimization

Prioritizes maximizing fees generated by the SPR. All existing liquidity would remain in the SPR and be deployed across the Hydrex protocol in the following proportions:

| Allocation | Deployment |
|---|---|
| 50% | High-Volume Base Ecosystem Assets |
| 30% | High-Volume RWA LPs |
| 20% | Bluechip Crypto LPs |

## Option 3: SPR Bribes

Prioritizes ensuring USDC collected by the SPR most directly makes its way to Hydrex Account operators. All existing liquidity would be removed from the SPR and used as follows:

- 100% is converted to USDC and bribed on Hydrex gauges
- Bribes executed at a rate of **$100,000/week** until the SPR is exhausted

## Option 4: Blended

A blended effort utilizing different components of the above options. SPR liquidity would be used as follows:

- 50% retained and deployed in proportions congruent with Option 1 (Conservative)
- 50% converted to USDC and bribed on Hydrex gauges
- Bribes executed at a rate of **$50,000/week** until the SPR is 50% exhausted (value taken from time of onchain proposal completion)

---

## Closing Notes

Regardless of the chosen outcome, all liquidity deployments will utilize automated liquidity management strategies (such as Ichi) or IL-free gauges (such as Morpho). No manual concentrated liquidity positions will be created or managed. This is intentional, to avoid excessive administrative overhead and guarantee liquidity stays in range to continually generate fees for Hydrex Account Holders.

Additionally, assume all future USDC collected by the SPR will be utilized in accordance with the selected option. For example, Option 1 would continue to deploy liquidity in those ratios, while Option 3 would continue to holistically bribe collected USDC.

Upon completion of Temp Check voting, the top option will be codified into a set of onchain actions associated with an onchain governance proposal detailing all specifics of how the proposal will go into effect.

title: 🎮 Base Brick Breaker — VRNouns Community Showcase
body:
## 🎮 Base Brick Breaker
![BBB.jpg](ipfs://bafybeievgxrz3dgxjtcrvlsytb3bstevrbjryic32jhcsfoi4wfg5in4bu)
Hey VRNouns 👋

I’m a VRNouns holder, and I wanted to share something I’ve been building on Base: **Brick Breaker**.

### 🟦 Why I built it on Base

One of the things I really enjoy about Base is its focus on **building**.

Base makes me want to experiment, create, and actually turn ideas into something people can use.

That was one of the main reasons I decided to build something myself.

I wanted to experience what it feels like to take an idea from my head, turn it into a real game, and see people actually play something I built on Base.

And honestly, that feeling has been one of the most rewarding parts of the project.

Brick Breaker may have started as a relatively simple idea, but building it on Base made me look at the project differently.

I wasn't just making a game.

I was learning by building, experimenting with onchain interactions, and trying to create something that could bring people into the Base ecosystem through something familiar and fun.

### 🧱 What is Base Brick Breaker?

At its core, Brick Breaker is an arcade game that almost everyone can understand.

Control the paddle, keep the ball alive, break the bricks, build your score, and try to go further than everyone else.

But I didn't want to make just another classic Brick Breaker clone.

I wanted to build something with progression, competition, and a small Web3/onchain layer behind the experience.

The game currently includes:

- 🏆 **Tournament Mode** — play on Base with a 0.00001 ETH entry fee per game
- 🕹️ **Practice Mode** — a way to play without entering the paid tournament experience
- 📊 **Leaderboard** — compete for the highest scores
- ⛓️ **Onchain Scores** — genuine new best scores can be submitted and recorded on Base
- 🧱 **20 different level formations** — including patterns such as Pyramid, Fortress, Diamond, Wings, Lightning, Spiral, Heart, Crown, Invader, Rocket and more
- 💥 **Multi-hit bricks** — later levels introduce stronger bricks that require multiple hits
- 🔥 **Combo System** — build longer combos to increase your score
- ⚡ **Fever Mode** — reach a high combo and activate a temporary 2X score multiplier
- 🛡️ **Combo Shield** — build your combo far enough to earn a shield that can save your run from losing a life
- 🎁 **Power-ups** — WIDE, FIRE, MULTI, LIFE and FREEZE, each changing the way you play
- 🎯 **Level Missions** — different objectives such as breaking bricks, reaching combos, collecting power-ups, achieving a target score, or clearing a level without losing a life
- 🏅 **Run Challenges** — additional challenges such as Brick Rush, Combo Hunter, Power Collector, Perfect Run and Elite Hunter
- ⭐ **XP & Progression** — actions during a run contribute to player progression
- 🏆 **Achievements** — milestones such as reaching Level 10, achieving high combos, collecting power-ups, destroying bricks and defeating bosses
- 👾 **Elite Core Bosses** — every 5th level introduces a boss encounter with its own health bar and a larger score reward

The game also has its own sound effects, background music, visual hit effects, particles, score feedback and combo animations to make the experience feel more like an actual arcade game rather than a basic browser experiment.

The different level formations and progressively stronger bricks are designed to make the game become more challenging as you progress. Power-ups also become more present as the levels advance, giving players more ways to approach each run. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}

### 🌐 Why connect this to crypto?

This is actually one of the ideas behind the project that I care about most.

Crypto can still feel intimidating to people who have never interacted with it.

Wallets, networks, transactions, gas, smart contracts, onchain applications and all the terminology around Web3 can create a pretty big barrier for newcomers.

I think games can offer a different way in.

Almost everyone understands how to play a game.

You don't need to understand blockchain technology to understand:

**"Keep the ball alive. Break the bricks. Get a higher score."**

So rather than starting someone's experience with crypto by giving them a long explanation about wallets, networks and transactions, I wanted to start with something much simpler:

> **Here is a game. Have fun.**

Then, naturally, the player can discover that there is something happening underneath the game.

Connect a wallet.

Play on Base.

Compete on a leaderboard.

Try to beat another player's score.

And, in the tournament experience, make a small Base transaction to play.

The goal isn't to force crypto into a game.

It's to make interacting with an onchain application feel **normal and approachable**.

I think that's one of the interesting opportunities for Web3: sometimes the best way to introduce people to the technology isn't to explain the technology first.

Give them something they actually want to use.

### ⛓️ Building an onchain game

Another important part of the project for me is that the blockchain integration isn't just a label saying "Build on Base."

The game actually interacts with Base.

Tournament games use a small ETH payment on Base, and when a player achieves a genuine new best score, the game can submit that score and level to a smart contract on Base. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}

That makes the game an experiment in combining a familiar Web2-style gaming experience with actual onchain interactions.

It's still a small project.

But that's exactly why I wanted to build it.

I wanted to learn by doing.

### 🟡 VRNouns Builders

I’m also sharing this because I’d love to see more VRNouns holders sharing the things **they** are building.

If you're working on a project, game, art, tool, or anything interesting, I think this could be a great way for the community to discover it.

Maybe there are already a lot of interesting things being built by VRNouns holders that most of us simply don't know about.

I'd love to see this become a small showcase for VRNouns builders — a place where people can introduce what they're working on, get feedback, and discover what other members of the community are creating.

### 🎮 Try Brick Breaker

If you'd like to try it:

🔗 **Play Brick Breaker:** https://base-brick-breaker.vercel.app/

Connect your wallet, give it a try, and see how far you can get.

If you're brave enough, try the Tournament Mode and see whether you can make it onto the leaderboard. 😄

I'd especially love to hear your feedback on whether the game succeeds in making the Base/onchain experience feel more approachable and fun.

### 🗳️ Community Vote

This is **not a governance proposal, funding request, or request for treasury support.**

It's simply a representative community vote to see what VRNouns holders think about the project and the idea behind it.

Do you like the project?

Do you think games can be a good way to introduce more people to crypto and onchain applications?

Would you like to see more projects like this from VRNouns builders?

Thanks for taking the time to check it out. 🫡

And most importantly:

**Keep building. 🟦**

title: [Proposal]: Upgrade the Gitcoin Governor
body:
[Proposal]: Upgrade the Gitcoin Governor
In March, Tally announced their shutdown. ScopeLift announced that they would be taking over the platform and its operations. As Gitcoin has used Tally for onchain governance, we explored a number of different options, and after internal due diligence decided to remain on the same platform and work with the ScopeLift team towards upgrades, most importantly security, especially after we had to move our treasury funds out of the timelock due to an open attack vector.

Summary
Upgrade the Gitcoin DAO’s on-chain Governor from GTC Governor Bravo to a modernized Governor built on OpenZeppelin v5. The upgrade preserves all current voting parameters and adds three capabilities: a Proposal Guardian that can cancel malicious proposals, late-quorum protection against last-minute vote manipulation, and a DAO-adjustable quorum.

Motivation
The current Governor has served the DAO well but predates several improvements in onchain governance tooling. This upgrade closes known safety gaps without changing the voter experience: delegates will propose, vote, and delegate exactly as they do today.

What Changes
Three new capabilities, additive only:

Proposal Guardian. A designated multisig can cancel proposals (only cancel, never modify or force execution). This is a safety valve against malicious, malformed, or compromised submissions. The DAO can remove or replace the guardian by governance vote. Those holding the seats of signers of the address will manage their own membership, and any change to a signer will be done through a governance vote. By definition, any proposal that does not go through our standard governance proposal process and follows the set format will be deemed malicious. Any proposal that follows the protocol but is highlighted as malicious will be reviewed by the guardian.

Late-quorum protection. If a proposal reaches quorum near the end of its voting window, the window automatically extends to guarantee a minimum reaction time for delegates. Closes a well-known category of last-block vote flips.

DAO-adjustable quorum. Quorum becomes a parameter the DAO can change by ordinary governance proposal rather than requiring another contract migration.

All other behavior is preserved. The new Governor is built from these OpenZeppelin extensions: GovernorCountingFractional (preserves ScopeLift’s flexible voting), GovernorSettableFixedQuorum, GovernorPreventLateQuorum, GovernorSettings, GovernorProposalGuardian, and GovernorVotesComp (GTC token compatibility).

Screenshot 2026-08-07 at 13.22.37
Screenshot 2026-08-07 at 13.22.37
1246×618 34.5 KB
Quorum, proposal threshold, voting delay, and voting period all remain DAO-adjustable after the upgrade.

Execution
The upgrade is a two-action proposal submitted to the current Governor Bravo:

The Timelock designates the new Governor as pending admin.

The new Governor accepts the admin role.

On execution, the old Governor can no longer control the DAO timelock, while the new Governor can. ScopeLift will update Cactus (formerly Tally) to reflect the new Governor immediately. All future governance actions will go through the new Governor.

Important for delegates: Do not submit new proposals to the old Governor between this proposal going onchain and its execution. Any proposal submitted to the old Governor after this one lands will not be executable and will need to be resubmitted to the new Governor.

Validation
ScopeLift’s simulation suite runs the full upgrade lifecycle against forked mainnet state, covering deployment, proposal submission, delegate voting, execution, and post-upgrade Governor operations (including quorum adjustments, Proposal Guardian powers, and parameter updates). ScopeLift will re-run the full suite against the live on-chain proposal data before voting opens. ScopeLift is an experienced team of smart contract engineers with a particular expertise in Governance contracts and onchain operations. They’ve successfully built and upgraded Governance contracts for many large DAOs, including Compound, ZKsync, Radworks, PoolTogether, and Gitcoin itself (during our last upgrade cycle).

Follow-up
A separate proposal to adopt the Franchiser for treasury delegation will follow after this upgrade executes.

Vote
FOR to upgrade the Gitcoin Governor
ABSTAIN from voting on upgrading the Gitcoin Governor
AGAINST upgrading the Gitcoin Governor

title: [Proposal #16] Community Vote to Delist
body:
Introduction

Orderly’s mission is to provide a high-quality trading environment with deep liquidity, sustainable trading activity, and transparent governance. While new listings bring growth and experimentation, it is equally important to evaluate underperforming markets and decide which should be removed.

This proposal introduces a new Community Vote to Delist. Instead of voting to remove tokens, the community will now vote to retain tokens from a pre-identified list, ensuring our resources are focused on assets with verifiable community support.

The Proposal

The Orderly Core Team has identified the following 7 tokens for potential delisting based on predefined criteria (e.g., sustained low liquidity, volume, and community activity).

Delisting Pool:

BZ
AXS
MORPHO
BCH
1000SHIB
GOAT
MEGA

The Vote & Outcome:

A "Vote to Retain" will be held for each token individually. For a token to be removed from the delisting pool and continue trading on Orderly, it must meet the following threshold:

3% of Total Staked $ORDER voting "AGAINST Delisting".

If none of the tokens meet the 3% retention threshold, all tokens in the pool will be delisted.

Rationale

This revised process ensures Orderly focuses liquidity on markets with active community engagement, while introducing a more efficient and decisive governance mechanism.

Efficiency & Clarity – Provides a clear, binary outcome for each asset based on measurable community support, eliminating ambiguity.

Community Empowerment – Directly measures which assets have sufficient stakeholder backing to merit ongoing platform support.

Protocol Integrity – Ensures resources are directed to ecosystems with engaged communities, driving sustainable growth.

Next Steps & Implementation

Community votes will be collected during the 7-day voting period.

After the vote, each token will be evaluated against the 3% retention threshold.

Tokens that fail to meet the threshold will be scheduled for delisting.

Orderly will issue a reminder at least 48 hours before any delisting is executed.

Voting Parameters

Retention Threshold: >3% of total staked $ORDER must vote "AGAINST Delisting" for a token to be saved.

Voting Period: 7 days

Eligibility: Only $ORDER staked before proposal submission counts toward voting power.

The Takeaway

This Vote to Retain empowers ORDER stakers to clearly signal support for the assets they value. This decisive process ensures Orderly maintains a vibrant market of high-engagement tokens, upholding our commitment to transparency and community-driven governance.

title: PIP-42: Launch of DAO-Operated Zone on Base, Ownership Transition & Compliance Changes
body:
**Summary**

This proposal:

1. Formally launches the DAO-operated Zone on Base upon confirmed completion and execution of all transactions and scripts required for the transition of ownership.

2. Completes the transition of the ownerSafeDao Safe on Base to full DAO control by removing the two remaining legacy individual signers and leaving the Ethereum DAO signers in control.

3. Raises the ZkpReserveController emission rate to approximately **16,000 ZKP per day** on Base.

4. Confirms the risk logic used when handling high-risk users for internal transfers and withdrawals.

5. Clarifies the Compliance Role funding arrangement established under PIP-41.

Together, these actions complete the Base launch and confirm the updated governance and compliance standards.

---

**Motivation**

Panther has been working towards the Base launch for some time, and these final actions bring that work to fruition.

For the launch to be successful, ownership of the relevant contracts must be under DAO control, consistent with the governance approach used on Polygon. Following this transition, future changes to the DAO-controlled deployment will require governance approval through subsequent PIPs.

To support internal transfers safely, this proposal also confirms the compliance logic designed to protect users against bad actors while preserving user sovereignty over their own funds.

Finally, this proposal clarifies a funding detail stated in PIP-41 so that no further ZKP minting is required to fund the Compliance Role.

Removing the legacy signers:

* Aligns control with DAO governance.
* Reduces operational risk.
* Simplifies key management.
* Strengthens decentralisation.
* Finalises the governance structure ahead of launch.

---

**Compliance Flow Rationale**

Panther's compliance logic is designed around a core principle: no user should have their funds trapped or effectively frozen within the protocol solely because of their risk classification.

This follows the approach taken by other privacy-preserving protocols, such as Privacy Pools, where users retain the ability to recover their own funds while controls prevent potentially illicit funds from being transferred to other users.

In line with this principle:

* High-risk or sanctioned users are restricted from sending funds to other users, whether through an internal transfer or withdrawal to a third-party wallet.

* All users, regardless of risk classification, retain the ability to withdraw their own funds back to their own wallet.

* The restriction is enforced automatically through smart contract logic and requires no discretionary action, case review, or manual authorisation by the Compliance Officer or another party.

* Panther DAO cannot intercept, reverse or freeze a transaction, and users retain the ability to exit the protocol to their own wallet.

---

**Compliance Risk Flow**

* **No-risk and low-risk users:** May interact freely with all protocol functions.

* **High-risk or sanctioned users:** Cannot send funds to other users through internal transfers or withdrawals to third-party wallets.

* **Withdrawals to own wallet:** All users may withdraw to their own wallet regardless of risk classification.

* **Enforcement:** The entire flow is automated and requires no Compliance Officer action, review or discretion.

---

**The Changes Made**

**1. Launch the DAO-operated Zone on Base**

The DAO-operated Zone on Base becomes the official live operational environment of Panther Protocol under DAO control.

Upon confirmation, the DAO Multisig:

* Formally declares the Zone live.
* Activates the production interface.
* Recognises the Base deployment as the official DAO-operated environment.

**2. Complete Safe ownership transition**

Remove the following two legacy signers from the Base Safe:

* Signer 1: `0xb83A3094272B6425f89BB5590b48928e2374eE11`
* Signer 2: `0xFee6D2Cb5816282D853fba79cB9C8b5EDB7908Cd`

Following their removal, the Safe remains controlled by the **five Ethereum DAO signers with a 2-of-5 threshold**.

**3. Raise Base ZKP reward emission**

Update the Base ZkpReserveController emission rate to:

`370370000000000000 wei/block`

This corresponds to approximately **16,000 ZKP per day on Base**.

The existing `minRewardedAmount` remains unchanged.

**4. Confirm compliance logic**

Confirm the compliance risk flow described above as the operational standard for internal transfers and withdrawals on the DAO-operated Base deployment.

---

**Compliance Grant Funding**

PIP-24 established the Compliance Officer's compensation at an agreed hourly rate.

PIP-41 subsequently authorized the DAO Council to use DAO Grants to fund the Compliance Role, consistent with the intent of PIP-24. However, the wording did not clearly distinguish between maintaining the agreed compensation rate and continuing payment specifically in ZKP.

This proposal clarifies that arrangement.

The Compliance Officer's compensation will continue at the hourly rate agreed under **PIP-24**, but will be settled in **USDT/USDC rather than ZKP**, sourced from DAO Council Grants.

This removes the need to mint additional ZKP to fund the Compliance Role while preserving the compensation arrangement previously approved by governance.

---

**Execution**

The governance execution takes place directly on **Base via the Reality module**, with no Ethereum-to-Base bridge transaction required for these actions.

The Reality module must be enabled on the Safe before execution.

Three Base transactions are required:

1. Remove legacy Signer 1 from the Base Safe.
2. Remove legacy Signer 2 from the Base Safe.
3. Update the ZkpReserveController emission rate to approximately 16,000 ZKP/day.

These calls are bundled into the governance execution batch.

---

**Voting**

**For**

Confirm the launch of the DAO-operated Zone on Base, execute the Safe ownership transition, raise the Base ZKP reward emission, approve the compliance standards described above, and approve the Compliance Role funding clarification.

**Against**

Do not launch the DAO-operated Zone on Base and make no changes to Safe ownership, ZKP reward emission, or compliance/funding policy at this time.

---

**Transactions for the Snapshot**

**PIP-42: Remove the Two Legacy Signers from the Base Safe and Raise the ZkpReserveController Emission**

**Addresses**

title: RSR Unlocking: The Burn Gauge (1 of 2)
body:
### Summary

RSR unlocking currently follows a fixed, time-based curve. [Two alternatives to that curve](https://forum.reserve.org/t/proposal-rsr-burn-gauge-vs-milestone-plan/1630) are being put to RSR holders at the same time. This proposal is **the Burn Gauge**.

Under the Burn Gauge, treasury RSR unlocking is tied directly to protocol-driven RSR burn. There is no time schedule: nothing unlocks unless the protocol is burning, and at the more conservative settings, protocol burn destroys additional treasury RSR rather than releasing any.

RSR holders set the gauge, and reset it every quarter.

### How the gauge is set

The gauge is not fixed at adoption. RSR holders choose its position on an ongoing basis:

- **Cadence:** quarterly.
- **Timing:** the vote happens after the quarterly update call and report, so Confusion Capital can share where things stand before holders choose.
- **Method:** a ranked choice vote on Snapshot across the five positions.
- **Term:** the winning position governs unlocking until the next quarterly vote replaces it.

Note that this is different from the vote you are casting now. **This** proposal is a simple For / Against / Abstain vote on whether to adopt the Burn Gauge at all. If it's adopted, the quarterly votes that follow are ranked choice.

### How it works

The gauge has five positions. Each sets a fixed ratio between RSR burned by the protocol and RSR either burned from, or unlocked out of, the treasury.

| Gauge position | Automatic effect of protocol burn | Additional unlocking |
|---|---|---|
| High Burn | 1 RSR burned by the protocol burns **4 RSR** from the treasury — no unlocking | Not available — nothing unlocks at this position |
| Low Burn | 1 RSR burned by the protocol burns **2 RSR** from the treasury — no unlocking | Not available — nothing unlocks at this position |
| Sustain | 2 RSR burned by the protocol unlocks **1 RSR** from the treasury | Available at **2:1** burned:unlocked — 2 treasury RSR burned per 1 extra RSR unlocked |
| Low Growth | 1 RSR burned by the protocol unlocks **2 RSR** from the treasury | Available at **1:2** burned:unlocked — 1 treasury RSR burned per 2 extra RSR unlocked |
| High Growth | 1 RSR burned by the protocol unlocks **4 RSR** from the treasury | Available at **1:4** burned:unlocked — 1 treasury RSR burned per 4 extra RSR unlocked |

**On the automatic column:** the amount is a function of realized protocol burn. If protocol burn is zero, nothing unlocks and nothing additional is destroyed.

**On the additional column:** at the three unlocking positions, Confusion Capital can unlock more than the automatic amount — but a portion of treasury RSR is burned in exchange for any additional unlock, at the ratio shown. Accelerating unlocking therefore costs supply. At the two burn positions there is no unlocking, automatic or otherwise.

### How this vote works

Two proposals are running simultaneously — this one (the Burn Gauge) and the Milestone Plan. They are **alternatives, not a package**.

**Please vote on both.** Quorum is measured separately on each proposal, so voting on only one makes it less likely that either reaches quorum. Vote For on the system you want and Against on the other.

- **If one passes and the other does not** — the one that passes is adopted.
- **If both pass** — the one with more total For votes is adopted.
- **If neither passes** — the existing Bitcoin-shaped unlocking curve remains in place.

### Voting details

- **Voting system:** Basic — For / Against / Abstain
- **Voting power:** `totalRSROwned`, measured across Ethereum, Base and BNB Chain at the snapshot block
- **Duration:** 7 days
- **Quorum:** 1,000,000,000 RSR, measured on this proposal alone

### Who is abstaining

The following are abstaining from both proposals: Nevin Freeman, Confusion Capital, ABC Labs, Best Friend Finance, and CC-incubated companies. Employees are eligible to vote.

### A note on what this vote binds

Confusion Capital has published a constitutional pledge to follow the outcome of RSR holder governance on unlocking. That pledge is a public commitment, not an on-chain enforcement mechanism.

### Background

- [Proposal: RSR Burn Gauge vs. Milestone Plan](https://forum.reserve.org/t/proposal-rsr-burn-gauge-vs-milestone-plan/1630)
- [Confusion Capital's Constitutional RSR Unlocking Governance Pledge](https://forum.reserve.org/t/confusion-capitals-constitutional-rsr-unlocking-governance-pledge/1621)
- [Prior discussion — forum post 1609](https://forum.reserve.org/t/1609)

title: RSR Unlocking: The Milestone Plan (2 of 2)
body:
### Summary

RSR unlocking currently follows a fixed, time-based curve. [Two alternatives to that curve](https://forum.reserve.org/t/proposal-rsr-burn-gauge-vs-milestone-plan/1630) are being put to RSR holders at the same time. This proposal is **the Milestone Plan**.

Under the Milestone Plan, treasury RSR unlocks in discrete tranches when the protocol hits defined business milestones — and only if RSR is trading in a range where unlocking is reasonable. There is no continuous release.

### How it works

**The milestone:** $2.5M Net Annualized Recurring Revenue (NARR). NARR in the current protocol design roughly equates to RSR burned by the protocol + staking rewards to RSR holders minus any incentives paid onchain or offchain to RToken holders, but it's broadly defined to be flexible with respect to future evolutions in how the ecosystem collects revenue.

**The unlock:** up to 3,000,000,000 RSR.

**The gate:** the 30-day moving average RSR price at the time the milestone is reached determines what actually happens.

| 30-day moving average RSR price | Outcome |
|---|---|
| **$0.005 – $0.015** | The full 3B RSR unlocks automatically. |
| **Below $0.005** | No unlock. The treasury either waits for the price to recover into the band, or proposes an alternative to RSR holders. |
| **Above $0.015** | Up to **$45M worth** of RSR unlocks at the current price — materially fewer than 3B tokens — or the treasury proposes an alternative to RSR holders. |

The price gate exists so that a fixed token count doesn't translate into a wildly different dollar amount depending on when the milestone lands.

### How this vote works

Two proposals are running simultaneously — this one (the Milestone Plan) and the Burn Gauge. They are **alternatives, not a package**.

title: 🗳️ Vote: Which Stock Drops First? Claim + Swap in One Tx with EIP-8130
body:
🗳️ Vote: Which Stock Drops First? Claim + Swap in One Tx with EIP-8130

Week one is on you.

Every terminal earns one of ten real tokenized stocks. Before the first distribution, the community decides which stock goes out first:

$NVDA · $AAPL · $TSLA · $GME · $SPCX
$SPY · $PLTR · $NFLX · $RDDT · $MSTR

What is EIP-8130?

EIP-8130 is native account abstraction, coming to Base with the Cobalt upgrade. It moves smart account features directly into the protocol, and the biggest one for us is native batch calls: multiple actions bundled into a single transaction. No bundlers, no relays, no extra infrastructure.

What it means for terminal holders: claim + swap in one tx

Today, if your terminal earns $GME but you'd rather hold $NVDA, that's multiple steps. Claim, approve, swap. Multiple signatures, gas paid more than once.

With EIP-8130 on Base:
→ Claim your stock rewards
→ Swap into the stock you actually want
→ One signature. One transaction.

It's also atomic. Either everything goes through or nothing does. No stuck state where the claim succeeded but the swap failed.

Why this changes how you should vote

Your reward is never locked into a ticker you didn't pick. So vote for the stock you believe should kick things off, knowing every holder can route into their own favorite in a single tx.

How to vote

Reply with one ticker. One vote per account. The most voted stock gets distributed in week one.

Voting closes in 48 hours. 📈

title: Banning projects identified in the high-severity Watchdog Program cases - APX Finance
body:
# Abstract

The following case from the [Watchdog Program](https://alt.gov.arbitrum.foundation/proposal/28485587559812799913134094629469849411398475232393607771326861344548198896843?govId=eip155:42161:0x789fc99093b09ad01c34dc7251d0c89ce743e5a4) has been deemed to constitute high-severity misuse. Accordingly, the Watchdog Committee is proposing to ban this project from the ArbitrumDAO:

-   [APX Finance](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/apx-finance-ltipp-application-final/21744) (formerly ApolloX)
    

# Rationale

To strengthen oversight of grant allocations by the DAO and reduce misuse, the ArbitrumDAO approved the [Watchdog Program](https://alt.gov.arbitrum.foundation/proposal/28485587559812799913134094629469849411398475232393607771326861344548198896843?govId=eip155:42161:0x789fc99093b09ad01c34dc7251d0c89ce743e5a4) to reward verifiable reports of misused funds. As of September 2, 2026; 90 reports have been submitted to the program, ~532K ARB has been recovered, and ~268K ARB has been distributed for reporter bounties.

### What constitutes a high-severity misuse?

As per the original Watchdog Proposal, high-severity misuse involves large-scale, deliberate misuse of DAO-allocated funds, including but not limited to fabrication of deliverables and theft.

As mentioned in the [Watchdog Retrospective Report](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/watchdog-retrospective/30732), the Watchdog Committee (comprising Entropy Advisors, MinistroDolar, the Arbitrum Foundation, and the OpCo) has deemed the following case to constitute high-severity misuse:

### APX Finance (formerly ApolloX)

**Rationale: Unreturned Funds + Late Distribution + Suspected Self-Sybil during** [**LTIPP**](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/apx-finance-ltipp-application-final/21744)

On-chain analysis uncovered multiple overlapping forms of misuse totaling 239,714 ARB. A substantial portion of LTIPP funds remained unutilized in the team's treasury addresses compared to distributor contracts as well as late distributions to said distributor contracts. Lastly, there was on-chain evidence linking a sybil cluster to team addresses.

The committee was unable to reach any team members for clarification or recovery.

# Steps to Implement

Before raising this proposal to an off-chain vote, this project had 1 week to present their case to the ArbitrumDAO as a reply on [this thread](https://forum.arbitrum.foundation/t/banning-projects-identified-in-the-high-severity-watchdog-program-cases/31407).

Unfortunately, the ArbitrumDAO did not receive a response from this project and the respective funds were not returned. Accordingly, the Watchdog Committee is seeking a vote from the ArbitrumDAO on the following:

-   Should APX Finance (formerly ApolloX) (including all founders, current team members, and affiliated contributors), be permanently banned from all future ArbitrumDAO programs?
    

The ArbitrumDAO will have the following voting options to choose from:

-   FOR - Ban APX Finance from the ArbitrumDAO
    
-   AGAINST - Do not ban APX Finance from the ArbitrumDAO
    
-   ABSTAIN
    

This proposal will not require an on-chain vote because there are no on-chain actions to be taken. Accordingly, this Snapshot vote aims to get social consensus from the DAO, and will serve as the final decision.

# Timeline

The following dates are tentative and subject to change.

1.  September 3rd: Publish proposal to the forum.
    
2.  September 10th: Deadline for projects to respond.
    
3.  September 10th: Publish off-chain vote to Snapshot.
    

If the DAO votes to ban this project, then the respective project will be ineligible to apply for any ArbitrumDAO programs going forward.
choices: AGAINST - Do not ban APX Finance

title: [HIP-53] Pausing Emissions
body:
# Summary

This proposal would wind down ongoing Hermes emissions and incentive activity while preserving users' ability to withdraw liquidity and claim any outstanding rewards.

Our intention is to continue the broader work started through Maia and Hermes through a new protocol, brand, and structure. We believe this gives us a better opportunity to secure the partnerships and capital required to build a sustainable protocol.

We're actively working to secure the funding required to launch it. If we do, our intention is for a portion of the new protocol's supply to be allocated to existing Maia and Hermes ecosystem participants. The exact allocation and structure cannot be determined until the project and fundraising structure are finalized.

Regardless of whether that succeeds, we believe Hermes should now decide whether continuing emissions serves a meaningful purpose.

## Why Wind Down Emissions

Hermes emissions were designed to support an actively growing protocol and incentive ecosystem.

If Hermes is no longer being actively developed under its current model, continuing emissions would increase token supply and maintain incentive activity without a clear long-term reason for doing so.

The proposed alternative is to deliberately bring emissions to an end while leaving existing users free to exit their positions whenever they choose.

Hermes has no outstanding vesting or locked user positions. Users can currently withdraw their LP positions and claim earned rewards at any time, so the wind-down does not require users to wait for future unlocks or vesting periods.

Hermes also has no treasury to distribute or preserve, meaning there is no separate treasury decision for Hermes holders as part of this proposal.

## What the Wind-Down Would Involve

If approved, the wind-down would:

-   End ongoing HERMES emissions.
    
-   End new protocol-funded incentive activity.
    
-   Stop encouraging the creation of new positions based on continued Hermes emissions.
    
-   Preserve users' ability to withdraw existing LP positions at any time.
    
-   Preserve users' ability to claim accrued rewards.
    
-   Keep all relevant withdrawal and claim actions accessible through the Hermes interface.
    
-   Preserve direct access to the underlying contracts independently of the frontend.
    

Any executable proposal would specify the exact onchain actions required to stop emissions safely.

## UI and Withdrawals

Ending emissions does **not** mean shutting down access to Hermes.

All existing withdrawal and claim functionality should remain accessible. Users should continue to be able to connect their wallets, view their existing positions, withdraw LPs, and claim rewards through the Hermes interface.

The UI should make Hermes' wind-down status clear and prioritize the actions that existing users still need, particularly **Withdraw** and **Claim**.

Where appropriate, functionality intended to attract or create new emissions-dependent positions should no longer be promoted once emissions have ended.

Users should also remain able to interact directly with the underlying contracts. Canonical contract addresses and the relevant withdrawal and claim methods should remain documented so that access to funds does not depend solely on the continued availability of a hosted frontend.

## Relationship to a New Protocol

Winding down Hermes emissions is not intended to mean abandoning the community built around Hermes.

If we successfully secure funding and launch the new protocol currently being developed, our intention is for a portion of its supply to be allocated to existing participants across the Maia and Hermes ecosystem.

We cannot guarantee that fundraising will succeed or that the new protocol will launch, and no particular allocation should be considered guaranteed today. The final structure would depend on the project, fundraising terms, and any applicable legal requirements.

If successful, we would view it as a continuation of the broader work started through Maia and Hermes rather than as an unrelated project that leaves the existing community behind.

## Decision

The question for Hermes governance is therefore straightforward:

**Should Hermes Protocol wind down ongoing emissions while preserving full withdrawal and reward-claim functionality for existing users?**

## Conclusion

We believe continuing Hermes emissions without active development or a clear long-term purpose would create additional supply without materially improving the protocol's position.

Winding them down would bring that process to a deliberate end without requiring users to take any immediate action or sacrificing access to existing positions. Users would remain free to withdraw their liquidity and claim rewards whenever they choose.

If the new protocol is successfully funded and launched, our intention is for the Maia and Hermes community to participate in what comes next. If it is not, winding down emissions still prevents Hermes from continuing to dilute its supply indefinitely without a clear purpose.

The decision now is simply whether Hermes should make that transition.

title: SCP-224: Engineering Workstream Renewal: October 1, 2026 – March 31, 2027
body:
## Abstract

This proposal seeks continued funding for the Engineering Workstream for six months, from October 1, 2026 through March 31, 2027.

It renews the team established under [SCP-212](https://forum.shapeshift.com/t/scp-212-engineering-workstream-renewal-april-1-2026-september-30-2026/3383) and expanded through [SCP-217](https://forum.shapeshift.com/t/scp-217-amendment-engineering-workstream-contributor-addition-june-1-september-30-2026/3457): kaladinlight as a full-time Senior Engineer, Apotheosis as fractional Workstream Leader & Senior Engineer, and discostu as a Business Development & Marketing contributor.

The main change is an increase in Apotheosis’s allocation from one to two days per week, at his current hourly rate. This provides dedicated time to stay across the codebase and contribute development work alongside the workstream’s administrative and leadership responsibilities. kaladinlight remains full-time.

The total requested budget is **$280,300 in USD value** for the six-month period, including infrastructure and a one-time discretionary allocation.

## Motivation

This renewal supports new partner acquisition and the engineering work needed to guide partners through technical evaluation, onboarding, and integration, alongside maintaining ShapeShift’s products and continuing development.

## Specification

### Team

**Apotheosis — Workstream Leader & Senior Engineer, two days per week**

Continues to lead the workstream, coordinate engineering priorities, support partner discussions, and manage the administrative responsibilities required to keep services running. The additional day provides regular capacity for code review, codebase familiarity, bug fixes, and product development. Specific development work will be scoped alongside kaladinlight according to current priorities.

**kaladinlight — Senior Engineer, full-time, five days per week**

Continues to lead day-to-day implementation, infrastructure maintenance, production incident resolution, and prioritized development. Works with Apotheosis to distribute suitable engineering tasks and share technical context.

**discostu — BD & Marketing

Leads API/Widget business development and new partner acquisition, with responsibility for partner onboarding and support, chain relationships, and basic marketing. This includes partner-facing communications, content, and coordinated marketing activities to support outreach and integrations. He also provides product input and targeted technical contributions in coordination with Engineering. Weekly written reporting continues, and Engineering retains authority over implementation priorities.

### Priorities

New partner acquisition and support for that process are explicit engineering priorities. Engineering will work closely with discostu on prospective partner calls, technical questions, integration guidance, and resolving issues that prevent partners from adopting the API/Widget. Partner feedback and integration needs will inform development priorities, with continued support as partners move into production.

Production stability, essential maintenance, and issues affecting existing users and integrations remain core responsibilities. The team will balance these needs with the work required to acquire and onboard new partners.

The team will also maintain practical service and access documentation to make operational handovers easier.

### Mandate

The Engineering Workstream’s existing mandate continues: responsibility for maintaining the ShapeShift GitHub namespace, including CODEOWNERS and administrative permissions, and reviewing external contributions to preserve code quality and stability.

## Budget

The following figures follow the [proposed October 2026–March 2027 budget](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1NHHTY2mp7YgwtaVlPIKzI3vgNqIZNoiFlAnWRvOIQFQ/edit?gid=979913471#gid=979913471). Amounts are expressed in USD value; payment assets are identified separately.

### Recurring costs

| Item                         | Allocation      |     Monthly |   Six months | Payment asset |
| ---------------------------- | --------------- | ----------: | -----------: | ------------- |
| Apotheosis                   | 2 days/week     |      $7,167 |      $43,000 | USDC          |
| kaladinlight                 | Full-time       |     $17,500 |     $105,000 | USDC          |
| discostu                     |                 |      $5,800 |      $34,800 | FOX           |
| **Contributor compensation** |                 | **$30,467** | **$182,800** |               |
| Infrastructure               | Monthly ceiling |     $15,000 |      $90,000 | USDC          |
| **Total recurring**          |                 | **$45,467** | **$272,800** |               |

Infrastructure funding covers the services required to operate ShapeShift’s products. The $15,000 monthly allocation is a spending ceiling, with unused funds returned to the DAO.

### Non-recurring costs

A **$7,500 USDC discretionary allocation** is requested for the entire six-month period. The **$2,500 increase** over the previous allocation accommodates additional marketing needs under discostu’s remit. These funds are separate from contributor compensation. Unspent funds will be returned to the DAO. No separate contingency allocation is requested.

### Total request

discostu’s compensation will be paid 100% in FOX. The funding request is split as follows:

| Payment asset | Monthly recurring | Six-month request, including discretionary |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| USDC | $39,667 | $245,500 |
| FOX, expressed in USD value | $5,800 | $34,800 |
| **Total USD value** | **$45,467** | **$280,300** |

The FOX amount above is a dollar-denominated compensation budget, not a fixed number of tokens.

### Changes from the amended budget

This comparison uses the monthly allocations in effect under SCP-212 as amended by SCP-217.

| Item | Previous monthly | Proposed monthly | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Apotheosis | $3,583 | $7,167 | +$3,584 |
| kaladinlight | $17,500 | $17,500 | $0 |
| discostu | $5,800 | $5,800 | $0 |
| Infrastructure | $15,000 | $15,000 | $0 |
| **Total recurring, USD value** | **$41,883** | **$45,467** | **+$3,584** |

Apotheosis’s allocation increases from one to two days per week at his current hourly rate. kaladinlight’s compensation remains unchanged.

The previous compensation figures come from the [SCP-212 budget](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1NHHTY2mp7YgwtaVlPIKzI3vgNqIZNoiFlAnWRvOIQFQ/edit?usp=sharing) and the [SCP-217 compensation amendment](https://forum.shapeshift.com/t/scp-217-amendment-engineering-workstream-contributor-addition-june-1-september-30-2026/3457). Comparisons use the published rounded monthly amounts.

### Variance

Unused funds from any budget category will be returned to the DAO at the end of the budget cycle. If additional funding is required, the workstream will raise a separate governance proposal.

## Benefits

- Adds regular engineering capacity and keeps workstream leadership closer to the codebase.
- Broadens the team's ability to review and implement changes, reducing reliance on one engineer.
- Makes new partner acquisition and technical support throughout evaluation, onboarding, and integration explicit engineering priorities.
- Retains engineering, business development, and basic marketing within one workstream.
- Continues discostu’s compensation entirely in FOX.

## Drawbacks

- The proposal increases total recurring spend and increases discretionary funding by $2,500 to accommodate marketing needs, drawing more on the DAO’s treasury.
- The team remains small. Production incidents and maintenance needs may delay planned development.
- Apotheosis remains fractional, so the additional day provides limited capacity and does not remove key-person risk.
- Product and partner work may support revenue growth, but this budget does not guarantee commercial outcomes.

## Vote

**FOR:** Renew the Engineering Workstream for October 1, 2026 through March 31, 2027, with the scope and budget described above.

**FOR WITH CHANGES:** Support renewal with specified modifications raised during discussion.

**AGAINST:** Do not approve this renewal.

title: Knight Miners Funding Proposal - Sdotdfs
body:
# Proposal: Seed the Knight Miners $DGEN Utility Flywheel

**Requested allocation:** **300,000 $DGEN**  
**Submitted by:** The Knight Miners Team  
**Target activation:** Official launch, currently expected around NFL Week 3 or Week 4  
**Product:** [Knight Miners Fantasy](https://de-fs.com/)  
**Contact:** winterfell@de-fs.com
**term:** NFL Weeks 3 & 4

## Summary

Knight Miners requests **300,000 $DGEN** to launch a mining-centered utility and rewards pilot:

| Use | Allocation |
|---|---:|
| Main Arena rewards | 210,000 $DGEN |
| Free Second String Siege rewards | 60,000 $DGEN |
| Mining-based $DGEN discoveries | 30,000 $DGEN |
| **Total** | **300,000 $DGEN** |

This is not intended to be a one-time giveaway. The goal is to make $DGEN useful throughout the Knight Miners experience:

> **Mine for free → discover or earn $DGEN → equip or enter → compete → recycle spent $DGEN into future rewards**

## Why Knight Miners

Knight Miners is a live-beta fantasy-football game where players mine Forge Gems, forge fantasy positions, and submit weekly Arena lineups. Unrostered positions stay in the player's Vault; rostered positions are burned.

Mining has become the product's strongest repeat-engagement mechanic. Players continue returning for daily seams and surprise veins even though beta rewards currently have no live-token value and the first official contest has not begun. Mining creates anticipation, community moments, progression, and the resources needed to build a lineup.

This proposal turns that existing behavior into recurring $DGEN utility rather than placing $DGEN only at the end of a leaderboard. It aligns with DGENDAO's stated goal of using $DGEN across games, leagues, tournaments, and ecosystem products.

## Proposed $DGEN Utility

### Mining

Basic and manual mining remain free. A capped portion of the allocation will appear as real $DGEN discoveries during eligible free mining strikes, with published reward inventory, per-user limits, and auditable randomness.

Forge Gems and $DGEN will remain clearly separate: Forge Gems are non-transferable game resources; $DGEN is the ecosystem token.

### Second String Siege

The RB2/WR2-focused **Second String Siege remains free to enter and awards $DGEN**. This feeder tournament gives every player an earn-first route into the Main Arena:

> **Free mining → free contest → earn $DGEN → enter the Main Arena**

No token purchase, NFT, or paid pickaxe will be required to compete in the Siege.

### Main Arena

The proposed starting entry is **500 $DGEN per weekly Main Arena lineup**. Each player receives one prize-eligible entry; there are no rebuys, extra paid entries, or paid scoring boosts.

Prizes will be sponsor-funded, fixed, and published before entry. They will not depend on the number of entrants or the amount collected. Existing beta miners will receive one non-transferable Founder's Entry Writ for their first eligible official Main Arena.

### Ready Pickaxe

The first Ready Pickaxe auto-arm each day remains free. Additional successful auto-arms may cost **100 $DGEN**, capped at five paid auto-arms per account per day.

Paying never improves rarity, strike value, Armor, shards, $DGEN-discovery odds, or fantasy score. It buys bounded convenience only, and a user is charged only when the auto-arm successfully claims an eligible strike.

## Direct $DGEN Access

Knight Miners will build an integrated portal where players can acquire $DGEN through Aerodrome without leaving the site, connect a supported wallet, and securely fund/increase their Knight Miners balance. This creates a simple bridge between on-chain $DGEN and its in-game utility while keeping transactions transparent and verifiable.

## How Spent $DGEN Returns to the Ecosystem

Main Arena entries and paid auto-arm fees will enter a dedicated, auditable program wallet. The proposed settlement during NFL Weeks 3 & 4 is:

- **70%** returned to future Knight Miners reward pools.
- **30%** sent to a DGENDAO-approved treasury lock or other transparent retirement mechanism.

For illustration, **50 Main Arena entries create 25,000 $DGEN of weekly product use**. Under this split, 17,500 returns to future rewards and 7,500 goes to the DAO-approved retirement route. This is arithmetic, not a participation or price forecast.

## Why the Allocation Is Measurable

- **100%** of the requested allocation funds player utility and rewards.
- Within the 300,000 $DGEN pool, **70%** begins in the Main Arena, **20%** in the free Siege, and **10%** in mining.
- $DGEN receives three immediate product roles: **reward, contest access, and convenience**.
- **0%** of the requested allocation herein goes to team compensation, development, operations, or general marketing.


## Safeguards

Knight Miners will:

- Preserve a meaningful free route through mining and Second String Siege.
- Never sell rarity, fantasy points, Armor, better randomness, or extra entries.
- Endeavor to publish and update contest rules, odds, limits, scoring, tie-breakers, and correction windows before play.
- Exclude team admins from prizes or participation beyond testing and administration until a fair route exists in future iterations of the platform.
- Pause affected mechanics for security, scoring, custody, or integrity incidents.
- Return unused funds to DGENDAO unless an extension or reallocation is approved.

Contests will remain sponsor-funded and no-purchase until viable and legal route exists in future iterations of the platform.

## Funding and Reporting

Funds will be maintained in a DAO-approved multisig. Knight Miners will publish allocations, distributions, transaction records, recycled amounts, remaining balances, and material incidents in a discord channel to be established and controlled by the DAO. Ordinary transaction fees shall be covered outside the requested allocation.

## Requested Vote

Approve **300,000 $DGEN** for the Knight Miners launch utility pilot:

- **300,000 $DGEN** for Main Arena rewards, free Second String Siege rewards, and capped mining discoveries.
- Authorization to test the bounded $DGEN entry and convenience utilities described above.

title: Survivor Fantasy Challenge Funding Proposal - Optreal
body:
SUMMARY
A new NFL fantasy game, that I don't think anyone else is doing right now. Survivor Fantasy Challenge

DESCRIPTION
A weekly NFL "full-team survivor" pool. Each week, every player builds a 7-slot lineup (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 TE) from currently-active NFL players. The combined team score (full-PPR, Draftkings scoring) must clear a weekly point threshold (100, adjustable) or that player is eliminated for the season. Every individual NFL player can only be used once, ever, by a given entrant.

It's a new fantasy game that has been brewing for a few years now. It started long ago around the time the DAO was first set up. The idea came from an X post by JBB, and JoeCandy and I noticed it. We wanted to spin it up back then, but just didnt have the time, or didnt happen for whatever reason. I did create a flyer for the idea, but it wasn't promoted. Basically everything is still the same regarding the details, other than the entry and prize amounts.

MOTIVATION
Currently, the idea is basically like any other app/game, poker, etc. The potential to rake some entry fees and continue to boost the DAO's treasury or future initiatives.
As it stands right now the entry fee split is as follows (adjustable): 5% organizer, 15% weekly top score(s), 80% grand prize to winner(s).

TECHNICAL DETAILS
How it will work, in general, for now (potential change given testing and feedback): Single HTML file, Supabase JS loaded via CDN (UMD build). Vanilla JS state + re-render pattern (render() dispatches to per-tab render functions), no framework. All writes go through Postgres functions (security definer), never direct table writes from the client - this is what makes rules like "picks are permanent," "commissioner-only actions," and "one player per season" actually enforced server-side, not just UI conventions. Direct insert/update policies deliberately don't exist on picks or profiles.

The cost is currently 0. I'm putting in sweat equity to get things going, and then if vote approves, a potential small compensation. I would like to stay on and help continue to develop and refine the game. I'd also like to help with the marketing/promo/social and low cost grass roots efforts to help get the word out and generate interest. To that extent I would like to be compensated 1% (out of the 5%) of the organizer fees. I would use that 1% for dev time, marketing/promo, etc.

Future costs like domain, hosting, updates etc. should be easily covered by the organizer fees collected. Larger dev/marketing costs can be decided by DAO vote.

BUDGET ANALYSIS
How it might affect the treasury will be this initial beta testing (prize pool) and then any future pools if the DAO decides they want to throw in some extra, or % match, etc. into the prize pool. Otherwise, it should be mostly a net positive with the 4-5% organizer fees. 

Survivor Fantasy Beta Season 0 is requesting the following:
200,000 $DGEN for the prize pool. Enough to entice players to jump in, play consistent week after week, and provide feedback about experience, bugs etc.
80% to the winner(s) and 20% to weekly top scores (first 10 weeks only.)

Note: Ive added a second-chance rebuy option/feature that can be used only during the first 5 weeks. (Players picked already do no reset.) Any rebuys added to the prize pool. To test out the mechanic, and maybe make it a permanent fixture, I was thinking about folding in the nft collection. For example, any holders with 10+ Knights gets a free second chance (if needed.)


USEFUL LINKS
Game app currently resides at [surfan.win] with dns to Cloudflare [survivor-fantasy.pages.dev] for hosting/testing. The domain also serves as the email smtp used between Supabase and Resend. If the game generates decent interest, then the DAO can decide what and how it wants to roll the game into its IP collection and where the app should reside.
