title: CoverQuest 2026 Season Rewards
body:
** Summary**

Authorize funding for the 2026 CoverQuest season across two reward systems:

1. **A fixed 1,000,000 DGEN prize pool** across 18 weekly contests and a season championship.

2. **The Knights Pass progression ladder** — an open-ended pool funded first from Pass sales, with treasury covering the shortfall. This cannot carry a hard cap, because every Pass sold adds a player who can climb the ladder.

The Pass ladder is designed so that a player who plays the full season more than recovers the Pass price. The DAO's objective is not Pass revenue — it is driving demand for tradeable Gamechangers, incentivizing Knight holders to come mint their gamechangers. This structure is built as an participatory DGEN airdrop where owning Knights increases your chances to accumulate DGEN through the marketplace or the prize pool. 

---

## Background

CoverQuest is DGEN DAO's weekly NFL spread contest. Players pick six sides per week and score the margin between their pick and the actual result.

The 2026 build adds mintable Gamechangers — Charges and Decrees minted from Knights of Degen traits, tradeable on a DGEN-denominated marketplace — and the Knights Pass, a 12-tier dual-track progression system purchased for the season.

---

## Part 1 — Prize pool (1,000,000 DGEN, capped)

 Fixed total, paid in full regardless of participation, and cannot be exceeded. The tables below are the entire commitment.

### Knights Pass track — 950,000 DGEN

**Weekly** (45,000 × 18 = 810,000)

| Place | DGEN |
|---|---|
| 1st | 32,000 |
| 2nd | 13,000 |

**Season championship** — 140,000

| Place | DGEN |
|---|---|
| 1st | 80,000 |
| 2nd | 38,000 |
| 3rd | 22,000 |

### Free-to-play track — 50,000 DGEN

**Weekly** (1,500 × 18 = 27,000)

| Place | DGEN |
|---|---|
| 1st | 1,000 |
| 2nd | 500 |

**Season championship** — 23,000

| Place | DGEN |
|---|---|
| 1st | 11,000 |
| 2nd | 7,000 |
| 3rd | 5,000 |

### Track eligibility

Purchasing a Knights Pass does not remove a player from the free progression ladder — Pass holders climb both tracks and collect both sets of tier rewards. It does remove them from the free-to-play **prize pool**. Pass holders compete on the Knights Pass leaderboard only. The two prize fields are separate.

---

## Part 2 — Knights Pass ladder (open-ended, revenue-offset)

**Knights Pass price: 20,000 DGEN for the season.**

Every player climbs the same ladder and collects the free track. Pass holders collect the Knights Pass track alongside it. XP only moves forward — a bad week costs nothing, so nobody drops out of the race in October.

| T | XP | Free track | Knights Pass track |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 500 | +1 Let It Ride | 2,000 DGEN |
| 2 | 1,000 | +1 Castle Wall | 2,000 DGEN |
| 3 | 1,700 | 1,000 DGEN | 1 Double Edge |
| 4 | 2,700 | — | 4,000 DGEN |
| 5 | 4,000 | 1,000 DGEN | 10,000 DGEN |
| 6 | 5,000 | — | 1 Double Edge |
| 7 | 6,000 | 1,000 DGEN | 5,000 DGEN |
| 8 | 7,000 | +1 Let It Ride | 1 Warlord |
| 9 | 7,800 | 1,000 DGEN | 5,000 DGEN |
| 10 | 8,600 | — | 1 Double Edge |
| 11 | 9,300 | 1,500 DGEN | 5,000 DGEN |
| 12 | 10,000 | 2,500 DGEN | 10,000 DGEN |

**Knights Pass track total: 43,000 DGEN** plus 3 Double Edge and 1 Warlord.
**Free track total: 8,000 DGEN** plus 2 Let It Ride and 1 Castle Wall uses.
**Combined ceiling for a Pass holder: 51,000 DGEN** in tier rewards.

Break-even for a Pass holder comes at **tier 5**, where the Knights Pass track has paid 18,000 DGEN and the free track another 2,000. Everything past tier 5 is net positive to the player.

### XP sources

| Action | XP |
|---|---|
| Submit a full slate | 100 |
| Each correct pick | 100 |
| Finish the week positive | 100 |
| Arm at least one Gamechanger | 100 |

A perfect week — six correct picks, full slate, positive, at least one Gamechanger armed — is **900 XP**. The ladder caps at 10,000, so a player at a perfect pace tops out around week 11. A realistic 550-650 XP per week reaches tier 12 near the end of an 18-week season, which is the intended pacing.

Arming is a single flat award for the week rather than one per Gamechanger. This is deliberate. Gamechanger uses scale with Knight count, so paying per arm would hand a large holder roughly 1,800 XP over the season — most of the way to tier 4 — before they pick a single game correctly. A flat award keeps the nudge to use Gamechangers without making the ladder a function of how many Knights someone holds.

The participation floor is 3,600 XP: 1,800 for submitting all 18 slates and 1,800 for arming something each week. That reaches tier 4 for a player who never picks correctly, and the remaining eight tiers are earned on results.

Marketplace demand does not rest on this XP award. A Gamechanger's value is that it wins money — Overkill doubles a pick, The Crown doubles the week's best, and the weekly Knights Pass prize is 32,000 DGEN. The XP nudge is on top of that, not the reason for it.

---

## Treasury exposure

The prize pool is capped at 1,000,000 DGEN and is the DAO's fixed commitment.

The ladder is not capped, and exposure scales with Pass sales:

| Passes sold | Revenue | Max ladder liability (KP track) | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 200,000 | 430,000 | (230,000) |
| 25 | 500,000 | 1,075,000 | (575,000) |
| 50 | 1,000,000 | 2,150,000 | (1,150,000) |

Max liability assumes every Pass holder reaches tier 12, which no realistic distribution produces. It is stated as the ceiling, not the expectation.

The free track adds 8,000 DGEN per player who reaches tier 12, across all participants including non-Pass holders.

**Requested authorization:** 1,000,000 DGEN for the prize pool, plus ladder funding from Pass revenue with treasury covering any shortfall, reported to the DAO at season end.

---

## Rationale for expedited handling

Week 1 opened September 9. Gamechanger minting is live and the Forge is open. The Pass ladder is an 18-week runway, and every week that passes shortens the runway a Pass buyer has to climb it — which makes the Pass progressively less attractive the later it launches. Authorizing now lets the Prize Pool be fully clear while the full ladder is still ahead of players.

title: Bonding Curve Protocol Upgrade Proposal (DDD-9360v3)
body:
DDD-9360v3 is an acceleration upgrade to the Bonding Curve Protocol v2.0 (DDD-9360v2). The upgraded system is designed to accelerate the distribution of DNA through a controlled swap price range of $0.30 to $0.50, with $0.01 price intervals, while preserving the listing price established by the final price of Bonding Curve v2.0.

The V3.0 mechanism does not redefine, reset, or replace the listing price established under Bonding Curve v2.0. Instead, it introduces an accelerated distribution phase intended to facilitate the decentralized distribution of the remaining public DNA allocation.

Price and Listing Mechanism
For clarity:

If Bonding Curve v2.0 (DDD-9360v2) reaches a final price of $3.30 before the upgrade, the listing price will remain $3.30, regardless of the subsequent swap price range under Bonding Curve v3.0.
Under Bonding Curve v3.0, DNA swaps are accelerated through a price range of $0.30 to $0.50, with $0.01 intervals.
The $0.30–$0.50 range is an acceleration-phase swap mechanism and is not the market listing price.
The final price established under Bonding Curve v2.0 is treated as the locked listing-price reference for the subsequent market listing.
Bonding Curve v3.0 is designated as the “Acceleration Phase”, intended to accelerate the distribution of DNA and support the transition toward decentralized market participation.
Reason for the Proposal
The proposal is introduced based on the following considerations:

Bonding Curve v1.0 (DDD-9360) and Bonding Curve v2.0 (DDD-9360v2) have been operating for approximately six months in aggregate, yet only around 10% of the total public DNA allocation has been distributed.
Approximately 90% of the public allocation remains undistributed, resulting in a significant portion of the public allocation remaining within the bonding curve mechanism.
The maximum targeted listing date is December 12, 2027. Based on the current distribution rate and the remaining allocation, the existing mechanism is not mathematically expected to distribute the full public allocation by the target date.
An acceleration mechanism is therefore proposed to improve distribution efficiency and allow the protocol to progress toward its intended market-listing phase within the available timeframe.
Developer Proposal
The Developer proposes to upgrade the Bonding Curve Protocol to its third version, DDD-9360v3.

The upgrade modifies the bonding curve contract deployed at:
0x8401A29293C5394A880856031b25C8Ee8810A2D0

The proposed upgrade is subject to DAO approval, requiring a minimum of 50.01% YES votes within seven (7) days of the proposal, in accordance with the applicable governance requirements.

Scope of the Upgrade
The Bonding Curve v3.0 upgrade includes the following changes:

1. No Reset of Bonding Curve History
The upgrade does not reset the existing Bonding Curve v2.0 distribution history, accumulated state, or established final price.
2. Listing Price Preservation
The listing price remains based on the final price established by Bonding Curve v2.0 prior to the V3.0 upgrade.
3. Acceleration Swap Mechanism
DNA swaps under V3.0 are redirected to an accelerated price range of $0.30–$0.50, with $0.01 intervals, to encourage faster distribution of the remaining public allocation.
4. Re-Architected Mathematical Model
V3.0 introduces a revised mathematical model governing price progression and swap behavior during the acceleration phase.
5. Distribution-Focused Design
The V3.0 mechanism is designed primarily to accelerate token distribution rather than to establish a new market valuation for DNA.

Objectives
The primary objectives of Bonding Curve v3.0 are:

Accelerate DNA distribution and advance the protocol toward its market-listing phase.
Provide a significantly faster distribution mechanism than the existing Bonding Curve v2.0 model.
Preserve the V2.0 final price as the locked listing-price reference.
Increase the amount of liquidity that can be prepared for future market expansion.
Support the transition from bonding-curve distribution toward broader decentralized and centralized market participation.
Improve accessibility for later participants while maintaining the established V2.0 listing-price reference.
Establish a more decentralized distribution of the public DNA allocation before and during the market-listing phase.
Expected Benefits
The proposed upgrade is expected to provide the following benefits:

1. Faster Distribution
A lower accelerated swap range may increase participation and improve the rate at which the remaining public DNA allocation is distributed.
2. Earlier Progress Toward Market Listing
Faster distribution may allow the protocol to reach its intended listing phase more efficiently.
3. Future CEX Readiness
The liquidity structure is designed to provide a dedicated allocation for potential future Centralized Exchange (CEX) listings.
4. Greater Accessibility for Late Participants
The acceleration phase may provide additional access to DNA for participants who did not participate during the earlier bonding curve phases.
5. Broader Decentralized Distribution
Increasing the number of distributed tokens may reduce concentration of the remaining public allocation within the bonding curve mechanism and strengthen decentralized participation.
6. Improved Governance Participation
A broader token distribution may potentially result in wider participation in governance during the market-listing and post-listing phases.

Risks and Trade-offs
The V3.0 upgrade introduces several risks and trade-offs that should be considered by DAO participants:

1. Increased Market Volatility
A significant difference between the accelerated swap range and the locked listing-price reference may create substantial price volatility once DNA begins trading in open markets.
2. Large Entry-Price Disparity
Participants who acquired DNA during earlier bonding curve phases may have a substantially higher average acquisition price than participants entering during the V3.0 acceleration phase.
3. Potential Selling Pressure
Once DNA becomes freely tradable, participants who acquired tokens during the acceleration phase may realize significant gains relative to their acquisition price, potentially increasing selling pressure.
4. Market Fragility During Initial Listing
The difference between available liquidity, market depth, and potential trading demand may result in increased price impact and volatility during the initial market-listing period.
5. CEX Listing Uncertainty
The allocation intended for future CEX liquidity does not guarantee that a CEX listing will occur. Any CEX listing remains subject to exchange requirements, market conditions, liquidity requirements, compliance procedures, and other external factors.
6. Liquidity Deployment Timing
A portion of the liquidity generated through the bonding curve may remain reserved until an appropriate CEX listing opportunity becomes available.

Liquidity Management in Bonding Curve v3.0
Upon completion of the Bonding Curve v3.0 distribution phase and achievement of the applicable listing conditions, the generated liquidity will be allocated as follows:

1. Initial DEX Liquidity — 40%
40% of the available bonding-curve liquidity will be allocated toward the initial listing on one or two selected Decentralized Exchanges (DEXs). This allocation is intended to provide the initial market depth required for DNA spot trading and to establish the first open-market liquidity venue.

2. Future CEX Liquidity Reserve — 60%
The remaining 60% of the available bonding-curve liquidity will be reserved for potential future Centralized Exchange (CEX) listings. This allocation is intended to support future CEX expansion, including potential Spot and Futures markets, subject to applicable exchange requirements and market conditions. The 60% allocation does not constitute a guarantee of a CEX listing or a guaranteed listing date. The liquidity may remain reserved until a suitable CEX listing opportunity is secured.

Governance and Approval
The implementation of Bonding Curve v3.0 is subject to approval through the applicable DAO governance process. The Developer will not unilaterally activate the proposed upgrade if the required governance approval is not obtained.

Conclusion
DDD-9360v3 introduces an acceleration-focused modification to the Bonding Curve Protocol designed to improve the distribution efficiency of the remaining public DNA allocation and facilitate progression toward the market-listing phase.

The upgrade does not reset the Bonding Curve v2.0 mechanism and does not replace its established final price as the listing-price reference. Instead, V3.0 introduces a separate acceleration phase in which DNA may be swapped within the $0.30–$0.50 range at $0.01 intervals.

The proposed liquidity structure allocates 40% toward the initial DEX listing and 60% as a reserve for potential future CEX listings. While this structure is intended to provide both immediate DEX liquidity and future CEX readiness, it also acknowledges that CEX listings are external opportunities and therefore cannot be guaranteed.

Overall, DDD-9360v3 is proposed as a mechanism to accelerate decentralized DNA distribution, improve liquidity preparation, and advance the protocol toward open-market participation while explicitly acknowledging the increased volatility, entry-price disparity, liquidity-depth risk, and CEX uncertainty associated with the acceleration strategy.

title: Introduce a Minimum Offer Threshold for Marketplace Sellers
body:
> by 0xbc02db030361121dd43bbb2fcbcb4f9f98c1dc7d (Bestie)

I propose that the Decentraland Marketplace introduce an option for sellers to set a minimum offer price for their listed items.

Currently, sellers can receive offers on their Marketplace items without being able to establish a minimum threshold. This can result in sellers receiving a large number of extremely low-value offers that are unlikely to be accepted

Problem

I have recently noticed increased activity from new users making very low-ball offers on Marketplace items. While offers are an important part of the Marketplace and can create opportunities for buyers and sellers, receiving offers that are significantly below a seller's expected price can create unnecessary noise.

For users who have email notifications enabled, each of these offers generates an email notification. While notifications can presumably be turned off, doing so creates another problem: sellers may miss a legitimate offer or a genuine opportunity to sell an item

The issue is therefore not simply the number of notifications. It is the lack of a mechanism for sellers to establish a reasonable minimum threshold for offers

Proposed Solution

Introduce a Minimum Offer Price setting for Marketplace sellers

When listing an item, or potentially after listing it, the seller would be able to specify the lowest offer they are willing to consider/accept

For example:

A seller lists an item for 1,000 MANA
The seller sets a minimum offer threshold of 750 MANA
Offers below 750 MANA would either be prevented from being submitted or would not trigger an offer notification to the seller

Offers at or above 750 MANA would be treated as valid offers and would notify the seller normally

The exact implementation could be determined by the Foundation (Regensis Labs) and community upon further discussion

title: Lido Alliance BORG Foundation Update: Appointment of Leeward Supervisors Limited as Supervisor
body:
### TL;DR

This vote seeks Lido DAO approval for the appointment of [Leeward Supervisors Limited ("Leeward")](https://leeward.ky) as Supervisor of [Lido Alliance BORG Foundation ("Lido Alliance BORG")](https://research.lido.fi/t/organize-the-lido-alliance-program-as-a-lido-dao-adjacent-borg/8173).

Leeward is a Cayman Islands governance, compliance and fiduciary services firm specialising in Web3 and digital assets, and the current Supervisor of Lido Labs Foundation. Through that role, it is already familiar with the structure and functions of the entities operating adjacent to Lido DAO.

### Background

Lido Alliance BORG is a Cayman Islands foundation company established to support the purposes assigned to it under its governing documents as approved by Lido DAO. It has no members or beneficiaries, and its business and affairs are managed by or under the control of its board of directors. It is funded through [the Ecosystem Grant gRequest (EGG)](https://research.lido.fi/t/2026-ecosystem-grant-grequest-egg-executing-goose-3/10951).

Under the [Lido Alliance BORG Bylaws](https://github.com/MetaLex-Tech/publicDocs/blob/main/BORG-legal-docs/Lido-BORGs/Lido-Alliance-BORG/Lido%20Alliance%20BORG%20Bylaws%20CLEAN%20PUBLIC%208.20.24.pdf), as [amended](https://research.lido.fi/t/lido-alliance-borg-amendment-of-bylaws-to-enable-goose-3-execution/10959), Lido Alliance BORG must have at least one Supervisor at all times, as required for a memberless Cayman Islands foundation company. The Supervisor is responsible for holding the board of directors accountable and overseeing compliance with the foundation company's constitutional documents and applicable law.

The Supervisor is responsible for enforcing Lido Alliance BORG's rules and has the right and power to hold BORG Personnel liable for:

- Any fraud or violation of applicable Legal Requirements committed by or on behalf of Lido Alliance BORG, or on behalf of BORG Personnel in connection with Lido Alliance BORG's activities.
- Any knowing and intentional material breach of a material term of the Governance Agreements by Lido Alliance BORG or BORG Personnel that could reasonably be expected to materially adversely impact Lido Alliance BORG or the Community, or any part of the Community.

The current Supervisor of Lido Alliance BORG is [MetaLeX Pro, LLP](https://www.metalex.tech/), which was appointed on a temporary basis. MetaLeX Pro, LLP has provided [notice of its resignation](https://app.metalex.tech/cybersign/1/0xe25f38025e5f588bd50630b759b3d8d7ec7d551c648e46fd9845b1b00c2d21c1) as Supervisor, to take effect upon the appointment of a new Supervisor. Accordingly, Lido Alliance BORG now proposes appointing a new entity to this role.

### Proposal

Approve the appointment of Leeward Supervisors Limited as Supervisor of Lido Alliance BORG.

If this proposal is approved:

- The board of Lido Alliance BORG will complete the necessary corporate actions to give effect to Leeward's appointment, in accordance with Lido Alliance BORG's governing documents.
- Upon Leeward's appointment becoming effective, MetaLeX Pro, LLP will resign as the current Supervisor.

title: [DIP-51] DAO Delegation Revision #1 | Introducing Auto-Delegation, Community Score, and Delegation Portal
body:
## Abstract

This proposal updates the DAO's delegation framework to enhance decentralization, simplify operations, and combat voting fatigue.

By implementing **Auto-Delegation**, the DAO simplifies and automates operations and expands outreach to external members to grow the quality voter cohort.

As thresholds are met, **locked SSV tokens** will progressively unlock to fund incentives, cover expenses, and reduce emissions.

The proposal also introduces refined, transparent **Community Scoring,** the inclusion of **Ethereum Communities** outside of SSV, and a dedicated **Delegation Portal UX/UI Grant** to streamline the delegation interface.

## Proposal Particulars

* Abstract
* Proposal Particulars
* Auto-Delegation
* Delegation Capital Unlock
* Delegated Policy Authority
* Scoring Updates
* Common Provisions
* Grandfathering and Transition
* Delegation Portal UX/UI Grant
* MC Delegate Removal Procedure
* Appendix 1: Scoring Specification

If this proposal passes, the following will be implemented:

1. Enable **Auto-Delegation** to improve delegation efficiency by allowing delegators to assign voting power via the DAO to multiple delegates automatically.
2. **Unlock SSV tokens** powering the current Delegation program in tranches when externally auto-delegated voting power hits certain thresholds. 
3. Update the **Community Score** to better reflect commitment and transparency and increase the number of delegates.
4. Include members from other **Ethereum Communities** using the **[HighSignal](https://app.highsignal.xyz) Score** across selected communities to increase outreach.
5. Provide a UI/UX grant to build a **Delegation Portal** to support the proposed changes.

## Auto-Delegation

Using “Split Delegation,” as technically implemented in DIP-25, the DAO itself can become the target of delegation to further distribute externally assigned voting power and voting power held by the DAO directly to delegates percentage-wise and automatically (hereby called “**Auto-Delegation**”).

Each cohort allocation is a target percentage of total available auto-delegatable voting power, scaling the program with participation. The following auto-delegation cohort allocations apply:

| Cohort                                                    | % of Auto-Delegation |
| :-------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------- |
| SSV Community *(Auto-Delegated by Community Score)*       | 45%|
| Verified Operators *(Operator Committee)*| 25%|
| Professional *(SSV Foundation)*| 10%|
| Grant Recipients *(Grants Committee)*| 15%|
| Ethereum Community *(Auto-Delegated by HighSignal Score)* | 5%|
| **Total**| **100%**|

Selection of delegates under the SSV and Ethereum Community cohorts will be algorithmically determined by the proposed scoring and the resulting leaderboard, with no manual adjustments other than a removal by the MC under the Common Provisions, while all other cohorts are determined by the delegated policy authority for each responsible committee.

## Delegation Capital Unlock

The DAO's initial allocation of 150’000 SSV under DIP-25 for the community, verified operator, and grantee cohort is partially released back to the DAO’s treasury in equal tranches, unlocked progressively as Auto-Delegation reaches defined thresholds.

Auto-Delegation reaches its threshold when SSV or cSSV holders delegate their voting power to the DAO’s auto-delegation Safe wallet, measured as the absolute amount of auto-delegated cSSV + SSV on the first day of the following month.

On every 1st MSIG batch, the Master of Coin checks the auto-delegated amount and triggers the tranche release if thresholds are met.

A permanent floor of 50’000 SSV tokens is retained in the delegation program at all times as a base that the DAO always delegates directly via its own auto-delegation.

If the absolute number of auto-delegated tokens falls below the threshold that unlocked the most recent tranche by the same measurements, the DAO tops the program back up to the level of the recent tranche.

| Tranche | Auto-Delegation trigger (cSSV + SSV tokens) | Unlocked SSV tokens |
| :------ | :------------------------------------------ | :------------------ |
| 1| 78000| 20000|
| 2| 99000| 20000|
| 3| 114000| 20000|
| 4| 132000| 20000|
| 5| 150000| 20000|

## Delegated Policy Authority

If this proposal were to pass, the following authority is granted:

* **Policy Authority:** 

  1. The Operator Committee (OC) and the Grants Committee (GC) will each be granted the policy-making authority to define their delegate selection and removal for the cohort they manage based on a self-imposed, published framework. 
  2. The SSV Foundation's published framework for professional delegates remains unchanged from DIP-25.

* **Published Framework:** Each committee must establish and publish a framework to select, nominate, rotate, and measure delegates, and report its selections:
  1. Any such policy must be published and voted on by a majority of the respective committee.
  2. The Grantee and the Verified Operator Cohort must have a minimum of 5 non-overlapping delegates each, nominated at any time.
  3. Acting committee members cannot be selected as targets by any committee delegation policy.
  4. The Committee's delegate selection must be submitted at most once a month to the MC no later than the 1st of the following month. If none is submitted, the current selection remains active.
  5. Within each cohort, voting power is allocated *equally* and cannot be overridden by policy, save for a removal by the MC under the Common Provisions.

## Scoring Updates

It is proposed to replace Karma Score with a new **SSV Community Score** (“Score”).

The new Score remains normalized to 0–100, but updates its calculation based on four independent, auditable pillars:

| Pillar | Measures | Source | Weight |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Community Contribution | Contribution quality across Discord + Forum | HighSignal (`app.highsignal.xyz`) | 3 |
| Token Holdings | Skin-in-the-game cSSV + SSV holdings over time | On-chain balances | 3 |
| Snapshot Participation | Recent vote participation | Snapshot | 10 |

For the out-of-band **Ethereum Community Cohort**, the score is taken 1:1 from HighSignal for the selected communities, and doesn’t impact the general community scoring:

| Pillar | Measures | Source | Communities |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Community Contribution | Discord + Forum + other quality participation across the non-SSV Ethereum Communities | HighSignal (app.highsignal.xyz) | Lido, Ethstaker, Rocketpool, Lighthouse, Eigenlayer |

## Common Provisions

The following provisions apply to the Community and the Ethereum Community cohorts:

* SSV tokens in the Immunefiy Bug Bounty Vault delegate their *SSV* voting power to the auto-delegation pool, but do not affect the calculation of the Auto-Delegation trigger policy or the permanent SSV floor, and do not contribute to the unlocking of delegation capital.
* Auto-delegation to the **SSV Community cohort** will occur proportionally across all addresses with an SSV Community Score of 20 or greater.
* Auto-delegation is capped to 500’000 voting power. Excess delegated voting power will be voided and will not increase the cohorts' and individual entities’ voting power.
* Auto-delegation to the **Ethereum Community cohort** will happen proportionally to all published high-signal users with a signal strength of mid or high who have their address shared with the SSV project on HighSignal or have made their address public. 
* Delegation happens independently of the completion of any delegation profile as long as the required minimum score is reached.
* Addresses explicitly indicating they wish to opt out via a signed message are exempt from any delegation.
* Acting members of any DAO committees identified by the governance addresses are no longer exempted from delegation and are scored as any other member.
* A person may receive auto-delegated voting power under one cohort only. Membership of a cohort disqualifies that person, and any address it controls, from receiving auto-delegated voting power under any other cohort. Where a person would otherwise qualify under more than one, the cohort with the higher per-delegate allocation prevails.
* No connected person of a delegate may receive auto-delegated voting power under a cohort other than that delegate's. A person is connected where, in the reasonable determination of the Multi-Sig Committee ("MC"), they are the same person as the delegate or under common control with it, an employee, officer, director, partner or contractor of the delegate or of an entity under common control with it, immediate family of the delegate, or acting in concert with the delegate on delegated voting power. A commercial, grant, operator or service relationship alone is not a connection.
* The MC may undelegate from any delegate, in any cohort, where it determines that either provision above is breached. The delegate remains ineligible for auto-delegation until the MC resolves otherwise. Voting power delegated directly by token holders outside Auto-Delegation is unaffected.
* The possibility for token holders to delegate their SSV or cSSV voting power directly to any delegate without using Auto-Delegation remains intact.
* For optimal operations, the Multi-Sig Committee (MC) is free to aggregate and organize funds across the DAO's various Safes to maximize efficiency and align with the general treasury management practice introduced in DIP-52. 
* The MC shall register matching ENS addresses in line with DIP-55 to make the resulting structure easily identifiable and interactions more secure. 

## Grandfathering and Transition

To provide a smooth transition between the old Karma-based scoring and the new scoring model, the following applies:

* A snapshot of the current leaderboard and cohort allocation is taken from Karma on the last day of the previous month in which this proposal passes. 
* The selected delegates, as per the snapshot taken across all cohorts, shall remain active and unchanged, regardless of their voting participation under the old delegation system, until new policies are published and all systems are fully functional.
* Collected profile information from the Karma snapshot (such as mapping of the address to forum or Discord handles or other information) shall be seeded into the new system as static information and remain there until actively updated by the owner of the entity.

## Delegation Portal UX/UI Grant

The Grants Committee shall spec and find an implementer to implement a Delegation Portal that supports all of the requirements above and enter, through the SSV Foundation, into an agreement under the current grants micro-grant regime.

## MC Delegate Removal Procedure

Any MC member may call a removal vote. Votes are cast as under DIP-2, by signing a message reading "Yes" or "No" from the member's designated wallet, and five (5) of nine (9) are required. The MC may act on its own initiative or on referral, need not investigate, and may decide on the information available to it. Each removal is published in the next monthly report with the cohort and the ground relied on. A removed delegate has no claim to the voting rights previously delegated to it.

## Appendix 1: Scoring Specification

| Dial | Default | What it does |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Community weight | 3 | How much community contribution counts |
| Holdings weight | 3 | How much stake counts |
| Votes weight | 10 | How much voting counts |

| Dial | Default | What it does |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| HOLD_REF | 10,000 | The holding that earns a perfect 100 |
| p | 0.5 | Whale flattening (square root) |
| T | 90 days | How much balance history is averaged |
| H | 90 days | How long a vote takes to lose half its weight |
| N | 10 | How many recent proposals count |

| Symbol | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| w_i | weight of pillar i — 3, 3, 10 |
| c | HighSignal score, already 0–100 |
| b_t | SSV + cSSV held on day b_t is the average over T days (the TWAB) |
| Rp | reference holding 10,000 and concavity 0.5 |
| v_j | 1 if they voted on proposal j, else 0 |
| a_j | age of proposal j in days; H is the half-life |

$$
\text{Score} = \frac{3 \times \text{Community} + 3 \times \text{Holdings} + 10 \times \text{Votes}}{16}
$$

$$
\text{Score} = \frac{\sum_i w_i S_i}{\sum_i w_i} \quad \text{where} \quad
\begin{cases}
S_{\text{com}} = c \in [0, 100] \\
S_{\text{hold}} = 100 \min\left(1, \left(\frac{\bar{b}}{R}\right)^p\right), \quad \bar{b} = \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^T b_t \\
S_{\text{vote}} = 100 \frac{\sum_{j=1}^N v_j 2^{-a_j/H}}{\sum_{j=1}^N 2^{-a_j/H}}
\end{cases}
$$

title: Authorize a Contingent LDO CEX Liquidity Market-Making Mandate
body:
### Summary

This proposal requests Lido DAO to authorize a contingent, capped market-making mandate for LDO on centralized exchanges (CEXs), to reduce the risk of LDO trading-pair degradation or delisting due to insufficient liquidity.

The authorization covers two funding caps from the Lido DAO Treasury, in addition to the approved EGG budget ([EGG-2026](https://research.lido.fi/t/ecosystem-grants-grequest-egg-a-budget-request-framework-in-the-service-of-goose/6053)).

- Up to the lower of $1,500,000 in LDO equivalent or 7,500,000 LDO, as a recallable facility for market-making inventory.
- Up to 480,000 USDC for fixed market-maker retainers and directly related costs; to be disbursed at the start of each quarter via Easy Track.

No funds may be drawn unless [the Lido Growth Committee](https://research.lido.fi/t/rationalizing-liquidity-observation-lab-rewards-share-committee-growth-committee/10133) determines that LDO liquidity on certain centralized exchanges is insufficient, or likely to become insufficient. The Lido Growth Committee shall have discretion to determine the materiality of any particular centralized exchange and whether this mechanism should be activated in respect of that exchange. If activated in any instance, the mandate may operate for up to 12 months from the activation date. If the mandate is not activated within two years from the date of this vote, the authorization expires.

### Motivation

The Lido Ecosystem Foundation does not currently engage any market makers for LDO pairs. However, declining trading volume increases the risk that market makers active in LDO markets withdraw liquidity or that exchanges delist pairs, often with little advance notice. To prepare for such cases, a capped, pre-approved mandate would allow contributors to respond within a defined scope if a venue begins a review, without rushing governance. The mandate is preventive: it is not a commitment to activate a market-making program immediately upon approval, but an option to activate at any time.

### What this vote approves

1. A contingent LDO CEX market-making mandate for up to 12 months from activation. Continuation beyond that term requires a new DAO authorization. 
2. A recallable LDO facility of up to $1,500,000 (withdrawable in LDO equivalent) from the Lido DAO Treasury, valued at the CoinGecko LDO closing price in USD on the day before the relevant Easy Track motion is initiated, and capped at 7,500,000 LDO.
3. A budget of up to 480,000 USDC from the Lido DAO Treasury for fixed market-maker retainers and directly related costs.
4. Authority for the Lido Growth Committee to decide whether the mandate is activated, as well as authority for the Liquidity Observation Lab to support execution and onward disbursement. Any market maker will contract with the Lido Ecosystem Foundation.
5. Disbursement of both amounts through Easy Track transfer motions to [the Liquidity Observation Lab multisig](https://docs.lido.fi/deployed-contracts/#liquidity-observation-lab-multisigs) on Ethereum mainnet, using the existing Easy Track setup for USDC transfers, and a new Easy Track instance for LDO transfers, deployed and registered through the relevant DAO on-chain vote. Any disbursement of either LDO or USDC needs to be accompanied by appropriate reporting on the Lido Research Forum by the Growth Committee outlining the amount and purpose of each payment. The relationship to this motion should be apparent from this reporting.

Both caps are in addition to the approved EGG budget. Each drawdown follows the ordinary Easy Track process, including the objection period, any applicable per-motion or per-period limit, and requires the Growth Committee's activation determination as a prerequisite.

This proposal does not approve any specific market maker, exchange, call option, warrant, token purchase right, price-support activity, or use of mandate LDO for governance voting.

### Structure and restrictions

If activated, a recallable LDO facility is made available from the Lido DAO Treasury to the Lido Ecosystem Foundation, which makes a back-to-back recallable facility available to the selected market maker, with the LDO disbursed operationally via the Liquidity Observation Lab. Where feasible, assets would be held in a Foundation-owned CEX account with the market maker limited to trading permissions and no withdrawal rights.

Any final agreement with a market maker should require that:

- LDO provided under the facility is not used for governance voting.
- Activity is limited to two-sided liquidity provision and related inventory management, not price support.
- Lending, pledging, rehypothecation and use in exchange yield or margin-lending products are prohibited (unless the Growth Committee determines that the adverse impact on mandate pricing is too large).
- Manipulative trading, wash trading, spoofing, and abusive practices are prohibited.
- Withdrawal permissions are disabled or tightly controlled where Foundation-owned CEX accounts are used.
- Market-maker uptime is at least 95% and KPIs should include market maker best bid / best ask spread, liquidity depth within that spread and at +/- 50, +/- 100 and +/- 200 bps.
- Contracts between the Lido Ecosystem Foundation and market makers shall include reporting, recall, as well as a right to terminate the agreement upon 30 days’ notice.
- No call options or similar upside instruments are granted without separate DAO approval.
- The agreement ceases upon delisting of the relevant pair, with no further costs incurred from that point.

Unused LDO or USDC should remain with, or be returned to, the DAO Treasury address no later than 30 calendar days from the time of disbursement. 

### DAO Oversight and Reporting

A Snapshot vote may end this authorization at any time, subject to any remaining terms of external agreements concluded with market makers under this mandate. Any change to scope or budget, or deviation from the approved caps or purpose, requires separate DAO approval. Material defaults, losses, recalls, terminations, or deviations from the approved mandate should be disclosed promptly where legally and operationally permissible. Lido DAO bears all financial and credit risk associated with the program.

If the mandate is activated, the Lido Growth Committee should maintain reporting on the Lido Research forum, including:

1. An activation notice confirming that the required determination has been made.
2. A high-level summary of the market-maker engagement, to the extent contractually permissible, including intended Easy Track drawdowns, LDO amount, expected monthly retainer, venue and pair scope where disclosable, and whether Foundation-owned CEX accounts are used.
3. Quarterly updates covering USDC spend, outstanding LDO, and high-level performance, including market-maker uptime and the share of time agreed liquidity-depth KPIs are met at 50, 100, and 200 basis points from the mid-price on a per-venue basis.
4. A completion report within two weeks after the program ends, covering LDO returned, USDC spent, and any residual assets.

### Next steps

If the vote concludes positively:

- The authorization takes effect from the date of the vote conclusion and expires two years from that date if not activated earlier.
- A new Easy Track instance for LDO transfers to the Liquidity Observation Lab will be deployed in one of the upcoming DAO on-chain votes. USDC transfers will use the existing Easy Track setup.
- If the Growth Committee activates the mandate, it will publish an activation notice on the forum, and reporting will follow the schedule above.

title: [1IP-106] Establish the 1inch DAO Security Council and Ratify a Rotation of the DAO Treasury Multisig Signers
body:
## Simple Summary

This proposal establishes the 1inch DAO Security Council as the formally ratified signer set of the DAO Treasury multisig and ratifies the replacement of 7 of the 12 current signers with the slate listed below, voted on as a single slate.

## Abstract

The 1inch DAO Treasury is controlled by a 7-of-12 Safe whose signers were selected in 2021. This proposal:

- Constitutes the treasury signer set as the 1inch DAO Security Council, with a defined mandate, duties, and disclosure policy
- Ratifies a 7-seat rotation as one slate
- Requires that this rotation and every future signer change be executed on-chain through the DAO's SafeSnap module, so signer changes demonstrably flow from governance
- Establishes signer protections: a DAO-ratified good-faith safe harbor and liability cap now, with contractual indemnification, defense-cost advancement, and insurance to follow upon adoption of a DAO legal wrapper

## Motivation

Every comparable DAO — Arbitrum, Optimism, ZKsync, ENS, Aave, Polygon, Compound, Lido — subjects its security council or guardian multisig to token-holder ratification. 1inch DAO does not: the current signers were appointed five years ago, there is no charter, no removal procedure, no liveness requirement, and past signer swaps bypassed governance entirely. Ratifying the signer set by DAO vote closes the single largest legitimacy gap in 1inch DAO's structure and follows the industry standard whole-slate ratification model used by Optimism, ENS, and Aave.

## Specification

### 1. Establishment of the Security Council

The Council's powers are limited to:

- executing transactions approved by DAO vote via the SafeSnap module;
- vetoing malicious or faulty payloads during the 72-hour timelock at the existing 7-of-12 threshold;
- emergency response to protect treasury assets.

The Council has no discretionary spending authority.

**Composition.** 12 members; threshold unchanged at 7-of-12.

**Term.** Until further notice: members serve until they resign, are removed, or are replaced by DAO vote. Any change to the signer set or threshold requires a Snapshot vote and execution via the SafeSnap module; owner-executed signer changes are prohibited.

If required, the full Council composition will be submitted for re-ratification by a single confirm-or-replace Snapshot vote every 12 months from execution. Re-ratification does not interrupt Council operations.

**Removal.** Any member may be removed by a standard Snapshot vote. A member who fails two consecutive liveness checks, or is unreachable for 30 consecutive days, is deemed inactive and will be scheduled for replacement. A removed member may only return through a subsequent DAO vote.

### 2. Incoming members

The incoming team consists of delegates, core contributors and an external contributor. They are: aegis, ampheatmin, bob, bonaci, faradaemon, spindoctor & tonet. The remaining 5 seats are held by continuing signers of the existing multisig, whose seats are ratified as part of this proposal.

### 3. Member requirements and key management

- Suspected key compromise is reported to the Council immediately; the affected member abstains from signing and a replacement process begins.
- Members maintain baseline proficiency in secure key management and signing standards.

### 4. Liveness and accountability

- Members acknowledge and act on signing requests within 72 hours in normal operations and within 24 hours during a declared emergency.
- The Council performs a scheduled liveness check at least once per year: a signed message or test transaction proving key access for every member.
- Failure to satisfy a scheduled liveness check feeds the inactive-member process defined under Removal above, mirroring the automatic-removal standard of the Optimism Security Council charter.

### 5. Disclosure and transparency

Members disclose material conflicts of interest on any transaction they are asked to sign and abstain where conflicted.

### 6. Emergency actions

Emergency response is limited to actions strictly necessary to protect treasury assets from imminent loss, such as vetoing a malicious or faulty payload during the timelock.

Emergency powers exclude discretionary transfers, investments, and any action that can safely wait for the standard governance process.

Within 72 hours of any non-drill emergency action, the Council publishes an incident report on the governance forum covering the threat, the action taken, and the rationale. The DAO may review and, where applicable, reverse the action by Snapshot vote.

### 7. Compensation

Council seats are not compensated under this proposal. Any future compensation requires a separate 1IP with a defined budget and funding source.

### 8. Signer protection and indemnification

**Charter protections.** The protections in this section are adopted by the DAO through this vote and bind through governance rather than through any legal entity. Each member acknowledges the charter in writing before activation; upon adoption of a DAO legal wrapper, the protections convert into contractual agreements per the Wrapper handover below.

**Good-faith safe harbor.** A member who in good faith signs, or declines to sign, a transaction pursuant to a valid DAO vote and this charter incurs no personal liability to the DAO or token holders for losses that later result. Council service is ministerial execution of DAO decisions and creates no fiduciary or trustee relationship beyond this charter.

**Carve-outs.** No protection under this section, and no wrapper-stage indemnification, advancement, or insurance, applies to fraud, deliberate misconduct, or knowing breach of this charter.

**Wrapper handover.** Upon the DAO adopting a legal wrapper, the wrapper executes uniform signer agreements with each member providing contractual indemnification, advancement of defense costs, and, where available on commercially reasonable terms, directors-and-officers insurance, supplementing the protections in this section.

**Survival.** These protections survive resignation, removal, or replacement in respect of acts and omissions during service.

### 9. Execution

Upon a passing Snapshot vote, the rotation is executed on-chain through the SafeSnap module against the DAO Treasury Safe (`eth:0x7951c7ef839e26F63DA87a42C9a87986507f1c07`) using atomic `swapOwner` calls. The Safe never leaves its 7-of-12 configuration during execution.

Execution passes the standard reality.eth escalation period (minimum 72 hours) and the 72-hour Timelock before taking effect.

Within 7 days of execution, the Council completes a verification signing exercise confirming every member has key access, and the published roster is updated.

## Rationale

Slate ratification and overall process follows industry standards and precedent set from other DAOs. Open-ended terms avoid election overhead.

A single-slate vote is atomic; it avoids partial outcomes in which some seats rotate and others do not, leaving the Safe in an unratified hybrid state. The 7-of-12 threshold is retained because it matches the existing veto quorum and is battle-tested for this treasury; changing composition and threshold in the same vote would confound the result. The annual re-ratification checkpoint preserves token-holder control without standing election machinery, as a lighter-weight alternative to the six-month cohort elections used by Arbitrum, proportionate to a treasury-scope council.

## Consideration

Alternatives considered:

1. Per-seat elections on the Arbitrum model, with staggered cohorts and standing election infrastructure — rejected at this stage as disproportionate for a treasury-scope council, and adoptable later by amending this charter.
2. Retaining appointment of signers — rejected because it perpetuates the legitimacy gap this proposal closes.

This proposal supersedes the selected signer arrangement described in the 1inch DAO Guidelines. The DAO governance documentation is updated to reflect the Security Council within 7 days of execution.

As a standard proposal, this vote requires the 10 million Unicorn Power quorum on a 7-day Snapshot vote. Delegates are encouraged to signal voting intentions during the temperature check so quorum coverage is visible before the Snapshot opens.

The signer protections in Section 8 involve no legal entity and no treasury spend: the safe harbor and liability cap are adopted by this vote and bind through governance; contractual indemnification, advancement, and insurance follow at the wrapper stage through uniform signer agreements. Until then, the protections operate as a governance commitment rather than a contract.

## Security Considerations

The rotation replaces a majority of a signer set whose key liveness is currently unverifiable. During execution, the Safe never drops below its 7-of-12 threshold because `swapOwner` replaces members atomically.

The SafeSnap question for this rotation must be actively monitored throughout the escalation window: fraudulent and spoofed questions have been observed across DAOs, and the bonding mechanism plus the 72-hour escalation period are the defense.

title: SAEP-21: Update Delegate Compensation
body:
# SAEP-21: Update Delegate Compensation - September 14, 2026

Spark's Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Phoenix Labs.

## Review

The Spark community can hereby express support or opposition to the following changes:

### Summary

The proposal recommends that Spark governance amend the [A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.6 - Incentives & Compensation](https://sky-atlas.io/#5e38acbd-f010-4bd1-af6c-acdd17b3e9e9) section of the Spark Artifact to give the Spark Foundation sole discretion to determine Delegate compensation, subject to limits of USD 4,000 per Delegate per calendar month and USD 20,000 in aggregate across all Delegates for the same month.

### Background

The current compensation provision was introduced by [SAEP-05: Modify Delegate Framework](https://snapshot.box/#/s:sparkfi.eth/proposal/0x1e65428aec69a2947d3bb4823755eec03599fde51fa6054d0a313239b81b29ed) and states: 

> Active Delegates receive USD 4,000 per calendar month.

The Spark Foundation administers compensation from its approved operating budget. Payments are monthly in arrears, prorated for partial months, and conditional on good standing and performance, with withholding or clawback available for non-performance or breach. The fixed amount limits the Foundation’s ability to reduce compensation expenditure when appropriate.

### Proposal Details

If approved, the following changes will be made in the Spark Artifact:

- Amend [A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.6 - Incentives & Compensation](https://sky-atlas.io/#5e38acbd-f010-4bd1-af6c-acdd17b3e9e9) to give the Spark Foundation sole discretion to determine compensation within both monthly ceilings, replace the historical startup dates with prospective notice and service-period treatment, and retain the approved-budget, arrears, proration, eligibility, clawback, and oversight provisions (Change 1).

### Justification

**The Foundation gains operational flexibility to reduce expenditure when appropriate.** The amendment allows the Spark Foundation to determine compensation within defined limits as part of its existing budget administration. The individual ceiling limits compensation for each Delegate, and the aggregate ceiling constrains total compensation as the number of Delegates changes. The Foundation must manage both limits within its approved operating budget.

**Prospective notice preserves the treatment of service already provided.** The Foundation communicates compensation and its effective date before the relevant service begins. Existing payment-in-arrears and proration rules continue to apply, and compensation for earlier service remains subject to the terms applicable to that service, including performance-related withholding and clawback.

**Compensation discretion reduces the certainty of a fixed stipend.** This may affect Delegate retention and create perceived pressure on voting independence. Advanced communication gives Delegates the opportunity to assess the terms on which they serve. Delegates remain subject to their responsibilities, including vote rationales and conflict disclosure, and must abstain where impartiality is compromised under [A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.3 - Delegate Responsibilities](https://sky-atlas.io/#f230ba4e-eb5a-444e-b07a-13a0292338bd). These controls remain relevant safeguards, while the possibility of influence through compensation remains a trade-off for governance to consider.
---

The required Spark Artifact changes can be found in the following pull request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/333

## Outcomes

- If "For" receives the most votes, the proposal will be approved. The associated pull request will be merged into Spark's artifact. When required, the listed changes will proceed to implementation by the relevant actors.
- If "Against" receives the most votes, the proposal will be rejected. No changes will be implemented.

title: SAEP-23: Update SubProxy Management Artifact Section
body:
# SAEP-23: Update SubProxy Management Artifact Section - September 14, 2026

Spark's Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Phoenix Labs.

## Review

The Spark community can hereby express support or opposition to the following changes:

### Summary

The proposal recommends that Spark governance amend the Spark [SubProxy Management](https://sky-atlas.io/#2ad53f55-44cb-44fd-9e68-6c7ed128e360) section of the Spark Artifact to:

- Increase the Spark Product Backstop in section [A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.2.3 - Parameters](https://sky-atlas.io/#7410ed94-db95-437a-a4d2-9120036ec7bd) from 1 million USDS to 5 million USDS.
- Deduct accrued but unrealized Spark Savings yield liabilities when calculating Current SubProxy Value in accordance with section [A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.3.1.1 - Current SubDAO Proxy Value](https://sky-atlas.io/#9705a4be-e92f-4195-8e85-1cfe19ec1a0d): USDS held in the Spark SubProxy on Ethereum, less the USDS value of yield accrued on Spark Savings depositors' positions that they have not withdrawn.
- Realign the [A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.3.2 - Operational Process](https://sky-atlas.io/#dfa483c7-5adb-480e-9f82-c97cf4d0f74e): calculate the value of the Spark SubProxy as of 16:00 UTC on the first (1st) day of each month; include the buyback transfer in the next available Spark proxy Spell with a voting date scheduled on or after the twenty-second (22nd) day of that month; and require the Buyback Executor to purchase SPK tokens through an onchain time-weighted average price (TWAP) mechanism over ninety (90) days in respect of each buyback transfer.

The proposed amendments are limited to the Target SubProxy Value and Excess SubProxy Funds Disposition Policy documents, including their definitions, parameters and operational process.

### Background

#### Current reserve and buyback policy
The Target SubProxy Value is calculated in accordance with the [A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.2.2 - Evaluation Method](https://sky-atlas.io/#99d4b8da-fa5c-49ce-b93c-70d07334d7aa) and is equal to the greater of the Required Risk Capital (RRC) plus the Spark Product Backstop, or the Operational Expense Reserve. The following parameters are in effect at this time: a Spark Product Backstop of 1 million USDS, an RRC Lookback Period of three (3) months and a Target Runway of twelve (12) months. The [Spark Product Backstop definition](https://sky-atlas.io/#ac10196b-18b2-4bc4-8627-0cacac8a3524) covers product risk exposures that are not covered by Sky’s Required Risk Capital framework.

The Current SubProxy Value is set to take into account the Spark SubProxy’s Ethereum USDS balance without deducting the USDS value of yield accrued on Spark Savings depositors’ positions that they have not withdrawn. Spark’s Q2 2026 financial report already reflects such yield as a treasury liability. The proposed amendment would align section [A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.3.1.1 - Current SubDAO Proxy Value](https://sky-atlas.io/#9705a4be-e92f-4195-8e85-1cfe19ec1a0d) to Spark’s financial reporting and cause the calculation of excess value and buyback amounts to account for these liabilities.

The Operational Process calculates the values immediately after Spark’s monthly settlement with Sky and directs the resulting buyback amount into the next available Spark proxy Spell. Its [parameter record](https://sky-atlas.io/#b52a4011-5346-4de7-9522-90ae66b81600) specifies a twenty-five percent (25%) Standard Buyback Rate, one hundred percent (100%) Enhanced Buyback Rate and two hundred percent (200%) Enhanced Buyback Threshold, with no absolute monthly transfer cap. The [Enhanced Buyback Threshold](https://sky-atlas.io/#e150176c-1da5-4adb-ba5d-f344d0be03ae) is a percentage of the Target SubProxy Value, and the [Enhanced Buyback Rate](https://sky-atlas.io/#0efbdfe8-3ccd-4e6a-8195-a52e7f63c1d9) applies to the Current SubProxy Value from and above that threshold.

#### Governance history and scope
[SAEP-06: SubDAO Proxy Management Plan](https://snapshot.box/#/s:sparkfi.eth/proposal/0x7a372d3f034aa966c72621d9e6b3762fa04c084e02243fcdaf9dac286a8641d9), approved on November 27, 2025, introduced these policies with a 5 million USDS Spark Product Backstop. [SAEP-09: Adjust SubDAO Proxy Management](https://snapshot.box/#/s:sparkfi.eth/proposal/0xdc4f3859185ca5caa7b7eb1c6ef732546469d4a9df68b7d8b31ec8ad9b0a72fc), approved on January 29, 2026, reduced the Spark Product Backstop to 1 million USDS and established the RRC Lookback Period, Target Runway and Standard Buyback Rate that are in effect at this time.

A search of all eighteen (18) consolidated Atlas content files by target UUID, document number and defined-term variants found the affected policy references to be entirely within the Spark [SubProxy Management](https://sky-atlas.io/#2ad53f55-44cb-44fd-9e68-6c7ed128e360) section. The proposed amendments as outlined in the Proposal Details under 1 through 3 address the proposed amendments in their entirety, including the Current SubProxy Value note that presently refers to the most up-to-date onchain value.

### Proposal Details

The proposal is for Spark governance to approve the following amendments to the Spark [SubProxy Management](https://sky-atlas.io/#2ad53f55-44cb-44fd-9e68-6c7ed128e360) section of the Spark Artifact:

- Amend [A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.2.3 - Parameters](https://sky-atlas.io/#7410ed94-db95-437a-a4d2-9120036ec7bd) to increase the Spark Product Backstop to 5 million USDS.
- Amend [A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.3.1.1 - Current SubDAO Proxy Value](https://sky-atlas.io/#9705a4be-e92f-4195-8e85-1cfe19ec1a0d) to deduct the USDS value of accrued but unrealized Spark Savings vault yield liabilities when calculating the Current SubProxy Value and apply the valuation timeframe specified in the Operational Process.
- Amend [A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.3.2 - Operational Process](https://sky-atlas.io/#dfa483c7-5adb-480e-9f82-c97cf4d0f74e) to establish valuation of the Spark SubProxy on the first day of the month, the Spark proxy Spell voting timeframe, and the ninety (90) day timeframe for the Buyback Executor to execute the buyback transfer onchain through TWAP, while preserving the Buyback Executor's obligation to transfer SPK tokens to the Spark SubProxy.

### Justification

**The increased Spark Product Backstop increases the product-risk reserve input.** Increasing the Spark Product Backstop to 5 million USDS increases the risk-capital branch of the target calculation while retaining the existing comparison with the Operational Expense Reserve. It may reduce the amount available for buybacks. Its adequacy remains dependent on actual exposures and the Required Risk Capital calculation and ongoing risk controls continue to apply.

**Deducting the accrued but unrealized Spark Savings yield liabilities when calculating the Current SubProxy Value reduces the amount treated as excess.** The deduction recognizes yield already accrued on Spark Savings depositors' positions before capital is allocated to buybacks. Its amount depends on accurate liability measurement. Defining the deduction in USDS and measuring it at the same time as the Spark SubProxy's USDS balance gives Spark a consistent basis for the calculation of the Current SubProxy Value and subsequent Spark proxy Spell preparation.

**The monthly valuation of the Spark SubProxy Value and the excess value and buyback amounts on the first (1st) day of the month provides a common valuation time.** A first-day valuation of the Spark SubProxy and a Spark proxy Spell voting date on or after the twenty-second (22nd) of the month separate the valuation of the Spark SubProxy from subsequent execution. The snapshot can become stale as balances, liabilities and risk exposures change. Spark's continuous capital obligations under [A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2 - Primes' Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management](https://sky-atlas.io/#3af8a3a2-25e5-44b3-87a4-7df1f2712685), and its existing requirement to take immediate action on an excessive Encumbrance Ratio, remain applicable throughout that interval.

**A separate TWAP period spreads each buyback transfer's purchases across ninety (90) days.** Execution over a longer period extends exposure to the Buyback Executor's custody, market prices and mechanism failures. The Buyback Executor retains responsibility for executing each buyback transfer to purchase SPK tokens and to transfer the purchased SPK tokens to the Spark SubProxy. A TWAP schedule does not guarantee a purchase price or eliminate execution risk.

The retained Spark SubProxy and Buyback Executor wallet addresses match those listed in the [Spark address registry](https://github.com/sparkdotfi/spark-address-registry/blob/ecea29bd2a1546bbbf4999e486b3c04f0e10b748/src/Ethereum.sol) at the time of this proposal. Their deployed contract code was verified through Etherscan V2 `eth_getCode` reads at Ethereum block 25,934,180 on 8 September 2026. Those reads are reproducible at that block and governance responsibilities are established by the cited Artifact sections.

---

The required Spark Artifact changes can be found in the following pull request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/335

## Outcomes

- If "For" receives the most votes, the proposal will be approved. The associated pull request will be merged into Spark's artifact. When required, the listed changes will proceed to implementation by the relevant actors.
- If "Against" receives the most votes, the proposal will be rejected. No changes will be implemented.

title: [Ethereum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Sentora x Spark RLUSD Force-Deallocate Penalty Update
body:
# [Ethereum] Spark Liquidity Layer - Sentora x Spark RLUSD Force-Deallocate Penalty Update - September 14, 2026

Spark's Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Phoenix Labs.

## Review

The Spark community can hereby express support or opposition to the following changes:

- Increase the force-deallocate penalty on the Sentora x Spark RLUSD vault’s existing Morpho market adapter from 0 to **0.01% (1 basis point)**.

### Required Context

The [Sentora x Spark RLUSD vault](https://app.morpho.org/ethereum/vault/0xFC8C624B6080a0a780583799f2A862DE936F6E22/sentora-x-spark-rlusd#overview) is an existing Morpho Vaults V2 vault onboarded to the Spark Liquidity Layer in the September 10, 2026 spell cycle. The scope of the deployment and onboarding context can be found under Item 5 in the [September 10, 2026 spell technical scope forum post](https://forum.skyeco.com/t/september-10-2026-proposed-changes-to-spark-for-upcoming-spell/28208)

This standalone change uses the vault’s existing curator authority. The penalty is stored **per adapter on the vault**. The target is its sole registered adapter, also its liquidity adapter, `MorphoMarketV1AdapterV2`. The vault owner, curator, sentinels, and allocator permissions are unchanged.

[Sentora instance](https://sky-atlas.io/#67d8abe9-a398-4c7c-9e0d-ee48e97489e1) identifies the curator as a 2-of-2 Safe controlled jointly by Soter Labs (GovOps in the operating plan) and Sentora. GovOps will initiate the curator Safe transaction. Sentora’s signer Safe will approve and execute it after initiation. The on-chain caller of `submit(bytes)` must be the curator Safe itself.

### Proposed Actions

If this proposal is approved, the Sentora x Spark RLUSD force-deallocate penalty will be set to **0.01% (1 basis point)** with the following actions:

#### 1. Submit the Penalty Change to the Vault’s Timelock

GovOps submits the penalty change to the vault’s timelock, scheduling the approved increase with the vault’s required delay and cancellation window. GovOps initiates the curator Safe transaction through its signer seat. Sentora’s signer Safe approves and executes the outer curator Safe transaction.

Parameter change:

- `forceDeallocatePenalty(adapter)`: 0 (0%) → `100000000000000` (1e14, 0.01%, 1 bp)
- `timelock(0x3e9d2ac7)`: `604800` seconds (7 days) → Unchanged

#### 2. Apply the Approved Change after the Timelock

After the timelock has passed (earliest on Thursday, September 24, 2026, at or after the exact UTC timestamp recorded by `executableAt(data)`), Sentora, as planned executor, applies the parameter change, provided the approved action remains queued.

The seven days begin with the mined vault submission, not Safe proposal creation or the first signature. September 24 is achievable only if `submit(data)` is mined on September 17 after poll approval, at the corresponding UTC time. A later submission shifts execution by the same amount. Once mature, execution is permissionless and has no automatic expiry.

If the poll is rejected, neither of the proposed actions is performed. If an unapproved or incorrect payload is nevertheless queued, the curator or a sentinel must call `revoke(bytes)` on the vault with that offending submission’s exact calldata before its recorded maturity. Withholding Sentora’s final signature alone does not cancel a mature vault action.

### Justification

A nonzero penalty gives permissionless forced deallocation a cost, discouraging callers from disrupting the allocator’s chosen allocations. A force-deallocation of 1,000,000 RLUSD would incur a 100 RLUSD-equivalent penalty, paid by burning shares from `onBehalf`. The retained assets benefit remaining vault shareholders. Ordinary withdrawals and allocator/sentinel `deallocate` do not invoke this penalty. Recognition of retained penalty assets is subject to the vault’s `maxRate accounting`. See the [force-deallocation implementation](https://github.com/morpho-org/vault-v2/blob/6f2af6602e05d9e123a87c1067712a4566608044/src/VaultV2.sol#L813-L831).
---
For more details, please see the [Technical Scope: Sentora x Spark RLUSD Force-Deallocate Penalty Update forum post](https://forum.skyeco.com/t/technical-scope-sentora-x-spark-rlusd-force-deallocate-penalty-update/28230/1)

title: SAEP-22: Update Risk Curation Framework
body:
# SAEP-22: Update Risk Curation Framework - September 14, 2026

Spark's Operational Facilitator has placed a proposal into the voting system on behalf of nested contributor Phoenix Labs.

## Review

The Spark community can hereby express support or opposition to the following changes:

### Summary

The proposal recommends that Spark governance update the [A.6.1.1.1.3.9 - Risk Curation Framework](https://sky-atlas.io/#78018ebc-c69d-44f6-b602-190edca11483) section of the Spark Artifact to:
- Exempt Sky-designated cancellation actors, including the Operational GovOps of an Operational Executor Agent, from curator/cancellation-authority independence requirements.
- Permit Curators to queue changes before polling closes when the timelock expires at least twenty-four (24) hours after the poll's expected close, with responsibility for cancelling unapproved changes before they become executable.

Vault appointments, contract permissions, configured timelock delays, and risk parameters remain unchanged.

### Background

#### Existing Independence Rule

[A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.3.1 - Cancellation Authority Independence](https://sky-atlas.io/#ea50c8da-008e-4f0f-b2df-ac666d5faf13) currently states:

> The cancellation authority holder controlled by the Operational Executor Agent must use a signer set separate from the signer set of the Curator multisig for the same smart contract instance, and at least one cancellation authority holder must be fully independent of every entity serving in the Curator role. Compromise or misalignment of the Curator role must not in itself remove the ability of the cancellation authority to cancel pending changes.

The framework uses cancellation authority for the guardian role in Morpho Vaults v1 and the sentinel role in v2 ([A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.3 - Cancellation Authority](https://sky-atlas.io/#900c4a0d-ed93-41ad-b914-f84d50d6940e)). This document is the only explicit Spark curator/cancellation independence rule. The five framework instance records and the Curator/Guardian address fields in the Allocation System describe role arrangements; the proposed exemption does not amend their recorded appointments.

#### Sky-designated Participation

Sky's operational criteria, as communicated to the proposer, require OEA participation in both curation and cancellation. The externally curated arrangement uses joint OEA and external-curator control; the nonexternally curated arrangement uses sole OEA curation. The supplied criteria also specify separate OEA cancellation signers. This proposal removes Spark's independence condition for the designated actors; Sky's own operational requirements continue to apply.

Sky Governance designates transitional [Executor Agents](https://sky-atlas.io/#2dc20bcf-08d7-4314-a2f2-aee9b41940e1). Spark's Executor Accord identifies Amatsu with [SoterLabs as its Operational GovOps](https://sky-atlas.io/#66845ee6-4405-4ed8-bb22-4a7558e63a52). The exemption includes that role and other actors expressly designated by Sky Governance for the relevant cancellation function.

#### Queueing before Polling Closes

The [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.4.1 - Polling Requirement](https://sky-atlas.io/#218f889f-6a5d-46a8-b8a3-cb0a075825c2) currently states:
> All curator-executed changes must be approved in advance by Spark governance through a polling process.

[A.6.1.1.1.3.9.4.2 - Execution Authority](https://sky-atlas.io/#48e6eeb9-86c0-4bfa-8be0-e9917d163118) then authorizes transaction submission following successful approval.

The proposed rule allows the timelock to run before the related poll is created or approved, provided that the pending change cannot become executable until at least twenty-four (24) hours after the expected poll close. Once the poll's actual closing time is known, cancellation on timing grounds is required only if less than twenty (20) hours remain between that close and the pending change becoming executable. Implementation still requires approval of the exact queued change. The existing minimum three (3) day [timelock requirement](https://sky-atlas.io/#9cb30c4c-ecbb-4874-a931-b900b868b888) and [public visibility requirement](https://sky-atlas.io/#4f45b29e-9f94-48d3-940c-1cd6b1f06f4b) continue to apply.

### Proposal Details

If approved, the following changes will be applied to the [A.6.1.1.1.3.9 - Risk Curation Framework](https://sky-atlas.io/#78018ebc-c69d-44f6-b602-190edca11483) section of the Spark Artifact:

- Amend [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.3.1 - Cancellation Authority Independence](https://sky-atlas.io/#ea50c8da-008e-4f0f-b2df-ac666d5faf13) to exempt the Operational GovOps of an Operational Executor Agent and other actors expressly designated by Sky Governance for the relevant cancellation function from the section's independence requirements, including separate signers and any requirement for an additional independent cancellation authority holder.
- Amend [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.3.2 - Scope of Authority](https://sky-atlas.io/#e4fb1a94-cfd8-40d3-ac79-966dd9f8db24), [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.4 - Governance Approval Process](https://sky-atlas.io/#e3ddbd39-ee57-4b17-b66e-8bc823a03098), [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.4.1 - Polling Requirement](https://sky-atlas.io/#218f889f-6a5d-46a8-b8a3-cb0a075825c2), and [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.4.2 - Execution Authority](https://sky-atlas.io/#48e6eeb9-86c0-4bfa-8be0-e9917d163118) to permit queueing before polling closes under the twenty-four (24) hour condition while retaining approval before implementation.
- Amend [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.3.3 - Reporting of Curator Actions](https://sky-atlas.io/#6f64ac9e-daf1-4339-8046-3894e57f4383) to identify the related poll, its approval status at queueing, and expected closing time when reporting an early queued change.
- Amend [A.6.1.1.1.3.9.6.2 - Cancellation Reasons](https://sky-atlas.io/#0e572cad-bdf2-437f-b272-0cd634424b19) to make the Curator and cancellation authority holders responsible for ensuring cancellation before execution eligibility when the poll does not approve the change or its actual closing time leaves less than twenty (20) hours before the change becomes executable.

### Justification

**The exemption avoids making Spark policy depend on enforcement of OEA signer arrangements.** Sky requires OEA participation in curation and cancellation. Spark does not have a clean mechanism to enforce the OEA's internal signer arrangements on Sky's behalf. Waiving this Spark condition accommodates the designated actor without adding a signer attestation, audit or enforcement procedure. The exemption leaves Sky's own requirements and the actor's underlying mandate in place.

**Timelocks and owner intervention retain a route to cancel harmful pending changes.** The framework retains governance approval before implementation, public visibility, cancellation reasons, and reporting. In the documented Morpho v1 and v1.1 implementations, the owner can cancel relevant pending actions directly. In v2, the owner can add a sentinel without a vault timelock, after which that sentinel can revoke the pending action. Appointing a role alone does not cancel the action. These capabilities are documented in the official [v1 implementation](https://github.com/morpho-org/metamorpho/blob/48b472b919791d898853fff9f9087cec0b130635/src/MetaMorpho.sol#L138-L181), [v1.1 implementation](https://github.com/morpho-org/metamorpho-v1.1/blob/89de5264c22e0e6e4e075a67046d120a7e7dbcff/src/MetaMorphoV1_1.sol#L154-L197), and [v2 implementation](https://github.com/morpho-org/vault-v2/blob/0777682f9d7e87687e2dbbc5a9cfde5247dc3a73/src/VaultV2.sol#L315-L379).

**The exemption accepts greater reliance on timely owner intervention.** The exempt arrangement can share signing control and institutional direction between curation and cancellation. Timelocks provide a response window, but detection, authorization, and transaction execution must complete before the harmful action executes. The owner must remain available and uncompromised. These safeguards do not reproduce an independent veto or eliminate the risk of correlated compromise.

**The general rule remains in place outside the exemption.** An external Curator's participation alongside OEA does not independently qualify that external Curator for an exemption in another arrangement. Qualification follows the specified OEA GovOps role or an express Sky Governance designation for the cancellation role in the relevant instance. The amendment retains the existing document identity and requires no renumbering.

**Overlapping polling and the timelock can reduce the wait after approval.** Queueing becomes permissible as soon as the configured timelock can expire at least twenty-four (24) hours after the expected poll close. This retains the full applicable timelock. Cancellation on timing grounds is required only if the actual poll close leaves less than twenty (20) hours before execution eligibility, allowing up to four (4) hours of posting delay at the initial boundary. The new permission applies to Curators generally, independently of the Sky-designated-actor exemption.

**Unapproved pending changes require active cancellation.** The Curator and cancellation authority holders must monitor the poll outcome and ensure that an unapproved change is cancelled before it becomes executable. One authorized actor can complete the cancellation for all of them. Reporting identifies the poll and relevant UTC times. If these actors fail to cancel in time, the unapproved change may become executable despite the policy prohibition; a timelock does not itself evaluate the poll result.

---

The required Spark Artifact changes can be found in the following pull request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/334

## Outcomes

- If "For" receives the most votes, the proposal will be approved. The associated pull request will be merged into Spark's artifact. When required, the listed changes will proceed to implementation by the relevant actors.
- If "Against" receives the most votes, the proposal will be rejected. No changes will be implemented.
